## rating-group

### Roles and attributes
- Given a Rating with `defaultValue: 1`, `length: 3` and `orientation: 'vertical'`, when rendered, then the first `role="radio"` item has `data-state="active"` and items 2 and 3 have no `data-state`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given a default Rating > should have default selected")
- Given a disabled Rating with `defaultValue: 1` and `length: 3`, when rendered, then the first item has `data-state="active"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given disabled Rating > should have default selected")
- Given a disabled Rating with `length: 3`, when rendered, then item 1 has both `disabled=""` and `data-disabled=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given disabled Rating > should have disabled attribute on item")
- Given a disabled Rating with `length: 3`, when rendered, then item 2 has both `disabled=""` and `data-disabled=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given disabled Rating > should have disabled attribute on item")
- Given a disabled Rating with `length: 3`, when rendered, then item 3 has both `disabled=""` and `data-disabled=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given disabled Rating > should have disabled attribute on item")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 3` and `max: 5`, when rendered, then the root has `role="slider"`, `aria-valuenow="3"`, `aria-valuemin="0"`, `aria-valuemax="5"`, `aria-valuetext="3 out of 5"`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, `aria-label="Rating"` and `tabindex="0"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Accessibility > should have proper ARIA attributes for slider role")
- Given a RatingGroup with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the root has `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="-1"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Accessibility > should have proper ARIA attributes when disabled")
- Given a RatingGroup with `required: true`, when rendered, then the root has `aria-required="true"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Accessibility > should have proper ARIA attributes when required")
- Given a RatingGroup with `max: 3`, when rendered, then each item has `role="presentation"` and neither an `aria-label` nor a `tabindex`, so only the root is focusable. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Accessibility > should have items with presentation role")
- Given a RatingGroup with `max: 3`, when rendered, then the root has `data-rating-group-root` and each item has `data-rating-group-item`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Data Attributes > should have bits data attrs")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 2.5`, `max: 5`, `disabled: true`, `readonly: true` and `orientation: 'vertical'`, when rendered, then the root has `aria-valuenow="2.5"`, `aria-valuemax="5"`, `data-disabled=""`, `data-readonly=""` and `data-orientation="vertical"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Data Attributes > should have correct data attributes on root")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 2.5`, `max: 3` and `allowHalf: true`, when rendered, then item 0 has `data-state="active"`, item 1 has `data-state="active"` and item 2 has `data-state="partial"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Data Attributes > should have correct data attributes on items")
- Given a RatingGroup with `orientation: 'vertical'`, when rendered, then the root has `aria-orientation="vertical"` and `data-orientation="vertical"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Orientation > should have correct aria-orientation for vertical")
- Given a RatingGroup with no `orientation` prop, when rendered, then the root has `aria-orientation="horizontal"` and `data-orientation="horizontal"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Orientation > should have correct aria-orientation for horizontal (default)")
- Given a RatingGroup with `max: 3`, when rendered, then items 0, 1 and 2 exist and item 3 does not. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Max Value > should render correct number of items based on max")
- Given a RatingGroup with `min: 1` and `max: 5`, when rendered, then the root has `aria-valuemin="1"` and `aria-valuemax="5"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Min Value > should use min value for aria-valuemin")
- Given a RatingGroup with `max: 5` and `value: 0`, when rendered, then the root has `aria-valuenow="0"` and `aria-valuetext="0 out of 5"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Value Display > should update aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext when value changes")

### Keyboard
- Given a vertical Rating with `defaultValue: 1` and `length: 3`, when the first item is focused and `ArrowDown` is pressed, then items 1 and 2 both have `data-state="active"` and focus has moved to item 2. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given a default Rating > on keyboard navigation > should select next item on keydown")
- Given a vertical Rating advanced to `2` by `ArrowDown`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then item 1 is `active` and item 3 has no `data-state`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given a default Rating > on keyboard navigation > on arrow up > should select the first item again")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 2` and the root focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed then `ArrowUp`, then the value goes `3` then `4`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should increment value with arrow right/up keys")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 3` and the root focused, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed then `ArrowDown`, then the value goes `2` then `1`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should decrement value with arrow left/down keys")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 2` and `allowHalf: true`, when `ArrowRight` is pressed twice then `ArrowLeft` once, then the value goes `2.5`, `3`, then back to `2.5`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should handle half steps when allowHalf is true")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 3` and the root focused, when `Home` is pressed, then the value is `0`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should go to minimum with Home key")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 2` and `max: 5`, when `End` is pressed, then the value is `5`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should go to maximum with End key")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 2`, when `PageUp` is pressed then `PageDown`, then the value goes `3` then back to `2`, so page keys step by one like the arrows. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should handle Page Up/Down keys")
- Given a RatingGroup with `max: 5` and the root focused, when `4` is typed then `0`, then the value goes `4` then `0`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should handle number keys for direct rating")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 2` and `disabled: true`, when the root is focused and `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the value stays `2`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should not respond to keyboard when disabled")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 2` and `readonly: true`, when the root is focused and `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the value stays `2`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should not respond to keyboard when readonly")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 1`, `min: 0` and `max: 3`, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then the value clamps at `0`, and after `End` reaches `3` a further `ArrowRight` leaves it at `3`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Keyboard Navigation > should clamp values to min/max bounds")
- Given a RatingGroup with `min: 1`, `max: 5` and `value: 3`, when `Home` is pressed, then the value is `1` rather than `0`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Min Value > should go to minimum with Home key")
- Given a RatingGroup with `min: 1`, `max: 5` and `value: 1`, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then the value stays `1`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Min Value > should not allow values below min with keyboard")
- Given a RatingGroup with `min: 2` and `max: 4`, when `1` is typed, then the value stays `2`; when `3` is typed the value becomes `3`; when `5` is typed the value stays `3`, so out of range digits are ignored. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Min Value > should only accept number keys within min-max range")
- Given a RatingGroup with `max: 5` and the root focused, when `5` is typed, then the value is `5`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Value Changes > should handle typing a number to set a value")
- Given a RatingGroup with `allowHalf: true` and `max: 5` under fake timers, when the sequence `2.5` is typed into the root and pending timers run, then the value is `2.5`, so a decimal point is buffered across keystrokes. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Decimal Input Sequences > should handle typing '2.5' sequence for half ratings")

- Given a disabled Rating with `defaultValue: 1`, when item 1 is clicked, then it stays `data-state="active"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given disabled Rating > should not select any item")
- Given a disabled Rating with `defaultValue: 1`, when item 2 is clicked, then it still has no `data-state`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given disabled Rating > should not select any item")
- Given a disabled Rating with `defaultValue: 1`, when item 3 is clicked, then it still has no `data-state`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given disabled Rating > should not select any item")

(reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given a hoverable Rating > should reset the preview to the model value on mouse leave")

- Given a RatingGroup with `hoverPreview: false`, when item 2 is hovered, then item states stay `active`, `inactive`, `inactive`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Hover Preview > should not show preview when hoverPreview is disabled")
- Given a RatingGroup with `disabled: true`, when item 2 is hovered, then item states stay `active`, `inactive`, `inactive`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Hover Preview > should not show preview when disabled")
- Given a RatingGroup with `readonly: true`, when item 2 is hovered, then item states stay `active`, `inactive`, `inactive`. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Hover Preview > should not show preview when readonly")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 1`, `max: 5` and `allowHalf: true`, when item 2 is hovered at position `x: 5, y: 5`, then states read `active`, `active`, `partial`, `inactive`, so the hovered item previews a half value from the pointer offset. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Hover Preview > should work with mouse pointer events for hover preview")
- Given a RatingGroup with `value: 3`, `min: 2`, `max: 5` and `hoverPreview: true`, when item 0 is hovered, then the preview floors at `min`, leaving states `active`, `active`, `inactive`, `inactive`. - Given a RatingGroup with `value: 1`, `min: 0` and `max: 5`, when the already active first item is clicked, then the value clears to `0`. ### Notes and edge cases
- Given reka's Rating, when rendered, then the root is `role="radiogroup"` and each item is `role="radio"`, in contrast to bits' single `role="slider"` root with `role="presentation"` items. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given a hoverable Rating > should preview the hovered rating")
- Given reka's Rating fixture, when `RatingRoot`'s default slot is used, then it yields `items`, `RatingItem` yields `steps`, and each `RatingItemIndicator` is positioned with the CSS custom properties `--reka-rating-item-step-width`, `--reka-rating-item-step-opacity` and `--reka-rating-item-step-z-index`. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given a default Rating > should have default selected")
- Given reka's Rating, when the hover preview is exercised, then it is opt in behind a `hoverable` prop, whereas bits' `hoverPreview` defaults to on and must be explicitly disabled. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given a hoverable Rating > should preview the hovered rating")
- Given reka's Rating keyboard tests, when a key is dispatched, then a `sleep(0)` tick is required before the `data-state` and focus assertions hold. (reka: packages/core/src/Rating/Rating.test.ts: "given a default Rating > on keyboard navigation > should select next item on keydown")
- Given bits' `RatingGroup.Root`, when rendered, then its `children` snippet yields `items` whose entries carry `index` and a `state` of `active`, `partial` or `inactive`, which the fixture mirrors into `state-<i>` text nodes. (bits: tests/src/tests/rating-group/rating-group.browser.test.ts: "Value Display > should provide correct state in item snippets")

## tabs

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default Tabs with two triggers and two contents, when rendered, then an element with `role="tabpanel"` exists in the tree. (reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "given default Tabs > should render tab's content")
- Given a Tabs whose `TabsList` holds two triggers and no `TabsContent` is rendered at all, when rendered, then neither trigger has an `aria-controls` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "given Tabs without TabsContent > should not render aria-controls on TabsTrigger")
- Given a Tabs with two triggers but only a `TabsContent` for `tab1`, when rendered, then the `tab1` trigger has `aria-controls` defined and the `tab2` trigger has no `aria-controls`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "given Tabs without TabsContent > should render aria-controls only for TabsTrigger with matching TabsContent")
- Given a Tabs with five tab values, when rendered, then the list element contains exactly five descendants with `role="tab"`. (melt: src/tests/tabs/Tabs.spec.ts: "tablist renders tabs")
- Given a Tabs with one item, when rendered, then the root has `data-tabs-root`, the list has `data-tabs-list`, the trigger has `data-tabs-trigger`, and the content has `data-tabs-content`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should have bits data attrs")
- Given a Tabs with three items, when rendered, then each content has `role="tabpanel"` and each trigger has `role="tab"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should apply appropriate `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` attributes to the `Tabs.Trigger` and `Tabs.Content` components")
- Given a Tabs with three items, when rendered, then each trigger's `aria-controls` equals the `id` of its paired content and each content's `aria-labelledby` equals the `id` of its paired trigger. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should apply appropriate `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` attributes to the `Tabs.Trigger` and `Tabs.Content` components")
- Given a Tabs mounted with `value="2"`, when rendered, then trigger 1 has `tabindex="-1"`, trigger 2 has `tabindex="0"`, and trigger 3 has `tabindex="-1"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should apply tabindex 0 to the active tab trigger on mount")
- Given a Tabs whose content is passed `tabindex={-1}`, when the first trigger is clicked, then the active content has `tabindex="-1"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should allow skipping the panel when its first content is focusable")

### Keyboard
- Given a default Tabs with the first trigger focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the second trigger becomes `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "given default Tabs > after changing tab > should focus on next tab")
- Given a default Tabs with the first trigger focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the second panel is rendered and its text "Change your password" is in the markup, so activation is automatic on focus move. (reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "given default Tabs > after changing tab > should render it's content")
- Given a Tabs with five tabs and the first trigger focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly, then focus advances one trigger per press through all five in order. (melt: src/tests/tabs/Tabs.spec.ts: "can navigate tabs with arrow keys")
- Given a Tabs with five tabs and the last trigger focused, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus moves back one trigger per press through all five in reverse order. (melt: src/tests/tabs/Tabs.spec.ts: "can navigate tabs with arrow keys")
- Given a Tabs with three items and trigger 1 focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then trigger 2 has focus, content 1 is not visible, and content 2 is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should navigate the tabs with the keyboard")
- Given trigger 3 focused in a three-item Tabs, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then focus wraps to trigger 1 and content 1 becomes visible while content 3 is hidden. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should navigate the tabs with the keyboard")
- Given trigger 1 focused in a three-item Tabs, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then focus wraps to trigger 3 and content 3 becomes visible while content 1 is hidden. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should navigate the tabs with the keyboard")
- Given a Tabs with `loop: false` and trigger 1 focused, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then trigger 3 does not receive focus and trigger 1 keeps focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should respect the loop prop")
- Given a Tabs with `loop: false` and trigger 3 focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then trigger 1 does not receive focus and trigger 3 keeps focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should respect the loop prop")
- Given a Tabs with `activationMode: "manual"` and trigger 1 focused, when `Enter` is pressed, then content 1 is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `activationMode: 'manual'` prop")
- Given a Tabs with `activationMode: "manual"`, when `ArrowRight` moves focus to trigger 2, then trigger 2 has focus, content 2 stays hidden, and content 1 stays visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `activationMode: 'manual'` prop")
- Given a Tabs with `activationMode: "manual"`, when `ArrowRight` moves focus on to trigger 3, then trigger 3 has focus, content 3 stays hidden, and content 1 is still the visible panel. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `activationMode: 'manual'` prop")
- Given a Tabs with `orientation: "vertical"` and trigger 1 focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then trigger 2 has focus, content 1 is hidden, and content 2 is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should navigate using up & down when orientation is vertical")
- Given a vertical Tabs with trigger 3 focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then focus wraps to trigger 1 and content 1 becomes the visible panel. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should navigate using up & down when orientation is vertical")
- Given a vertical Tabs with trigger 1 focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then focus wraps to trigger 3 and content 3 becomes the visible panel. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should navigate using up & down when orientation is vertical")
- Given a vertical Tabs, when `ArrowUp` is pressed from trigger 3 and then from trigger 2, then focus moves to trigger 2 then trigger 1 and the matching content becomes visible at each step. (bits: tests/src/tests/tabs/tabs.browser.test.ts: "should navigate using up & down when orientation is vertical")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a Tabs with `:default-value="1"` matching the first trigger and content, when rendered, then the first panel is the one shown and its text "Make changes" is in the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "given default Tabs > should render tab's content")

### SSR and hydration
- Given a Tabs rendered by `createSSRApp` under a `ConfigProvider` supplying a counting `useId`, when `renderToString` runs with `app.config.idPrefix = "v-1"`, then the markup contains `id="reka-tabs-nuxt-1-trigger-account"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "ssr hydration > uses ConfigProvider ids when Vue app id prefixes differ")

(reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "ssr hydration > uses ConfigProvider ids when Vue app id prefixes differ")

(reka: packages/core/src/Tabs/Tabs.test.ts: "ssr hydration > uses ConfigProvider ids when Vue app id prefixes differ")

## accordion

### Roles and attributes
- Given a single-type Accordion with item 1 disabled, when rendered, then the first item and first trigger both have `data-state="closed"` and neither has `data-disabled`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Expansion Behavior > should have expected data attributes")
- Given a single-type Accordion with item 1 disabled, when the first trigger is clicked, then the first item and trigger have `data-state="open"` while the disabled item and its trigger both have `data-disabled`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Expansion Behavior > should have expected data attributes")
- Given an isolated Accordion, when rendered, then the root has `data-accordion-root`, the item `data-accordion-item`, the header `data-accordion-header`, the content `data-accordion-content`, and the trigger `data-accordion-trigger`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "Shared Behavior > should have bits data attrs")
- Given an isolated Accordion whose trigger is passed `tabindex: -1`, when rendered, then the trigger has `tabindex="-1"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "Shared Behavior > should respect custom tabindex on trigger")
- Given an isolated Accordion with no explicit tabindex, when rendered, then the trigger has `tabindex="0"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "Shared Behavior > should have default tabindex of 0 on trigger")
- Given a single-type Accordion where the first item's header is given `level: 1` and the rest keep `level: 3`, when rendered, then the first header has `data-heading-level="1"` and `aria-level="1"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should respect the `level` prop for headers")
- Given the same Accordion, when the second header is inspected, then it has `data-heading-level="3"` and `aria-level="3"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should respect the `level` prop for headers")
- Given a multiple-type Accordion where the first item's header is given `level: 1`, when rendered, then the first header has `data-heading-level="1"` and `aria-level="1"` and the second has `data-heading-level="3"` and `aria-level="3"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should respect the `level` prop for headers")
- Given a multiple-type Accordion with item 1 disabled, when rendered, then the first item and trigger have `data-state="closed"` and no `data-disabled`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Expansion Behavior > should have expected data attributes")
- Given a multiple-type Accordion with item 1 disabled, when the first trigger is clicked, then the first item and trigger have `data-state="open"` and the disabled item and trigger have `data-disabled`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Expansion Behavior > should have expected data attributes")
- Given a melt Accordion, when a trigger is clicked, then the matching item element gains `data-state="open"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "expands item on click")
- Given a melt Accordion rendered with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the item has `data-state="closed"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "does not expand item when disabled")

### Keyboard
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the second trigger becomes `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > on `ArrowDown` > should move focus to the next trigger")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the last of four triggers focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then focus wraps to the first trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > on `ArrowDown` > should move focus to the first item if at the end")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the third trigger focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then the second trigger becomes `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > on `ArrowUp` > should move focus to the previous trigger")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then focus wraps to the fourth trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > on `ArrowUp` > should move focus to the last item if at the beginning")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `Home` is pressed, then the first trigger holds focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > on `Home` > should move focus to the first trigger")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `End` is pressed, then the fourth trigger receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > on `End` > should move focus to the last trigger")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the second trigger receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > on `ArrowDown` > should move focus to the next trigger")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then focus wraps to the fourth trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > on `ArrowUp` > should move focus to the previous trigger")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `Home` is pressed, then the first trigger holds focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > on `Home` > should move focus to the first trigger")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `End` is pressed, then the fourth trigger receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > on `End` > should move focus to the last trigger")
- Given a melt Accordion with `multiple: false` and trigger 1 focused, when `Enter` is pressed, then item 1 has `data-state="open"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "expands item when pressing enter")
- Given a melt Accordion with `multiple: false` and trigger 1 focused, when `Space` is pressed, then item 1 has `data-state="open"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "expands item when pressing space")
- Given a melt Accordion with trigger 1 focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then trigger 1 loses focus and trigger 2 has focus. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "focuses on item below when pressing key arrow down")
- Given a melt Accordion with trigger 2 focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then trigger 2 loses focus and trigger 1 has focus. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "focuses on item above when pressing key arrow up")
- Given a melt Accordion with trigger 3 focused, when `Home` is pressed, then trigger 3 loses focus and trigger 1 has focus. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "focuses on first item when pressing key home")
- Given a melt Accordion with trigger 1 focused, when `End` is pressed, then trigger 1 loses focus and trigger 3 has focus. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "focuses on last item when pressing key end")
- Given each closed item of a single-type bits Accordion with its trigger focused, when `Enter` is pressed, then that item's content holds the item's text and the item and trigger have `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Expansion Behavior > should expand when the trigger is focused and \"{Enter}\" key is pressed")
- Given each closed item of a single-type bits Accordion with its trigger focused, when `Space` is pressed, then that item's content holds the item's text and the item and trigger have `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Expansion Behavior > should expand when the trigger is focused and \"{ }\" key is pressed")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed four times, then focus steps through triggers 2, 3, 4 and wraps back to trigger 1. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should focus the next item when `ArrowDown` key is pressed")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion with the first trigger focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed four times, then focus wraps to trigger 4 then steps to 3, 2, and back to 1. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should focus the previous item when the `ArrowUp` key is pressed")
- Given each trigger of a single-type bits Accordion focused in turn, when `Home` is pressed, then trigger 1 has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should focus the first item when the `Home` key is pressed")
- Given each trigger of a single-type bits Accordion focused in turn, when `End` is pressed, then trigger 4 has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should focus the last item when the `End` key is pressed")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion whose item 1 is disabled and trigger 0 focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then trigger 1 does not receive focus and trigger 2 does. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should skip over disabled items when navigating with Arrow Keys")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion with `loop: true` and trigger 0 focused, when `ArrowUp` then `ArrowDown` are pressed, then focus wraps to trigger 3 and then back to trigger 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should loop through the items when the `loop` prop is true")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion with `loop: false` and trigger 0 focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then trigger 3 does not receive focus and trigger 0 keeps focus, and a following `ArrowDown` moves focus to trigger 1. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should not loop through the items when the `loop` prop is false")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion with `orientation: "horizontal"` and trigger 0 focused, when `ArrowLeft` then `ArrowRight` are pressed, then focus wraps to trigger 3 and then returns to trigger 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should navigate using ArrowLeft/Right when `orientation` is `horizontal`")
- Given a horizontal bits Accordion with `loop: true` and trigger 0 focused, when `ArrowLeft` then `ArrowRight` are pressed, then focus wraps to trigger 3 and then returns to trigger 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should loop using ArrowLeft/Right when `orientation` is `horizontal` and `loop` is true")
- Given a horizontal bits Accordion with `loop: false` and trigger 0 focused, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then trigger 3 does not receive focus and trigger 0 keeps focus, and a following `ArrowRight` moves focus to trigger 1. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Keyboard Navigation > should not loop using ArrowLeft/Right when `orientation` is `horizontal` and `loop` is false")
- Given each closed item of a multiple-type bits Accordion with its trigger focused, when `Enter` is pressed, then that item's content shows its text and the item and trigger have `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Expansion Behavior > should expand when the trigger is focused and `Enter` key is pressed")
- Given each closed item of a multiple-type bits Accordion with its trigger focused, when `Space` is pressed, then that item's content shows its text and the item and trigger have `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Expansion Behavior > should expand when the trigger is focused and `Space` key is pressed")
- Given a multiple-type bits Accordion with trigger 0 focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed four times, then focus steps through triggers 1, 2, 3 and wraps back to trigger 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Keyboard Navigation > should focus the next item when `ArrowDown` key is pressed")
- Given a multiple-type bits Accordion with trigger 0 focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed four times, then focus wraps to trigger 3 then steps to 2, 1, and back to 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Keyboard Navigation > should focus the previous item when the `ArrowUp` key is pressed")
- Given each trigger of a multiple-type bits Accordion focused in turn, when `Home` is pressed, then trigger 0 has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Keyboard Navigation > should focus the first item when the `Home` key is pressed")
- Given each trigger of a multiple-type bits Accordion focused in turn, when `End` is pressed, then trigger 3 has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Keyboard Navigation > should focus the last item when the `End` key is pressed")
- Given a multiple-type bits Accordion with item 1 disabled and trigger 0 clicked, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then trigger 1 does not receive focus and trigger 2 does. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Keyboard Navigation > should respect the `disabled` prop for items")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion with item 1 disabled and the first trigger clicked with `force`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then trigger 1 does not receive focus and trigger 2 does. ### Pointer
- Given a single-type reka Accordion, when the first trigger is clicked, then the "Content One" element is present in the document markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > when clicking a trigger > should show the content")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first item already open, when the same trigger is clicked again, then "Content One" stays in the markup, so a single Accordion without `collapsible` cannot be closed by its own trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > then clicking the trigger again > should not close the content")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when the second trigger is clicked, then "Content Two" appears in the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > then clicking another trigger > should show the new content")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when the second trigger is clicked, then "Content One" is no longer in the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > then clicking another trigger > should hide the previous content")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion, when the first trigger is clicked, then "Content One" is present in the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > when clicking a trigger > should show the content")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when the same trigger is clicked again, then "Content One" is removed from the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > then clicking the trigger again > should hide the content")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when the second trigger is clicked, then "Content Two" appears in the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > then clicking another trigger > should show the new content")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when the second trigger is clicked, then "Content One" remains in the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > then clicking another trigger > should not hide the previous content")
- Given a melt Accordion with three items, when trigger 3 is clicked, then the text "Description 3" is visible. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "displays content when item is expanded")
- Given a melt Accordion rendered with `disabled: true`, when trigger 2 is clicked, then item 2 still has `data-state="closed"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "does not expand item when disabled")
- Given a melt Accordion with `multiple: false` and both items closed, when trigger 1 is clicked, then item 1 has `data-state="open"` and item 2 has `data-state="closed"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "expands only one item when multiple is false")
- Given a melt Accordion with `multiple: false` and item 1 open, when trigger 2 is clicked, then item 1 flips to `data-state="closed"` and item 2 to `data-state="open"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "expands only one item when multiple is false")
- Given a melt Accordion with `multiple: true` and both items closed, when trigger 1 is clicked, then item 1 has `data-state="open"` and item 2 stays `data-state="closed"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "expands multiple items when multiple is true")
- Given a melt Accordion with `multiple: true` and item 1 open, when trigger 2 is clicked, then both item 1 and item 2 have `data-state="open"`. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "expands multiple items when multiple is true")
- Given each item of a single-type bits Accordion starting closed with hidden content, when its trigger is clicked, then that item's content holds the item's text and the item and trigger have `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Expansion Behavior > should display content when an item is expanded")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion after every trigger has been clicked in turn, when counting `[data-state='open'][data-accordion-item]` elements, then exactly 1 item is open. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Expansion Behavior > should expand only one item at a time")
- Given each item of a multiple-type bits Accordion starting closed with hidden content, when its trigger is clicked, then that item's content holds the item's text and the item and trigger have `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Expansion Behavior > should display content when an item is expanded")
- Given a multiple-type bits Accordion after all four triggers have been clicked, when counting `[data-state='open'][data-accordion-item]` elements, then 4 items are open. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Expansion Behavior > should allow expanding multiple items")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion with `disabled: true` on the root, when triggers 0, 1, and 2 are clicked with `force: true`, then each stays `data-state="closed"` and each carries `data-disabled`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should disable everything when true on root")
- Given a multiple-type bits Accordion with `disabled: true` on the root, when rendered, then triggers 0, 1, and 2 each have `data-state="closed"` and `data-disabled`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should disable everything when the `disabled` prop is true")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a single-type reka Accordion, when the first trigger is clicked, then `update:modelValue` is emitted with the string `"One"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > when clicking a trigger > should call update:modelValue")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when its trigger is clicked again, then the total count of `update:modelValue` emissions stays at 1. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > then clicking the trigger again > should not call update:modelValue")
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when the second trigger is clicked, then the second `update:modelValue` emission carries `"Two"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > then clicking another trigger > should call update:modelValue")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion, when the first trigger is clicked, then `update:modelValue` is emitted with the array `["One"]`. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > when clicking a trigger > should call update:modelValue")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when its trigger is clicked again, then the second `update:modelValue` emission carries the empty array `[]`. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > then clicking the trigger again > should call update:modelValue")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with the first item open, when the second trigger is clicked, then the second `update:modelValue` emission carries `["One", "Two"]`. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > then clicking another trigger > should call onValueChange")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion using `bind:value` starting at `""`, when the `item-0` trigger is clicked, then the displayed bound value becomes `"item-0"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should update the `bind:value` prop when the value changes")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion using `bind:value` starting at `""` with `item-1` closed, when an external button sets the bound value to `"item-1"`, then the display shows `"item-1"` and `item-1` gains `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should handle programmatic changes to the \"value\" prop")
- Given a single-type bits Accordion with an `onValueChange` mock and trigger 0 focused, when `Enter` is pressed, then the callback receives `"item-0"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should call `onValueChange` with the new value when an item is expanded")
- Given the same Accordion, when `ArrowDown` then `Enter` are pressed, then `onValueChange` receives `"item-1"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should call `onValueChange` with the new value when an item is expanded")
- Given the same Accordion with `item-1` open, when `Enter` is pressed again on its trigger, then `onValueChange` receives the empty string `""`, so a single bits Accordion collapses its open item to an empty value. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should call `onValueChange` with the new value when an item is expanded")
- Given a multiple-type bits Accordion using `bind:value` starting at `[]`, when the `item-0` trigger is clicked, then the displayed bound value becomes `"item-0"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should update the `bind:value` prop when the value changes")
- Given a multiple-type bits Accordion using `bind:value` starting at `[]` with `item-1` closed, when an external button pushes `"item-1"` onto the bound array, then `item-1` gains `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should handle programmatic changes to the \"value\" prop")
- Given a multiple-type bits Accordion with an `onValueChange` mock and trigger 0 focused, when `Enter` is pressed, then the callback receives `["item-0"]`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should call `onValueChange` with the new value when an item is expanded/collapsed")
- Given the same Accordion, when `ArrowDown` then `Enter` are pressed, then `onValueChange` receives `["item-0", "item-1"]`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should call `onValueChange` with the new value when an item is expanded/collapsed")
- Given the same Accordion with both items open, when `Enter` is pressed again on trigger 1, then `onValueChange` receives `["item-0"]`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should call `onValueChange` with the new value when an item is expanded/collapsed")
- Given the same Accordion with only `item-0` open, when `ArrowUp` then `Enter` are pressed, then `onValueChange` receives the empty array `[]`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should call `onValueChange` with the new value when an item is expanded/collapsed")

### Animation and presence
- Given a single-type bits Accordion whose contents use `forceMount` with a `child` snippet, when rendered with all items closed, then every item's content element is visible in the document. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true")
- Given a force-mounted single-type bits Accordion with a mutation observer on the first content, when the first trigger is clicked, then at some point the content carries `data-starting-style`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should apply transition attrs to content during open and close")
- Given the same observed content now open, when the first trigger is clicked again, then at some point the content carries `data-ending-style`. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > should apply transition attrs to content during open and close")
- Given a force-mounted single-type bits Accordion whose `child` snippet renders only when the snippet's `open` prop is true, when rendered with all items closed, then no content element exists for any item. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > works properly when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used to conditionally render the content")
- Given the same Accordion, when the first trigger is clicked, then the first item's content element exists and is visible while the second item's content element still does not exist. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Props and Bindings > works properly when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used to conditionally render the content")

### SSR and hydration
- Given a single-type collapsible Accordion rendered by `createSSRApp` under a `ConfigProvider` with a counting `useId`, when `renderToString` runs with `app.config.idPrefix = "v-1"`, then the markup contains `id="reka-accordion-trigger-nuxt-1"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "ssr hydration > uses ConfigProvider ids when Vue app id prefixes differ")
- Given the same server render, when inspecting the output, then the markup contains `id="reka-collapsible-content-nuxt-2"`, so the content id comes from the collapsible layer and uses the next id from the provider. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "ssr hydration > uses ConfigProvider ids when Vue app id prefixes differ")
- Given server markup produced with `idPrefix = "v-1"`, when a client app with `idPrefix = "v-0"` hydrates the same container, then the first `button` id and the `[role="region"]` id are unchanged from the server values. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "ssr hydration > uses ConfigProvider ids when Vue app id prefixes differ")
- Given hydration with mismatched Vue app id prefixes, when hydration completes, then `console.warn` never receives "Hydration attribute mismatch" and `console.error` never receives "Hydration completed but contains mismatches". (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "ssr hydration > uses ConfigProvider ids when Vue app id prefixes differ")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a single-type reka Accordion with four items, when run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a multiple-type reka Accordion with four items, when run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a multiple Accordion > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a melt Accordion rendered with no items, when run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "has no accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given the reka story fixture, when mounted, then `AccordionRoot` receives emit handlers via `useEmitAsProps(emits)` and each `AccordionItem` renders its `AccordionContent` inside a `v-for`, so an item can hold more than one content node. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > when clicking a trigger > should show the content")
- Given the reka single-type story, when its `type` prop is left at the default, then `type: "single"` is used without `collapsible`, which is why re-clicking an open trigger neither closes it nor emits. (reka: packages/core/src/Accordion/Accordion.test.ts: "given a single Accordion > then clicking the trigger again > should not close the content")
- Given the melt builder, when `createAccordion` is destructured, then it returns `elements` holding `root`, `item`, `trigger`, and `content` plus `helpers` holding `isSelected`, and the fixture uses `$isSelected(id)` to decide whether to render content at all. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "displays content when item is expanded")
- Given the melt fixture, when `disabled` is passed to `createAccordion`, then it applies at the root level and blocks expansion for every item. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: "does not expand item when disabled")
- Given the bits multiple-controlled fixture, when the update button runs `value.push("item-1")`, then mutating the `$state` array in place is enough to open the item, so the array is deeply reactive. (bits: tests/src/tests/accordion/accordion.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Props and Bindings > should handle programmatic changes to the \"value\" prop")

## collapsible

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default closed reka Collapsible, when rendered, then a `[hidden]` content element exists and its text content is empty. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a default Collapsible > should have hidden content")
- Given a reka Collapsible with `unmountOnHide: false`, when rendered closed, then the content's `hidden` attribute is the empty string under jsdom. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a Collapsible with `unmountOnHide:false` > should have hidden attribute")
- Given a reka Collapsible with `unmountOnHide: false` that was opened and closed again, when the content is inspected, then it has `data-state="closed"`, `hidden=""`, and its markup is still present in the tree. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a Collapsible with `unmountOnHide:false` > and clicking the trigger again > should close the content")
- Given a bits Collapsible, when rendered, then the root has `data-collapsible-root`, the trigger has `data-collapsible-trigger`, and the content has `data-collapsible-content`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Data Attributes > should have bits data attrs")
- Given a bits Collapsible with `open: false` and `hiddenUntilFound: true`, when rendered, then the content has `hidden="until-found"` and the bound value display reads `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Hidden Until Found Behavior > should render content with hidden='until-found' when closed and hiddenUntilFound is true")
- Given a bits Collapsible with `open: false` and `hiddenUntilFound: false`, when rendered, then the content has `hidden=""` and the bound value display reads `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Hidden Until Found Behavior > should not have hidden='until-found' when hiddenUntilFound is false")
- Given a bits Collapsible with `hiddenUntilFound: true`, when the trigger is clicked twice to open and close it, then the content again has `hidden="until-found"` rather than a plain `hidden`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Hidden Until Found Behavior > should maintain hidden='until-found' after closing when hiddenUntilFound is true")

### Pointer
- Given a default closed reka Collapsible, when the trigger is clicked, then the content text "Content" is rendered inside the component. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a default Collapsible > when clicking the trigger > should open the content")
- Given an open reka Collapsible, when the trigger is clicked again, then the content markup is no longer in the rendered text, so the content unmounts by default. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a default Collapsible > and clicking the trigger again > should close the content")
- Given a reka Collapsible with `unmountOnHide: false`, when the trigger is clicked, then the content text "Content" is rendered. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a Collapsible with `unmountOnHide:false` > when clicking the trigger > should open the content")
- Given a reka Collapsible with `defaultOpen: true`, when the trigger is clicked, then the content markup leaves the rendered text. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given an open uncontrolled Collapsible > should close the content")
- Given a closed melt Collapsible, when the trigger is clicked, then the content becomes visible, and clicking again hides it. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "Toggles when clicked")
- Given a melt Collapsible rendered with `disabled: true`, when the trigger is clicked, then the content stays not visible. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "Should be disabled when disabled prop is true")
- Given a closed bits Collapsible, when the trigger is clicked, then the content becomes visible, and clicking again makes it not visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "State and Interaction > should toggle the `open` state when clicked")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a reka Collapsible with `defaultOpen: true`, when rendered, then the content text is present without any interaction. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given an open uncontrolled Collapsible > should open the content by default")
- Given a reka Collapsible wrapper that forwards props and emits, when `update:open` is emitted with `false`, then the first emission payload is `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given an open uncontrolled Collapsible > should call `update:open` prop with `false` value")
- Given a melt Collapsible with `defaultOpen: true`, when rendered, then the content is visible. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "Should be open when open prop is true")
- Given a melt Collapsible with `defaultOpen: false`, when rendered, then the content is not visible. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "Should be closed when open prop is false")
- Given a melt Collapsible driven by an external writable store set to `false`, when the store is set to `true` and a tick passes, then the content becomes visible. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "Correctly handles controlled store updates")
- Given the same store-controlled melt Collapsible now open, when the trigger is clicked, then the external store's value reads `false`. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "Correctly handles controlled store updates")
- Given a melt Collapsible whose `onOpenChange` callback always returns `false`, when the trigger is clicked, then the content stays not visible, so the change function can veto the new state. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "Respects `onOpenChange` callback when the open state changes")
- Given a closed bits Collapsible, when rendered, then the root and trigger exist and the content is not visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "State and Interaction > should hide content when `open` is false")
- Given a bits Collapsible with `bind:open` starting at `false`, when the trigger is clicked, then the bound value display changes from `false` to `true`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Props and Events > should respect binds to the `open` prop")
- Given the same Collapsible now open, when an external button outside the component toggles the bound variable, then the bound value display reads `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Props and Events > should respect binds to the `open` prop")
- Given a bits Collapsible with an `onOpenChange` mock, when the trigger is clicked, then the callback is called with `true`, and on a second click with `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Props and Events > should call `onOpenChange` when the open state changes")

### Animation and presence
- Given a bits Collapsible whose content uses `forceMount` with a `child` snippet that ignores the snippet `open` prop, when rendered closed, then the content element is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Force Mount Behavior > should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true")
- Given a force-mounted bits Collapsible with a mutation observer on the content, when the trigger is clicked to open, then at some point the content carries `data-starting-style`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Force Mount Behavior > should apply transition attrs to content during open and close")
- Given the same observed content now open, when the trigger is clicked to close, then at some point the content carries `data-ending-style`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Force Mount Behavior > should apply transition attrs to content during open and close")
- Given a force-mounted bits Collapsible whose `child` snippet renders the element only when the snippet's `open` prop is true, when rendered closed, then no content element exists in the document. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Force Mount Behavior > should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used")
- Given the same Collapsible, when the trigger is clicked, then the content element exists and is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Force Mount Behavior > should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default closed reka Collapsible, when run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a default Collapsible > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a reka Collapsible with `unmountOnHide: false`, when run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a Collapsible with `unmountOnHide:false` > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a default melt Collapsible, when run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "No accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a bits Collapsible with `open: false` and `hiddenUntilFound: true`, when a `beforematch` event is dispatched on the content, then the bound `open` value display changes to `true`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Hidden Until Found Behavior > should open collapsible when beforematch event is triggered")
- Given a bits Collapsible with `hiddenUntilFound: true` and an `onOpenChange` mock, when a `beforematch` event is dispatched on the content, then the callback is called with `true`. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Hidden Until Found Behavior > should call onOpenChange when beforematch event opens the collapsible")
- Given a bits Collapsible already `open: true` with `hiddenUntilFound: true` and an `onOpenChange` mock, when a `beforematch` event is dispatched on the content, then the callback is never called. (bits: tests/src/tests/collapsible/collapsible.browser.test.ts: "Hidden Until Found Behavior > should not trigger open change when already open and beforematch is fired")
- Given the reka test comment on the `unmountOnHide: false` case, when read, then it records that jsdom reports `hidden=""` where a real browser would report `hidden="until-found"`, so the stricter assertion is commented out. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given a Collapsible with `unmountOnHide:false` > should have hidden attribute")
- Given the melt builder, when `createCollapsible` is destructured, then it returns `elements` holding `root`, `trigger`, and `content`, `states` holding `open`, and `options` holding `disabled`, and the story pushes prop changes back through `localOpen.set` and `localDisabled.set`. (melt: src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts: "Correctly handles controlled store updates")
- Given the reka wrapper fixture, when props and emits are forwarded with `useForwardPropsEmits`, then the same component accepts `defaultOpen` and `unmountOnHide` and re-emits `update:open`. (reka: packages/core/src/Collapsible/Collapsible.test.ts: "given an open uncontrolled Collapsible > should call `update:open` prop with `false` value")

## stepper

### Roles and attributes
- Given a reka Stepper mounted with `modelValue: 2`, when rendered, then the second step item has `aria-current="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > respects a default value if provided")
- Given a linear reka Stepper with step 2 active, when the third item is inspected, then it does not have `data-disabled=""`, so the step after the current one is enabled. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > enables the next step for linear steppers")
- Given a linear reka Stepper after step 3 is selected, when the fourth item is inspected, then it does not have `data-disabled=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > enables the next step for linear steppers")

### Keyboard
- Given a five-step reka Stepper with the first trigger focused by click, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the second trigger has focus, and a following `ArrowLeft` returns focus to the first. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > navigates horizontally using the keyboard")
- Given a reka Stepper with `orientation: "vertical"` and the first trigger focused by click, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the second trigger has focus, and a following `ArrowUp` returns focus to the first. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > navigates vertically using the keyboard")
- Given a reka Stepper with `linear: true` and the first trigger focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the second trigger has focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > prevents navigation to other elements if linear is true")
- Given the same linear Stepper with the second trigger focused but step 1 still active, when `ArrowRight` is pressed again, then the third trigger does not receive focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > prevents navigation to other elements if linear is true")
- Given a reka Stepper with `linear: false` and the first trigger focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed twice, then focus moves to the second and then the third trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > allows navigation to other elements if linear is false")
- Given a reka Stepper with the first trigger clicked and `ArrowRight` pressed, when `Enter` is pressed, then the second item has `aria-current="true"`, and repeating `ArrowRight` plus `Enter` makes the third item `aria-current="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > selects a step using the {Enter} key")
- Given a reka Stepper with the first trigger clicked and `ArrowRight` pressed, when `Space` is pressed, then the second item has `aria-current="true"`, and repeating `ArrowRight` plus `Space` makes the third item `aria-current="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > selects a step using the { } key")

### Pointer
- Given a five-step reka Stepper, when the second trigger is clicked, then the second item has `aria-current="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > selects a step on click")
- Given a reka Stepper with `linear: true` and step 1 active, when the third trigger is clicked, then it does not receive focus, so non-adjacent steps cannot be reached by pointer. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > prevents navigation to other elements if linear is true")
- Given a reka Stepper with `linear: false`, when the fourth trigger is clicked, then it receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > allows navigation to other elements if linear is false")
- Given a linear reka Stepper, when the second trigger is clicked, then the second item has `aria-current="true"`, and clicking the third trigger then makes the third item `aria-current="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > enables the next step for linear steppers")

### Focus management
- Given a five-step reka Stepper, when the first trigger is clicked, then that trigger has focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > navigates horizontally using the keyboard")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a reka Stepper rendering five triggers and exposing `totalSteps` through the root's default slot, when mounted, then the displayed total reads `5`. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > keeps the total step count in sync when triggers unmount and remount")
- Given the same Stepper, when it is re-rendered with only three visible steps, then the displayed total reads `3`. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > keeps the total step count in sync when triggers unmount and remount")
- Given the same Stepper reduced to three steps, when it is re-rendered back to five, then the displayed total reads `5` rather than drifting upward. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > keeps the total step count in sync when triggers unmount and remount")
- Given repeated toggling of the visible step count, when the Stepper is re-rendered with one step and then five again, then the displayed total reads `1` and then `5`, so no stale trigger elements leak into the registered set. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > keeps the total step count in sync when triggers unmount and remount")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default reka Stepper, when its root element is run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given the reka Stepper setup helper, when the component renders, then the element with `data-testid="stepper"` is visible before any other assertion runs. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given the reka Stepper fixture, when mounted, then each `StepperItem` wraps a `StepperTrigger` holding `StepperIndicator`, `StepperTitle`, and `StepperDescription`, and a `StepperSeparator` is rendered for every step except the last. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > selects a step on click")
- Given the dynamic reka Stepper fixture, when `StepperRoot` is used with `v-slot="{ totalSteps }"`, then the root exposes the live trigger count to its slot. (reka: packages/core/src/Stepper/Stepper.test.ts: "stepper > keeps the total step count in sync when triggers unmount and remount")

## dialog

### Roles and attributes
- Given a Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false`, when opened then closed with Escape, then the content element is still matched by `[role="dialog"]`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should keep content in DOM when closed after being opened")
- Given a Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false` that has been opened and closed, when inspecting the page, then `document.body` has no `aria-hidden` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should not apply aria-hidden to body after open then close")
- Given an open Dialog, when the overlay is located, then it carries `data-state="open"` and is a `div` with no `role` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when clicking the overlay > should close the content")
- Given an open Dialog, when inspecting trigger, overlay, close, title, description and content, then each carries its own `data-dialog-<part>` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Data Attributes > should have bits data attrs")
- Given an open Dialog, when inspecting the overlay and the content, then both have `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Data Attributes > should have expected data attributes")
- Given an open Dialog, when inspecting the content, then `aria-describedby` equals the id of the `Dialog.Description` element. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "ARIA Attributes > should apply the correct `aria-describedby` attribute to the `Dialog.Content` element")
- Given an open Dialog, when inspecting the title, then it has `role="heading"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "ARIA Attributes > should have role='heading'")
- Given an open Dialog with no `level` prop on the title, when inspecting the title, then it has `aria-level="2"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "ARIA Attributes > should apply a default `aria-level` attribute to the `Dialog.Title` element")
- Given an open Dialog whose title is given `level: 3`, when inspecting the title, then it has `aria-level="3"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "ARIA Attributes > should allow setting a custom level for the `Dialog.Title` element")
- Given an open Dialog whose description id is `description-id` and is then reactively changed to `new-id`, when the id changes, then the description's `id` becomes `new-id` and the content's `aria-describedby` follows it.
