- Given a Dialog built from a Melt builder with custom `ids` for content, title and description, when rendered, then each element's `id` equals the supplied value. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Applies custom ids when provided")

### Keyboard
- Given an open Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content's inline `display` becomes `none`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should keep content in DOM when closed after being opened")
- Given an open non-modal Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content's inline `display` becomes `none`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a non-modal Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should keep content in DOM when closed after being opened")
- Given an open Dialog, when `Escape` is pressed, then the close button's markup is no longer in `document.body`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when pressing escape > should close the content")
- Given an open Dialog, when `Escape` is pressed, then focus returns to the trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when pressing escape > should focus trigger")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is not visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Closes when Escape is hit")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `escapeBehavior: 'ignore'`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Respects the `escapeBehavior` prop")
- Given an open Melt dialog with focus on a child that calls `stopPropagation()` on `Escape` keydown, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Doesn't close on escape if child intercepts event")
- Given an open Melt dialog with a transition on content and overlay, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed from the DOM after the transition. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Closes when Escape is pressed")
- Given an open nested Melt dialog set, when `Escape` is pressed, then the outer content is removed from the DOM. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogNested.spec.ts: "Nested Dialogs > Closes when Escape is hit")
- Given an open bits Dialog, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed and focus returns to the trigger. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Open/Close Behavior > should close when the `Escape` key is pressed") [skipped]
- Given an open bits Dialog with `escapeKeydownBehavior: 'ignore'`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content remains and the trigger does not have focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "should respect the the `escapeKeydownBehavior: 'ignore'` prop")
- Given an open bits Dialog whose content holds exactly one focusable element, when `Tab` is pressed, then focus stays on that close button, and a following `Escape` still closes the dialog. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should trap focus and allow Escape to close when only one focusable element exists")
- Given a bits Dialog containing a dropdown menu and a popover, when `Escape` is pressed with the dropdown open, then only the dropdown closes and the dialog stays open; the same holds for the popover, and a final `Escape` closes the dialog. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Integration with other components > should allow opening nested floating components within the dialog")

### Pointer
- Given an open Dialog, when `pointerdown` fires on the overlay, then the close button's markup is removed from `document.body`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when clicking the overlay > should close the content")
- Given an open Dialog, when `pointerdown` fires on the overlay, then focus returns to the trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when clicking the overlay > should focus trigger")
- Given a Dialog whose content is nested inside the overlay, when `pointerdown` with `button: 0` is dispatched on a text input inside the content, then the event's `defaultPrevented` is `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with content nested inside the overlay > when pressing down on a control inside the content > should not prevent the default pointerdown action")
- Given a Dialog whose content is nested inside the overlay, when `pointerdown` fires on a text input inside the content, then the dialog stays open. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with content nested inside the overlay > when pressing down on a control inside the content > should keep the dialog open")
- Given a closed Dialog, when the trigger is clicked, then the content opens and the close button is present in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > should open the content")
- Given a closed Melt dialog, when the trigger is clicked, then the content becomes visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Opens when trigger is clicked")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when the close element is clicked, then the content is not visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Closes when closer is clicked")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when the overlay is clicked, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Closes when overlay is clicked")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when the content itself is clicked, then the content stays visible, and the pattern still holds after closing via the closer and reopening. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Doesn't close when clicking content")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when `pointerdown` happens inside the content and the matching `pointerup` happens on the overlay, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Doesn't close on pointerup if the previous pointerdown occurred inside the dialog")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when both `pointerdown` and `pointerup` happen on the overlay, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Closes on pointerup if the previous pointerdown occurred outside the dialog")
- Given an open Melt dialog on a touch device, when `pointerdown`, `touchstart`, `pointerup` and `touchend` are all fired on the overlay, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Closes on touchend if the previous touchstart occurred outside the dialog")
- Given a nested Melt dialog set with the outer dialog open, when the inner trigger is clicked, then the inner content appears while the outer content stays mounted. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogNested.spec.ts: "Nested Dialogs > Opens when nested trigger is clicked")
- Given both dialogs of a nested Melt set open, when the inner closer is clicked, then the inner content is removed and the outer content stays in the DOM. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogNested.spec.ts: "Nested Dialogs > Closes when closer is clicked")
- Given an open nested Melt dialog set, when the outer overlay is clicked, then the outer content is removed from the DOM. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogNested.spec.ts: "Nested Dialogs > Closes when overlay is clicked")
- Given a closed Melt dialog with transitions, when the trigger is clicked, then the content appears in the DOM. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Opens when trigger is clicked")
- Given an open Melt dialog with transitions, when the closer is clicked, then the content is removed from the DOM. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Closes when closer is clicked")
- Given an open Melt dialog with transitions, when the overlay is clicked, then the content is removed from the DOM. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Closes when overlay is clicked")
- Given a closed bits Dialog, when the trigger is clicked, then the content exists in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Open/Close Behavior > should open when the trigger is clicked")
- Given an open bits Dialog, when the close button is clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Open/Close Behavior > should close when the close button is clicked")
- Given an open bits Dialog, when the overlay is clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Open/Close Behavior > should close when the overlay is clicked")
- Given an open bits Dialog, when the content is clicked, then the content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Open/Close Behavior > should not close when content is clicked")
- Given an open bits Dialog, when the content is clicked, then the content stays in the DOM (top-level duplicate of the same assertion). (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "should not close when content is clicked")
- Given a bits Dialog opened from a tooltip trigger with `disableCloseOnTriggerClick` true, when the trigger is hovered, clicked, the dialog closed and the trigger hovered again, then the tooltip content shows on the first hover, disappears once the dialog opens, and shows again on the second hover. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Integration with other components > should not break tooltip when opened from tooltip trigger and disableCloseOnTriggerClick is true")
- Given the docs dialog page on a touch device with the dialog open and the "View code" button positioned under the overlay but not under the content, when the overlay is tapped at that button's centre coordinates, then the content becomes hidden and the "View code" button's `data-state` is still `unchecked`. (melt: e2e/dialog.spec.ts: "dialog > touch device > doesn't leak events when tapping overlay")

### Focus management
- Given a Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false` that is force-mounted but closed, when the page mounts, then `document.activeElement` is `document.body` and no focus is pulled into the hidden content. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should not pull focus into the content while closed on mount")
- Given a Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false`, when the trigger is clicked, then the close button becomes `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should focus the close button on open")
- Given a Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false` that has been opened, closed with Escape and reopened, when it reopens, then the close button is focused again, so focus is re-applied on each `present` false to true transition rather than only on physical mount. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should re-focus the content when reopened")
- Given an open Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false`, when `Escape` is pressed, then focus returns to the trigger element. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should restore focus to trigger on close")
- Given a non-modal Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false`, when it is closed on mount then opened by trigger click, then `document.activeElement` starts as `document.body` and becomes the close button. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a non-modal Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should focus the close button on open")
- Given an open non-modal Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false`, when `Escape` is pressed, then focus returns to the trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a non-modal Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should restore focus to trigger on close")
- Given an open Dialog, when the close button is looked up after the trigger click, then it is `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > should focus the close button")
- Given two Dialogs with `unmountOnHide=false` where the second (hidden, later-mounted) scope exists, when the first modal dialog is open and focus is moved to the second dialog's trigger outside it, then the focus trap pulls focus back inside the first content. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given two Dialogs with unmountOnHide=false > should keep the modal focus trap active despite the hidden later-mounted scope")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when it opens, then `document.activeElement` is the content element. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Focuses first focusable item upon opening")
- Given an open Melt dialog with focus on the content, when `Tab` is pressed, then focus wraps back to the content element. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Tabbing on last item focuses first item")
- Given a Melt dialog with `openFocus` returning the `#openFocus` element, when the dialog opens, then that element has focus. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Respects the `openFocus` prop")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `closeFocus` returning the `#closeFocus` element, when `Escape` is pressed, then that element has focus. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Respects the `closeFocus` prop")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `escapeBehavior: 'ignore'`, when `Escape` is pressed and then `Tab` is pressed ten times, then focus stays inside the content every time, so the focus trap was not deactivated. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Doesn't deactivate focus trap on escape provided `escapeBehavior` false")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `closeOnOutsideClick: false`, when the overlay is clicked and then `Tab` is pressed ten times, then focus stays inside the content every time. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Doesn't deactivate focus trap on outside click provided `closeOnOutsideClick` false")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when the `open` store is set to `false` from a button inside the content, then the trigger has focus. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Returns focus to trigger when manually setting `open` state to false")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `closeFocus` returning `#closeFocus`, when the `open` store is set to `false` from inside the content, then `#closeFocus` has focus rather than the trigger. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Respects the `closeFocus` prop when manually setting `open` state to false")
- Given an open Melt dialog whose child stops propagation of `Escape`, when `Escape` is pressed and `Tab` is pressed ten times, then focus stays inside the content. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Doesn't deactivate focus trap on escape that is intercepted")
- Given an open Melt dialog, when an outside click interceptor button is clicked and `Tab` is pressed ten times, then focus stays inside the content. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Doesn't deactivate focus trap on outside click that is intercepted")
- Given an open nested Melt dialog set, when the outer dialog opens, then `document.activeElement` is the outer content element. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogNested.spec.ts: "Nested Dialogs > Focuses first focusable item upon opening")
- Given an open nested Melt dialog set with focus on the outer content, when `Tab` is pressed, then focus wraps back to the outer content. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogNested.spec.ts: "Nested Dialogs > Tabbing on last item focuses first item")
- Given an open Melt dialog with transitions, when it opens, then `document.activeElement` is the content element. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Focuses first focusable item upon opening")
- Given an open Melt dialog with transitions and focus on the content, when `Tab` is pressed, then focus wraps back to the content. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Tabbing on last item focuses first item")
- Given a force-mounted bits Dialog rendered with `withOpenCheck` true, when it is opened and `Escape` is pressed, then the trigger has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should focus the trigger when the dialog is closed (force mount: true)")
- Given a force-mounted bits Dialog rendered with `withOpenCheck` false, when it is opened and `Escape` is pressed, then the trigger has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should focus the trigger when the dialog is closed (force mount: false)")
- Given a bits Dialog whose `onOpenAutoFocus` calls `preventDefault()` and focuses `#open-focus-override`, when it opens, then that override element has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should respect `onOpenAutoFocus` prop")
- Given a force-mounted bits Dialog with `withOpenCheck` true whose `onOpenAutoFocus` overrides focus, when it opens, then `#open-focus-override` has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should respect `onOpenAutoFocus` prop (force mount: true)")
- Given a force-mounted bits Dialog with `withOpenCheck` false whose `onOpenAutoFocus` overrides focus, when it opens, then `#open-focus-override` has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should respect `onOpenAutoFocus` prop (force mount: false)")
- Given a force-mounted bits Dialog with `withOpenCheck` true whose `onCloseAutoFocus` calls `preventDefault()` and focuses `#close-focus-override`, when it is opened and `Escape` is pressed, then that override element has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should respect `onCloseAutoFocus` prop (force mount: true)")
- Given a force-mounted bits Dialog with `withOpenCheck` false whose `onCloseAutoFocus` overrides focus, when it is opened and `Escape` is pressed, then `#close-focus-override` has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should respect `onCloseAutoFocus` prop (force mount: false)")
- Given an open bits Dialog whose `onCloseAutoFocus` overrides focus, when `Escape` is pressed, then `#close-focus-override` has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should respect `onCloseAutoFocus` prop")
- Given an open bits Dialog, when it opens, then the close button has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should focus first focusable item upon opening")
- Given a bits Dialog opened programmatically via a toggle button while an outside element held focus, when `Escape` closes it, then focus returns to the toggle button that was focused at open time, not the outside element. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should return focus to programmatically focused element when closed")
- Given a bits Dialog opened programmatically whose `onCloseAutoFocus` overrides focus, when `Escape` closes it, then `#close-focus-override` has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Focus Management > should still respect onCloseAutoFocus when opened programmatically")
- Given a bits nested Dialog fixture with the first dialog open, when `Tab` is pressed repeatedly, then focus cycles between the first close button and the second dialog's trigger; pressing `Enter` on that trigger opens the second dialog and focuses its close button, and `Enter` again closes it and returns focus to the second trigger. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Nested Dialogs > should handle focus scoping correctly")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a bits Dialog bound to `open`, when the trigger is clicked then `Escape` pressed, then the binding text reads `true` then `false`, and clicking the external toggle re-opens the content. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "should respect binding to the `open` prop")
- Given a Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false` and an `openAutoFocus` handler, when the component mounts closed, then the handler has been called zero times, and it is called exactly once after the trigger click. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false, openAutoFocus > should not emit openAutoFocus while closed and emit once per open")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given two Dialogs with `unmountOnHide=false` where a hidden non-modal one mounted after the open modal one, when `Escape` is pressed, then the first content's inline `display` becomes `none` and focus returns to its trigger, so the hidden later layer does not swallow Escape. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given two Dialogs with unmountOnHide=false > should close the open dialog on Escape even though a hidden one mounted after it")
- Given two Dialogs with `unmountOnHide=false` both closed, when `pointerdown` fires on `document.body` after the outside-listener `setTimeout(0)` window, then the closed keep-mounted dialog's `interactOutside` handler is not called. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given two Dialogs with unmountOnHide=false > should not emit interactOutside on a closed keep-mounted dialog")
- Given a modal Dialog with no explicit prop and no overlay, when it opens, then `document.body.style.pointerEvents` is `none`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a modal Dialog (#2677) > should lock body pointer-events by default")
- Given a modal Dialog with `disableOutsidePointerEvents="false"` on the content, when it opens, then `document.body.style.pointerEvents` is not `none`, so the prop is not hardcoded. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a modal Dialog (#2677) > should respect disableOutsidePointerEvents=false on the content")
- Given a modal Dialog with `disableOutsidePointerEvents="true"` on the content, when it opens, then `document.body.style.pointerEvents` is `none`. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a modal Dialog (#2677) > should still lock body pointer-events when explicitly true")
- Given an open Melt dialog whose `onOutsideClick` calls `preventDefault()`, when the overlay is clicked, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Prevents closing on outside click if `defaultPrevented` in `onOutsideClick` callback")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `closeOnOutsideClick: false`, when the overlay is clicked, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Respects the `closeOnOutsideClick` prop")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `closeOnOutsideClick: false` and a floating close button rendered outside the content, when that floating closer is clicked, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > When closeOnOutsideClick is false, clicking floating closer closes dialog")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a mouse device, when an outside button that stops propagation of `click` is clicked, then the content stays visible, and a subsequent overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Mouse Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with click interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a mouse device, when an outside button that stops propagation of `pointerdown` is clicked, then the content stays visible, and a subsequent overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Mouse Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with pointerdown interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a mouse device, when an outside button that stops propagation of `pointerup` is clicked, then the content stays visible, and a subsequent overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Mouse Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with pointerup interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a mouse device, when an outside button that stops propagation of `mousedown` is clicked, then the content stays visible, and a subsequent overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Mouse Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with mousedown interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a mouse device, when an outside button that stops propagation of `mouseup` is clicked, then the content stays visible, and a subsequent overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Mouse Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with mouseup interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a touch device, when a full touch sequence hits an outside button that stops propagation of `click`, then the content stays visible, and a later overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with click interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a touch device, when a full touch sequence hits an outside button that stops propagation of `pointerdown`, then the content stays visible, and a later overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with pointerdown interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a touch device, when a full touch sequence hits an outside button that stops propagation of `pointerup`, then the content stays visible, and a later overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with pointerup interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a touch device, when a full touch sequence hits an outside button that stops propagation of `mousedown`, then the content stays visible, and a later overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with mousedown interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a touch device, when a full touch sequence hits an outside button that stops propagation of `mouseup`, then the content stays visible, and a later overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with mouseup interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a touch device, when a full touch sequence hits an outside button that stops propagation of `touchstart`, then the content stays visible, and a later overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with touchstart interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and a touch device, when a full touch sequence hits an outside button that stops propagation of `touchend`, then the content stays visible, and a later overlay click still closes it. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Doesn't close when interacting outside with touchend interceptor")
- Given an open Melt dialog and an outside button whose `touchend` handler calls `preventDefault()` and `stopPropagation()`, when a `touchstart`/`touchend` pair hits it, then the content stays visible, and a following overlay click still closes the dialog, showing `interceptedEvents` is reset without a `click` event. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Touch Device > Resets `interceptedEvents` when calling `preventDefault()` on touch event")
- Given an open bits Dialog with an `onInteractOutside` spy, when the overlay is clicked, then the spy is called. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "should close on outside click")
- Given an open bits Dialog with an `onInteractOutside` spy, when the content is clicked, then the content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "should not close when clicking within bounds")
- Given an open bits Dialog with `interactOutsideBehavior: 'ignore'`, when the overlay is clicked, then the content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `interactOutsideBehavior: 'ignore'` prop")
- Given an open bits Dialog with a `DismissibleLayer` whose `ref` getter is instrumented, when a `focusin` event fires on the content and the component is unmounted synchronously before the pending focus work runs, then the layer is removed from the global `bitsDismissableLayers` map and the ref is not read again after the next tick. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "DismissibleLayer teardown (derived_inert / #2080) > should not read the layer ref from pending focus work after unmount")
- Given a bits Dialog rendered already `open` and unmounted while the layer is live, when 50ms pass, then no `derived_inert` console warning is emitted. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "DismissibleLayer teardown (derived_inert / #2080) > should not emit derived_inert when unmounted while open")
- Given a bits Dialog opened, closed via the close button and immediately reopened via the trigger, when 50ms pass, then the content is still present and no `derived_inert` warning is emitted, so stale document listeners do not auto-dismiss the new layer. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "DismissibleLayer teardown (derived_inert / #2080) > should not auto-dismiss on sequential open after close via trigger-cycle")
- Given a bits Dialog toggled open and closed six times then unmounted, when a `pointerdown` is dispatched on `document.body`, then no `derived_inert` warning is emitted, so `TextSelectionLayer` left no document listener behind. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "TextSelectionLayer teardown (derived_inert) > should not emit derived_inert on document pointerdown after teardown")
- Given a bits nested Dialog fixture, when the first, second and third dialogs are opened and then closed in reverse, then each content's `--bits-dialog-depth` is `0`, `1` and `2` respectively, each ancestor's `--bits-dialog-nested-count` counts its open descendants, ancestors gain `data-nested-open=""` on content and overlay while a descendant is open, nested contents carry `data-nested=""`, and every counter and attribute unwinds as each level closes. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Nested Dialogs > should track dialog depth correctly")
- Given a bits fixture with an Alert Dialog nested inside a Dialog, when the alert dialog is opened and then cancelled, then the dialog content's `--bits-dialog-nested-count` goes `0` to `1` to `0`, the alert content's `--bits-dialog-depth` is `1` with its own nested count `0`, the dialog content and overlay gain and lose `data-nested-open=""`, and the alert content carries `data-nested=""`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Nested Alert Dialogs and Dialogs > should handle Alert Dialog nested inside Dialog with correct depth tracking")
- Given a bits fixture with a Dialog nested inside an Alert Dialog, when the inner dialog is opened and then closed, then the alert content's `--bits-dialog-nested-count` goes `0` to `1` to `0`, the inner dialog's `--bits-dialog-depth` is `1`, the alert content and overlay gain and lose `data-nested-open=""`, and the inner dialog content carries `data-nested=""`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Nested Alert Dialogs and Dialogs > should handle Dialog nested inside Alert Dialog with correct depth tracking")
- Given a bits three-level Dialog to Alert Dialog to Dialog nesting, when all three are opened, then depths are `0`, `1`, `2`, nested counts are `2`, `1`, `0`, only the two ancestors carry `data-nested-open=""` on content and overlay, and closing the innermost then the alert unwinds the counts to `1`/`0` and then `0`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Nested Alert Dialogs and Dialogs > should handle three-level nesting: Dialog -> Alert Dialog -> Dialog")
- Given a bits Dialog on a page whose `html` sets `scrollbar-gutter: stable` and is 200vh tall, when the dialog opens, then `document.body.style.paddingRight` is unchanged from before opening, so no scrollbar compensation padding is added. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Scroll Lock > should not add padding when scrollbar-gutter: stable is applied")

### Positioning
- Given an open Melt dialog with no `portal` prop, when the portalled element is inspected, then its `parentElement` is `document.body`. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Portalled el attaches dialog to body")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `portal: '#portal-target'`, when the portalled element is inspected, then its `parentElement` is the portal target element. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Attaches portal el to the portal target if prop provided")
- Given an open Melt dialog with `portal: null`, when the portalled element is inspected, then its `parentElement` is the in-place `main` element. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Does not portal if `null` is passed as portal prop")
- Given an open Melt dialog with transitions and no `portal` prop, when the portalled element is inspected, then its `parentElement` is `document.body`. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Portals the portalled el into the body when no portal prop is passed")
- Given an open Melt dialog with transitions and `portal: '#portal-target'`, when the portalled element is inspected, then its `parentElement` is the portal target. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Portals the portalled el into the correct target if one is passed via the `portal` prop")
- Given an open Melt dialog with transitions and `portal: null`, when the portalled element is inspected, then its `parentElement` is the in-place `main` element. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > Does not portal the portalled el if `null` is passed as the `portal` prop")
- Given an open bits Dialog using the portal element, when the content is inspected, then its `parentElement` is `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Portal Behavior > should portal to body when using portal element")
- Given an open bits Dialog with `portalProps.disabled` true, when the content is inspected, then its `parentElement` is not `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Portal Behavior > should not portal to body when portal is disabled")
- Given an open bits Dialog with `portalProps.to: '#portalTarget'`, when the content is inspected, then its `parentElement` is the portal target element. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Portal Behavior > should portal to the target if passed as a prop")

### Animation and presence
- Given a force-mounted bits Dialog, when the trigger is clicked, then both content and overlay pass through a state with `data-starting-style` present, and after `Escape` both pass through a state with `data-ending-style` present. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Data Attributes > should apply transition attrs to content and overlay during open and close")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default Dialog, when axe is run on `document.body` both closed and after the trigger is clicked, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given an open Dialog with `unmountOnHide=false`, when axe is run on `document.body`, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false > should pass axe accessibility tests when open")
- Given a rendered Melt dialog, when axe is run on the container, then there are no violations. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > No accessibility violations")
- Given a rendered nested Melt dialog fixture, when axe is run on the container, then there are no violations. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogNested.spec.ts: "Nested Dialogs > No accessibility violations")
- Given a rendered Melt dialog with transitions, when axe is run on the container, then there are no violations. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogTransitions.spec.ts: "Dialog with Transitions > No accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given an open Dialog whose content has no description, when it opens, then `console.warn` is called exactly once. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when no description has been provided > should warn to the console")
- Given a Dialog with neither a title nor a description, when the trigger is clicked, then `console.warn` is called exactly once. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when no title has been provided > should warn to the console")
- Given a Dialog with a title and `:aria-describedby="undefined"` on the content, when the trigger is clicked, then `console.warn` is not called, so passing `undefined` explicitly opts out of the missing-description warning. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when aria-describedby is set to undefined > should not warn to the console")
- Given reka's outside-click dismissal, when the test needs to click the overlay, then it must first await a `setTimeout(0)` because `DismissableLayer` registers the document `pointerdown` listener asynchronously, and a further ~10ms for the `FocusScope` cleanup timer. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a default Dialog > after clicking the trigger > when clicking the overlay > should focus trigger")
- Given force-mounted reka Dialog content, when a test finishes, then the wrapper must be unmounted explicitly or the layer leaks into `DismissableLayer`'s module-level tracking set across tests. (reka: packages/core/src/Dialog/Dialog.test.ts: "given a Dialog with unmountOnHide=false")
- Given Melt's nested-dialog and transition suites, when they run, then `requestAnimationFrame` is stubbed to a 16ms `setTimeout` so Svelte transitions advance under jsdom. (melt: src/tests/dialog/DialogNested.spec.ts: "Nested Dialogs")
- Given Melt's dialog fixture, when focus-trap behavior is asserted, then the content element itself is treated as the first focusable element because trap assertions were flaky otherwise. (melt: src/tests/dialog/Dialog.spec.ts: "Dialog > Focuses first focusable item upon opening")
- Given the melt e2e dialog spec, when it runs, then it is a Playwright test navigating a real browser to the docs route `/docs/builders/dialog`, waiting for JS availability, with `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'parallel' })`, and it uses `page.tap` plus bounding-box maths rather than jsdom fakes. (melt: e2e/dialog.spec.ts: "dialog > touch device > doesn't leak events when tapping overlay")
- Given bits' dismissal assertions, when a dialog is opened in a test helper, then the helper waits until the content's layer appears in the global `bitsDismissableLayers` map before interacting, because listeners attach asynchronously. (bits: tests/src/tests/dialog/dialog.browser.test.ts: "Open/Close Behavior > should open when the trigger is clicked")

- Given an open bits Alert Dialog, when inspecting the content, then `aria-describedby` equals the description element's id. (bits: tests/src/tests/alert-dialog/alert-dialog.browser.test.ts: "ARIA Attributes > should apply the correct `aria-describedby` attribute to the `Dialog.Content` element")

### Positioning

### Animation and presence

(bits: tests/src/tests/alert-dialog/alert-dialog.browser.test.ts: "Props and Rendering > should forceMount the content and overlay when their `forceMount` prop is true and the `open` snippet prop is used")

### Notes and edge cases

## drawer

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default Drawer, when the trigger is clicked, then an element matching `[role="dialog"]` exists in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > after clicking the trigger > should have role=\"dialog\" on content")
- Given an open Drawer with a `DrawerTitle`, when the content is inspected, then its `aria-labelledby` is a non-empty id whose element's `textContent` is the title text. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > after clicking the trigger > should have aria-labelledby pointing to title")
- Given an open Drawer with a `DrawerDescription`, when the content is inspected, then its `aria-describedby` is a non-empty id whose element's `textContent` is the description text. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > after clicking the trigger > should have aria-describedby pointing to description")
- Given a swipe that passes the dismiss threshold, when the pointer is released, then the element gains a `data-swipe-dismissed` attribute so consumers can style a swipe close differently from a click or Escape close. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — dismiss vs cancel CSS var clearing > preserves movement CSS vars on dismiss so close animation runs from drag position")
- Given a swipe that stays below the dismiss threshold, when the pointer is released, then the element does not have `data-swipe-dismissed`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — dismiss vs cancel CSS var clearing > clears movement CSS vars on cancel so drawer animates back to rest")
- Given a drag against the dismiss direction that is cancelled, when the pointer is released, then the element does not have `data-swipe-dismissed`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — non-dismissable direction (elastic pull) > damps and tracks a drag away from the dismiss direction")
- Given a drag in progress on the element the composable is attached to, when two pointer moves have been processed, then `data-swiping` is not set on that element because the marker is written by the consumer rather than the composable. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — releases the popup never sees > treats a move with no button held as the missing pointerup")

### Keyboard
- Given an open Drawer, when `Escape` is pressed on the active element, then the title text is no longer in `document.body`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > after clicking the trigger > should close on Escape key")

### Pointer
- Given a default Drawer, when the trigger is clicked, then the title element is contained in `document.body`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > after clicking the trigger > should show drawer content")
- Given an open Drawer, when the close button is clicked, then the close text is no longer in `document.body`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > after clicking the trigger > should close when close button is clicked")
- Given a Drawer with two snap points `[0.5, 1]` open at snap `0.5`, when a pointer drag upward past the snap threshold is released, then `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` and `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` are both `0px`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts: "drawer snap points — integration > swipe release does not leave stale movement var > clears --drawer-swipe-movement-y after snap-to-snap release")
- Given a Drawer open at snap `0.5` with `--drawer-snap-point-offset: 400px`, when a large upward drag is released, then the offset becomes `0px` in the same synchronous step that clears `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` to `0px`, so the transform does not revert to the old snap for a frame. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts: "drawer snap points — integration > swipe release does not leave stale movement var > updates --drawer-snap-point-offset synchronously on snap-to-snap release (smooth drag)")
- Given a `down`-dismiss swipe harness, when a 60px downward drag past the 40px default threshold is released, then `onDismiss` is called once and `onCancel` is not called. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — dismiss vs cancel CSS var clearing > preserves movement CSS vars on dismiss so close animation runs from drag position")
- Given a `down`-dismiss swipe harness, when a 15px downward drag below the threshold is released, then `onCancel` is called once and `onDismiss` is not called. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — dismiss vs cancel CSS var clearing > clears movement CSS vars on cancel so drawer animates back to rest")
- Given a `down`-dismiss swipe harness, when the drag first pulls up 50px and then reverses down to +70px from origin before release, then `onDismiss` is called once and `onCancel` is not called, so the dismiss direction is adopted on reversal. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — non-dismissable direction (elastic pull) > still adopts the dismiss direction when the drag reverses into it")
- Given a `down`-dismiss harness where one gesture drags down 60px, reverses to +15px to latch the cancel state and never receives a `pointerup`, when a fresh press with a new `pointerId` drags down 70px and releases, then `onDismiss` is called once and `onCancel` is not called. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — releases the popup never sees > does not leak state from an unfinished gesture into the next one")

### Focus management
- Given a Drawer trigger clicked, when `Escape` is dispatched on `document.activeElement`, then that active element is inside the opened drawer, so opening the drawer moved focus into the content. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > after clicking the trigger > should close on Escape key")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a Drawer with an `update:open` listener, when the trigger is clicked, then the handler is called with `true` and `{ reason: 'trigger-press' }`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "update:open change event details > emits trigger-press reason on trigger click")
- Given an open Drawer with an `update:open` listener, when the close button is clicked, then the handler is called with `false` and `{ reason: 'close-press' }`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "update:open change event details > emits close-press reason on close click")
- Given an open modal Drawer, when the trigger is clicked a second time, then `update:open` is called with `false` and `{ reason: 'trigger-press' }`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "update:open change event details > closes on a second trigger click (toggle)")
- Given an open Drawer with `modal: false`, when the trigger is clicked a second time via `userEvent`, then `update:open` is called exactly once with `false` and `{ reason: 'trigger-press' }`, so the non-modal outside-click path does not double-fire. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "update:open change event details > closes on a second trigger click in non-modal mode")
- Given snap points `[200, 400, 500]` with `popupHeight` 500, when `resolvedSnapPoints` is read, then it has three entries sorted by ascending height with `offset = popupHeight - height`, so `{200, 300}`, `{400, 100}` and `{500, 0}`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > resolves numeric pixel snap points and computes offsets")
- Given snap points `['50%', 300, 500]`, when `resolvedSnapPoints` is read, then the unsupported-unit `'50%'` entry is dropped and only heights `300` and `500` remain. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > drops unknown-unit snap points (parseSnapPoint returns null)")
- Given snap points `['abcpx', '-100px', -50, 300, 500]`, when `resolvedSnapPoints` is read, then the NaN and negative entries are dropped and only heights `300` and `500` remain. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > drops non-finite and negative snap points (NaN / negatives)")
- Given `activeSnapPoint` of `'400px'` against resolved points storing numeric `400`, when a 20px down drag is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `400`, so the active snap is matched by parsed-height equivalence rather than raw value. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > resolves the active snap by parsed-height equivalence, not just raw value")
- Given active snap `400` (offset 100) in non-sequential mode, when a 20px down drag with velocity `y: 0.1` is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `400`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > snaps to the closer snap point on small drag with zero velocity")
- Given active snap `500` (offset 0) in non-sequential mode, when a 250px down drag with velocity `y: 0.1` is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `200` because target offset 250 is 50 away from offset 300 and 150 away from offset 100. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > snaps to a lower snap point when dragged most of the way there")
- Given active snap `200` (offset 300) in non-sequential mode, when a 180px down drag with velocity `y: 0.1` is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `null`, dismissing because the target offset 480 is 20 from fully-closed and 180 from the nearest snap. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > dismisses when closer to fully-closed than to any snap")
- Given active snap `500` in non-sequential mode, when only a 50px down drag is released with velocity `y: 2`, then the velocity boost of `clamp(vel, -4, 4) * 300 = 600` pushes the projected offset to 650 and `onSnapPointChange` receives `null`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > fast flick adds velocity offset that pushes target past a snap")
- Given an `up` drawer with active snap `400` in non-sequential mode, when a 300px dismiss-direction drag with velocity `y: -0.1` is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `200`, so velocity sign is flipped for `up`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > non-sequential mode (snap to closest) > honors up-drawer sign convention")
- Given active snap `500` in sequential mode, when a 30px down drag with velocity `y: 1.0` (same direction, `|vel| >= 0.5`) is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `400`, advancing exactly one step. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > sequential mode > fast swipe advances exactly one snap point in drag direction")
- Given active snap `500` in sequential mode, when a 20px down drag with velocity `y: 0.1` is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `500`, keeping the active snap. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > sequential mode > slow swipe without crossing keeps active snap")
- Given active snap `500` in sequential mode, when a 150px down drag with velocity `y: 0.1` physically crosses the adjacent snap's offset 100, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `400`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > sequential mode > slow swipe that physically crosses the adjacent snap advances")
- Given active snap `200` (the lowest) in sequential mode, when a 180px down drag with velocity `y: 0.1` is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `null`, so the close-vs-snap comparison overrides sequential stepping. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > sequential mode > dismisses from the lowest snap point when dragged most of the way closed")
- Given snap points `[200, 500]` with active `500` (fully open), when a -1000px drag with velocity `y: -2` is released, then the target offset clamps via `max(0, min(popupHeight, ...))` to 0 and `onSnapPointChange` receives `500`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > overshoot clamping (drag past fully-open) > clamps a huge up-drag at fully-open snap=1.0 offset (0)")
- Given snap points `[200, 500]` with active `200` (offset 300), when a -1500px drag with velocity `y: -3` is released, then the clamped drag offset 0 plus the -900 velocity offset yields -900 and `onSnapPointChange` receives `500` because the nearest snap distance 900 beats the 1400 close distance. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > overshoot clamping (drag past fully-open) > clamps a huge up-drag when starting from a mid snap")
- Given an `up` drawer with snap points `[200, 500]` and active `500`, when a -1000px drag (against dismiss) with velocity `y: 2` is released, then `onSnapPointChange` receives `500`, so the clamp holds under the flipped sign convention. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math > overshoot clamping (drag past fully-open) > also works for `up` drawers (sign-flipped)")
- Given a swipe harness with a timed drag past threshold anchored to `performance.now()`, when the pointer is released, then `onRelease` is called once with a velocity object whose `x` and `y` are numbers and whose `y` is greater than 0. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — dismiss vs cancel CSS var clearing > fires onRelease with the measured velocity vector")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given a drag in progress with a movement var already written, when a `pointermove` arrives with `buttons: 0`, then `onCancel` is called once and `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` becomes `0px`, treating the buttonless move as the missing `pointerup`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — releases the popup never sees > treats a move with no button held as the missing pointerup")
- Given a drag in progress on the popup, when `pointerup` is dispatched on `document.body` rather than the popup, then `onCancel` is called once and `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` becomes `0px`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — releases the popup never sees > finishes on a pointerup that only reaches the document")
- Given a drag in progress, when a `blur` event fires on `window`, then `onCancel` is called once and `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` becomes `0px`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — releases the popup never sees > finishes when the window loses focus mid-drag")
- Given a `right`-dismiss drawer whose content is vertically scrollable, when a touch flick drifts 3px right while moving 40px down, then neither `touchmove` is `defaultPrevented`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` stays unset, and neither `onDismiss` nor `onCancel` fires. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — cross-axis scroll arbitration > yields a mostly-vertical flick to the content scroll on a right drawer")
- Given a `right`-dismiss drawer where a vertical scroll has already claimed the gesture, when a hard 120px horizontal curve follows, then that `touchmove` is not `defaultPrevented`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` stays unset, and `onDismiss` does not fire, so arbitration is not re-run mid-gesture. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — cross-axis scroll arbitration > keeps yielding for the rest of the gesture once the cross axis has won")
- Given a `right`-dismiss drawer with a vertically scrollable child, when a touch drag moves 80px horizontally with only 4px of vertical drift, then the `touchmove` is `defaultPrevented`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` is `80px`, and `onDismiss` fires once. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — cross-axis scroll arbitration > still swipes when the drag is decisively along the dismiss axis")
- Given a `right`-dismiss drawer whose child scrolls only horizontally (no cross-axis scroller), when a 2px horizontal, 30px vertical touch move occurs, then it is `defaultPrevented` and `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` is `2px`, so no arbitration takes place. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — cross-axis scroll arbitration > does not arbitrate when the content has no cross-axis scroller")
- Given a `right`-dismiss drawer whose first `touchmove` is non-cancelable (a native scroll already under way), when a decisive 120px horizontal move follows, then it is not `defaultPrevented`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` stays unset, and `onDismiss` does not fire. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — cross-axis scroll arbitration > yields when the browser has already committed the gesture to a native scroll")
- Given a `down`-dismiss drawer whose child is horizontally scrollable, when a touch drag moves 40px left with only 3px of vertical drift, then neither `touchmove` is `defaultPrevented`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` stays unset, and `onDismiss` does not fire. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — cross-axis scroll arbitration > yields a horizontal drift on a bottom drawer to horizontally scrollable content")
- Given a `right`-dismiss drawer where a vertical scroll won a gesture that never received a `touchend`, when a fresh `touchstart` followed by an 80px horizontal drag occurs, then that `touchmove` is `defaultPrevented` and `onDismiss` fires once, so the previous verdict is not inherited. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — cross-axis scroll arbitration > starts clean after a gesture whose end was never seen")

### Animation and presence
- Given a Drawer with snap points `[0.5, 1]`, a mocked 800px popup height and `window.innerHeight` 800, when it is opened at snap `0.5`, then `--drawer-snap-point-offset` on the content is `400px` (`800 - round(0.5 * 800)`). (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts: "drawer snap points — integration > mount-time snap offset write (reopen bug) > writes --drawer-snap-point-offset on initial open for snap=0.5")
- Given a Drawer with snap points that has already been opened once and closed (so `popupHeight` is cached on the root context), when it is reopened, then `--drawer-snap-point-offset` is `400px` again rather than staying unset at `0px`, because the offset is written explicitly in `onMounted` instead of by a lazy watcher. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts: "drawer snap points — integration > mount-time snap offset write (reopen bug) > writes --drawer-snap-point-offset on REOPEN after close (lazy-watcher bug)")
- Given a Drawer opened at snap `0.5`, closed and reopened after a snap transition, when it reopens, then `--drawer-snap-point-offset` reflects the current active snap point and is `400px`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts: "drawer snap points — integration > mount-time snap offset write (reopen bug) > writes --drawer-snap-point-offset on REOPEN after snap transition + close")
- Given a Drawer whose `defaultSnapPoint` is `1`, when it is opened, then `--drawer-snap-point-offset` is `0px` (`800 - 800`). (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts: "drawer snap points — integration > mount-time snap offset write (reopen bug) > writes a snap=1.0 offset (0px) when defaultSnapPoint is 1")
- Given a dismissing swipe, when the pointer is released, then `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` is neither `0px` nor empty, so the close animation starts from the released drag position instead of snapping back for a frame. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — dismiss vs cancel CSS var clearing > preserves movement CSS vars on dismiss so close animation runs from drag position")
- Given a cancelled swipe, when the pointer is released, then `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` and `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` are both `0px` so the drawer animates back to rest. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — dismiss vs cancel CSS var clearing > clears movement CSS vars on cancel so drawer animates back to rest")
- Given a `down`-dismiss drawer with only `['down']` allowed, when the pointer pulls up 100px, then `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` is `-10px` (sqrt-damped from -100) and `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` is `0px`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — non-dismissable direction (elastic pull) > damps and tracks a drag away from the dismiss direction")
- Given a drawer whose allowed directions are `['down', 'up']` (the snap-point configuration), when the pointer pulls up 100px, then `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` is `-100px` with no damping. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — non-dismissable direction (elastic pull) > leaves an allowed direction undamped when both axes directions are allowed")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a closed default Drawer, when axe is run on `document.body`, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > should pass axe accessibility tests when closed")
- Given an open default Drawer, when axe is run on `document.body`, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > should pass axe accessibility tests when open")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a Drawer whose content has no `DrawerTitle`, when the trigger is clicked, then `console.warn` is called. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.test.ts: "given a default Drawer > when no title is provided > should warn to the console")
- Given `getDisplacement`, when called as `('down', 0, 50)`, `('up', 0, -50)`, `('right', 50, 0)` and `('left', -50, 0)`, then each returns `50`, so movement in the dismiss direction is positive. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "getDisplacement > returns positive when moving in the dismiss direction")
- Given `getDisplacement`, when called as `('down', 0, -50)` and `('up', 0, 50)`, then each returns `-50`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "getDisplacement > returns negative when moving against the dismiss direction")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` with `releaseVelocity: 0.1`, when called for a `down` drawer of size 500 dragged 100, then it returns `null` because velocity is below `MIN_SWIPE_RELEASE_VELOCITY` of 0.2. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > returns null when velocity is below MIN_SWIPE_RELEASE_VELOCITY (0.2)")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` with `releaseVelocity: -1` on a `down` drawer, when called, then it returns `null` because the directional velocity is negative. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > returns null when moving against the dismiss direction")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` with `axisDelta` equal to the full `size` of 500, when called, then it returns `null` because the remaining distance is 0. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > returns null when remaining distance is 0")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` for a `down` drawer with size 500, `axisDelta` 100 and velocity 1, when called, then it returns a number in `[0.1, 1]`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > returns a scalar in [0.1, 1] for a reasonable release")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` with 450px remaining and the maximum velocity 4, when called, then the duration clamps to 112.5ms within `[80, 360]` and the returned scalar is below 0.3. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > short remaining + high velocity → near the minimum scalar (fast)")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` with 480px remaining and velocity 0.21 just above the minimum, when called, then the duration clamps to the 360ms maximum and the returned scalar is approximately 1. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > long remaining + low velocity → near the maximum scalar (slow)")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` for an `up` drawer with `axisDelta: -100` and `releaseVelocity: -1`, when called, then it returns a number in `[0.1, 1]`, so the sign convention is flipped for `up`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > handles up-drawer sign convention")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` with `snapPointOffset: 100` on a `down` drawer, `axisDelta` 50 and velocity 2, when called, then the translation seeds at 150, the duration is 175ms and the scalar is approximately 0.405. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > respects snapPointOffset when computing translation")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` for a `right` drawer with `snapPointOffset: 100`, when compared against the equivalent `down` call, then the two scalars match to five decimal places. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > respects snapPointOffset for horizontal (right) drawers")
- Given `computeSwipeReleaseScalar` for a `left` drawer with `snapPointOffset: 100`, negative `axisDelta` and negative velocity, when compared against the equivalent `up` call, then the two scalars match to five decimal places. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/utils.test.ts: "computeSwipeReleaseScalar > respects snapPointOffset for horizontal (left) drawers")
- Given jsdom has no `ResizeObserver`, no layout and zero `offsetHeight`/`offsetWidth`, when the snap integration suite runs, then it installs a `ResizeObserver` stub reporting a fixed 800px contentRect on the next microtask, redefines `window.innerHeight` to 800 so fraction snap maths stay whole, stubs `offsetHeight` to 800 and `offsetWidth` to 400, and polyfills `PointerEvent` plus `setPointerCapture`/`releasePointerCapture`/`hasPointerCapture`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts: "drawer snap points — integration")
- Given the snap integration suite's teardown, when a test ends, then it calls testing-library `cleanup()` rather than clearing `document.body.innerHTML`, because clearing innerHTML leaves Vue's DOM references stale and crashes the next unmount. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts: "drawer snap points — integration")
- Given jsdom assigns synthetic events strictly increasing real-clock `timeStamp` values, when the swipe unit suite dispatches pointer events, then every event defaults to `timeStamp` 0 so gesture classification depends on displacement alone, and only tests that need measurable velocity pass timestamps anchored to `performance.now()`. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — dismiss vs cancel CSS var clearing > fires onRelease with the measured velocity vector")
- Given jsdom's inconsistent `TouchEvent`/`Touch` support and zero-size boxes, when the cross-axis arbitration suite runs, then it builds touch events by hand with a `touches` array and marks a child scrollable by defining `scrollHeight`/`clientHeight` (or the horizontal pair) plus an `overflow` style. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useSwipeDismiss.test.ts: "useSwipeDismiss — cross-axis scroll arbitration")
- Given `useDrawerSnapPoints` is exercised directly with plumbed refs and a null `viewportRef`, when its release maths is tested, then the DOM layer is bypassed entirely and `onSnapPointChange` calls are the only observable output. (reka: packages/core/src/Drawer/composables/useDrawerSnapPoints.test.ts: "useDrawerSnapPoints — snap release math")

## popover

### Roles and attributes
- Given a closed Popover, when rendered, then the trigger button has no `aria-controls` attribute at all. (reka: packages/core/src/Popover/Popover.test.ts: "should only render aria-controls while open")
- Given a Popover, when the trigger is clicked open, then the trigger's `aria-controls` value resolves to an element that exists in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/Popover/Popover.test.ts: "should only render aria-controls while open")
- Given an open Popover, when rendered, then the `trigger`, `content`, `close`, and `arrow` elements each carry a `data-popover-<part>` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should have bits data attrs")
- Given an open Popover with an overlay, when rendered, then the overlay element carries `data-popover-overlay`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should have bits data attrs for overlay")
- Given an open Popover with an overlay, when rendered, then the overlay has `data-state="open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should have correct data-state attribute on overlay when open")
- Given a closed Popover whose overlay uses `forceMount`, when rendered, then the overlay has `data-state="closed"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should have correct data-state attribute on overlay when closed with forceMount")
- Given an open Popover with a `style` object passed to content, when rendered, then the content element's inline `background-color` is `rgb(255, 0, 0)`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should apply custom style prop to content")
- Given a force-mounted Popover content with a `style` object, when rendered while closed, then the content element's inline `background-color` is `rgb(0, 255, 0)`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should apply custom style prop to content (static)")
- Given a Popover created with explicit `ids` for trigger and content, when rendered, then `trigger.id` is `id-trigger` and `content.id` is `id-content`. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given an open Popover overlay rendered through the `child` snippet, when rendered, then the child element carries `data-popover-overlay`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should render overlay with child snippet")

### Keyboard
- Given a focused Popover trigger, when `Enter` is pressed, then the content is mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should open on enter")
- Given a focused Popover trigger, when `Space` is pressed, then the content is mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should open on space")
- Given an open Popover, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should close on escape keydown by default")
- Given an open Popover, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is no longer visible. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Closes on escape")
- Given an open Popover with `escapeKeydownBehavior: "ignore"`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should allow ignoring the escapeKeydownBehavior")
- Given an open Popover whose `onEscapeKeydown` calls `preventDefault` only the first time, when `Escape` is pressed twice, then the content survives the first press and is removed on the second. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should allow cancelling the `onEscapeKeydown` event")
- Given an open Popover with `escapeBehavior: "ignore"`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays visible and keeps focus on itself. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Doesn't deactivate focus trap on escape provided `escapeBehavior` false")
- Given an open Popover with a button inside that calls `stopPropagation` on `Escape` keydown, when that button is focused and `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Doesn't deactivate focus trap on escape that is intercepted")

### Pointer
- Given a closed Popover, when the trigger is clicked, then the content becomes visible. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Opens on click")
- Given a closed Popover, when the trigger is clicked, then the content is mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should open on click")
- Given an open Popover, when the trigger is clicked again, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Toggles open state on trigger click")
- Given an open Popover, when a click lands inside the content, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Closes when click outside content")
- Given an open Popover, when a click lands inside the content, then the content stays mounted and the `onInteractOutside` handler is not invoked. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should not close when clicking within bounds")
- Given an open Popover, when the dedicated close button is clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should close when the close button is clicked")
- Given an open Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 0`, when the trigger is hovered, then the content is mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should open on hover when openOnHover is true")
- Given a Popover with default props, when the trigger is hovered, then the content stays unmounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should not open on hover when openOnHover is false (default)")
- Given a Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 100`, when the trigger is hovered, then the content is absent immediately and appears within 200ms. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should respect openDelay before opening")
- Given a hover-opened Popover with `closeDelay: 0`, when the pointer moves to an outside element, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should close on hover out when no interaction")
- Given a hover-opened Popover with `closeDelay: 100`, when the pointer moves outside, then the content is still present immediately after leaving and is removed within 200ms. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should respect closeDelay before closing")
- Given a hover-opened Popover, when the pointer moves from the trigger onto the content, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should stay open when moving from trigger to content (grace area)")
- Given a hover-opened Popover with the pointer on the content, when the pointer moves back onto the trigger, then the content stays mounted without flicker. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should stay open when moving from content back to trigger")
- Given a hover-opened Popover with the pointer on the content, when the pointer moves to an outside element without any interaction, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should close when leaving content without interaction")
- Given a hover-opened Popover, when the trigger is clicked while hovered and the pointer then moves outside, then the content stays mounted because the open is now click-based. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should stay open after clicking trigger while hovering (converts to click-opened)")
- Given a hover-opened Popover, when text inside the content is clicked and the pointer then moves outside, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should stay open after clicking inside content (interaction)")
- Given a hover-opened Popover, when a button inside the content is focused and the pointer then moves outside, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should stay open after focusing interactive element inside content")
- Given a hover-opened Popover, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should close on escape even when hover-opened")
- Given a hover-opened Popover, when an outside element is clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should close on outside click even when hover-opened")
- Given a Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 300`, when the trigger is clicked, then the content is mounted immediately without waiting for the hover delay. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should still open via click when openOnHover is true")
- Given a Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 300`, when the trigger is focused and `Enter` is pressed, then the content is mounted immediately. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should still open via keyboard when openOnHover is true")
- Given a Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 200`, when the pointer leaves the trigger before the delay elapses, then the content is still absent 300ms later. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should cancel open timeout if pointer leaves before delay completes")
- Given a hover-opened Popover with `closeDelay: 200`, when the pointer leaves and re-enters the trigger before the delay elapses, then the content is still present 300ms later. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should cancel close timeout if pointer re-enters before delay completes")
- Given a hover-opened Popover converted to click-opened by one click, when a second click closes it, then the content stays absent 50ms later even though the pointer is still over the trigger. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should close on second click and not reopen immediately via hover")
