- Given a Popover closed by a second trigger click, when the pointer leaves the trigger and hovers it again, then the content reopens. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should allow hover reopen after leaving and re-entering trigger")
- Given a Popover closed by a second trigger click while the pointer is still in the hover cooldown, when the trigger is clicked a third time, then the content is mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover > should allow click to explicitly reopen while in cooldown")
- Given a force-mounted Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 0`, when the trigger is hovered, then the content text is mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should open on hover when openOnHover is true")
- Given a force-mounted Popover with default props, when the trigger is hovered, then the content text stays unmounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should not open on hover when openOnHover is false (default)")
- Given a force-mounted Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 100`, when the trigger is hovered, then the content text is absent immediately and appears within 200ms. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should respect openDelay before opening")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover with `closeDelay: 0`, when the pointer moves outside, then the content text is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should close on hover out when no interaction")
- Given a force-mounted Popover closed by hovering out, when the trigger is hovered a second time, then the content text is mounted again. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should reopen on second hover after closing via hover out (forceMount)")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover with `closeDelay: 100`, when the pointer moves outside, then the content text is still present immediately and removed within 200ms. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should respect closeDelay before closing")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover, when the pointer moves from the trigger onto the content, then the content text stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should stay open when moving from trigger to content (grace area)")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover with the pointer on the content, when the pointer moves back onto the trigger, then the content text stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should stay open when moving from content back to trigger")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover with the pointer on the content, when the pointer moves outside without interaction, then the content text is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should close when leaving content without interaction")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover, when the trigger is clicked and the pointer then moves outside, then the content text stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should stay open after clicking trigger while hovering (converts to click-opened)")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover, when the content is clicked and the pointer then moves outside, then the content text stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should stay open after clicking inside content (interaction)")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover, when a button inside the content is focused and the pointer then moves outside, then the content text stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should stay open after focusing interactive element inside content")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content text is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should close on escape even when hover-opened")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover, when an outside element is clicked, then the content text is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should close on outside click even when hover-opened")
- Given a force-mounted Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 300`, when the trigger is clicked, then the content text appears immediately. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should still open via click when openOnHover is true")
- Given a force-mounted Popover with `openOnHover: true` and `openDelay: 300`, when the trigger is focused and `Enter` is pressed, then the content text appears immediately. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should still open via keyboard when openOnHover is true")
- Given a force-mounted Popover with `openDelay: 200`, when the pointer leaves the trigger before the delay elapses, then the content text is still absent 300ms later. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should cancel open timeout if pointer leaves before delay completes")
- Given a force-mounted hover-opened Popover with `closeDelay: 200`, when the pointer leaves and re-enters the trigger, then the content text is still present 300ms later. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should cancel close timeout if pointer re-enters before delay completes")
- Given a force-mounted Popover closed by a second trigger click, when 50ms pass with the pointer still over the trigger, then the content text stays absent. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should close on second click and not reopen immediately via hover")
- Given a force-mounted Popover closed by a second trigger click, when the pointer leaves and re-enters the trigger, then the content text reappears. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should allow hover reopen after leaving and re-entering trigger")
- Given a force-mounted Popover closed by a second trigger click during hover cooldown, when the trigger is clicked a third time, then the content text reappears. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "openOnHover with forceMount > should allow click to explicitly reopen while in cooldown")

### Focus management
- Given an open Popover with `openFocus` returning the `#openFocus` element, when the popover opens, then that element holds focus. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Respects `openFocus` prop")
- Given an open Popover with `closeFocus` returning the `#closeFocus` element, when `Escape` closes it, then that element holds focus. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Respects `closeFocus` prop")
- Given an open Popover, when `open` is flipped to false from a button inside the content, then focus returns to the trigger. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Returns focus to trigger when manually setting `open` state to false")
- Given an open Popover with a `closeFocus` target, when `open` is flipped to false programmatically, then the `closeFocus` element holds focus rather than the trigger. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Respects the `closeFocus` prop when manually setting `open` state to false")
- Given an open Popover with `escapeBehavior: "ignore"`, when 10 `Tab` presses follow an `Escape`, then focus stays inside the content on every press. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Doesn't deactivate focus trap on escape provided `escapeBehavior` false")
- Given an open Popover with `closeOnOutsideClick: false`, when an outside element is clicked and then 10 `Tab` presses occur, then focus stays inside the content. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Doesn't deactivate focus trap on outside click provided `closeOnOutsideClick` false")
- Given an open Popover, when a button that stops click propagation is clicked and then 10 `Tab` presses occur, then the content stays visible and focus stays inside it. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Doesn't deactivate focus trap on outside click that is intercepted")
- Given three sibling Popovers, when each trigger is clicked in turn, then the previous content unmounts, the new content mounts, and the new content's close button receives focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should correctly handle focus when closing one popover by clicking another popover's trigger")
- Given a Popover with three triggers sharing one content, when each trigger opens it and `Escape` closes it, then focus returns to the specific trigger that opened it. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should restore focus to the trigger that opened the popover")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a Popover with `bind:open`, when the popover is opened the binding reads `true`, `Escape` sets it to `false`, and clicking the binding button reopens it to `true`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should allow binding the `open` prop")
- Given a force-mounted Popover overlay with `child` snippet, when open and then closed by `Escape`, then the child's `data-open` reads `true` then the child unmounts. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should pass open snippet prop to overlay child")
- Given a force-mounted Popover overlay rendered via `child`, when closed then opened, then the child's `data-open` goes from `"false"` to `"true"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should pass open snippet prop to overlay children")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given an open Popover, when an outside element is clicked, then `onInteractOutside` fires exactly once. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should close on outside click")
- Given an open Popover, when an outside element is clicked, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Closes when click outside content")
- Given an open Popover whose `onOutsideClick` calls `preventDefault`, when outside elements are clicked twice, then the content remains visible. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "doesnt close when preventDefault called in `onOutsideClick`")
- Given an open Popover with `interactOutsideBehavior: "ignore"`, when an outside element is clicked, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should allow ignoring the interactOutsideBehavior")
- Given an open Popover and a sibling Popover on the page, when the sibling trigger is clicked, then the first content becomes not visible and the sibling content becomes visible. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "closes popover when opening a sibling popover")
- Given a closed Popover with `withOverlay`, when rendered, then no overlay element exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should not render overlay when popover is closed")
- Given an open Popover with `withOverlay`, when rendered, then the overlay element exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should render overlay when popover is open")
- Given a closed Popover whose overlay has `forceMount: true`, when rendered, then the overlay element exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should forceMount overlay when forceMount is true")

### Positioning
- Given an open Popover with default portal settings, when rendered, then the content's floating wrapper is a direct child of `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should portal to the body by default")
- Given an open Popover with `portalProps.to: "#portal-target"`, when rendered, then the content's floating wrapper is a child of that target element. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should portal to a custom element if specified")
- Given an open Popover with `portalProps.disabled: true`, when rendered, then the content's floating wrapper stays inside the `main` element in the component tree. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should not portal if `disabled` is passed to the portal")
- Given an open Popover with an overlay and default portal, when rendered, then the overlay's parent is `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should portal overlay along with content by default")
- Given an open Popover with an overlay and `portalProps.to`, when rendered, then the overlay's parent is the custom portal target. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should portal overlay to custom element if specified")
- Given an open Popover anchored below its trigger with more than 180px of space beneath, when the page is smooth-scrolled 40px down and back up while the wrapper style is sampled, then `data-side` stays `"bottom"` for every sample and the trigger-to-wrapper gap drifts by at most 0.3px. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should stay stably anchored during tiny page scroll bursts when preventScroll is false")
- Given an open Popover whose trigger sits in a tab panel positioned beyond 100px from the viewport origin, when an outside tab click hides the trigger, then the content unmounts and the open binding reads `false` without the wrapper ever being visible at a position within 20px of the viewport top-left. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should close before content visibly jumps to viewport origin when outside interaction hides the trigger")

### Animation and presence
- Given a Popover whose content and overlay both use `forceMount`, when the trigger is clicked open, then both elements gain `data-starting-style` at some point, and when clicked closed both gain `data-ending-style`. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should apply transition attrs to content and overlay during open and close")
- Given a Popover content with `forceMount: true`, when rendered while closed, then the content element exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true")
- Given a Popover content with `forceMount: true` that also gates rendering on the `open` snippet prop, when closed the content is absent and after the trigger is clicked the content exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used to conditionally render the content")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a closed Popover, when axe runs over the mounted wrapper, then no violations are reported. (reka: packages/core/src/Popover/Popover.test.ts: "given default Popover > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a Popover opened by clicking the trigger, when axe runs over `document.body` with the `aria-dialog-name` rule disabled, then no violations are reported. (reka: packages/core/src/Popover/Popover.test.ts: "after opening popover > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a closed Popover, when axe runs over the render container, then no violations are reported. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "No accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given reka's Popover tests, when they run, then `globalThis.ResizeObserver` must be stubbed with no-op `observe`/`unobserve`/`disconnect` because jsdom lacks it, which is what the positioning layer depends on. (reka: packages/core/src/Popover/Popover.test.ts: "given default Popover")
- Given melt's `createPopover`, when destructured in the test fixture, then it yields `elements` (`trigger`, `content`, `arrow`, `close`) and `states.open`, and the fixture flips `open` via `open.update` to exercise programmatic close. (melt: src/tests/popover/Popover.spec.ts: "Returns focus to trigger when manually setting `open` state to false")
- Given bits' Popover tests, when a content locator is opened, then the suite waits on the global `bitsDismissableLayers` registry via `waitForDismissibleLayer` before asserting dismissal, so outside-click listeners are known to be attached. (bits: tests/src/tests/popover/popover.browser.test.ts: "should close on outside click")

## hover-card

### Roles and attributes
- Given an open HoverCard, when rendered, then the `trigger` and `content` elements each carry a `data-link-preview-<part>` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should have bits data attrs")
- Given a default HoverCard, when a touch `pointerup` is dispatched on the anchor trigger, then the trigger keeps `data-state="closed"` 100ms later. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "a touch tap on the trigger > should not open the hover card by default")
- Given a LinkPreview created with explicit `ids`, when rendered, then `trigger.id` is `id-trigger` and `content.id` is `id-content`. (melt: src/tests/link-preview/LinkPreview.spec.ts: "Custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given an open HoverCard with a `style` object on content, when rendered, then the content element's inline `background-color` is `rgb(255, 0, 0)`. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should apply custom style prop to content")

### Keyboard
- Given a HoverCard opened by hover and clicked, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/link-preview/LinkPreview.spec.ts: "Closes on escape")
- Given a HoverCard with `escapeBehavior: "ignore"`, when `Escape` is pressed after opening, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/link-preview/LinkPreview.spec.ts: "Respects the `escapeBehavior` prop")
- Given an open HoverCard, when the content is clicked and `Escape` is pressed, then the `onEscapeKeydown` handler fires exactly once. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should close on escape keydown")
- Given an open HoverCard with `escapeKeydownBehavior: "ignore"`, when the content is clicked and `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `escapeKeydownBehavior` prop")

### Pointer
- Given a LinkPreview with `openDelay: 0`, when the trigger is hovered, then the content becomes visible and stays visible after clicking it. (melt: src/tests/link-preview/LinkPreview.spec.ts: "Opens on hover")
- Given a closed HoverCard, when the trigger is hovered, then the content is mounted and stays mounted after being clicked. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should open on hover")
- Given an open LinkPreview, when the pointer hovers an element outside the trigger and content, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/link-preview/LinkPreview.spec.ts: "Closes when pointer moves outside")
- Given an open HoverCard, when the pointer hovers an outside element, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "closes when pointer moves outside the trigger and content")
- Given an open HoverCard, when the pointer hovers the content itself, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should stay open when hovering content")
- Given a HoverCard with `enableTouch: true`, when a touch `pointerup` is dispatched on the trigger, then `data-state` becomes `"open"`, and a second touch `pointerup` returns it to `"closed"`. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "given a HoverCard with enableTouch > should toggle open/closed on touch tap")
- Given a HoverCard with `enableTouch: true`, when a `pointerup` with `pointerType: "mouse"` is dispatched on the trigger, then `data-state` stays `"closed"`. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "given a HoverCard with enableTouch > should ignore non-touch pointers")
- Given a HoverCard with `enableTouch: true` and `openDelay: 100`, when the trigger is focused to schedule a delayed open, then touch-tapped open, then touch-tapped closed, then after 150ms the trigger still has `data-state="closed"` because the pending focus timer was cancelled. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "given a HoverCard with enableTouch > should not reopen from a pending focus timer after closing on touch")
- Given an open LinkPreview, when an outside element is clicked, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/link-preview/LinkPreview.spec.ts: "Closes on outside click by default") [skipped]

### Focus management
- Given a closed HoverCard, when the trigger element is focused programmatically the content is mounted, and when it is blurred the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should open on focus and close on blur")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given an open HoverCard with `interactOutsideBehavior: "ignore"` and `bind:open`, when the binding is read it is `true`, `Escape` sets it to `false` and unmounts the content, and clicking the binding button sets it back to `true` and remounts the content. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should respect binding the open prop")
- Given a force-mounted HoverCard gated on the `open` snippet prop, when the trigger is hovered the binding reads `true`, hovering outside sets it to `false` and unmounts content, and hovering the trigger again sets it back to `true`. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should reopen on hover after closing via hover out with forceMount")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given an open HoverCard with `interactOutsideBehavior: "ignore"`, when the content is clicked and then an outside element is clicked, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `interactOutsideBehavior` prop")

### Positioning
- Given an open HoverCard with default portal settings, when rendered, then the content's grandparent is `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should portal to the body by default")
- Given an open HoverCard with `portalProps.to: "#portal-target"`, when rendered, then the content's grandparent is that target element. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should portal to a custom element if specified")
- Given an open HoverCard with `portalProps.disabled: true`, when rendered, then the content's grandparent is the `main` element. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should not portal if `disabled` is passed as portal prop")

### Animation and presence
- Given a HoverCard content with `forceMount: true`, when rendered while closed, then the content element exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true")
- Given a force-mounted HoverCard, when the trigger is hovered the content gains `data-starting-style`, and when the pointer moves outside it gains `data-ending-style`. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should apply transition attrs to content during open and close")
- Given a HoverCard content with `forceMount: true` gated on the `open` snippet prop, when closed the content is absent and after hovering the trigger the content exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/link-preview/link-preview.browser.test.ts: "should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used to conditionally render the content")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a closed HoverCard, when axe runs over the mounted wrapper, then no violations are reported. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "given a default HoverCard > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a HoverCard with `openDelay: 100`, when `mouseenter` fires on the anchor trigger and 100ms pass, then axe over `document.body` reports no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "after mouse enter for a 100ms > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a closed LinkPreview, when axe runs over the render container, then no violations are reported. (melt: src/tests/link-preview/LinkPreview.spec.ts: "No accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given reka's HoverCard fixture, when mounted, then the trigger is an `<a href>` with `target="_blank"`, so the trigger role under test is a link rather than a button. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "given a default HoverCard")
- Given reka's HoverCard fixture, when the content is rendered with `as-child` inside a `<Transition>`, then the exit animation wrapper and the arrow with `:width="8"` are part of the tree axe scans. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "after mouse enter for a 100ms > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given reka's HoverCard tests, when they run, then `globalThis.ResizeObserver` is stubbed with no-ops in both describe blocks. (reka: packages/core/src/HoverCard/HoverCard.test.ts: "given a HoverCard with enableTouch")
- Given melt's `createLinkPreview`, when destructured, then it returns `elements` with `trigger`, `content`, and `arrow`, and the fixture forces `openDelay: 0` so hover opens are synchronous. (melt: src/tests/link-preview/LinkPreview.spec.ts: "Opens on hover")

## tooltip

### Roles and attributes
- Given an open Tooltip, when rendered, then the `trigger` and `content` elements each carry a `data-tooltip-<part>` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should have bits data attrs")
- Given an open Tooltip, when rendered, then the content has a non-empty `id` and the trigger's `aria-describedby` equals that id. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should render an id on the content and reference it via aria-describedby on the trigger")
- Given a Tooltip whose `Root` sets no delay but whose `Provider` sets `delayDuration={0}`, when rendered, then the trigger has `data-delay-duration="0"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should use provider delay duration if provided and the tooltip.root did not provide one")
- Given a Tooltip trigger with `tabindex: -1`, when rendered, then the trigger has `tabindex="-1"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should respect custom tabindex on trigger")
- Given a default Tooltip, when rendered, then the trigger has `tabindex="0"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should have default tabindex of 0 on trigger")
- Given an open Tooltip with a `style` object on content, when rendered, then the content element's inline `background-color` is `rgb(255, 0, 0)`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should apply custom style prop to content")
- Given a Tooltip opened by hover with default provider settings, when rendered, then the content element's inline `pointer-events` is `auto`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should have pointer-events: auto on content by default")
- Given a Tooltip whose provider sets `disableHoverableContent: true`, when opened, then the content element's inline `pointer-events` is `none`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should have pointer-events: none on content when disableHoverableContent is true")
- Given a Tooltip created with explicit `ids`, when rendered, then `trigger.id` is `id-trigger` and `content.id` is `id-content`. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "Applies custom ids when provided")
- Given a Tooltip inside a `TooltipProvider` with no `content` prop, when the trigger is focused, then the provider's `content` prop is `undefined` and the rendered markup contains `data-side="top"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "given tooltip within TooltipProvider > should use the provider content values")
- Given an open Tooltip, when the provider's `content` prop is set to `{ side: 'left' }`, then the provider's `content` prop equals that object and the rendered markup contains `data-side="left"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "given tooltip within TooltipProvider > should use the provider content values")
- Given a provider with `delayDuration: 150` and `skipDelayDuration: 500`, when the first trigger receives `pointerenter`, then that trigger's `data-state` is `"delayed-open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "provider: should not re-enable delay while switching between tooltips")
- Given a provider with `delayDuration: 150` and `skipDelayDuration: 500` and one tooltip already open, when a second trigger receives `pointerenter`, then within 80ms that trigger's `data-state` is `"instant-open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "provider: should not re-enable delay while switching between tooltips")
- Given a provider with `skipDelayDuration: 500` and a tooltip that has stayed open for 650ms, when the original trigger receives `pointerenter` and 180ms pass, then its `data-state` is `"instant-open"`, so the skip window does not re-arm the delay while a tooltip is open. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "provider: should not re-enable delay while switching between tooltips")
- Given a singleton Tooltip with `delayDuration: 50` and `skipDelayDuration: 300`, when the first trigger opens it the content has `data-state="delayed-open"` and after sliding to the second trigger the content has `data-state="instant-open"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should use instant-open state (no enter animation) when sliding between triggers within skipDelayDuration window")
- Given a singleton Tooltip with `delayDuration: 50` and `skipDelayDuration: 0`, when the first trigger opens it and the pointer slides to the second trigger, then the content has `data-state="delayed-open"` both times, so the enter animation replays. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should use delayed-open state (re-animate) when sliding between triggers with skipDelayDuration=0")
- Given a singleton Tooltip with two triggers, when the first is hovered then the second, then `aria-describedby` pointing at the content id is present only on the currently active trigger and absent on the other. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton edge: should keep aria-describedby only on active trigger")

### Keyboard
- Given a Tooltip opened by hover, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should close on escape keydown")
- Given a Tooltip with `escapeKeydownBehavior: "ignore"`, when the content is clicked and `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should allow ignoring escapeKeydownBehavior")

### Pointer
- Given a closed Tooltip, when the trigger is hovered, then the content is mounted and stays visible after being clicked. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should open on hover")
- Given a closed Tooltip with `openDelay: 0` and `closeDelay: 0`, when the trigger is hovered the content becomes visible, and when the pointer leaves the trigger it becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "It opens when hovered, and closes when left")
- Given an open Tooltip, when the pointer moves to an outside element, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should close when pointer moves outside the trigger and content")
- Given an open Tooltip, when the pointer hovers the content, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should stay open when hovering content")
- Given a Tooltip whose provider sets `disableHoverableContent: true`, when the pointer moves from the trigger to an outside element, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should close when hovering content with disableHoverableContent: true")
- Given a Tooltip opened by hover, when the trigger is left-clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should close when the trigger is clicked")
- Given a Tooltip opened by hover, when the trigger is right-clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should close when the trigger is right clicked")
- Given a Tooltip opened by hover, when a `pointerdown` with `button: 1` is dispatched on the trigger, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should close when the trigger is middle clicked")
- Given a Tooltip with `disableCloseOnTriggerClick: true`, when a `pointerdown` with `button: 2` is dispatched on the trigger, then the content stays visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should not close on non-primary button press when `disableCloseOnTriggerClick` is true")
- Given a Tooltip with `delayDuration: 300` whose trigger is offset by margin, when `pointerenter` starts the delay and a `pointerdown` with `button: 2` follows, then the content is still absent 500ms later because the pending delayed open was cancelled. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should cancel a pending delayed open when the trigger is right clicked")
- Given an open Tooltip, when a `scroll` event bubbles from the `main` element that contains the trigger, then the content is removed while the trigger stays visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should close on scroll when the scrolled target contains the trigger")
- Given an open Tooltip, when a `scroll` event fires on `document`, then the content becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "When tooltip is open and the user scrolls outside the content, it closes")
- Given an open Tooltip whose content is clicked, when a `scroll` event fires on the content element, then the content is still visible 50ms later. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "When the tooltip is open and the user scrolls inside the content, it stays open")
- Given an open Tooltip on a page where a rail element sits between the trigger and content, when the pointer hovers the rail on the way to the content, then the content stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should stay open when moving through an intermediate element toward content")
- Given a tethered singleton Tooltip freshly opened by hovering the top trigger, when a `pointerleave` is dispatched at the trigger's bottom edge with the floating wrapper as `relatedTarget`, then the content stays mounted and the open binding reads `true`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should stay open on first hover when pointer moves through gap between trigger and content")
- Given a tether with two sibling triggers in a shared card, when the left trigger emits `pointerleave` toward the card, a document `pointermove` lands in the gap, and the right trigger is then hovered, then the content stays mounted, the payload reads `Right`, the open binding reads `true`, and `data-state` never passes through `"closed"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "tether: should stay open when moving across a sibling-trigger gap")
- Given a tether with two sibling triggers, when the left trigger emits `pointerleave` and the right trigger emits `pointerenter` with the shared card as `relatedTarget`, then one animation frame later the content is still mounted, the payload reads `Right`, and the open binding reads `true`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "tether: should not close on frame after sibling handoff via shared container")
- Given a tether with two sibling triggers, when the left trigger emits `pointerleave` and a document `pointermove` idles in the gap for 260ms, then the content is removed and the open binding reads `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "tether: should close when pointer idles in the sibling gap")

### Focus management
- Given a closed Tooltip, when the trigger is focused, then `document.body.innerHTML` contains the content text `Add to library`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "should open when focus")
- Given a Tooltip, when `document.body` is focused instead of the trigger, then the content text `Add to library` is not present. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "after focusing out > should close the tooltip")
- Given a closed Tooltip, when the trigger element is focused the content is mounted, and when it is blurred the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should open on focus and close on blur")
- Given a closed Tooltip, when the trigger is focused the content becomes visible, and when blurred it becomes not visible. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "It opens when focused, and closes when blurred")
- Given a Tooltip opened by focusing the trigger, when the pointer hovers and then unhovers the trigger, then the content stays visible, and only blurring the trigger closes it. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "When the tooltip was opened by focusing, leaving the trigger does not close it")
- Given a Tooltip opened by hovering the trigger, when the trigger is focused and then blurred, then the content stays visible, and only unhovering the trigger closes it. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "When the tooltip was opened by pointer, blurring the trigger does not close it")
- Given a Tooltip opened by dispatching a `focus` event on the trigger, when the content is clicked, then the content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "When focusing the trigger, you should be able to click the content")
- Given a tethered singleton Tooltip with detached triggers, when the top trigger is focused the payload reads `Top` and the trigger binding reads `trigger-top`, when the bottom trigger is focused they read `Bottom` and `trigger-bottom`, and when it is blurred the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should work with detached triggers through tether")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a Tooltip with `bind:open`, when opened by hover the binding reads `true`, `Escape` sets it to `false` and unmounts content, and clicking the binding button sets it to `true` and remounts content. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should respect binding the open prop")
- Given a disabled Tooltip, when the trigger is focused, then the content text `Add to library` is not present. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "disabled tooltip > should not be open when focus")
- Given an open Tooltip, when a `TOOLTIP_OPEN` `CustomEvent` is dispatched on `document`, then the content text `Add to library` is removed, so one open tooltip closes another via the document broadcast. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "should close when another tooltip broadcasts that it opened")
- Given two Tooltips both with `group: true` and open stores `true`/`false`, when the second store is set to `true`, then the first store becomes `false` and the second stays `true`. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "2 tooltips, group=true > When a tooltip opens, the other closes")
- Given two Tooltips with `group: true` both rendered with `open` already `true`, when rendered, then the first store is `false` and the second is `true`. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "2 tooltips, group=true > When both are rendered with open=true, the first closes")
- Given two Tooltips in different groups `A` and `B`, when the second opens, then both stores read `true`. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "2 tooltips, different groups > When a tooltip opens, the other stays open")
- Given two Tooltips with `group: false`, when the second opens, then both stores read `true`. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "2 tooltips, group=false > When a tooltip opens, the other stays open")
- Given two Tooltips with `group: undefined`, when the second opens, then both stores read `true`. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "2 tooltips, group=undefined > When a tooltip opens, the other stays open")
- Given a single Tooltip with `group: true`, when its open store is set to `false` then back to `true`, then the store reads `true`, so group coordination does not close the tooltip against itself. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "Single tooltip, group=true > Tooltip does not prevent itself from opening")
- Given a singleton Tooltip with two triggers, when the first trigger is hovered the payload reads `Bold` and the trigger binding reads `trigger-1`, when the second is hovered they read `Italic` and `trigger-2`, and hovering outside removes the content. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should open with either trigger and update payload")
- Given a singleton Tooltip, when the pointer switches from the first trigger to the second, then `page.getByTestId("content").element()` is the identical DOM node as before and the payload reads `Italic`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should reuse the same content node while switching triggers")
- Given a tethered singleton Tooltip, when the imperative open buttons for top and bottom are clicked in turn the payload and trigger binding follow, and when the tether close button is clicked the content is removed and the open binding reads `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should support imperative tether open/close")
- Given a controlled singleton Tooltip, when programmatic buttons switch the active trigger, then the payload reads `One` then `Two`, setting the trigger to null makes the trigger binding read `null`, and clicking close removes the content with the open binding at `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: controlled mode should support programmatic trigger changes")
- Given a singleton Tooltip open from the first trigger, when that trigger is unmounted, then the content is removed, the open binding reads `false`, and the trigger binding reads `null`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton edge: should close when active trigger unmounts")
- Given a singleton Tooltip open from the first trigger, when the second trigger is made disabled and then hovered, then the content is removed and the open binding reads `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton edge: disabled trigger interaction should close open content")
- Given a tethered singleton Tooltip open from the top trigger, when a detached disabled trigger is hovered, then the content is removed and the open binding reads `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should close when hovering a detached disabled trigger")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given a trigger that is both a Tooltip trigger and a Popover trigger, when it is hovered the tooltip content appears, and when it is clicked the popover content appears and the tooltip content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should open when composed with another floating trigger")

### Positioning
- Given an open Tooltip with default portal settings, when rendered, then the content's floating wrapper is a child of `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should portal to the body by default")
- Given an open Tooltip with `portalProps.to: "#portal-target"`, when rendered, then the content's floating wrapper is a child of that target. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should portal to a custom element if specified")
- Given an open Tooltip with `portalProps.disabled: true`, when rendered, then the content's floating wrapper stays inside the `main` element. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should not portal if `disabled` is passed to the portal")
- Given a singleton Tooltip whose content has `customAnchor` toggled on, when the second trigger is hovered, then the content's left edge is within 20px of the custom anchor's left edge and differs from the left edge measured without the custom anchor. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton edge: customAnchor should override active trigger anchoring")
- Given a Tooltip fixture that accepts a `customAnchor` element, when the trigger is hovered, then the content is mounted and the `customAnchor` prop type-checks against `Tooltip.Content`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should use the custom anchor element when `customAnchor` is provided")

### Animation and presence
- Given a Tooltip content with `forceMount: true`, when rendered while closed, then the content is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true")
- Given a force-mounted Tooltip, when the trigger is hovered the content gains `data-starting-style`, and when the pointer moves outside it gains `data-ending-style`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should apply transition attrs to content during open and close")
- Given a force-mounted Tooltip gated on the `open` snippet prop, when closed the content is absent and after hovering the trigger the content exists and is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used to conditionally render the content")
- Given a force-mounted Tooltip gated on `open`, when the trigger is hovered the binding reads `true` and the content mounts, and when the pointer moves outside the binding reads `false` and the content unmounts. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should open and close correctly with forceMount + open check")
- Given a force-mounted Tooltip with no open check, when the trigger is hovered and then left, then the content element stays visible the whole time while the open binding toggles `false` to `true` to `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should keep open state behavior when forceMount keeps content mounted")
- Given a force-mounted Tooltip gated on `open`, when the trigger is hovered and left twice in sequence, then the content mounts and unmounts each cycle with the binding following `true`/`false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should close on trigger leave after reopening with forceMount")
- Given a singleton Tooltip with the default `skipDelayDuration`, when the pointer slides from the first trigger to the second while `data-state` mutations are recorded, then the recorded history never contains `"closed"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should not transition through closed state when moving directly between sibling triggers (skipDelayDuration > 0)")
- Given a singleton Tooltip with `delayDuration: 50` and `skipDelayDuration: 0`, when the pointer slides from the first trigger to the second, then the recorded `data-state` history does contain `"closed"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton: should transition through closed state when moving between triggers with skipDelayDuration=0")
- Given a force-mounted singleton Tooltip, when the first trigger is hovered the payload reads `Alpha` and the open binding `true`, when the second is hovered they become `Beta` and `trigger-2`, and hovering outside sets the open binding to `false` while the content node stays mounted. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton forceMount: should keep mounted content and update payload")
- Given a force-mounted singleton Tooltip gated on `open`, when the first trigger is hovered the content node mounts with payload `Alpha`, and hovering outside unmounts it. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "singleton forceMount: should support open-check conditional rendering")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a closed Tooltip, when axe runs over the mounted wrapper and again over `document.body` after the trigger is focused, then no violations are reported in either pass. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "given default Tooltip > should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given 80 Tooltip instances rendered at once, when `window.addEventListener` calls are counted, then exactly one `scroll` listener is registered, so the scroll-to-close handler is shared rather than per instance. (bits: tests/src/tests/tooltip/tooltip.browser.test.ts: "should not add a scroll listener per tooltip instance")
- Given reka's Tooltip provider test, when mounting, then the `teleport` component is stubbed to a plain `<div><slot /></div>` so the portalled content is findable inside the wrapper markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "given tooltip within TooltipProvider > should use the provider content values")
- Given reka's Tooltip fixture, when mounted, then open state is driven by `v-model:open` on `TooltipRoot` and the content sets `:side-offset="5"` with animation classes keyed on `data-[state=delayed-open]` and `data-[side=*]`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tooltip/Tooltip.test.ts: "should open when focus")
- Given melt's `createTooltip`, when destructured, then it returns `elements` (`trigger`, `content`) plus `options`, and the fixture writes `options.group.set(group)` reactively to retest group membership. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "2 tooltips, group=true > When a tooltip opens, the other closes")
- Given melt's Tooltip fixture, when created, then it forces `openDelay: 0`, `closeDelay: 0`, and `closeOnPointerDown: false`, so the delay machinery is deliberately out of scope for these tests. (melt: src/tests/tooltip/Tooltip.spec.ts: "It opens when hovered, and closes when left")

## toast

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `Toast` opened from its trigger, when the toast appears, then the `li` wrapping the toast text has `tabindex="0"`, so the visible toast is focusable. (reka: packages/core/src/Toast/Toast.test.ts: "should have visible toast that is focusable")
- Given an open toast with a title and description, when two animation frames have passed, then a `[role="alert"][aria-live]` live region exists whose text contains `Scheduled: Catch up` and contains none of the characters `[`, `]`, or `"`, guarding against Vue JSON-stringifying the `announceTextContent` array. (reka: packages/core/src/Toast/Toast.test.ts: "should announce title and description as plain text (not JSON)")

### Keyboard
- Given an open toast, when Escape is pressed on the active element, then the toast content is removed from the document. (reka: packages/core/src/Toast/Toast.test.ts: "when pressing escape > should close the content")

### Pointer
- Given a default `Toast`, when the trigger is clicked, then the close button's markup is present in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/Toast/Toast.test.ts: "after clicking the trigger > should open the content")
- Given an open toast, when the close button is clicked, then the close button's markup is gone from the document. (reka: packages/core/src/Toast/Toast.test.ts: "when clicking close button > should close the content")

### Animation and presence
- Given an open toast that registered pause and resume listeners on the shared `ol` viewport, when the toast is dismissed, then `removeEventListener` is called with both the viewport pause and the viewport resume event names, so the detached toast and its listeners can be collected. (reka: packages/core/src/Toast/Toast.test.ts: "should remove viewport event listeners when the toast is dismissed")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given the document before any toast is open and again after the trigger is clicked, when audited with axe both times, then there are no violations in either state. (reka: packages/core/src/Toast/Toast.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

## menu

### Roles and attributes
- Given a Menu rendered from four `MenuGroup` blocks, when rendered, then four elements expose `role="group"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a default Menu > should have all the groups")
- Given the first group of a default Menu, when queried, then it contains five elements with `role="menuitem"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a default Menu > should render item in group")
- Given a default Menu, when the first `menuitem` receives DOM focus, then the markup around that item contains `data-highlighted`. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a default Menu > after focusing on item > should have highlighted state")
- Given a Menu containing a `MenuSub`, when rendered, then the sub trigger is one of the `menuitem` elements and carries `aria-haspopup="menu"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a Menu with submenu > should highlight sub trigger on pointermove")
- Given an open submenu, when the submenu content is rendered, then it is an element matching `[role="menu"][aria-labelledby]`. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a Menu with submenu > should keep the submenu open when the pointer moves within its focused trigger")
- Given an open dropdown menu, when the parts are inspected, then `Group` has `role="group"`, `Separator` has `role="separator"`, and `GroupHeading` has no `role` attribute at all. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should not expose the group heading and separator as groups")
- Given an open dropdown menu with a group heading, when the group is inspected, then its `aria-labelledby` equals the heading element's `id`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should not expose the group heading and separator as groups")
- Given an open context menu, when the parts are inspected, then `Group` has `role="group"`, `Separator` has `role="separator"`, and `GroupHeading` has no `role` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should have bits data attrs")
- Given a checkbox group whose `value` is `["1"]`, when the menu opens, then the first checkbox group item has `aria-checked="true"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `value` prop on CheckboxGroup")
- Given a checkbox group whose `value` is `["1"]`, when the context menu opens, then the first checkbox group item has `aria-checked="true"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `value` prop on CheckboxGroup")
- Given a closed submenu after the pointer moved away, when a sibling item is hovered, then that item has the `data-highlighted` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should close submenu when pointer intent changes away from submenu")
- Given a closed submenu after the pointer moved away, when a sibling item is hovered in a context menu, then that item has the `data-highlighted` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should close submenu when pointer intent changes away from submenu")
- Given an open menu with a disabled item, when the disabled item is rendered, then it is marked `data-disabled` by the fixture and is never focusable by arrow navigation. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Focus when opened with click")

### Keyboard
- Given a menu opened by click, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the first item receives focus. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Focus when opened with click")
- Given focus on the first item, when `ArrowDown` is pressed again, then the disabled second item is skipped and the first checkbox item receives focus. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Focus when opened with click")
- Given a `forceVisible` menu opened by click, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the first item receives focus, and a second `ArrowDown` skips the disabled item and focuses the first checkbox item. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > Focus when opened with click")
- Given a `forceVisible` menu opened with `Enter`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the disabled item is skipped and the first checkbox item receives focus. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > Doesnt focus disabled menu items") [skipped]
- Given an open menu with the pointer hovering the first item, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the hovered item loses focus and the first checkbox item gains focus. - Given an open menu with the pointer hovering the first checkbox item, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then the hovered item loses focus and the first item gains focus. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Pressing arrow keys while hovering over item goes to next/prev item")
- Given a `forceVisible` open menu with the pointer hovering the first item, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then focus moves from the hovered item to the first checkbox item. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > Pressing arrow keys while hovering over item goes to next/prev item")
- Given a `forceVisible` open menu with the pointer hovering the first checkbox item, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then focus moves from the hovered item to the first item. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > Pressing arrow keys while hovering over item goes to next/prev item")
- Given an open context menu with the pointer hovering the first item, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then focus moves from the hovered item to the first checkbox item. - Given an open context menu with the pointer hovering the first checkbox item, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then focus moves from the hovered item to the first item. - Given an open context menu, when `ArrowDown` is pressed twice from the first item, then the disabled second item is skipped and the first checkbox item receives focus. (melt: src/tests/context-menu/ContextMenu.spec.ts: "Context Menu > Focus when opened")
- Given an open submenu reached by hovering the sub trigger, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the first submenu item receives focus. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Arrow right when subtrigger hover focuses first item in submenu")
- Given focus on the first submenu item, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then the second submenu item receives focus. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Arrow right when subtrigger hover focuses first item in submenu")
- Given focus inside an open submenu, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then the submenu becomes not visible and focus returns to the sub trigger. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Arrow right when subtrigger hover focuses first item in submenu")
- Given a `forceVisible` submenu opened by hover, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the first submenu item receives focus and a following `ArrowDown` focuses the second submenu item. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > Arrow right when subtrigger hover focuses first item in submenu")
- Given focus inside a `forceVisible` submenu with the pointer over the second submenu item, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then focus returns to the sub trigger. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > Arrow right when subtrigger hover focuses first item in submenu")
- Given an open context menu submenu reached by hover, when `ArrowRight` is pressed then `ArrowDown`, then the first submenu item takes focus and then the second submenu item takes focus. (melt: src/tests/context-menu/ContextMenu.spec.ts: "Context Menu > Arrow right when subtrigger hover focuses first item in submenu")
- Given `loop: true` and an open menu, when `ArrowDown` is pressed past the last item, then focus wraps to the first item, and `ArrowUp` from the first item wraps to the last item (the sub trigger). - Given the default (`loop` unset) and an open menu, when `ArrowDown` is pressed on the last item, then focus stays on the last item (the sub trigger) and does not wrap to the first item; `ArrowUp` from the first item likewise keeps focus on the first item. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > does not loop through items when loop prop false/undefined")
- Given a menu opened with the keyboard and focus moved to the sub trigger, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the sub content is rendered and the first sub item has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should open submenu with keyboard on subtrigger")
- Given an open context menu with focus on the sub trigger, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then the sub content is rendered and the first sub item has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should open submenu with keyboard on subtrigger")
- Given a menu opened with the keyboard, when `ArrowDown` walks the items, then the two disabled items are never focused and focus lands on the checkbox item instead. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should skip over disabled items when navigating with the keyboard")
- Given an open context menu, when `ArrowDown` walks the items, then the two disabled items are never focused and focus lands on the checkbox item. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should skip disabled items when navigating with the keyboard")
- Given content with `loop: false`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed past the last focusable item, then focus does not return to the first item. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should not loop through the menu items when the `loop` prop is set to false/undefined")
- Given content with `loop: true`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed past the last focusable item, then focus wraps around to the first item. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should loop through the menu items when the `loop` prop is set to true")
- Given context menu content with `loop: false`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed past the last item, then focus does not return to the first item. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should not loop through the menu items when the `loop` prop is set to false")
- Given context menu content with `loop: true`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed past the last item, then focus wraps back to the first item. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should loop through the menu items when the `loop` prop is set to true")
- Given `ArrowDown` navigation through an open context menu with `loop: true`, when each press is observed, then the visit order is item, sub trigger, checkbox item, item 2, radio item, radio item 2, checkbox group item 1, checkbox group item 2. - Given an open force-mounted context menu, when `Tab` is pressed, then the content is removed and the next tabbable element receives focus. ### Pointer
- Given a Menu with a submenu, when a `pointermove` with `pointerType: "mouse"` is dispatched on the sub trigger, then the sub trigger gains the `data-highlighted` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a Menu with submenu > should highlight sub trigger on pointermove")
- Given a `pointermove` on the sub trigger, when it is handled, then the sub trigger also receives DOM focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a Menu with submenu > should keep the submenu open when the pointer moves within its focused trigger")
- Given a sub trigger hovered for 100ms of fake timers, when the timers advance, then `aria-expanded` on the sub trigger becomes `"true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a Menu with submenu > should keep the submenu open when the pointer moves within its focused trigger")
- Given an already open submenu whose trigger is focused, when another `pointermove` fires on that same trigger, then `aria-expanded` stays `"true"` and the submenu content remains in the DOM. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a Menu with submenu > should keep the submenu open when the pointer moves within its focused trigger")
- Given an open menu, when the sub trigger is hovered, then the submenu becomes visible and the sub trigger has focus. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Hovering over subtrigger opens submenu")
- Given an open `forceVisible` menu, when the sub trigger is hovered, then the submenu is rendered, becomes visible, and the sub trigger has focus. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > Hovering over subtrigger opens submenu")
- Given an open context menu, when the sub trigger is hovered, then the submenu is rendered and the sub trigger has focus. (melt: src/tests/context-menu/ContextMenu.spec.ts: "Context Menu > Hovering over subtrigger opens submenu")
- Given an open submenu with `openDelay: 0`, when `pointerleave` fires on the sub trigger toward the submenu (coordinates measured from the real trigger and content rects) followed by a document `pointermove` at the midpoint between trigger and content, then the sub content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should keep submenu open while pointer is moving toward it")
- Given an open submenu with `openDelay: 0`, when `pointerleave` fires at the midpoint toward the submenu and then a document `pointermove` lands 8px beyond the submenu edge away from it, then the sub content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should close submenu when pointer intent changes away from submenu")
- Given an open context menu submenu with `openDelay: 0`, when `pointerleave` toward the submenu is followed by a `pointermove` at the midpoint between trigger and content, then the sub content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should keep submenu open while pointer is moving toward it")
- Given an open context menu submenu with `openDelay: 0`, when the pointer moves to coordinates outside the grace area away from the submenu, then the sub content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should close submenu when pointer intent changes away from submenu")
- Given an open menu, when the sub trigger is clicked, then the sub content is rendered. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `onSelect` prop on SubTrigger")
- Given an open menu with a sub trigger `onSelect` handler, when the sub trigger is clicked, then `onSelect` is called. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `onSelect` prop on SubTrigger")
- Given an open context menu with a sub trigger `onSelect` handler, when the sub trigger is clicked, then `onSelect` is called. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `onSelect` prop on SubTrigger")
- Given an open menu in a scroll-padded page, when one item is hovered and then a second item is hovered, then `HTMLElement.focus` is called with `{ preventScroll: true }` on both items and on the content element, and `window.scrollY` is unchanged. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should call `focus` with `preventScroll: true` on hover and item-leave so `scroll-padding` does not scroll the page")

### Focus management
- Given a default Menu, when the first item is focused and then clicked, then a single `select` event is emitted. (reka: packages/core/src/Menu/Menu.test.ts: "given a default Menu > after selecting the item > should emit select")
- Given content whose `onOpenAutoFocus` calls `preventDefault`, when the menu is opened with the keyboard, then the first item does not have focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should allow preventing autofocusing first item with `onOpenAutoFocus`  prop")

(bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `onOpenAutoFocus` prop")
- Given content whose `onCloseAutoFocus` prevents default and focuses a custom element, when `Escape` closes the context menu, then the custom override element has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `onCloseAutoFocus` prop")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given an open menu, when the first `menuitem` is clicked, then the `[role="menu"]` element is removed from the DOM. (reka: packages/core/src/DropdownMenu/DropdownMenu.test.ts: "given default DropdownMenu > after opening the dropdown > after selecting the first item > should close the modal")
- Given an open menu, when the first `menuitem` is clicked, then exactly one `select` event is emitted. (reka: packages/core/src/DropdownMenu/DropdownMenu.test.ts: "given default DropdownMenu > after opening the dropdown > after selecting the first item > should emit select event")

- Given a sub item with `closeOnSelect: false`, when it is clicked, then the sub content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `closeOnSelect=false` prop on the sub item")
- Given an open menu, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should close the menu on escape")
- Given content with `escapeKeydownBehavior: "ignore"`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `escapeKeydownBehavior` prop")
- Given an open context menu, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should close the menu on escape")
- Given context menu content with `escapeKeydownBehavior: "ignore"`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `escapeKeydownBehavior: 'ignore'` prop")
- Given content with `interactOutsideBehavior: "ignore"`, when an outside element is force-clicked, then the content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `interactOutsideBehavior` prop - ignore")
- Given content with `interactOutsideBehavior: "close"`, when an outside element is force-clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `interactOutsideBehavior` prop - close")
- Given context menu content with `interactOutsideBehavior: "ignore"`, when a `pointerdown` is dispatched on `document.body`, then the content stays in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `interactOutsideBehavior: 'ignore'` prop")
- Given `escapeBehavior: "ignore"` and an open menu, when `Escape` is pressed, then the menu remains visible and arrow navigation still works. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > respects `escapeBehavior` prop")
- Given `closeOnOutsideClick: false` and an open menu, when an element outside the menu is clicked, then the menu remains visible. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > respects close on outside click prop")
- Given an `onOutsideClick` handler that calls `preventDefault`, when an element outside the menu is clicked, then the menu remains visible. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Doesn't close on outsideClick if defaultPrevented in onOutsideClick")
- Given an open context menu, when an element outside it is clicked, then the menu is removed from the DOM. (melt: src/tests/context-menu/ContextMenu.spec.ts: "Context Menu > Should close on outside click by default")
- Given an open context menu, when `Escape` is pressed, then the menu is removed from the DOM. (melt: src/tests/context-menu/ContextMenu.spec.ts: "Context Menu > Should close on escape")
- Given a context menu with `escapeBehavior: "ignore"`, when `Escape` is pressed, then the menu remains visible and arrow navigation still works. (melt: src/tests/context-menu/ContextMenu.spec.ts: "Context Menu > respects `escapeBehavior` prop")
- Given a context menu with `closeOnOutsideClick: false`, when an outside element is clicked, then the menu remains visible. (melt: src/tests/context-menu/ContextMenu.spec.ts: "Context Menu > respects close on outside click prop")
- Given a context menu whose `onOutsideClick` calls `preventDefault`, when an outside element is clicked, then the menu remains visible. (melt: src/tests/context-menu/ContextMenu.spec.ts: "Context Menu > Doesn't close on outsideClick if defaultPrevented in onOutsideClick")

### Positioning
- Given no `portal` prop, when the menu opens, then the content wrapper's parent is `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should portal to the body if a `portal` prop is not passed")
- Given `portalProps.to: "#portal-target"`, when the menu opens, then the content wrapper's parent is the portal target element. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should portal to the portal target if a valid `portal` prop is passed")
- Given `portalProps.disabled: true`, when the menu opens, then the content wrapper's parent is the original in-tree container and not `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should not portal if `disabled` is passed to the portal")
- Given no `to` prop on the context menu portal, when the menu opens, then the content wrapper's parent is `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should portal to the body if a `to` prop is not passed to the Portal")
- Given `to: "#portal-target"` on the context menu portal, when the menu opens, then the content wrapper's parent is the portal target element. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should portal to the portal target if a valid `to` prop is passed to the portal")
- Given a disabled context menu portal, when the menu opens, then the content wrapper's parent is the original container and not `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should not portal if portal is disabled")
- Given a menu with an arrow element, when the menu is opened by clicking the trigger, then the arrow is visible. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (Default) > Opens when trigger is clicked")
- Given a `forceVisible` menu with an arrow element, when the menu is opened by clicking the trigger, then the arrow is visible. (melt: src/tests/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.spec.ts: "Dropdown Menu (forceVisible) > Opens when trigger is clicked")
- Given `contentProps.style` with `backgroundColor: "rgb(255, 0, 0)"`, when the menu opens, then the content element's inline `style.backgroundColor` is `rgb(255, 0, 0)`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should apply custom style prop to content")
- Given context menu `contentProps.style` with `backgroundColor: "rgb(255, 0, 0)"`, when the menu opens, then the content element's inline `style.backgroundColor` is `rgb(255, 0, 0)`. (bits: tests/src/tests/context-menu/context-menu.browser.test.ts: "should apply custom style prop to content")

### Animation and presence
- Given `forceMount` content, when the component renders without the menu being opened, then the content already exists in the DOM. (bits: tests/src/tests/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu.browser.test.ts: "should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true")
