### Focus management
- Given a closed Select, when the trigger receives a bare `click` with no preceding `pointerdown`, then `trigger.focus()` is called. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "trigger mouse interop > should focus the trigger on click without a preceding pointerdown")
- Given a Select already opened by `pointerdown`, when the follow-up `click` fires on the trigger, then `trigger.focus()` is not called again. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "trigger mouse interop > should not re-focus the trigger on click after opening via pointerdown")
- Given a Select opened with a full mouse click sequence of `pointerdown`, `mousedown`, `mouseup` and `click`, when the content is shown, then `document.activeElement` is not the trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "trigger mouse interop > should not leave focus on the trigger after opening via mouse click")
- Given a Melt select opened by trigger click, when the menu is visible, then the trigger still has focus. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "Closes on escape keydown")
- Given an open Select, when `Escape` closes it, then focus returns to the trigger. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should allow navigating after navigating to the bottom, closing, and reopening the menu")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a single-value Select, when an option is selected by pointer, then the content closes and no `role="group"` remains in the tree. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given default Select > after selecting a value > should close the modal")
- Given a `multiple` Select, when an option is selected by pointer, then the `role="group"` content remains in the tree, so the popup stays open. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select with multiple props > after selecting a value > should close the modal")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `Banana` selected, when a second option is selected, then the value box contains both `Banana` and `Blueberry`. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select with multiple props > after selecting another value > should show value correctly")
- Given a `multiple` Select with two options selected, when the second selection completes, then the content is still mounted. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select with multiple props > after selecting another value > should not close the modal")
- Given a Select with object options, when `banana` is selected, then the content closes and no `role="group"` remains. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select with object type > should close the modal")
- Given a Melt select created with `defaultSelected` of `Chocolate`, when rendered, then the trigger text is `Chocolate`. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "Shows correct label when defaultValue is provided")
- Given a Melt select, when the `selected` store is set imperatively to `{ value: 'Chocolate', label: 'Chocolate' }`, then the trigger text becomes `Chocolate`. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "Manually setting the value updates the label")
- Given a Melt select whose option list is mutated to add `Vanilla` and the `selected` store is then set to it, when the DOM settles, then the trigger text becomes `Vanilla`. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "Updating options and setting the value updates the label")
- Given an open Melt select in `multiple` mode, when a second option is clicked, then the menu stays visible and the trigger text becomes `Caramel, Chocolate`. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "Selects multiple items when `multiple` is true")
- Given an open Select with `bind:open`, when `Escape` closes it, then the bound readout is `false`, and clicking the binding button sets it to `true` and remounts the content. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should respect binding the `open` prop")
- Given an open `multiple` Select with `bind:open`, when `Escape` closes it, then the bound readout is `false`, and clicking the binding button reopens the content. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should respect binding the `open` prop")
- Given a Select with `value: "1"`, when the value binding button resets the value, then the bound readout becomes empty. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should respect binding the `value` prop")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `value: ["1", "2"]`, when the value binding button clears the array, then the bound readout goes from `1,2` to empty. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should respect binding the `value` prop")
- Given a Select with `value: "2"`, when opened, then the `2-indicator` exists, the trigger text is `B`, the hidden input value is `2`, and that item is selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should select a default item when provided")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `value: ["2"]`, when opened, then the `2-indicator` exists, the trigger text is `B`, the hidden input value is `2`, and that item is selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should select a default item when provided")
- Given a `Select.Value` `child` snippet in single mode, when rendered with no value, then `selection.type` is `single`, `selection.selected` is absent so the value reads `none`, the label falls back to the placeholder `Pick a theme`, and `disabled` is `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - value > should expose child snippet props in single mode and update when setValue is called")
- Given a `Select.Value` `child` snippet in single mode, when `selection.setValue("2")` is called, then the exposed value is `2`, the exposed label is `B`, the hidden input value is `2`, and reopening shows item `2` selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - value > should expose child snippet props in single mode and update when setValue is called")
- Given a `Select.Value` `children` snippet in multiple mode, when rendered with no value, then `selection.type` is `multiple`, the values read `none`, the label falls back to the placeholder `Pick themes`, and `disabled` is `false`. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - value > should expose children snippet props in multiple mode and update when setValue is called")
- Given a `Select.Value` `children` snippet in multiple mode, when `selection.setValue(["1", "3"])` is called, then the values read `1,3`, the label reads `A, C`, two hidden inputs hold `1` and `3`, and reopening shows both items selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - value > should expose children snippet props in multiple mode and update when setValue is called")
- Given a disabled Select whose `Select.Value` `child` snippet guards on the exposed `disabled` flag, when the set-value button is clicked, then `disabled` reads `true`, the selection stays `none` with the placeholder label, and the hidden input value stays empty. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - value > should pass disabled state to value snippets so consumers can block setValue")

### Forms
- Given a Select with `name="test"` rendered in a form, when inspected, then a native `select` element exists in the DOM as the hidden form control. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select in a form > should have hidden input field")
- Given a Select with `name="test"` and `nullable-value="null"` and a nullish value, when inspected, then the first `option` of the hidden `select` has value `null`. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "should use the nullableValue for the hidden select when the value is nullish")
- Given a Select in a form with `Banana` selected, when the form is submitted, then the submit handler runs once and the collected form data is `{ test: 'Banana' }`. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select in a form > after selecting option and clicking submit button > should trigger submit once")
- Given the same form Select reselected to `Pineapple`, when the form is submitted again, then the handler has run twice and the second submission is `{ test: 'Pineapple' }`. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select in a form > after selecting other option and click submit button again > should trigger submit once")
- Given a Select with a non-empty `name` prop, when rendered, then a hidden `input[name="test"]` is in the document. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should render an input if the `name` prop is passed")
- Given a Select with `name: ""`, when rendered, then no hidden input is in the document. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should not render an input if the `name` prop isn't passed or is an empty string/undefined")
- Given a Select with `value: "test"`, when rendered, then the hidden input's value is `test`. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should sync the value prop to the hidden input")
- Given a Select with `required: true`, when rendered, then the hidden input has the `required` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should sync the required prop to the hidden input")
- Given a Select with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the hidden input has the `disabled` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should sync the disabled prop to the hidden input")
- Given a Select with `autocomplete: "one-time-code"`, when rendered, then the hidden input has `autocomplete="one-time-code"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should forward the `autocomplete` prop to the hidden input")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `value: ["a", "b"]`, when rendered, then two hidden inputs exist and both carry `name="test"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should render a hidden input for each value in the `value` array, each with the same `name` prop")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `value: ["a", "b"]`, when rendered, then the two hidden inputs hold values `a` and `b`. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should sync the value prop to the hidden inputs")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `required: true` and two values, when rendered, then every hidden input has the `required` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should sync the required prop to the hidden inputs")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `disabled: true` and two values, when rendered, then every hidden input has the `disabled` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should sync the disabled prop to the hidden inputs")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `name="themes"` and nothing selected, when the form is submitted, then the form data for `themes` is a single-entry array holding an empty string. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should submit an array with a single empty string when the user submits the form without selecting any items")
- Given a `multiple` Select whose `name` is not `themes` and nothing selected, when the form is submitted, then the form data for `themes` is empty. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should not submit an array with a single empty string when the `name` prop is passed but no items are selected")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given a Melt select created with `closeOnOutsideClick: false`, when an element outside the menu is clicked, then the menu stays visible. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "Respects the `closeOnOutsideClick` prop")
- Given a Melt select whose `onOutsideClick` calls `preventDefault`, when an element outside the menu is clicked, then the menu stays visible. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "doesn't close when preventDefault called in `onOutsideClick`")
- Given an open Select, when an element outside the content is clicked, then the content unmounts. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should close on outside click")
- Given an open `multiple` Select, when an element outside the content is clicked, then the content unmounts. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should close on outside click")

### Positioning
- Given a Select with default portal props, when opened, then the content's grandparent element is `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should portal to the body by default")
- Given a Select with `portalProps: { to: "#portal-target" }`, when opened, then the content's grandparent is the custom portal target element. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should portal to a custom element if specified")
- Given a Select with `portalProps: { disabled: true }`, when opened, then the content's grandparent is the in-tree `main` element. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should not portal if `disabled` is passed as portal prop")
- Given a `multiple` Select with default portal props, when opened, then the content's grandparent element is `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should portal to the body by default")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `portalProps: { to: "#portal-target" }`, when opened, then the content's grandparent is the custom portal target. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should portal to a custom element if specified")
- Given a `multiple` Select with `portalProps: { disabled: true }`, when opened, then the content's grandparent is the in-tree `form` element. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should not portal if `disabled` is passed as portal prop")
- Given a Select whose `Select.Viewport` has no padding, when opened, then the first item has `data-highlighted` and the second item does not. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should highlight the first item when Select.Viewport has no padding")
- Given a page scrolled to y 640 holding a 120-item Select with value `90` and `preventScroll={false}`, when the trigger is clicked to open, then the window scroll position drifts by at most 1 pixel over 30 frames. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should not scroll the page when opening on trigger click")
- Given an open 60-item Select with overlaid scroll buttons scrolled to the bottom so the scroll down button unmounts, when a small upward wheel scroll remounts the button, then the viewport's `scrollTop` stays within 20 pixels of the user's position instead of snapping back to the highlighted first item. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should keep the user's scroll position when the scroll down button remounts")
- Given a 60-item Select with `value: "55"`, when opened, then the selected item's bounding rect lies fully inside the viewport's bounding rect. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should still scroll the selected item into view when opening")

### Animation and presence
- Given a force-mounted Select content observed for transition attributes, when the trigger is clicked, then `data-starting-style` appears at some point in the mutation history, and after an outside click `data-ending-style` appears. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should apply transition attrs to content during open and close")
- Given a Select content with `forceMount` and no `open` guard, when rendered closed, then the content is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true")
- Given a Select content with `forceMount` whose `child` snippet gates on `props.open`, when rendered closed, then no content exists, and clicking the trigger makes it exist. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - single > should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used to conditionally render the content")
- Given an open Select that is then closed, when the whole `SelectRoot` is unmounted while the delayed presence timers are still pending, then `clearTimeout` is called and the pending timer count drops below the count observed right after closing. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given SelectContent cleanup > should clear delayed presence updates when unmounted after closing")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a closed default Select, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given default Select > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given an open default Select, when audited with axe with the `aria-required-children` rule disabled, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given default Select > opening the modal > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a closed `multiple` Select, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select with multiple props > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given an open `multiple` Select, when audited with axe with the `aria-required-children` rule disabled, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select with multiple props > opening the modal > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a rendered Melt select, when audited with `jest-axe`, then there are no violations. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "No accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a Melt select, when a disabled option is present, then the assertion that a disabled select cannot be opened is declared but not implemented. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "Disabled select cannot be opened") [skipped]
- Given a Melt select, when the `loop` prop is set, then the assertion that options loop is declared but not implemented. (melt: src/tests/select/Select.spec.ts: "Options loop when loop prop is set") [skipped]
- Given the reka Select tests, when an option is activated, then two `pointerup` events are required because `SelectContentImpl` suppresses the first one as an accidental pointerup after opening. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given default Select > after selecting a value")
- Given the reka Select content cleanup suite, when it runs, then it installs `vi.useFakeTimers()` in `beforeEach` and restores real timers in `afterEach`, and the assertions read `vi.getTimerCount()` directly, so the behavior is timing dependent. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given SelectContent cleanup")
- Given the reka Select test environment, when the suite boots, then `releasePointerCapture`, `hasPointerCapture` and a stub `ResizeObserver` are installed on the globals because jsdom lacks them. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "beforeAll")
- Given the reka Select story fixture, when it renders, then the content uses `position="popper"` with `:side-offset="5"` and is portalled to a sibling `#here` element, and the item list is wrapped in `SelectViewport`, `SelectLabel`, `SelectGroup` and `SelectSeparator`. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given default Select")
- Given the reka Select story fixture, when options are passed as `{ label, value }` objects, then the same `SelectItem` markup handles object values through the default equality comparison. (reka: packages/core/src/Select/Select.test.ts: "given Select with object type")
- Given the bits `select - multiple` loop test, when it runs, then it calls `openSingle` rather than `openMultiple`, so it exercises single-mode looping under a multiple-mode test name. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "select - multiple > should navigate through the items using the keyboard (loop = true)")
- Given the bits select helpers, when an item has an empty-string or null value, then its test id is generated as `empty` so the empty-value item can be addressed. (bits: tests/src/tests/helpers/select.ts: "getTestId")
- Given a bits Select opened in a test, when the content mounts, then the test waits for the content node to appear in the global `bitsDismissableLayers` registry before interacting, so dismissal listeners are attached first. (bits: tests/src/tests/select/select.browser.test.ts: "openSingle / openMultiple")

## listbox

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default Listbox, when rendered, then `ListboxContent` is `role="listbox"` and each `ListboxItem` is `role="option"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given default Listbox")
- Given a default Listbox whose content just received focus, when the first item is inspected, then it has `data-highlighted=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when focus on content > should have highlighted state on first item")
- Given a focused Listbox, when the third item is clicked, then it has `aria-selected="true"` and `data-state="checked"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when focus on content > should highlight and select item when clicked")
- Given a focused Listbox, when `Enter` selects the highlighted first item, then it keeps `data-highlighted=""` and gains `aria-selected="true"` and `data-state="checked"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "after pressing `Enter` > should select the highlighted item")
- Given a Listbox whose first item is selected, when `Enter` is pressed again, then that item keeps `data-highlighted=""` but reads `aria-selected="false"` and `data-state="unchecked"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "after pressing `Enter` > should deselect after pressing `Enter`")
- Given a Listbox with the first item selected, when `ArrowDown` twice then `Enter` moves selection, then the first item reads `aria-selected="false"` with `data-state="unchecked"` and the third reads `aria-selected="true"` with `data-state="checked"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "after selecting other item and press `Enter` > should select the third item")
- Given a `ListboxRoot` with `highlightOnHover: true`, when an item receives `pointermove` with `pointerType: 'mouse'`, then that item gains `data-highlighted=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a Listbox with hover highlighting > emits the highlighted item without querying the collection")
- Given a `ListboxItem` with a reactive `disabled` prop starting `false`, when `disabled` becomes `true`, then the item gains both `data-disabled=""` and `disabled=""`, and turning it back off removes both. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given ListboxItem with reactive `disabled` prop > should update DOM attributes when `disabled` toggles without highlight/selection change")
- Given a `ListboxItem` with a fallthrough `data-testid` of `option-a`, when the bound value changes to `option-b`, then the rendered `data-testid` becomes `option-b`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given ListboxItem with reactive fallthrough attrs > should update DOM attributes when an attr changes without highlight/selection change")
- Given a `ListboxItem` whose fallthrough attribute key changes from `data-variant-a` to `data-variant-b` while the value stays `same`, when rendered again, then `data-variant-a` is gone and `data-variant-b` is `same`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "should update DOM attributes when an attr key changes while its value stays the same")
- Given a virtualized Listbox of three options where filtering leaves only the last, when the row at `data-index="0"` survives, then its text is `default`, its `data-testid` is `option-default`, and its `aria-setsize` is `1`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "should re-render a surviving virtualizer row when filtering shrinks the options")
- Given a horizontal Listbox with `orientation: 'horizontal'` whose content just received focus, when the first item is inspected, then it has `data-highlighted=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > when focus on content > should have highlighted state on first item")
- Given a horizontal Listbox, when the third item is clicked, then it has `aria-selected="true"` and `data-state="checked"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > should highlight and select item when clicked")
- Given a horizontal Listbox, when `Enter` selects the highlighted first item, then it keeps `data-highlighted=""` and reads `aria-selected="true"` with `data-state="checked"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > after pressing `Enter` > should select the highlighted item")
- Given a horizontal Listbox with the first item selected, when `Enter` is pressed again, then that item reads `aria-selected="false"` with `data-state="unchecked"` while keeping `data-highlighted=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > should deselect after pressing `Enter`")

### Keyboard
- Given a focused Listbox with the first item highlighted, when `Enter` is pressed, then that item becomes selected. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "after pressing `Enter` > should select the highlighted item")
- Given a focused Listbox, when `ArrowDown` is pressed twice, then highlight moves from the first item to the third. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "after selecting other item and press `Enter` > should select the third item")
- Given a focused Listbox, when the letter `b` is typed on the content, then `document.activeElement` is the first item whose text starts with `B`, so typeahead moves focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when typing letter > should highlight text starting with B")
- Given a focused `multiple` Listbox with `selectionBehavior: 'toggle'`, when `Enter` and `ArrowDown` are interleaved to toggle items 0, 1, 2 and 4, then items 0, 1, 2 and 4 read `aria-selected="true"` and item 3 reads `aria-selected="false"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given multiple `true` Listbox > should select multiple items")
- Given a `multiple` Listbox with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'` and item 0 selected, when `Shift` plus `ArrowDown` is pressed, then items 0 and 1 read `aria-selected="true"` and item 2 reads `aria-selected="false"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when keypress Shift + ArrowDown > should select the next item")
- Given a `multiple` Listbox with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'` and item 0 selected, when `Shift` plus `ArrowDown` is pressed eleven times, then items 0 through 10 all read `aria-selected="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when keypress Shift + ArrowDown > should select more items")
- Given a horizontal Listbox with item 0 selected, when `ArrowRight` is pressed twice and then `Enter`, then selection moves to the third item, so horizontal orientation uses the left and right arrows. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > after selecting other item and press `Enter` > should select the third item")

### Pointer
- Given a focused Listbox, when an item is clicked, then it becomes both highlighted and selected. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when focus on content > should highlight and select item when clicked")
- Given a `ListboxRoot` with `highlightOnHover: true`, when each item receives `pointermove`, then the last `highlight` payload is `{ ref: <item element>, value: <item text> }` and the content's `querySelectorAll` is never called. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a Listbox with hover highlighting > emits the highlighted item without querying the collection")
- Given a `ListboxRoot` with `highlightOnHover: true` and an item already highlighted, when the same item receives `pointermove` again, then no additional `highlight` event is emitted and `querySelectorAll` is still not called. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a Listbox with hover highlighting > emits the highlighted item without querying the collection")
- Given a Listbox with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'`, when the same item is clicked twice, then it is not toggled off and focus stays on it. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when selection behavior `replace` > should not toggle off the selected value")
- Given a Listbox with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'`, when a second item is clicked after the first, then focus moves to the second item, so the selection is replaced rather than extended. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when selection behavior `replace` > should select and replace another item")
- Given a `multiple` Listbox switched to `selectionBehavior: 'replace'` with item 0 clicked, when item 0 is clicked again, then it is not toggled off and focus stays on it. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given multiple `true` Listbox > when selection behavior `replace` > should not toggle off the selected value")
- Given a `multiple` Listbox with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'` and item 0 selected, when item 1 is clicked, then focus moves to item 1. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given multiple `true` Listbox > when selection behavior `replace` > should select and replace another item")

### Focus management
- Given a default Listbox, when the `role="listbox"` content receives `focus`, then `document.activeElement` becomes the first item. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when focus on content > should pass the focus to the first item")
- Given a freshly mounted Listbox, when the immediate highlight watcher settles, then the first item has `data-highlighted=""` but `scrollIntoView` was never called and `document.activeElement` is not that item. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a Listbox on initial mount > should highlight the first item without scrolling the page or stealing focus")
- Given a freshly mounted Listbox, when the content receives `focus`, then the first item becomes `document.activeElement` and `scrollIntoView` is called. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a Listbox on initial mount > should focus and scroll once the user interacts")
- Given a virtualized `multiple` Listbox of 100 options freshly mounted, when the highlight cycle settles, then the first rendered item has `data-highlighted=""` while `scrollIntoView` was never called and it is not `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a virtualized Listbox on initial mount > should highlight the first item without scrolling the page or stealing focus")
- Given a virtualized Listbox mounted with `modelValue` equal to option 3 by structural comparison, when the highlight cycle settles, then the row at `data-index="3"` has `data-highlighted=""`, the row at `data-index="0"` has none, `scrollIntoView` was never called, and the checked row is not `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a virtualized Listbox on initial mount > should highlight a pre-selected item on mount without scrolling the page or stealing focus")
- Given a virtualized `multiple` Listbox, when the content receives `focus`, then the first item becomes `document.activeElement` and `scrollIntoView` is called. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a virtualized Listbox on initial mount > should focus and scroll the first item when the user enters the listbox")
- Given a horizontal Listbox, when the content receives `focus`, then `document.activeElement` becomes the first item. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > when focus on content > should pass the focus to the first item")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a default Listbox, when the content receives `focus`, then a `highlight` event is emitted with a truthy payload. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "when focus on content > should emit `highlight` event")
- Given a focused Listbox, when `Enter` selects the first item, then `update:modelValue` is emitted with that item's text. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "after pressing `Enter` > should emit `update:modelValue` event")
- Given a `multiple` Listbox with `selectionBehavior: 'toggle'`, when `Enter`, `ArrowDown`, `Enter`, `ArrowUp` and `Enter` are pressed, then `update:modelValue` emits `[item0]`, then `[item0, item1]`, then `[item1]`, so the third press toggles item 0 back off. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given multiple `true` Listbox > should emit `update:modelValue` event")
- Given a `multiple` Listbox switched to `selectionBehavior: 'replace'` with item 0 already clicked, when `Enter`, `ArrowDown` and `Enter` are pressed, then `update:modelValue` emits `[item0]`, `[item0]` again, then `[item1]`, and the duplicate second emission is flagged in the test as a known bug. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given multiple `true` Listbox > when selection behavior `replace` > should emit `update:modelValue` event")
- Given a horizontal Listbox, when the content receives `focus`, then a `highlight` event is emitted with a truthy payload. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > when focus on content > should emit `highlight` event")
- Given a horizontal Listbox, when `Enter` selects the first item, then `update:modelValue` is emitted with that item's text. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > after pressing `Enter` > should emit `update:modelValue` event")

### Forms
- Given a Listbox with `name="test"` and `default-value="Afghanistan"` inside a form, when rendered, then an `input[data-hidden]` element exists. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given Listbox in a form > should have hidden input field")
- Given a Listbox in a form with its default value selected, when the form is submitted, then the handler runs once and the collected data is `{ test: <first item text> }`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given Listbox in a form > after selecting option and clicking submit button > should trigger submit once")
- Given the same form Listbox with the fifth option clicked, when the form is submitted again, then the handler has run twice and the second submission is `{ test: <fifth item text> }`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given Listbox in a form > after selecting other option and click submit button again > should trigger submit once")

### RTL and i18n
- Given a `ListboxFilter` on a non-Android user agent, when a plain-text composition fires `compositionstart`, `compositionupdate` with `xiang` and `input`, then no `update:modelValue` is emitted during the preedit. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "should not update modelValue during plain-text composition off Android (desktop Pinyin preedit)")
- Given a `ListboxFilter` on an Android user agent, when a plain-text autocorrect composition fires `compositionupdate` with `Br` and `input`, then `update:modelValue` is emitted live with `Br`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "should update modelValue live during plain-text (autocorrect) composition on Android")
- Given a `ListboxFilter` on an Android user agent, when a CJK IME composition fires `compositionupdate` with `かんじ` and `input`, then nothing is emitted until `compositionend`, at which point `update:modelValue` is emitted once with `かんじ`. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "should not update modelValue during CJK IME composition on Android until compositionend")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default Listbox, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given default Listbox > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a horizontal Listbox, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given horizontal Listbox > should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given the reka Listbox test environment, when the suites boot, then `releasePointerCapture`, `hasPointerCapture` and `scrollIntoView` are stubbed on `HTMLElement.prototype` because jsdom lacks them, and `scrollIntoView` is re-spied per suite to assert scroll behavior. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given default Listbox")
- Given the reka Listbox story fixture, when it renders, then `ListboxContent` carries `aria-label="options"` and the first 50 entries of a country list are rendered as items, with `data-highlighted`, `data-state=checked` and `data-disabled` driving the visual states. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given default Listbox")
- Given a virtualized Listbox under jsdom, when mounted, then `getBoundingClientRect` must be stubbed to a non-zero 200 by 200 rect and `scrollTo` plus `ResizeObserver` must be stubbed, otherwise `@tanstack/virtual-core` renders no rows. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a virtualized Listbox on initial mount")
- Given a virtualized Listbox with a pre-selected value, when the mount highlight runs, then the checked row is brought into the internal scroll container through `scrollToIndex` and made the roving-tabindex target without a document-level scroll. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a virtualized Listbox on initial mount > should highlight a pre-selected item on mount without scrolling the page or stealing focus")
- Given the reka virtualized Listbox tests, when they await settling, then they must flush watcher, `nextTick`, `requestAnimationFrame` and a further `nextTick` in sequence, so these assertions are timing dependent. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given a virtualized Listbox on initial mount > flush")
- Given `ListboxItem` uses `v-memo`, when only `disabled` or a fallthrough attribute changes without a highlight or selection change, then the memo must still invalidate, which is the regression guarded for reka issues 2644 and 2904. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given ListboxItem with reactive `disabled` prop")
- Given the reka Listbox suite, when read, then a `TODO` comment notes that selecting the first item when a `ListboxFilter` is present is not yet asserted. (reka: packages/core/src/Listbox/Listbox.test.ts: "given default Listbox") [skipped]

- Given a Combobox where an option was selected and the popup reopened, when that option is inspected, then it has `data-state="checked"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "given default Combobox > opening the popup > after selecting a value > after opening the modal again > should focus on the selected value")
- Given a Combobox where an option was selected and the popup reopened, when that option's markup is inspected, then it contains an `svg` rendered inside `ComboboxItemIndicator`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "given default Combobox > opening the popup > after selecting a value > after opening the modal again > should render the icon")
- Given a Combobox with `multiple`, when the trigger is clicked, then the popup markup contains the option text `Apple`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "given a Combobox with multiple prop > opening the popup > should show the popup content")

- Given a Combobox created with an `ids` object, when rendered, then the input id is `id-trigger`, the menu id is `id-menu`, and the label id is `id-label`. (melt: src/tests/combobox/Combobox.spec.ts: "Combobox > Applies custom ids when provided")

### Forms
- Given a Combobox inside a form, when rendered, then an `input[data-hidden]` element exists. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "given combobox in a form > should have hidden input field")

(reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "given combobox in a form > after selecting other option and click submit button again > should trigger submit once")

- Given a Combobox with `name: ""`, when rendered, then no hidden input is in the document. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - single > should not render an input if the `name` prop isn't passed or is an empty string/undefined")
- Given a Combobox with `value: "test"`, when rendered, then the hidden input value is `test`. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - single > should sync the value prop to the hidden input")
- Given a Combobox with `required: true`, when rendered, then the hidden input has the `required` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - single > should sync the required prop to the hidden input")
- Given a Combobox with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the hidden input has the `disabled` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - single > should sync the disabled prop to the hidden input")
- Given a multiple Combobox with a `name` prop and no selected value, when rendered, then zero hidden inputs exist. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - multiple > should not render a hidden input if the `name` prop is passed and a value is not selected")
- Given a multiple Combobox with `value: ["a", "b"]`, when rendered, then two hidden inputs exist and both carry `name="test"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - multiple > should render a hidden input for each value in the `value` array, each with the same `name` prop")
- Given a multiple Combobox with `value: ["a", "b"]`, when rendered, then the hidden input values are `a` and `b` in order. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - multiple > should sync the value prop to the hidden inputs")
- Given a multiple Combobox with `required: true` and two values, when rendered, then every hidden input has the `required` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - multiple > should sync the required prop to the hidden inputs")
- Given a multiple Combobox with `disabled: true` and two values, when rendered, then every hidden input has the `disabled` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - multiple > should sync the disabled prop to the hidden inputs")
- Given a multiple Combobox with `name: "themes"` and nothing selected, when the submit button is clicked, then `FormData.getAll("themes")` has length 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - multiple > should submit an empty array when the user submits the form without selecting any items")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given an open Combobox, when an outside element is clicked, then the menu becomes not visible. [skipped] (melt: src/tests/combobox/Combobox.spec.ts: "Combobox (forceVisible) > Closes on outside click by default")
- Given an open `forceVisible` Combobox, when `Escape` is pressed, then the menu element unmounts. (melt: src/tests/combobox/Combobox.spec.ts: "Combobox (forceVisible) > Closes on escape by default")

- Given the `closeOnOutsideClick` prop, when an outside click occurs, then the prop decides whether the menu closes. [skipped] (melt: src/tests/combobox/Combobox.spec.ts: "Combobox > Respects the `closeOnOutsideClick` prop")
- Given an open Combobox, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - single > should close on escape keydown")
- Given an open Combobox, when an outside element is clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - single > should close on outside click")
- Given an open multiple Combobox, when `Escape` is pressed, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - multiple > should close on escape keydown")
- Given an open multiple Combobox, when an outside element is clicked, then the content is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - multiple > should close on outside click")

### Positioning
- Given a popper Combobox with 60 options, when the trigger is clicked and the stubbed `ResizeObserver` fires twice, then the content default slot has rendered 3 times, and after one macrotask it has rendered 4 times rather than once per position update. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "comboboxContent with popper positioning > does not rerender option slot content after popper position updates")
- Given an open popper Combobox listing `Option 0` through `Option 59`, when `Option 59` is typed into the input, then the text contains `Option 59` and no longer contains `Option 1`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "comboboxContent with popper positioning > updates visible options when filtering while popper content is open")
- Given a popper Combobox opened by the trigger with no input, when the highlighted option is focused, then it is focused with `{ preventScroll: true }` and never with no argument, no `scrollIntoView` runs before `placed`, and exactly one `scrollIntoView` runs after `placed`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > prevents trigger-only option focus from scrolling before placement")
- Given a popper Combobox filtered by typing `a`, when `placed` is emitted twice, then `scrollIntoView` is called exactly once and on the highlighted element. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > defers the opening highlight scroll until placement and handles repeated placement idempotently")
- Given a virtualized popper Combobox mounted open with the fourth option selected, when `placed` is emitted, then an option carries `data-highlighted` and `scrollIntoView` is never called. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > does not flush the virtualizer mount highlight after placement")
- Given a virtualized popper Combobox, when the exposed `highlightSelected` is called with a `keydown` event, then the highlighted option is focused with `{ preventScroll: true }`, no scroll happens before `placed`, and one `scrollIntoView` runs after `placed`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > prevents virtualized option focus from scrolling before placement")
- Given a popper Combobox whose portal content was replaced by a second instance and the first unmounted, when the input is filtered to `b`, then the highlight is `Beta`, no scroll happens before `placed`, and one `scrollIntoView` runs after `placed`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > ignores an outgoing content unmount after replacement content mounts")
- Given a popper Combobox opened with zero items and already `placed`, when items are added by a prop change, then the highlight becomes `Beta` and `scrollIntoView` runs exactly once. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > resumes normal highlight scrolling when options mount after placement")
- Given a popper Combobox with `forceMount` content that is placed while closed, when the trigger is later clicked to open it, then `scrollIntoView` runs exactly once and not before opening. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > tracks force-mounted content that is placed while closed")
- Given a popper Combobox whose content unmounted after a selection, when the input is filtered to `b` and the content remounts, then no scroll happens until `placed` and then `scrollIntoView` runs once on the `Beta` element. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > suppresses highlight scrolling again when content remounts")
- Given a Combobox with `position="inline"` content, when the input is filtered to `a`, then the highlight is `Alpha` and `scrollIntoView` is called immediately with `{ block: 'nearest' }`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "combobox highlight scrolling with popper positioning > leaves inline Combobox highlight scrolling immediate")

### Animation and presence
- Given a Combobox with `forceMount` on the content, when rendered without opening, then the content is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - single > should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true")
- Given a Combobox with `forceMount` whose `child` snippet gates on `props.open`, when rendered, then the content is absent, and after the trigger is clicked it is present. (bits: tests/src/tests/combobox/combobox.browser.test.ts: "combobox - single > should forceMount the content when `forceMount` is true and the `open` snippet prop is used to conditionally render the content")

### RTL and i18n
- Given a Combobox mid IME composition, when `input` fires with the value `xiang`, then no `role="listbox"` element exists. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "handle IME composition > should not update filter during IME composition")
- Given a Combobox mid IME composition with the value `zzzzz`, when `compositionend` fires, then the `role="listbox"` element exists and carries `data-empty`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "handle IME composition > should update filter after composition ends")
- Given a non-Android user agent and a `compositionupdate` carrying plain-text preedit `xiang`, when `input` fires, then no `role="listbox"` element exists. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "handle IME composition > should not update filter during plain-text composition off Android (desktop Pinyin preedit)")
- Given an Android user agent and a `compositionupdate` carrying plain-text `zzzzz`, when `input` fires, then the `role="listbox"` element exists with `data-empty`, so the filter updates live during autocorrect composition. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "handle IME composition > on Android soft keyboard > should update filter live during plain-text (autocorrect) composition")
- Given an Android user agent and a `compositionupdate` carrying CJK text `かんじ`, when `input` fires, then no `role="listbox"` exists until `compositionend`, after which the listbox exists with `data-empty`. (reka: packages/core/src/Combobox/Combobox.test.ts: "handle IME composition > on Android soft keyboard > should not update filter during CJK IME composition until compositionend")

- Given an open Autocomplete with `resetSearchTermOnBlur: true` and the typed text `Testing`, when `Escape` is pressed, then after 50ms the input value is still `Testing` because the typed text is the model value and reset only clears internal filter state. ### Pointer

- Given an open Autocomplete, when the second option is clicked, then the `role="group"` element no longer exists. (reka: packages/core/src/Autocomplete/Autocomplete.test.ts: "given default Autocomplete > opening the popup > after selecting a value > should close the popup")
- Given an Autocomplete where `Banana` was selected, when the trigger is clicked to reopen the popup, then the input still shows `Banana`. (reka: packages/core/src/Autocomplete/Autocomplete.test.ts: "given default Autocomplete > opening the popup > after selecting a value > after opening the popup again > should still show the selected text in the input")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given an open Autocomplete, when `Custom text` is typed into the input, then the last `update:modelValue` payload is `Custom text`, so typing writes the model value directly. ### Forms

- Given a non-Android user agent and a `compositionupdate` carrying plain-text preedit `xiang`, when `input` fires, then the content has no `data-empty` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/Autocomplete/Autocomplete.test.ts: "given default Autocomplete > opening the popup > handle IME composition > should not filter during plain-text composition off Android (desktop Pinyin preedit)")
- Given an Android user agent and a `compositionupdate` carrying plain-text `zzzzz`, when `input` fires, then the content has `data-empty` and the last `update:modelValue` payload is `zzzzz`. (reka: packages/core/src/Autocomplete/Autocomplete.test.ts: "given default Autocomplete > opening the popup > handle IME composition > on Android soft keyboard > should filter and update modelValue live during plain-text (autocorrect) composition")
- Given an Android user agent and a `compositionupdate` carrying CJK text `かんじ`, when `input` fires, then the content has no `data-empty` and no new `update:modelValue` is emitted, and after `compositionend` the content has `data-empty` and the last payload is `かんじ`. ### Accessibility tooling

- Given an open Autocomplete with the `aria-required-children` rule disabled, when axe runs, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Autocomplete/Autocomplete.test.ts: "given default Autocomplete > opening the popup > should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given an `_Autocomplete.vue` fixture with `AutocompleteEmpty`, three `AutocompleteGroup`s (Fruits, Vegetables, Chinese) and an `AutocompleteSeparator`, when items are filtered to nothing, then the empty state and `data-empty` come from the primitive's own filtering rather than a consumer-derived list, unlike Combobox in bits. - Given an Autocomplete where typing sets the model value directly, when text is typed and the popup closed, then the input keeps the typed text instead of snapping back to a selected option label, which is the behavioral split from `ComboboxRoot`. (reka: packages/core/src/Autocomplete/Autocomplete.test.ts: "given default Autocomplete > opening the popup > typing free-form text > should keep the typed text after closing")

## command

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default Command with two groups of items, when rendered, then the first item `Introduction` has the `data-selected` attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should select the first item by default")
- Given a Command with `value: "Introduction"`, when rendered, then `Introduction` has `data-selected`. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should allow forcing the selected value")
- Given a Command with `value: "Radio Group"` (an item in the second group), when rendered, then `Radio Group` has `data-selected` and `Introduction` does not. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should respect initial value when it's not the first item")
- Given a Command with `value: "Styling"` (the last item of the first group), when rendered, then `Styling` has `data-selected` and `Introduction` does not. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should respect initial value for items in the first group")
- Given a default grid Command with `columns={3}`, when rendered, then `Introduction` has `data-selected`. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should select the first item by default")
- Given a grid Command with `value: "Introduction"`, when rendered, then `Introduction` has `data-selected`. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should allow forcing the selected value")

### Keyboard
- Given a default Command, when `d` is typed into the input, then the input value is `d`, `Delegation` has `data-selected`, and it is the first child of the first group's items container. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should restore original order when search is cleared")
- Given a Command filtered by `d`, when `Backspace` clears the input, then the input value is the empty string, `Introduction` has `data-selected`, and it is the first child of the first group's items container again. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should restore original order when search is cleared")
- Given a grid Command, when `d` is typed into the input, then `Delegation` has `data-selected` and is the first child of the first group's items container. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should restore original order when search is cleared")
- Given a grid Command filtered by `d`, when `Backspace` clears the input, then `Introduction` has `data-selected` and is the first child of the first group's items container. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should restore original order when search is cleared")
- Given a grid Command with `columns={3}` and `Introduction` selected, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then `Calendar` (same column, next row) becomes selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should navigate to the correct column in the next row")
- Given a grid Command with `Calendar` selected, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then `Introduction` becomes selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should navigate to the correct column in the next row")
- Given a grid Command with `Introduction` selected, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then `Delegation` (the next column in the same row) becomes selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should navigate to the correct column in the next row")
- Given a grid Command with `Delegation` selected in column 2, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then `Radio Group` (column 2 of the next row) becomes selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should navigate to the correct column in the next row")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a default Command with an empty search, when the separator is inspected, then it exists, and after `a` is typed into the input it is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should render the separator when search is empty and remove it when search is not empty")
- Given a Command whose separator has `forceMount: true`, when `a` is typed into the input, then the separator still exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should always render the separator when forceMount")
- Given a default Command, when no search is entered, then the empty state element is absent, and after typing `zzzzzzzz` into the focused input it exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should show empty state when no items are found")
- Given a default Command, when `radio` is typed into the input, then the first group is not visible, the second group is visible, and `Radio Group` has `data-selected`. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should hide the group if all items are filtered out")
- Given a grid Command with an empty search, when the separator is inspected, then it exists, and after `a` is typed into the input it is removed. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should render the separator when search is empty and remove it when search is not empty")
- Given a grid Command whose separator has `forceMount: true`, when `a` is typed into the input, then the separator still exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should always render the separator when forceMount")
- Given a grid Command, when `zzzzzzzz` is typed into the focused input, then the empty state element exists, having been absent before. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should show empty state when no items are found")
- Given a grid Command, when `radio` is typed into the input, then the first group is not visible, the second group is visible, and `Radio Group` has `data-selected`. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-grid.browser.test.ts: "should hide the group if all items are filtered out")

### Positioning
- Given a Command whose viewport is capped at 150px with 40px items and `value: "Popover"` (the last item), when rendered and 150ms elapse, then the selected item's bounding rect sits within the viewport rect, allowing 1px tolerance on each edge. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-scroll.browser.test.ts: "should scroll initial value into view when it's not the first item")
- Given the same scrollable Command with `value: "Radio Group"` (a mid-list item), when rendered and 150ms elapse, then the selected item's bounding rect sits within the viewport rect within 1px. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-scroll.browser.test.ts: "should scroll initial value in the middle of the list into view")
- Given a scrollable Command with `value: "Popover"` and `disableInitialScroll: true`, when rendered and 150ms elapse, then `viewport.scrollTop` is 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-scroll.browser.test.ts: "should respect disableInitialScroll prop and not scroll")
- Given a scrollable Command with `value: "Introduction"` (the first item), when rendered and 150ms elapse, then `viewport.scrollTop` is 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command-scroll.browser.test.ts: "should not scroll when initial value is the first item")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when the value and search are identical (`"test"`, `"test"`), then the score is exactly 1. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > returns 1 for exact matches")
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when case differs (`"Test"` or `"TEST"` against `"test"`), then the score is close to 0.9999. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > handles case insensitive matches")
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when `"test"` is scored against the prefix `"te"` versus the interior `"es"`, then the prefix score is greater. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > scores prefix matches higher")
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when `"test"` is scored against continuous `"te"` versus skipping `"tt"`, then the continuous score is greater. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > penalizes non-continuous matches")
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when `"cp"` is scored against `"copy paste"` versus `"copy/paste"`, then the space-separated value scores higher than the slash-separated one. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > handles word boundaries in commands")
- Given `computeCommandScore` with keywords `["math", "add", "subtract"]`, when `"Calculator"` is scored against `"add"`, then the score is greater than 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > considers keywords in scoring")
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when `"string"` is scored against `"st"` versus the transposed `"ts"`, then the correct order scores higher and the transposed score is still greater than 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > handles transposed characters")
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when `"test"` is scored against `"xyz"`, then the score is exactly 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > returns 0 for no matches")
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when `"cp"` is scored against `"copy@paste"`, `"copy#paste"` and `"copy[paste]"`, then every score is greater than 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > handles special characters in commands")
- Given `computeCommandScore`, when both inputs are empty, then the score is 1; when the search is empty against `"test"`, the score is 0.99; when the value is empty against `"test"`, the score is 0. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/compute-command-score.test.ts: "computeCommandScore > handles empty inputs")
- Given the Command fixture, when items declare a `keywords` array such as `["getting started", "tutorial"]` on `Introduction`, then filtering and scoring consider those keywords alongside the item text. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should show empty state when no items are found")
- Given the Command composition `Root > Input > List > Viewport > (Empty, Group > GroupHeading + GroupItems, Separator)`, when a search filters all items out of a group, then the group element stays in the DOM but reports as not visible rather than unmounting. (bits: tests/src/tests/command/command.browser.test.ts: "should hide the group if all items are filtered out")

## tags-input

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default `TagsInput` story, when rendered, then the first `[data-reka-collection-item]` contains the initial tag text `Test`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should render the initial tags")
- Given `defaultTags: ['svelte','ts']`, when rendered, then each `tag-<i>` element exists and contains its tag text. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "Default tags are present")

### Keyboard
- Given a focused input with tags already added, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then the last tag gets `data-state="active"`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should select the last tags")
- Given the last tag active, when ArrowLeft is pressed again, then the last tag becomes `inactive` and the one before it becomes `active`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should select the previous tag when press ArrowLeft")
- Given a tag is active, when Home is pressed, then the first tag becomes `active` and the last becomes `inactive`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should select the first item when press Home")
- Given the first tag active after Home, when End is pressed, then the first becomes `inactive` and the last becomes `active`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should select the last item when press End")
- Given the last tag active, when ArrowRight is pressed, then it becomes `inactive`, so focus returns to the input. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should remove active state when press ArrowRight")
- Given an active tag, when Backspace is pressed, then the root emits `removeTag` with that tag's value. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should trigger `removeTag` event")
- Given an active tag, when Backspace is pressed, then that tag element is gone from the DOM and the tag count drops to two. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should remove the active tag")
- Given an active tag removed by Backspace, when the removal settles, then the new last tag becomes `active`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should select the new last tag")
- Given a value typed into the input, when Enter is pressed, then the value becomes a new tag. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should add value on keydown:enter")
- Given `addOnTab: true` and a typed value, when Tab is pressed, then the value becomes a new tag. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should add value on keydown:tab")
- Given a fresh tags input, when a tag is typed followed by Enter, then the input is cleared and the tag text is in the document. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "New tag can be added")
- Given a tags input whose first tag is disabled and second is removable, when Backspace is pressed twice, then the removable tag is removed, only the disabled tag remains, and `removeTag` was emitted with the removable tag's value. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "removes the selected removable tag, not the disabled one")
- Given only a disabled tag remains, when Backspace is pressed twice more, then the disabled tag is still present. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "does not remove the disabled tag when it is the only remaining tag")

### Pointer
- Given `addOnBlur: true` and a typed value, when the input blurs, then the value becomes a new tag. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should add value on blur")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a focused input, when two tags are added in sequence, then the root emits `addTag` with `'123'` and then `'Asd'`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should emit `addTag` event")
- Given two tags added, when the DOM settles, then the new tag text appears in the markup at the expected index. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should add a new tag")
- Given a tag was just added, when the DOM settles, then the input is still `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should have focus on input")
- Given a tag was just added, when the DOM settles, then the input's value is the empty string. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should clear off the value in input")
- Given `unique: true` and the tag already present, when the same text is submitted, then the input keeps its value, so the duplicate is rejected. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "Respect uniqueness")
- Given `unique: true`, `trim: false`, and a custom `add` that trims, when the tag is typed with trailing spaces, then the input keeps its value because the trimmed result duplicates an existing tag. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "Respect uniqueness with custom add function")
- Given `trim: true`, when a tag is typed with trailing spaces and submitted, then the input is cleared and the trimmed text is in the document. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "Auto trim")
- Given `unique: true` and `trim: true` with the tag already present, when the same text with trailing spaces is submitted, then the input keeps its value. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "Respect uniqueness with auto trim")
- Given an `allowed` list containing one value, when a value outside the list is submitted the input keeps its text, and when the allowed value is submitted the input clears and the tag appears. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "Respect allowed list")
- Given an `allowed` list plus `trim: true`, when the disallowed and then the allowed value are submitted with trailing spaces, then only the allowed one is accepted. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "Respect allowed list with auto trim")
- Given an `allowed` list plus a custom trimming `add` function, when the disallowed and then the allowed value are submitted with trailing spaces, then only the allowed one is accepted. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "Respect allowed list with custom add")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default `TagsInput`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a default melt tags input, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (melt: src/tests/tags-input/TagsInput.spec.ts: "No accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given `displayValue: item => 'Person: ' + item.name` and object values, when rendered, then the tags read `Person: Durward Reynolds` and `Person: Kenton Towne`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should display the initial tags")
- Given `convertValue` turning a string into `{ name, id }`, when a new tag is typed and Enter pressed, then the last tag reads `Person: Moriah Stanton` and the bound array holds objects with numeric `id` and string `name`. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should update the tags")
- Given object values with `displayValue` but no `convertValue`, when a tag is submitted, then the app error handler is called exactly once with the message "You must provide a `convertValue` function when using objects as values." (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should throw an error if props are not ok")
- Given `delimiter: ','` and `addOnPaste: true`, when `tag1,` is typed, then a tag `tag1` is created from the delimiter alone. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should add tag on typing single delimiter character")
- Given `delimiter: /[ ,;]+/`, when `tag1,`, `tag2 `, and `tag3;` are typed in turn, then three tags are created, one per delimiter character class match. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should add tag on typing multiple delimiter characters")
- Given `delimiter: ','` and `addOnPaste: true`, when `tag1,tag2,tag3` is pasted, then three tags are created. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should add multiple tags on pasting text with single delimiter character")
- Given `delimiter: /[ ,;]+/`, when `tag1, tag2;tag3 tag4` is pasted, then four tags are created. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should add multiple tags on pasting text with multiple delimiter characters")
- Given `delimiter: ','`, when a `compositionstart` is fired and then an `input` event carrying the delimiter arrives, then no new tag is created and the input still holds the comma, so IME composition suppresses delimiter splitting. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should not create tag when delimiter is typed during IME composition")
- Given the same setup with the value `hello,` during composition, when `compositionend` fires and the same input event is replayed, then the tag `hello` is created, so the deferred value is processed after composition. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "should process value after composition ends")
- Given the reka tests stub `window.getComputedStyle` to return an empty object, note that the component's own style reads are effectively disabled in the default and disabled-tag suites. (reka: packages/core/src/TagsInput/TagsInput.test.ts: "given default TagsInput")
