### Pointer
- Given a default `Editable`, when the preview is clicked, then the edit trigger becomes visible. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "changes to editable mode when clicking on the preview")
- Given a default `Editable`, when the edit button is clicked, then the input becomes visible. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "changes to editable mode when clicking on the edit button")
- Given `activationMode: 'dblclick'`, when the preview is double-clicked, then the input becomes visible. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "changes to editable mode when double clicking on the preview")
- Given `submitMode: 'blur'`, when the preview is double-clicked, text typed, and an outside element clicked, then the preview shows the new text. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "submits the value on blur")
- Given `submitMode: 'both'`, when the same blur sequence runs, then the preview shows the new text. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "submits the value on blur if submitMode is both")

### Focus management
- Given `defaultValue: 'Default Value'` and `selectOnFocus: true`, when the input is clicked, then it has focus, its value is the default, and both `selectionStart` and `selectionEnd` equal the value length. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "selects the input value when entering edit mode and selectOnFocus is true")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given `defaultValue: 'Default Value'`, when rendered, then the preview shows that text. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "respects a default value if provided")
- Given `modelValue: 'Default Value'`, when rendered, then the preview shows that text, so the controlled prop also seeds the preview. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "respects a default value if provided - `modelValue`")
- Given `placeholder: 'Enter text...'` with no value, when rendered, then the preview shows the placeholder. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "sets the placeholder value if any value isn't set")
- Given `startWithEditMode: true`, when rendered, then the input is already visible. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "starts in edit mode if the property is set")
- Given `disabled: true`, when the preview is clicked, then the edit trigger is not visible. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "prevents entering edit mode when disabled")
- Given `readonly: true` and a default value, when the edit button is clicked and text is typed, then the input is visible but its value is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "prevents editing the input value when readonly")
- Given `maxLength: 10`, when a 26-character string is typed, then the input's value is truncated to `lorem ipsu`. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "should prevent user input text more than given `maxLength`")

### Animation and presence
- Given `autoResize: true`, when rendered in preview mode the input has `visibility: hidden`, and after the edit button is clicked the preview has `visibility: hidden`, so both nodes stay in the layout and swap visibility. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "uses the proper styles when autoResize is true")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default `Editable`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Editable/Editable.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

## tree

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default `Tree` with `selectionBehavior: 'toggle'`, when snapshotted, then the root is a `ul` with `role="tree"`, `tabindex="0"`, `data-orientation="vertical"`, `dir="ltr"`, and `outline: none`, and each `li` has `role="treeitem"`, `tabindex="-1"`, `data-reka-collection-item=""`, `aria-setsize="3"`, a 1-based `aria-posinset`, `aria-selected="false"`, `aria-level="1"`, `data-indent="1"`, and `margin-left: 1rem`, with collapsible rows additionally carrying `aria-expanded="false"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should render snapshot")
- Given one item marked `disabled`, when rendered, then it has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled=""` while an enabled sibling has neither attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should set aria-disabled and data-disabled attributes")

### Keyboard
- Given a collapsed folder row, when ArrowRight is pressed on it, then its first child row is revealed. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should expand the item, revealing it's item")
- Given an expanded folder row, when ArrowLeft is pressed on it, then the children are hidden and the next row is the following sibling. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should close when press ArrowLeft")
- Given focus on a child row, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus moves to the parent row. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should focus on parent when press ArrowLeft on child item")
- Given an already expanded folder row, when ArrowRight is pressed again, then focus moves to its first child. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should focus on child item when press ArriwRight")
- Given an expanded folder whose child is itself a folder, when ArrowRight is pressed on the child, then the grandchild row is revealed. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should expand the nested item, revealing it's item")
- Given the tree container focused, when the letter `l` is pressed, then focus moves to the first row whose text starts with `l`, exercising the shared typeahead. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should highlight text starting with l")
- Given `multiple: true` and `selectionBehavior: 'toggle'`, when Enter selects the first row, ArrowDown moves down twice, and Enter selects the third row, then rows one and three are `aria-selected="true"` and row two is `"false"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should select multiple items")
- Given `multiple: true` with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'` and the first row selected, when Shift+ArrowDown is pressed twice, then the selection grows to the first two and then the first three rows. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should select the next item")
- Given a custom `getChildren` that merges `directories` and `files`, when ArrowRight expands a folder then a nested folder, then the revealed rows are `tree` and then `Tree.vue`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "given a Tree with a custom children structure > when expand item > should expand the item, revealing it's item")
- Given the same custom structure, when the nested folder is expanded, then its first file row is revealed. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "given a Tree with a custom children structure > when expand nested item > should expand the nested item, revealing it's item")

### Pointer
- Given `selectionBehavior: 'toggle'`, when a row is clicked twice, then `aria-selected` goes `true` then `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should select and deselect item")
- Given `selectionBehavior: 'replace'`, when the same row is clicked twice, then `aria-selected` stays `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "when selection behavior `replace` > should not toggle off the selected value")
- Given `selectionBehavior: 'replace'`, when a second row is clicked, then the first becomes `false` and the second becomes `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "when selection behavior `replace` > should select and replace another item")
- Given `multiple: true` with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'`, when the selected row is clicked again, then it stays selected. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "given multiple `true` Tree > when selection behavior `replace` > should not toggle off the selected value")
- Given `multiple: true` with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'`, when a second row is clicked, then the first is deselected and the second selected. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "given multiple `true` Tree > when selection behavior `replace` > should select and replace another item")
- Given `propagateSelect: true` and `bubbleSelect: true` over a three-level tree, when the root row is clicked, then all four rows become `aria-selected="true"`, and clicking it again clears all four. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "propagates changes down the tree")
- Given the same tree, when one leaf is clicked only that leaf is selected, when the second leaf is clicked all four rows become selected, when the first leaf is clicked again only the other leaf stays selected, and when that one is clicked nothing is selected. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "bubbles change up the tree")
- Given a disabled row, when it is clicked and then Enter is pressed on it, then `aria-selected` stays `"false"` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should not select a disabled item on click or keydown")
- Given a disabled folder row that is expanded, when it is clicked and then ArrowLeft is pressed, then the visible row count stays at six, so a disabled row cannot be collapsed. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should not toggle a disabled item")
- Given `disabled` on the tree root, when rendered every row has `aria-disabled="true"`, and when the first row is clicked it stays unselected. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "should disable all items when root is disabled")

### Focus management
- Given a text input rendered inside a tree item and focused, when ArrowRight is dispatched on it, then the event is not `defaultPrevented`, focus stays on the input, and the row count is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "leaves ArrowRight to the caret instead of walking the tree")
- Given the same input focused, when ArrowLeft is dispatched, then the event is not prevented, focus stays on the input, and no row collapses. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "leaves ArrowLeft to the caret instead of jumping to the parent row")
- Given the same input focused, when the character `c` is dispatched, then focus stays on the input even though two rows start with `c`, so typeahead is suppressed inside text fields. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "does not run typeahead while typing")
- Given a native `select` inside a tree item and focused, when `c` is dispatched, then focus stays on the select so its own option typeahead wins. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "does not run typeahead while a select inside an item is focused")
- Given an expanded folder row with no form control focused, when ArrowLeft is dispatched on the row itself, then the visible row count decreases, so tree navigation still works outside inputs. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "still walks the tree when the key lands on the item itself")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default `Tree`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "given default Tree > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a `Tree` with one folder expanded, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "when expand item by press ArrowRight > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a `Tree` with a nested folder expanded, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Tree/Tree.test.ts: "when expand nested item > should pass axe accessibility tests")

## avatar

### Roles and attributes
- Given an `Avatar` with a root, image, and fallback, when rendered, then the three parts carry `data-avatar-root`, `data-avatar-image`, and `data-avatar-fallback`. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "Data Attributes > should have bits data attrs")
- Given an `Avatar` whose image has `alt="Colm Tuite"`, when rendered, then an element is findable by that alt text. (reka: packages/core/src/Avatar/Avatar.test.ts: "should have alt text on the image")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given an `Avatar` with a mocked `Image` that loads after 350ms, when first rendered, then the fallback text `CT` is in the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Avatar/Avatar.test.ts: "should render the fallback initially")
- Given the same avatar, when first rendered, then the `img` element exists but carries `display: none`. (reka: packages/core/src/Avatar/Avatar.test.ts: "should render the image, but show `display:none` initially")
- Given an `Avatar` with `delay: 300`, when first rendered, then the fallback text is absent, so the fallback itself is delayed rather than shown immediately. (reka: packages/core/src/Avatar/Avatar.test.ts: "should not render a fallback immediately")
- Given the same delayed avatar, when the delay elapses, then the fallback text appears inside the root element. (reka: packages/core/src/Avatar/Avatar.test.ts: "should render a fallback after the delay")
- Given a valid `src`, when rendered, then the image's `src` attribute is that URL. (melt: src/tests/avatar/Avatar.spec.ts: "renders the image with the correct src")
- Given an empty `src`, when rendered, then the fallback text `RH` is in the document. (melt: src/tests/avatar/Avatar.spec.ts: "renders the fallback with the correct text")
- Given a valid GitHub avatar `src`, when rendered, then the image found by alt text has that exact `src`. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "Rendering Behavior > should render the image with the correct src")
- Given `src: "invalid"`, when the load fails, then the image is not visible and the fallback text `HJ` is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "should render the fallback when an invalid image src is provided")
- Given a loaded avatar, when a clear button empties the `src`, then the image becomes invisible and the fallback becomes visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "should remove the avatar when the src is removed")
- Given `src: "invalid"`, when the fallback renders, then its inline style is not the literal string `display: undefined`, guarding against a stringified undefined leaking into the style attribute. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "should not have invalid style on the fallback if the image is not loaded")
- Given a stubbed `Image` class and fake timers, when `src` changes from `first.png` to `replacement.png` and the first image then fires `error` and `load`, then `onLoadingStatusChange` is not called and the root's `data-status` is `loading`, and only the second image's `load` reports `loaded` exactly once. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "Image load cleanup > ignores obsolete image events after src becomes \"replacement.png\"")
- Given the same stub, when `src` changes from `first.png` to the empty string and the obsolete image fires events, then no status change is reported and the root's `data-status` is `error`. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "Image load cleanup > ignores obsolete image events after src becomes \"\"")
- Given `delayMs: 100` and a first image that has already fired `load`, when `src` changes before the delay expires, then advancing 100ms reports nothing and `data-status` is `loading`, and the replacement's `load` reports `loaded` only after the full 100ms (nothing at 99ms). (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "cancels a pending display delay when src changes")
- Given `delayMs: 100` with no load fired yet, when the component unmounts and the image then fires `error` and `load`, then no status change is reported even after the timer advances. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "cancels image work on destroy (load already fired: false)")
- Given `delayMs: 100` with `load` already fired, when the component unmounts and further events arrive, then no status change is reported. (bits: tests/src/tests/avatar/avatar.browser.test.ts: "cancels image work on destroy (load already fired: true)")

### Animation and presence
- Given the pre-load state, when snapshotted, then the recorded HTML has the `img` with `style="display: none;"` and a sibling fallback `span` containing `CT`. (reka: packages/core/src/Avatar/Avatar.test.ts: "should match before image loaded snapshot")
- Given the post-load state after the fallback is removed from the DOM, when snapshotted, then the recorded HTML has the `img` with an empty `style` attribute and `<!--v-if-->` where the fallback used to be. (reka: packages/core/src/Avatar/Avatar.test.ts: "should match after image loaded snapshot")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default `Avatar`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Avatar/Avatar.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

## pagination

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default `Pagination` over 10 pages, when rendered, then `[aria-label="Page 1"]` has `data-selected="true"` and `[aria-label="Page 2"]` has no `data-selected`. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given default Pagination > should have first page selected by default")
- Given `total: 13` with a default page size, when rendered, then exactly two `[data-type="page"]` buttons exist. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given small total value > should have only 2 page button")
- Given `showEdges: true` on page 5, when rendered, then exactly one `[data-type="ellipsis"]` element exists. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should have right ellipsis")

### Pointer
- Given a default `Pagination` on page 1, when Next Page is clicked, then page 1 loses `data-selected` and page 2 gains `data-selected="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "after clicking on Next Page trigger > should have set to page 2")
- Given a default `Pagination`, when the Page 3 button is clicked, then page 3 becomes the selected page. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "after clicking on Page 3 trigger > should have set to page 2")
- Given a default `Pagination`, when Last Page is clicked, then page 10 is selected and the Page 1 button no longer exists in the window. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "after clicking on Last Page trigger > should have set to page 10")
- Given all pagination buttons rendered `as="a"` on page 1, when Previous Page is clicked, then page 1 stays selected. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should not unselect page 1 after clicking on Prev Page trigger")
- Given all buttons `as="a"` and the last page selected, when Next Page is clicked, then the selected page's `aria-label` is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should not unselect last page after clicking on Next Page trigger")
- Given `showEdges: true` on page 1, when Next Page is clicked, then page 2 becomes selected. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given show-edges Pagination > after clicking on Next Page trigger > should have set to page 2")
- Given `showEdges: true`, when Last Page is clicked, then page 10 is selected and Page 1 still exists because edges are pinned. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given show-edges Pagination > after clicking on Last Page trigger > should have set to page 10")
- Given `showEdges: true`, when Page 5 is clicked, then pages 2, 3, and 4 are present. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should have page 2")
- Given `showEdges: true` on page 5, when the window is inspected, then pages 6 and 7 exist and page 8 does not. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should not have page 8")
- Given `total: 13`, when Next Page is clicked, then page 2 becomes selected. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given small total value > after clicking on Next Page trigger > should have set to page 2")
- Given `total: 13`, when Last Page is clicked, then page 2 is selected and page 1 still exists. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given small total value > after clicking on Last Page trigger > should have set to page 2")
- Given a pagination component on page 1, when prev is clicked it stays on 1, then next twice moves to 2 and 3, then prev moves back to 2. (melt: src/tests/pagination/cmp.spec.ts: "Next and prev buttons should work accordingly")
- Given the same component, when the page 2 button and then the page 10 button are clicked, then the selected `data-value` becomes `2` then `10`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/cmp.spec.ts: "Should change page to clicked button")
- Given `count: 100`, when prev is force-clicked on page 1 it stays on 1, then next twice reaches 3, then prev returns to 2. (bits: tests/src/tests/pagination/pagination.browser.test.ts: "should navigate previous and Next button accordingly")
- Given `count: 100`, when the page 2 then page 10 buttons are clicked, then the current page text becomes `2` then `10`. (bits: tests/src/tests/pagination/pagination.browser.test.ts: "should change on clicked button")
- Given `count: 100` with a page size of 10, when rendered the range reads 1 to 10, and when next is clicked it reads 11 to 20. (bits: tests/src/tests/pagination/pagination.browser.test.ts: "should display the correct range of items being displayed")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given `showEdges: true`, when rendered, then page 1 is selected by default and page 2 is not. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given show-edges Pagination > should have first page selected by default")
- Given `showEdges: true`, when rendered, then both the Page 1 and Page 2 buttons exist. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should always show Page 1 & Page 10")
- Given `total: 13`, when rendered, then page 1 is selected by default. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given small total value > should have first page selected by default")
- Given `total: 0`, when rendered, then page 1 is still selected by default. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given 0 total value > should have first page selected by default")
- Given `total: 0`, when rendered, then the First, Previous, Next, and Last buttons all carry a `disabled` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "all button should disabled")
- Given all buttons `as="a"`, page 2 selected, and the root then set to `disabled`, when First Page is clicked, then the selection stays on page 2. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should ignore clicking on First Page trigger")
- Given the same disabled state, when Last Page is clicked, then the selection stays on page 2. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should ignore clicking on Last Page trigger")
- Given the same disabled state, when any non-selected page button is clicked, then the selection stays on page 2. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "should ignore clicking on any non-selected page")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default `Pagination`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given default Pagination > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a `Pagination` whose First, Previous, page item, Next, and Last parts are all rendered `as="a"`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given Pagination with <a> as buttons > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given the `as="a"` pagination with the root disabled, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given Pagination with <a> as buttons and disabled > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given `showEdges: true`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given show-edges Pagination > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given `total: 13`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given small total value > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given `total: 0`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Pagination/Pagination.test.ts: "given 0 total value > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a rendered pagination, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (melt: src/tests/pagination/cmp.spec.ts: "No accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given 100 total pages and no explicit page, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,2,3,4,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page undefined siblingCount undefined")
- Given 100 pages and page 3, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,2,3,4,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 3")
- Given 100 pages and page 4, when `getPageItems` runs, then a leading ellipsis appears: `1,...,3,4,5,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 4")
- Given 100 pages and page 5, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,...,4,5,6,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 5")
- Given 100 pages and page 97, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,...,96,97,98,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 97")
- Given 100 pages and page 98, when `getPageItems` runs, then the trailing ellipsis disappears: `1,...,97,98,99,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 98")
- Given 5 pages and page 3, when `getPageItems` runs, then every page is listed with no ellipsis. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 5 page 3")
- Given 6 pages and page 4, when `getPageItems` runs, then every page is listed. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 6 page 4")
- Given 7 pages and page 4, when `getPageItems` runs, then both ellipses appear: `1,...,3,4,5,...,7`, so 7 is the threshold where truncation starts at the default sibling count. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 7 page 4")
- Given 3 pages and page 2, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,2,3`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 3 page 2")
- Given 4 pages and page 2, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,2,3,4`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 4 page 2")
- Given 100 pages, no page, and `siblingCount: 2`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,2,3,4,5,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 siblingCount 2")
- Given 100 pages, no page, and `siblingCount: 3`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,2,3,4,5,6,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 siblingCount 3")
- Given 100 pages, page 5, and `siblingCount: 3`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,2,3,4,5,6,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 5 siblingCount 3")
- Given 100 pages, page 6, and `siblingCount: 3`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,...,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 6 siblingCount 3")
- Given 100 pages, page 97, and `siblingCount: 3`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,...,95,96,97,98,99,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 97 siblingCount 3")
- Given 100 pages, page 96, and `siblingCount: 3`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is the same `1,...,95,96,97,98,99,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 96 siblingCount 3")
- Given 100 pages, page 95, and `siblingCount: 3`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,...,92,93,94,95,96,97,98,...,100`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 100 page 95 siblingCount 3")
- Given 7 pages, page 4, and `siblingCount: 2`, when `getPageItems` runs, then all seven pages are listed. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 7 page 4 siblingCount 2")
- Given 8 pages, page 5, and `siblingCount: 2`, when `getPageItems` runs, then all eight pages are listed. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 8 page 5 siblingCount 2")
- Given 9 pages, page 1, and `siblingCount: 2`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,2,3,4,5,...,9`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 9 page 1 siblingCount 2")
- Given 9 pages, page 5, and `siblingCount: 2`, when `getPageItems` runs, then the window is `1,...,3,4,5,6,7,...,9`. (melt: src/tests/pagination/helpers.spec.ts: "getPageItems totalPages 9 page 5 siblingCount 2")

## splitter

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `SplitterPanel` with `size-unit="px"`, `collapsible`, `collapsed-size` 80, `default-size` 300 and `min-size` 150 in a 923px group, when the layout initializes, then the panel's `data-state` is `expanded`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/Splitter.test.ts: "nested px SplitterGroup layout re-initialization (issue #2509) > should set data-state=\"collapsed\" for a collapsed px panel")
- Given that same px panel, when `collapse()` is called through the panel's exposed API, then its `data-state` becomes `collapsed` despite the px-to-percent conversion leaving the panel size a float epsilon off `collapsedSize`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/Splitter.test.ts: "nested px SplitterGroup layout re-initialization (issue #2509) > should set data-state=\"collapsed\" for a collapsed px panel")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a horizontal `SplitterGroup` whose container reports only 3.45px before its panels register, when the container later resizes to 923px, then the last emitted `layout` event has the px sidebar at approximately 200px (its `default-size`) and the percent content panel above 50. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/Splitter.test.ts: "nested px SplitterGroup layout re-initialization (issue #2509) > should re-initialize layout when container grows from a tiny initial size")
- Given a percent panel with `onResize`, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs with layout `[50]` and a 1000px group, then `onResize` is called with `(50, undefined)` and the size map records `50`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onResize > should call onResize with percentage values for percent-based panels")
- Given a px panel with `onResize`, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs with layout `[20]` and a 1000px group, then `onResize` is called with `(200, undefined)` and the size map records `200`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onResize > should convert percentage to pixels for px-based panels")
- Given a px panel resized from 20% to 25% of a 1000px group, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs twice, then `onResize` is called twice and the last call is `(250, 200)`, so the previous size is reported in the panel's native unit. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onResize > should pass previous size in native units")
- Given a px panel and a `null` `groupSizeInPixels`, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs with layout `[20]`, then `onResize` is called with `(20, undefined)`, falling back to the percentage. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onResize > should fall back to percentage when groupSizeInPixels is not available")
- Given one percent and one px panel, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs with layout `[70, 30]` and a 1000px group, then the percent panel's `onResize` gets `(70, undefined)` and the px panel's gets `(300, undefined)`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onResize > should handle mixed percent and pixel panels")
- Given a px panel called twice with the same layout `[20]` and group size, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs, then `onResize` is called only once. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onResize > should not call onResize if size has not changed")
- Given a px panel with `onResize` and no `groupSizeInPixels` argument at all, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs with layout `[20]`, then `onResize` is called with `(20, undefined)`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > edge cases > should handle groupSizeInPixels of undefined (no arg)")
- Given a px panel with an empty callbacks object, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs with layout `[20]` and a 1000px group, then it does not throw and the size map records `200`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > edge cases > should handle panels with no callbacks")
- Given a px panel and a percent panel, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs with `[30, 70]` then `[25, 70]` on a 1000px group, then the size map holds `300` then `250` for the px panel and `70` for the percent panel, the px panel's `onResize` fires twice and the percent panel's only once. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > edge cases > should track sizes independently per panel in sizeMap")
- Given a px panel held at 20% while the group size changes from 1000px to 800px, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs twice, then `onResize` is last called with `(160, 200)` and has fired twice, so a group resize alone counts as a size change for px panels. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > edge cases > should handle different group sizes for the same percentage")
- Given a collapsible px panel with `collapsedSize` 48, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs at 20% (200px) and then 4.8% (48px) of a 1000px group, then `onExpand` fires once on the first call (expanding from `undefined`) and `onCollapse` fires once on the second with no further `onExpand`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onCollapse / onExpand for pixel-sized panels > should call onCollapse when pixel panel reaches collapsedSize")
- Given a collapsible px panel whose size map already records the collapsed 48px, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs at 20% (200px), then `onExpand` fires once and `onCollapse` does not fire. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onCollapse / onExpand for pixel-sized panels > should call onExpand when pixel panel expands from collapsedSize")
- Given a px panel with `collapsible: false` and `collapsedSize` 48, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs at 4.8% (exactly the collapsed size), then neither `onCollapse` nor `onExpand` fires. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onCollapse / onExpand for pixel-sized panels > should not fire collapse/expand for non-collapsible panels")
- Given a collapsible percent panel with `collapsedSize` 5, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs at 30, then 5, then 25, then `onExpand` fires, then `onCollapse` fires, then `onExpand` fires again, with the other callback silent each time. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > onCollapse / onExpand for percent-based panels > should still work for percentage panels")
- Given a collapsible px panel with `collapsedSize` 0, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs at 20% then 0%, then `onExpand` fires once and then `onCollapse` fires once. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > edge cases > should handle collapsedSize of 0 for pixel panels")
- Given a collapsible px panel with `collapsedSize` 48, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs at `4.800000000000001%` of 1000px (48.00000000000001px), then `onCollapse` still fires once, so the comparison is fuzzy rather than strict. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > edge cases > should use fuzzy comparison for floating point precision")
- Given a collapsible px panel with `collapsedSize` 48 cycled 200px, 48px, 200px, 48px, when `callPanelCallbacks` runs each time, then `onExpand` fires twice, `onCollapse` fires twice, and `onResize` fires four times with `(200, undefined)`, `(48, 200)`, `(200, 48)` and `(48, 200)`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/callPanelCallbacks.test.ts: "callPanelCallbacks > edge cases > should handle collapse/expand cycle correctly for pixel panels")

### Positioning
- Given panels where none declares `sizeUnit: 'px'`, when `hasPixelSizedPanel` is called, then it returns `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "hasPixelSizedPanel > should return false when no panels use px")
- Given panels where at least one declares `sizeUnit: 'px'`, when `hasPixelSizedPanel` is called, then it returns `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "hasPixelSizedPanel > should return true when at least one panel uses px")
- Given a percent panel with `minSize` 10, `maxSize` 80 and `defaultSize` 50, when `convertPanelConstraintsToPercent` runs against a 1000px group, then the constraints come back unchanged with `sizeUnit` `'%'`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "convertPanelConstraintsToPercent > should return constraints as-is for percent panels")
- Given a px panel with `minSize` 200, `maxSize` 400, `defaultSize` 300 and `collapsedSize` 50, when `convertPanelConstraintsToPercent` runs against a 1000px group, then the results are 20, 40, 30 and 5 with `sizeUnit` `'%'`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "convertPanelConstraintsToPercent > should convert px constraints to percent")
- Given a px panel and a `null` `groupSizeInPixels`, when `convertPanelConstraintsToPercent` runs, then it returns `null`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "convertPanelConstraintsToPercent > should return null when px panel exists but groupSize is null")
- Given a px sidebar (`defaultSize` 250, `minSize` 150, `maxSize` 350) beside a percent content panel with `minSize` 30, when `convertPanelConstraintsToPercent` runs against a 1000px group, then the sidebar becomes 25, 15 and 35 while the content panel's `minSize` stays 30. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "convertPanelConstraintsToPercent > should handle mixed percent and px panels")
- Given two percent panels, when `recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels` runs for a group resize from 1000px to 800px, then it returns `null`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels > should return null if no pixel panels exist")
- Given a px sidebar at 20% and a percent content panel at 80%, when the group resizes from 1000px to 800px, then `recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels` returns `[25, 75]`, holding the sidebar at its 200px while the percent panel absorbs the change. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels > should maintain pixel panel size when group resizes")
- Given a px panel and a percent panel, when `recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels` is given a `null` `prevGroupSize` or a `nextGroupSize` of 0, then it returns `null` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels > should return null for invalid group sizes")
- Given px, percent and px panels at `[20, 60, 20]`, when the group resizes from 1000px to 800px, then `recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels` returns 25 for each px panel and 50 for the percent panel. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels > should handle multiple pixel panels")
- Given two all-px panels at `[50, 50]` resizing from 920px to 921px, when `recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels` runs, then the returned values sum to 100 within 1e-9, so the output is normalized against floating-point drift. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels > should normalize result to exactly 100% when floating-point drift occurs (bug #2509)")
- Given three all-px panels at equal thirds resizing from 900px to 901px, when `recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels` runs, then the returned values sum to 100 within 1e-9. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/units.test.ts: "recalculateLayoutForPixelPanels > should normalise when three all-px panels produce fractional remainders")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given the splitter story with a horizontal group containing a nested vertical group and a `max-size="20"` panel, when axe is run on the mounted element with the `label` and `nested-interactive` rules disabled, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/Splitter.test.ts: "test splitter functionalities > should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given an empty layout and empty panel constraints, when `validatePanelGroupLayout` is called, then it returns `[]` and `console.warn` is not called. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/validation.test.ts: "validatePanelGroupLayout > should validate an empty group silently")
- Given a layout of `[50, 50]` with zero panel constraints, when `validatePanelGroupLayout` is called, then it throws an error containing `Invalid 0 panel layout`. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/utils/validation.test.ts: "validatePanelGroupLayout > should throw when the layout length does not match the panel constraints")
- Given the nested-px regression suite, when it runs, then it stubs `ResizeObserver` with a mock that records callbacks so the test can fire a synthetic `contentRect` width, replicating the browser timing where an inner group is measured at 3.45px before the outer group finishes laying out. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/Splitter.test.ts: "nested px SplitterGroup layout re-initialization (issue #2509)")
- Given the reka Splitter suite, when read as a whole, then the only component-level coverage is one axe check (the file calls it a "Simple a11y test for now") plus the two `#2509` layout regressions, so keyboard resizing, drag resizing via the resize handle, and persisted layout storage are not asserted anywhere in these files. (reka: packages/core/src/Splitter/Splitter.test.ts: "test splitter functionalities > should pass axe accessibility tests")

## scroll-area

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `ScrollArea` with root, viewport, both scrollbars, both thumbs, and a corner, when rendered with `type: "always"`, then the parts carry `data-scroll-area-root`, `data-scroll-area-viewport`, `data-scroll-area-scrollbar` (both axes), `data-scroll-area-thumb` (both axes), and `data-scroll-area-corner`. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should have bits data attrs")
- Given a default `ScrollArea`, when rendered, then the root and viewport elements are in the document. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should render the root and viewport elements")
- Given a default `ScrollArea` with mocked 500px offsets over 2000px scroll content, when rendered, then the snapshot records the content and the HTML contains no `data-orientation="vertical"`, so no scrollbar is mounted before interaction. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "given default ScrollArea > should render content, but not scrollbar")
- Given `type="always"`, when rendered, then the HTML contains `data-orientation="vertical"` and the snapshot records the mounted scrollbar. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "given prop:type=\"always\" ScrollArea > should render content and scrollbar")
- Given `type="scroll"` with `scrollTop` mocked at 20, when rendered, then the snapshot records the content and the HTML still contains no `data-orientation="vertical"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "given prop:type=\"scroll\" ScrollArea > should render content and scrollbar")

### Keyboard
- Given a bits scroll area with overflowing content, when the viewport is clicked and ArrowDown, PageDown, End, and Home are pressed, then `scrollTop` increases for the first three and returns to `0` for Home. Skipped on WebKit by an early return. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should handle keyboard navigation")

### Pointer
- Given a default `ScrollArea`, when `pointerenter` fires on the root and 100ms pass, then the snapshot records a mounted scrollbar. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "given default ScrollArea > on hover > should render scrollbar")
- Given `type="scroll"`, when `scrollTop` changes to 40 and a `scroll` event fires on `[data-reka-scroll-area-viewport]`, then after 10ms the HTML contains `data-orientation="vertical"` and the snapshot records the visible scrollbar. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "given prop:type=\"scroll\" ScrollArea > on scroll > should render scrollbar")
- Given `type="hover"` with both scrollbars and a corner, and a ResizeObserver mock that fires its callback immediately on `observe`, when the pointer enters, leaves after 700ms, and enters again, then the corner content exists, is removed, and exists again, which is the regression for issue 2669. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "keeps the corner in sync with the scrollbars across repeated hover cycles")
- Given overflowing content, when the root is hovered, then the vertical scrollbar and its thumb exist. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should show scrollbars when content overflows")
- Given content that fits, when the root is hovered, then neither the vertical scrollbar nor its thumb exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should hide scrollbars when content fits")
- Given non-wrapping text in a 50px-wide area, when the root is hovered, then the horizontal scrollbar and thumb exist. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should show horizontal scrollbar when text doesn't wrap")
- Given wrapping text, when the root is hovered, then the horizontal scrollbar and thumb do not exist. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should hide horizontal scrollbar when text wraps")
- Given content overflowing on both axes, when the root is hovered, then the corner element exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should show corner when both scrollbars are visible")
- Given content overflowing on only one axis, when the root is hovered, then the corner does not exist. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should hide corner when only one scrollbar is visible")
- Given `type: "hover"`, when the root is not hovered the vertical scrollbar does not exist, when hovered it exists, and when unhovered it is removed again. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should show scrollbars on hover when type is 'hover'")
- Given `type: "always"`, when the root is hovered and then unhovered, then the vertical scrollbar exists throughout. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should always show scrollbars when type is 'always'")
- Given `type: "scroll"`, when the viewport is clicked and ArrowDown scrolls it, then the vertical scrollbar appears. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should show scrollbars on scroll when type is 'scroll'")
- Given overflowing content on both axes, when the viewport is clicked and ArrowDown then ArrowRight are pressed, then both `scrollTop` and `scrollLeft` increase while both scrollbars and the corner exist. Skipped on WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should handle both scrollbars simultaneously")
- Given overflowing content, when the viewport is hovered and then scrolled, then `scrollTop` ends greater than its initial value. Skipped on WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should allow wheel scrolling")
- Given `type: "always"` and a visible vertical scrollbar, when a `pointerdown` is dispatched on the scrollbar then `body.style.webkitUserSelect` is `none`, and when `lostpointercapture` is dispatched instead of `pointerup` then it is restored to the empty string. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should restore webkitUserSelect when pointer capture is lost without pointerup")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given `type: 'always'`, when rendered, then both the x and y scrollbars are visible. (melt: src/tests/scroll-area/ScrollArea.spec.ts: "Displays the scrollbars when `type` is \"always\"")
- Given `type: 'always'` and a 10px width, when rendered, then the x scrollbar is visible. (melt: src/tests/scroll-area/ScrollArea.spec.ts: "Displays the x scrollbar when `type` is \"auto\" and content overflows")
- Given `type: 'always'` and a 10px height, when rendered, then the y scrollbar is visible. (melt: src/tests/scroll-area/ScrollArea.spec.ts: "Displays the y scrollbar when `type` is \"auto\" and content overflows")
- Given `type: 'auto'` with a 5000px by 5000px area that content cannot overflow, when rendered, then neither scrollbar is visible. (melt: src/tests/scroll-area/ScrollArea.spec.ts: "Doesn't display the scrollbars when `type` is 'auto' and content doesn't overflow")
- Given `type: 'hover'` on a 10px area, when the pointer enters and then leaves the root, then the scrollbars appear and disappear. [skipped] The file comments the skip as "I hate vitest/testing library sometimes." (melt: src/tests/scroll-area/ScrollArea.spec.ts: "Displays the scrollbars on hover")
- Given `type: "auto"` with overflowing content, when rendered, then the vertical scrollbar exists without any hover. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should show scrollbars when content overflows when type is `auto`")
- Given a non-overflowing area, when the paragraph count is raised to 20 through the harness input, then hovering the root reveals the vertical scrollbar. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should respond to dynamic content changes")
- Given a 400px-tall area holding 20 paragraphs with no scrollbar, when the height input is set to 100, then hovering the root reveals the vertical scrollbar. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should respond to size changes")

### RTL and i18n
- Given `dir: "rtl"` with non-wrapping content, when the viewport is clicked and ArrowLeft is pressed, then `scrollLeft` changes from its initial value while the horizontal scrollbar exists. Skipped on WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should handle RTL direction")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default `ScrollArea`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "given default ScrollArea > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given `type="always"`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "given prop:type=\"always\" ScrollArea > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given `type="scroll"`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/ScrollArea/ScrollArea.test.ts: "given prop:type=\"scroll\" ScrollArea > should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given `type: "always"` and a stubbed `ResizeObserver` whose callbacks are fired manually, when the observers fire and the component then unmounts, then no `setTimeout` with a 10ms delay is scheduled and no `derived_inert` warning is logged within the following 20ms. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should not schedule resize work that can outlive a always ScrollArea")
- Given `type: "auto"` and the same stubbed observer, when the observers fire and the component unmounts, then no 10ms timer survives and no `derived_inert` warning is logged. (bits: tests/src/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.browser.test.ts: "should not schedule resize work that can outlive a auto ScrollArea")

## calendar

### Roles and attributes
- Given a Calendar with `modelValue` set to a `CalendarDate` of 1980-01-20, when rendered, then the single `[data-selected]` cell reads `20` and the heading reads `January 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > respects a default value if provided - `CalendarDate`")
- Given a Calendar with `modelValue` set to a `CalendarDateTime` of 1980-01-20T12:30, when rendered, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `20` and the heading reads `January 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > respects a default value if provided - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a Calendar with `modelValue` set to a `ZonedDateTime` in `America/New_York`, when rendered, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `20` and the heading reads `January 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > respects a default value if provided - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a Calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2` and a January 1980 value, when rendered, then the heading reads `January - February 1980`, the day cell for January 12 carries `data-value="1980-01-12T00:00:00"` and the second grid's February 15 cell carries the matching February `data-value`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > displays multiple months when `numberOfMonths` is greater than 1")
- Given a Calendar with `fixedWeeks: true` starting at August 2024, when the next button is clicked through 14 consecutive months, then every view contains exactly six `[data-week]` rows and the first day of the following month is always rendered. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > always renders six weeks when `fixedWeeks` is `true`")
- Given a Calendar with `isDateUnavailable` matching day 3, when rendered, then the January 3 cell reads `3`, has `data-unavailable` and has `aria-disabled="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > handles unavailable dates appropriately")
- Given a Calendar with `isDateDisabled` matching day 3, when rendered, then the January 3 cell reads `3`, has `data-disabled` and has `aria-disabled="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > handles disabled dates appropriately")
- Given a Calendar with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the grid has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, the January 1 and January 10 cells each have `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, the January 1 cell has no `tabindex` attribute, and both the prev and next buttons are disabled. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > doesnt allow focus or interaction when `disabled` is `true`")
- Given a Calendar with `readonly: true`, when rendered, then the grid has `aria-readonly="true"` and `data-readonly`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > prevents selection but allows focus when `readonly` is `true`")
- Given a Calendar with `weekdayFormat: 'narrow'`, when rendered, then the seven head cells read `S`, `M`, `T`, `W`, `T`, `F`, `S`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > formats the weekday labels correctly - `'narrow'`")
- Given a Calendar with `weekdayFormat: 'short'`, when rendered, then the seven head cells contain `Su`, `Mo`, `Tu`, `We`, `Th`, `Fr`, `Sa`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > formats the weekday labels correctly - `'short'`")
- Given a Calendar with `weekdayFormat: 'long'`, when rendered, then the seven head cells read `Sunday` through `Saturday`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > formats the weekday labels correctly - `'long'`")

### Keyboard
- Given a Calendar with the selected January 20 cell focused, when `Enter` is pressed, then the value is cleared and no `[data-selected]` element remains. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > allows deselection with %s key" with `{Enter}`)
- Given a Calendar with the selected January 20 cell focused, when `Space` is pressed, then the value is cleared and no `[data-selected]` element remains. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > allows deselection with %s key" with `{Space}`)
- Given a Calendar whose `placeholder` is a `ZonedDateTime` in January 1980, when the January 2 cell is focused and `Enter` is pressed, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `2`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > allows selection with %s key" with `{Enter}`)
- Given a Calendar whose `placeholder` is a `ZonedDateTime` in January 1980, when the January 2 cell is focused and `Space` is pressed, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `2`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > allows selection with %s key" with `{Space}`)
- Given a Calendar with `maxValue` 1980-03-31 and January 1 focused, when `ArrowDown` is pressed repeatedly, then focus steps a week at a time through January 8, 15, 22, 29 into February 5 (heading `February 1980`), through February 12, 19, 26 into March 4 (heading `March 1980`), through March 11, 18, 25, and then stays on March 25 with the heading still `March 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > does not navigate after `maxValue` (with keyboard)")
- Given a Calendar with `minValue` 1979-12-01 and January 1 focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then focus moves to December 25 1979 and the heading becomes `December 1979`, further presses reach December 18, 11 and 4, and the next press keeps focus on December 4. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > does not navigate before `minValue` (with keyboard)")
- Given a Calendar with January 20 focused and a document-level `keydown` listener, when plain `Enter` is pressed, then the event does not reach the document listener because the cell stops propagation. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > stops propagation for plain Enter but lets Ctrl+Enter bubble to parent listeners")
- Given the same Calendar and listener, when `Control+Enter` is pressed, then the event does reach the document listener. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > stops propagation for plain Enter but lets Ctrl+Enter bubble to parent listeners")
- Given a Calendar with `isDateDisabled` matching day 3 and January 2 focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then focus skips the disabled January 3 and lands on January 4, and `ArrowLeft` returns to January 2. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > handles disabled dates appropriately")
- Given the same Calendar with January 10 focused, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then focus moves to December 27 1979, and `ArrowDown` returns to January 10. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > handles disabled dates appropriately")
- Given a Calendar with `defaultPlaceholder` January 1980 and `maxValue` 1980-02-15 with January 31 focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then focus moves to February 1, and `ArrowLeft` returns to January 31. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > handles maxValue correctly using arrow keys")
- Given a Calendar with `defaultPlaceholder` January 1980 and `minValue` 1979-12-15 with January 1 focused, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then focus moves to December 31 1979, and `ArrowRight` returns to January 1. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > handles minValue correctly using arrow keys")
- Given a Calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2` and `maxValue` 1980-03-15 with the second grid's February 29 focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then focus moves to the second grid's March 1 cell, and `ArrowLeft` moves to the first grid's February 29 cell. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "numberOfMonths > 1 > handles maxValue correctly using arrow keys")
- Given a Calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2` and `minValue` 1979-12-15 with the first grid's January 1 focused, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed, then focus moves to the first grid's December 31 cell, and `ArrowRight` moves to the second grid's January 1 cell. - Given a Calendar with `defaultPlaceholder` 2025-01-01 and `numberOfMonths: 2` with the second grid's February 28 focused, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then focus moves to the second grid's March 1 cell, and `ArrowLeft` moves to the first grid's February 28 cell.
