### Pointer
- Given a Calendar showing January 1980, when the next button is clicked once per month across a year, then the heading walks `January 1980` through `December 1980` and ends at `January 1981`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > navigates the months forward using the next button")
- Given a Calendar showing January 1980, when the prev button is clicked repeatedly, then the heading walks `December 1979` back through `February 1979` and ends at `January 1979`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > navigates the months backwards using the prev button")
- Given a Calendar with `prevPage` set to subtract 10 years, when the plain prev button is clicked, then the heading reads `January 1970`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > navigates 10 years into the past when setting the `prevPage` function to subtract 10 years")
- Given a Calendar with `nextPage` set to add 10 years, when the plain next button is clicked, then the heading reads `January 1990`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > navigates 10 years into the future when setting the `nextPage` function to add 10 years")
- Given a Calendar whose root has `nextPage` adding 10 years but whose next button passes its own `nextPage` adding one year, when that button is clicked, then the heading reads `January 1981`, so the button-level prop wins. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > overwrites the `nextPage` function from `CalendarRoot`")
- Given a Calendar whose root has `prevPage` subtracting 10 years but whose prev button passes its own `prevPage` subtracting one year, when that button is clicked, then the heading reads `January 1979`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > overwrites the `prevPage` function from `CalendarRoot`")
- Given a Calendar with a prev-year button, when it is clicked three times, then the heading walks `January 1979`, `January 1978`, `January 1977`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > should navigate one year in the past (prev year button)")
- Given a Calendar with a next-year button, when it is clicked three times, then the heading walks `January 1981`, `January 1982`, `January 1983`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > should navigate one year in the future (next year button)")
- Given a Calendar with `modelValue` 1980-01-20 wired back through `update:modelValue`, when the selected day is clicked, then no `[data-selected]` element remains in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > allows dates to be deselected by clicking the selected date")
- Given a Calendar whose `placeholder` is a `ZonedDateTime`, when the January 2 cell is clicked, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `2`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > allows selection with mouse")
- Given a Calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2`, when the next button is clicked then prev twice, then the heading walks `February - March 1980`, `January - February 1980`, `December 1979 - January 1980`, moving one month at a time. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > properly handles multiple months correctly")
- Given a Calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2` and `pagedNavigation: true`, when the next button is clicked then prev twice, then the heading walks `March - April 1980`, `January - February 1980`, `November - December 1979`, moving two months at a time. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > properly handles `pagedNavigation` with multiple months")
- Given a Calendar with `minValue` 1979-11-25, when the prev button is clicked a third time after reaching November 1979, then the heading stays `November 1979`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > should not allow navigation before the `minValue` (prev button)")
- Given a Calendar with `maxValue` 1980-03-25, when the next button is clicked a third time after reaching March 1980, then the heading stays `March 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > should not allow navigation after the `maxValue` (next button)")
- Given a Calendar with an unavailable January 3, when that cell is clicked, then it does not gain `data-selected`. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > handles unavailable dates appropriately")
- Given a Calendar with a disabled January 3, when that cell is clicked, then it does not receive focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > handles disabled dates appropriately")
- Given a Calendar with `disabled: true`, when the January 1 and January 10 cells are clicked, then neither gains `data-selected` and neither takes focus when `focus()` is called. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > doesnt allow focus or interaction when `disabled` is `true`")
- Given a Calendar with `readonly: true`, when the January 1 and January 10 cells are clicked, then neither gains `data-selected`, yet each takes focus when `focus()` is called. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > prevents selection but allows focus when `readonly` is `true`")
- Given a multiple-selection Calendar with two selected dates wired through `update:modelValue`, when the first selected day is clicked, then one `[data-selected]` cell remains. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar - `multiple` > allows deselection")
- Given a multiple-selection Calendar with one selected date and `preventDeselect: true`, when that date is clicked twice, then exactly one `[data-selected]` cell remains after each click. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar - `multiple` > prevents deselection when only one date is selected and `preventDeselect` is `true`")
- Given a Melt calendar showing January 1980, when next is clicked then prev twice, then the heading walks `February 1980`, `January 1980`, `December 1979`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > month navigation")
- Given a Melt calendar with a `ZonedDateTime` default value, when the selected day is clicked, then the reported inside value reads `undefined`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > allow deselection")
- Given a Melt calendar whose `defaultPlaceholder` is a `ZonedDateTime`, when the January 2 cell is clicked, then it gains `data-selected` and the reported value equals the placeholder set to day 2. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > selection with mouse")
- Given a Melt calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2`, when next is clicked then prev twice, then the heading walks `February - March 1980`, `January - February 1980`, `December 1979 - January 1980`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > should display multiple months with numberOfMonths prop")
- Given a Melt calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2` and `pagedNavigation: true`, when next is clicked then prev twice, then the heading walks `March - April 1980`, `January - February 1980`, `November - December 1979`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > multiple months (paged navigation)")
- Given a Melt calendar with `fixedWeeks: true`, when next is clicked 12 times and then prev 12 times from the reset value, then a sixth week row is present after every click. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > fixedWeeks always renders 6 weeks")
- Given a Melt calendar with `minValue` 1979-11-25, when the prev button is clicked a third time, then the heading stays `November 1979`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > calendar does not navigate before minValue")
- Given a Melt calendar with `maxValue` 1980-04-01, when the next button is clicked a fourth time, then the heading stays `April 1980`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > calendar does not navigate after maxValue")
- Given a Melt multiple-selection calendar with two selected dates and default `preventDeselect`, when the first selected day is clicked, then one selected cell remains and it reads `5`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > multiple select - prevent deselect false (default)")
- Given a Melt multiple-selection calendar with two selected dates and `preventDeselect: true`, when the first selected day is clicked, then both selected cells remain, reading `2` and `5`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > multiple select -  prevent deselect true")
- Given a Melt calendar with an unavailable January 3, when that cell is clicked, then it does not gain `data-selected`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > unavailable dates behavior")
- Given a Melt calendar with `disabled: true`, when the January 1 cell is clicked, then it does not receive focus. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > disabled prop prevents calendar focus & interaction")
- Given a Melt calendar with `readonly: true`, when the January 1 cell is clicked, then it receives focus but gains no `data-selected`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > readonly prop prevents selecting dates but allows focus")
- Given a Bits calendar showing January 1980, when the next button is clicked once per month across a year, then the heading walks `January 1980` through `December 1980` and ends at `January 1981`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Navigation > should navigate the months forward using the next button")
- Given a Bits calendar showing January 1980, when the prev button is clicked repeatedly, then the heading walks back through 1979 and ends at `January 1979`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Navigation > should navigate the months backwards using the prev button")
- Given a Bits calendar with `minValue` 1979-11-25, when the prev button is force-clicked a third time, then the heading stays `November 1979`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Navigation > should not allow navigation before the `minValue` (prev button)")
- Given a Bits calendar with `maxValue` 1980-03-25, when the next button is force-clicked a third time, then the heading stays `March 1980`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Navigation > should not allow navigation after the `maxValue` (next button)")
- Given a Bits calendar with `value` 1980-01-20, when the selected day is clicked, then the reported value becomes `undefined`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Selection and Deselection > should allow dates to be deselected by clicking the selected date")
- Given a Bits calendar whose `placeholder` is a `ZonedDateTime`, when the January 2 cell is clicked, then the reported value equals the placeholder set to day 2. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Selection and Deselection > should allow selection with mouse")
- Given a Bits calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2`, when next is clicked then prev twice, then the heading walks `February - March 1980`, `January - February 1980`, `December 1979 - January 1980`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Multi-Month Display > should display multiple months when `numberOfMonths` is greater than 1")
- Given a Bits calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2` and `pagedNavigation: true`, when next is clicked then prev twice, then the heading walks `March - April 1980`, `January - February 1980`, `November - December 1979`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Multi-Month Display > should handle `pagedNavigation` with multiple months")
- Given a Bits calendar with an unavailable January 3, when that day is force-clicked, then it does not gain `data-selected`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Availability and Interaction > should handle unavailable dates appropriately")
- Given a Bits calendar with `disabled: true`, when the January 1 and January 10 days are force-clicked, then neither gains `data-selected` and neither takes focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Availability and Interaction > should not allow focus or interaction when `disabled` is `true`")
- Given a Bits calendar with `readonly: true`, when the January 1 and January 10 days are force-clicked, then neither gains `data-selected` yet each can be focused. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Availability and Interaction > should prevent selection but allow focus when `readonly` is `true`")
- Given a Bits multiple-selection calendar with two selected dates, when the first selected day is clicked, then one selected day remains. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Selection and Deselection > should allow deselection")
- Given a Bits multiple-selection calendar with one selected date and `preventDeselect: true`, when that day is clicked twice, then one selected day remains after each click. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Selection and Deselection > should prevent deselection when only one date is selected and `preventDeselect` is `true`")
- Given a Bits multiple-selection calendar with two selected dates and `maxDays: 2`, when a third date January 8 is clicked, then the selection resets to just that one day reading `8`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > maxDays constraints in multiple mode > should reset selection when adding a date violates maxDays constraint")
- Given a Bits multiple-selection calendar with one selected date and `maxDays: 3`, when two more dates are clicked, then the selection grows to two and then three days. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > maxDays constraints in multiple mode > should allow valid selections within maxDays constraint")
- Given an empty Bits multiple-selection calendar with `maxDays: 3`, when four dates are clicked in turn, then the selection grows to one, two and three days and the fourth click resets it to a single day reading `15`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > maxDays constraints in multiple mode > should work with maxDays constraint")
- Given a Bits multiple-selection calendar with three selected dates and `maxDays: 5`, when two of them are clicked in turn, then the selection shrinks to two and then one day. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > maxDays constraints in multiple mode > should allow deselection even with constraints")
- Given an empty Bits multiple-selection calendar with `maxDays: 2`, when three dates are clicked in turn, then the selection grows to one and two days and the third click resets it to a single day reading `12`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > maxDays constraints in multiple mode > should handle constraints when no initial value is provided")
- Given a Bits calendar with a `Calendar.MonthSelect` on January 1980, when `3` is selected in it, then the March grid is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "Calendar Select Components > Calendar.MonthSelect > should update calendar when month is changed")
- Given a Bits calendar with a `Calendar.YearSelect` limited to 1979 through 1981, when `1981` is selected, then the January grid is still visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "Calendar Select Components > Calendar.YearSelect > should update calendar when year is changed")
- Given a Bits calendar with both selects, when month `3` and year `1981` are selected, then the March grid is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "Calendar Select Components > Integration > should work together to navigate to specific month/year")
- Given a Bits calendar whose `Calendar.MonthSelect` offers January through April, when February and then April are selected, then the `option[selected]` reads `February` and then `April`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "Calendar Select Components > Integration > should maintain selections when switching between months")

### Focus management
- Given a Calendar with no selected date whose placeholder month contains no `[data-today]` cell, when `handleCalendarInitialFocus` is called on the calendar element, then the January 1 cell receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar - edge cases > handles initial focus when no date is selected and today is out of view")
- Given a Melt calendar with `disabled: true`, when the first day of the month is clicked, then it does not have focus. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > disabled prop prevents calendar focus & interaction")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a multiple-selection Calendar whose `modelValue` holds 1980-01-02 and 1980-05-05, when rendered, then the heading reads `May 1980` (the placeholder follows the last value) and only one selected cell is visible in that month. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar - `multiple` > sets placeholder to last value in `value` prop")
- Given a Melt calendar with a `value` store holding a `CalendarDate`, when rendered, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `20` and the heading reads `January 1980`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > populated with controlled value - CalendarDate")
- Given a Melt calendar with a `value` store holding a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `20` and the heading reads `January 1980`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > populated with controlled value - CalendarDateTime")
- Given a Melt calendar with a `value` store holding a `ZonedDateTime`, when rendered, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `20` and the heading reads `January 1980`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > populated with controlled value - ZonedDateTime")
- Given a Melt calendar bound to an initially `undefined` `value` store, when the store is set to 1980-01-20 and then 2023-10-11, then the reported inside value reads `undefined`, then `1980-01-20`, then `2023-10-11`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > controlled value should update selected value")
- Given a Melt calendar with `defaultValue` 1980-01-20 and a controlled `placeholder` store, when the placeholder store is set to 2023-10-11, then the heading becomes `October 2023` while the value stays `1980-01-20`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > controlled placeholder should change view")
- Given a Melt multiple-selection calendar with a `value` store of two dates, when rendered, then two `[data-selected]` cells exist reading `2` and `5`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > multiple select controlled value")
- Given a Melt multiple-selection calendar with `defaultValue` of two dates, when rendered, then two `[data-selected]` cells exist reading `2` and `5`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > multiple select default Value")
- Given a Melt multiple-selection calendar with `defaultValue` of two dates, when rendered, then two `[data-selected]` cells exist. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > multiple select - allow deselect")
- Given a Melt multiple-selection calendar whose `onValueChange` returns the previous value when the next array exceeds two entries, when a third date is clicked after a second one, then the selection stays at two cells. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > overridable with multiple")
- Given a Melt single calendar whose `onValueChange` always returns 1980-01-25, when January 3 is clicked, then the `[data-selected]` cell reads `25`. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > overridable with single")
- Given a Melt calendar with default options, when the `numberOfMonths` option store is incremented, then a second grid appears alongside the first. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > dynamically change numberOfMonths option")
- Given a Melt calendar navigated forward until no sixth week row exists, when the `fixedWeeks` option store is toggled on, then a sixth week row appears. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > dynamically change fixedWeeks option")
- Given a Melt calendar with default options, when the `weekdayFormat` option store is cycled once and then again, then the weekday labels change from narrow to `Sun`-style short and then to `Sunday`-style long. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > dynamically change weekdayFormat option")
- Given a Bits calendar bound to a `CalendarDate` value, when the add-day, add-month and add-year buttons are clicked in turn, then the reported value walks `1980-01-21`, `1980-02-21`, `1981-02-21`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Value Handling > should bind to `value` - `CalendarDate`")
- Given a Bits calendar bound to a `CalendarDateTime` value, when the add-day, add-month and add-year buttons are clicked, then the reported value walks `1980-01-21`, `1980-02-21`, `1981-02-21`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Value Handling > should bind to `value` - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a Bits calendar bound to a `ZonedDateTime` value, when the add-day, add-month and add-year buttons are clicked, then the reported value walks `1980-01-21`, `1980-02-21`, `1981-02-21`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Value Handling > properly binds to `value` - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a Bits calendar with `value` 1980-01-20, when the external add-day button is clicked, then the selected day cell text changes from `20` to `21` and exactly one day stays selected. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Value Handling > should update the selected date when value controlled externally")
- Given a Bits calendar with a `CalendarDateTime` value whose time is set to 15:15:15.015, when the January 1 day is clicked, then the reported value keeps that time and only the day changes. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Value Handling > should persist time when selecting a date (CalendarDateTime)")
- Given a Bits calendar with a `ZonedDateTime` value whose time is set to 15:15:15.015, when the January 1 day is clicked, then the reported value keeps that time and zone and only the day changes. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Value Handling > should persist time when selecting a date (ZonedDateTime)")
- Given a Bits calendar bound to a `placeholder` of January 1980, when the add-month button is clicked, the add-year button, then add-month three more times, then the heading walks `February 1980`, `February 1981`, `May 1981`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Navigation > should change view when controlled placeholder changes")
- Given a Bits calendar with only `minValue` set two years in the future, when rendered with no value, then the heading shows February of that `minValue` year, so the default placeholder is clamped up to `minValue`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Navigation > should set default placeholder greater than `minValue`")
- Given a Bits calendar with only `maxValue` set two years in the past, when rendered with no value, then the heading shows November of that `maxValue` year, so the default placeholder is clamped down to `maxValue`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Navigation > should set default placeholder lower than `maxValue`")
- Given a Bits multiple-selection calendar whose values are 1980-01-02 and 1980-05-05, when rendered, then only one selected day is visible and the heading reads `May 1980`, so the placeholder follows the last value. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='multiple' > Value Handling > should set placeholder to last value in `value` prop")

### RTL and i18n
- Given a Bits calendar with `weekStartsOn: 2` and `weekdayFormat: 'short'`, when rendered, then the first head cell reads exactly `Tue`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Rendering Options > should respect the `weekStartsOn` prop")
- Given a Bits calendar with `weekStartsOn: 2`, `weekdayFormat: 'short'` and `locale: 'fr'`, when rendered, then the first head cell reads `mar.`, so the explicit `weekStartsOn` beats the locale default. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Rendering Options > should respect the `weekStartsOn` prop regardless of locale")
- Given a Bits calendar with `locale: 'fr'`, `weekdayFormat: 'short'` and no `weekStartsOn`, when rendered, then the first head cell reads `lun.`, so the locale's first weekday is used. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Rendering Options > should default the first day of the week to the locale's first day of the week if `weekStartsOn` is not provided")
- Given a Melt calendar with default options, when the `weekStartsOn` option store is advanced by one, then the weekday row rotates left by one so the previous first label moves to the end. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > dynamically change weekStartsOn option")
- Given a Melt calendar whose first weekday label is `S`, when the `locale` option store is set to `it`, then the first weekday label becomes `L`, so changing locale also changes the week start. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > dynamically changing the locale option also update weekStartsOn")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default Calendar, when the calendar element is run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a default Melt calendar, when the container is run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > Accessibility > has no accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a Calendar with `numberOfMonths: 2`, when the next button is clicked, then the previously rendered January 12 cell is removed from the document and reappears with the same `data-value` when prev is clicked once, so month grids are re-keyed rather than reused. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > displays multiple months when `numberOfMonths` is greater than 1")
- Given the Reka fixture, when `numberOfMonths` is greater than 1, then day test ids are prefixed by grid index (`date-<gridIndex>-<month>-<day>`) while single-month fixtures use `date-<month>-<day>`, so cross-grid focus assertions distinguish the two grids for the same date. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "numberOfMonths > 1 > handles minValue correctly using arrow keys")
- Given the Reka Vue fixture, when the controlled pattern is exercised, then the test wires `update:modelValue` to `rerender({ modelValue: data })`, and deselection tests depend on that round trip. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > allows dates to be deselected by clicking the selected date")
- Given the Reka test suite, when any `ZonedDateTime` assertion runs, then it runs under `process.env.TZ = 'US/Eastern'` pinned in `packages/core/vitest.setup.ts`, so `America/New_York` values line up with the ambient zone and `data-value` strings carry no offset surprises. (reka: packages/core/src/Calendar/Calendar.test.ts: "calendar > respects a default value if provided - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given the Melt builder, when `createCalendar` is destructured, then the fixture reads `elements` (`calendar`, `heading`, `grid`, `cell`, `prevButton`, `nextButton`), `states` (`value`, `months`, `headingValue`, `weekdays`) and `options` (`weekdayFormat`, `numberOfMonths`, `fixedWeeks`, `weekStartsOn`, `locale`), and the option stores are writable so the dynamic-option tests mutate them directly. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > dynamically change numberOfMonths option")
- Given the Melt fixture, when a day cell is rendered, then the `td` wrapper carries `role="gridcell"` while the `use:melt={$cell(...)}` div inside carries the `data-selected`, `data-disabled`, `data-unavailable`, `data-outside-month`, `data-outside-visible-months`, `data-range-highlighted` and `data-value` attributes the tests query. (melt: src/tests/calendar/Calendar.spec.ts: "Calendar > unavailable dates behavior")
- Given the Melt formatter test for a `CalendarDateTime`, when the expected string is built, then the time zone suffix is derived from the ambient `Intl` zone at run time rather than hardcoded, so the assertion is zone-independent; this is a unit test of the date helpers. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/date/tests/formatter.spec.ts: "Formatter > should properly format selected dates")
- Given the Bits Svelte 5 fixture, when the calendar is wired, then it uses `bind:placeholder` and `bind:value` on `Calendar.Root` with a `children` snippet receiving `{ months, weekdays }`, and external buttons mutate the bound value through `value.cycle(field, 1)`. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Value Handling > should bind to `value` - `CalendarDate`")
- Given the Bits helpers, when selected days are collected, then the selector is `[data-bits-day][data-selected]`, so only day triggers and not their cell wrappers are counted. (bits: tests/src/tests/helpers/calendar.ts)
- Given Bits browser tests navigating past a boundary, when a disabled prev or next button must still be clicked, then the tests use `click({ force: true })` because the element is marked `aria-disabled` and not pointer-interactive. (bits: tests/src/tests/calendar/calendar.browser.test.ts: "type='single' > Navigation > should not allow navigation before the `minValue` (prev button)")

## range-calendar

### Roles and attributes
- Given a RangeCalendar with `modelValue` of the `CalendarDate` range 1980-01-20 to 1980-01-25, when rendered, then six `[data-selected]` cells exist and the heading reads `January 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > respects a default value if provided - `CalendarDate`")
- Given a RangeCalendar with a `CalendarDateTime` range, when rendered, then six `[data-selected]` cells exist and the heading reads `January 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > respects a default value if provided - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a RangeCalendar with a `ZonedDateTime` range in `America/New_York`, when rendered, then six `[data-selected]` cells exist and the heading reads `January 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > respects a default value if provided - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a RangeCalendar with a selected range, when the endpoints are inspected, then `[data-selection-start]` reads `20` and `[data-selection-end]` reads `25`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > resets range on select when a range is already selected")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `placeholder` 1980-01-20 and `maximumDays: 5` after clicking January 20, when the pointer enters January 24, then exactly five cells have `data-highlighted`, January 20 has `data-highlighted-start`, January 24 has `data-highlighted-end` and January 25 has no `data-highlighted`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > caps highlighted range to maximumDays (forward)")
- Given the same calendar after clicking January 20, when the pointer enters January 16, then exactly five cells have `data-highlighted`, January 16 has `data-highlighted-start`, January 20 has `data-highlighted-end` and January 15 has no `data-highlighted`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > caps highlighted range to maximumDays (backward)")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `fixedWeeks: true`, when the next button is clicked 12 times and then 24 more times, then every view contains exactly six `[data-week]` rows. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > always renders six weeks when `fixedWeeks` is `true`")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `minValue` 1979-11-25, when the view reaches November 1979, then the prev button has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, and at December 1979 it has neither. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > should not allow navigation before the `minValue` (prev button)")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `maxValue` 1980-03-25, when the view reaches March 1980, then the next button has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, and at February 1980 it has neither. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > should not allow navigation after the `maxValue` (next button)")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the grid has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, the January 1 and January 10 cells each have `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, January 1 has no `tabindex`, and both navigation buttons are disabled. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > doesnt allow focus or interaction when `disabled` is `true`")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `isDateUnavailable` matching day 3, when rendered, then the January 3 cell reads `3`, has `data-unavailable` and has `aria-disabled="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > handles unavailable dates appropriately")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `weekdayFormat: 'narrow'`, when rendered, then the head cells read `S`, `M`, `T`, `W`, `T`, `F`, `S`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > formats the weekday labels correctly - `'narrow'`")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `weekdayFormat: 'short'`, when rendered, then the head cells read `Sun` through `Sat`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > formats the weekday labels correctly - `'short'`")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `weekdayFormat: 'long'`, when rendered, then the head cells read `Sunday` through `Saturday`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > formats the weekday labels correctly - `'long'`")
- Given a RangeCalendar with `numberOfMonths: 2` and a January range, when rendered, then the heading reads `January - February 1980`, the first selected cell reads `20`, the last reads `25`, the first grid's January 12 cell carries its `data-value` and the second grid's February 15 cell carries the matching February `data-value`. - Given a RangeCalendar with `placeholder` 1980-01-15 and `maximumDays: 5` after clicking January 15, when January 20 is clicked, then January 20 has `data-disabled` and no `data-selected` while January 19 has no `data-disabled`. ### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a RangeCalendar rendered with `modelValue: undefined`, when the prop is later set to a `ZonedDateTime` range, then the heading reads `January 1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > respects programmatically updated value")
- Given a RangeCalendar rendered with `modelValue: null`, when rendered and then updated to a `ZonedDateTime` range, then it starts with zero selected cells, does not throw, and ends with six selected cells. - Given a Melt range calendar with a `value` store holding a `CalendarDate` range, when rendered, then six `[data-selected]` cells exist and the heading reads `January 1980`. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > populated with controlled value - CalendarDate")
- Given a Melt range calendar with a `value` store holding a `CalendarDateTime` range, when rendered, then six `[data-selected]` cells exist and the heading reads `January 1980`. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > populated with controlled value - CalendarDateTime")
- Given a Melt range calendar with a `value` store holding a `ZonedDateTime` range, when rendered, then six `[data-selected]` cells exist and the heading reads `January 1980` (this test name duplicates the `CalendarDateTime` one in the file). (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > populated with controlled value - CalendarDateTime")
- Given a Melt range calendar bound to an initially `undefined` `value` store, when the store is set to the January 1980 range and then to 2023-08-10 through 2023-10-11, then the reported start and end walk `undefined`, `1980-01-20`/`1980-01-25`, then `2023-08-10`/`2023-10-11`. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > controlled value should update selected value")
- Given a Melt range calendar with `defaultValue` and a controlled `placeholder` store, when the placeholder store is set to 2023-10-11, then the heading becomes `October 2023` while the reported start and end stay `1980-01-20` and `1980-01-25`. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > controlled placeholder should change view")
- Given a Melt range calendar whose `onValueChange` always returns the February 25 to 27 range, when January 3 is clicked, then three cells end up selected. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > overridable store functions as expected")
- Given a Melt range calendar with default options, when the `numberOfMonths` option store is incremented, then a second grid appears. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > dynamically change numberOfMonths option")
- Given a Melt range calendar navigated until no sixth week row exists, when the `fixedWeeks` option store is toggled on, then a sixth week row appears. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > dynamically change fixedWeeks option")
- Given a Melt range calendar with default options, when the `weekdayFormat` option store is cycled twice, then the weekday labels go narrow, short, long. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > dynamically change weekdayFormat option")
- Given a Bits range calendar with only `minValue` set two years in the future, when rendered with no value, then the heading shows February of that year, so the default placeholder is clamped up to `minValue`. (bits: tests/src/tests/range-calendar/range-calendar.browser.test.ts: "should set default placeholder greater than `minValue`")
- Given a Bits range calendar with only `maxValue` set two years in the past, when rendered with no value, then the heading shows November of that year, so the default placeholder is clamped down to `maxValue`. (bits: tests/src/tests/range-calendar/range-calendar.browser.test.ts: "should set default placeholder lower than `maxValue`")

### RTL and i18n
- Given a Bits range calendar with `weekStartsOn: 2`, `weekdayFormat: 'short'` and `locale: 'fr'`, when rendered, then the first head cell reads `mar.`. (bits: tests/src/tests/range-calendar/range-calendar.browser.test.ts: "should respect the `weekStartsOn` prop regardless of locale")
- Given a Bits range calendar with `locale: 'fr'`, `weekdayFormat: 'short'` and no `weekStartsOn`, when rendered, then the first head cell reads `lun.`. (bits: tests/src/tests/range-calendar/range-calendar.browser.test.ts: "should default the first day of the week to the locale's first day of the week if `weekStartsOn` is not provided")
- Given a Melt range calendar with default options, when the `weekStartsOn` option store is advanced by one, then the weekday row rotates left by one. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > dynamically change weekStartsOn option")
- Given a Melt range calendar whose first weekday label is `S`, when the `locale` option store is set to `it`, then the first weekday label becomes `L`. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > dynamically changing the locale option also update weekStartsOn")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a mounted default RangeCalendar, when the root element is run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a RangeCalendar with the January 20 to 25 range, when the calendar is run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "handles maximumDays > a11y > should pass axe accessibility tests when closed")
- Given a RangeCalendar with no props, when the calendar element is clicked and run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "handles maximumDays > a11y > should pass axe accessibility tests when open")
- Given a default Melt range calendar, when the container is run through `axe`, then there are no accessibility violations. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > Accessibility > has no accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given the Reka range fixture, when `numberOfMonths` is greater than 1, then day test ids gain a grid-index prefix (`date-<gridIndex>-<month>-<day>`), and cross-grid arrow assertions rely on the same date existing in two grids. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "numberOfMonths > 1 > handles minValue correctly using arrow keys")
- Given a Reka `RangeCalendarPrev` rendered with `as="div"`, when it is disabled by `minValue`, then the click is inert even though a `div` has no native `disabled`, so the disabled behavior does not depend on the `button` element. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > does not navigate when prev is disabled and rendered as div")
- Given the Reka range tests, when hover previews are asserted, then some use `fireEvent.mouseEnter` plus `waitFor` and others use `user.hover`, and `maximumDays` capping is asserted through `data-highlighted-start`, `data-highlighted` and `data-highlighted-end`. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > caps highlighted range to maximumDays (forward)")
- Given the Reka controlled-range pattern, when the parent handles `update:modelValue`, then the tests re-render with `{ calendarProps: { modelValue: data } }`, and one test deliberately preserves the previous `end` to prove the component respects a parent-supplied end. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > keeps controlled end when parent preserves it after start edit")
- Given the Reka suite's pinned `process.env.TZ = 'US/Eastern'` from `packages/core/vitest.setup.ts`, when the `ZonedDateTime` range in `America/New_York` is rendered, then its day numbers match the ambient zone rather than shifting. (reka: packages/core/src/RangeCalendar/RangeCalendar.test.ts: "rangeCalendar > respects a default value if provided - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given the Melt range fixture, when the range state is reported, then `start-value` and `end-value` paragraphs print `$insideValue?.start` and `$insideValue?.end`, which is why a reset range shows `undefined` in both while the day cell still carries `data-selected`. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > selection after range selected resets range")
- Given the Melt range fixture, when a day is rendered, then the outer `td` carries `role="gridcell"` and the inner `use:melt={$cell(...)}` element carries `data-selected`, `data-focused`, `data-highlighted`, `data-disabled`, `data-unavailable` and `data-value`. (melt: src/tests/range-calendar/RangeCalendar.spec.ts: "Range Calendar > selection with keyboard")
- Given the Bits range fixture, when `minDays` or `maxDays` or `excludeDisabled` rejects a range, then the component never keeps a partial two-ended range: it collapses to the most recently clicked date as the new start with the end `undefined`. (bits: tests/src/tests/range-calendar/range-calendar.browser.test.ts: "minDays and maxDays constraints > should reset range when selection violates minDays constraint")
- Given the Bits range tests, when selected days are counted, then the selector is the shared `[data-bits-day][data-selected]`, so `data-selection-start` and `data-selection-end` are additive markers on top of `data-selected`. (bits: tests/src/tests/range-calendar/range-calendar.browser.test.ts: "range selection data attributes > should set correct data attributes for selected range")

## date-field

### Roles and attributes
- Given a date field with `modelValue` of `CalendarDate(1980, 1, 20)`, when rendered, then the `month`, `day`, and `year` segments show `1`, `20`, and `1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > populates segment with value - `CalendarDate`")
- Given a date field with `modelValue` of `CalendarDateTime(1980, 1, 20, 12, 30, 0, 0)`, when rendered, then the `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, and `minute` segments show `1`, `20`, `1980`, `12`, and `30`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > populates segment with value - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a date field with a `ZonedDateTime` in `America/New_York`, when rendered, then the `dayPeriod` segment shows `PM` and the `timeZoneName` segment shows `EST`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > populates segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a date field whose value is unavailable per `isDateUnavailable`, when the value is entered, then the root input element carries a bare `data-invalid` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > correctly marks the field as invalid if the value is invalid")
- Given a date field whose value is unavailable per `isDateUnavailable`, when the value is entered, then every segment (`month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `dayPeriod`, `timeZoneName`) carries `aria-invalid="true"` and `data-invalid`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > correctly marks the field as invalid if the value is invalid")
- Given a `disabled` date field, when each segment is inspected, then no segment has a `tabindex` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > prevents interaction when `disabled`")
- Given a date field, when a segment is inspected, then it carries `data-reka-date-field-segment` naming the segment part (`month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`). (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > prevents modification when `readonly`")
- Given a date field with `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then the `hour` segment has `aria-valuemin="1"` and `aria-valuemax="12"`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "useDateField – characterization tests (coverage gaps) > hourSegmentAttrs hourCycle=12 aria-value bounds (lines 129-130) > hour segment has aria-valuemin=1 and aria-valuemax=12 when hourCycle is 12")
- Given a date field with `hourCycle` of `24`, when rendered, then the `hour` segment has `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="23"`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "useDateField – characterization tests (coverage gaps) > hourSegmentAttrs hourCycle=12 aria-value bounds (lines 129-130) > hour segment has aria-valuemin=0 and aria-valuemax=23 when hourCycle is 24")
- Given a date field with no value, when rendered, then the `month`, `day`, and `year` segments show the placeholder text `mm`, `dd`, and `yyyy`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > should clear all segment when `modelValue` is set to nullish")
- Given a melt date field with `defaultValue` of `CalendarDate(1980, 1, 20)`, when rendered, then the `month`, `day`, `year` segments show `1`, `20`, `1980` and the `inside-value` readout shows `1980-01-20`. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > segments populated with defaultValue - CalendarDate")
- Given a melt date field with `defaultValue` of `CalendarDateTime(1980, 1, 20, 12, 30, 30, 0)`, when rendered, then `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute` show `1`, `20`, `1980`, `12`, `30` and the `inside-value` readout shows the `CalendarDateTime` string. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > segments populated with defaultValue - CalendarDateTime")
- Given a melt date field with a `ZonedDateTime` in `America/New_York`, when rendered, then the `dayPeriod` segment shows `PM`, the `timeZoneName` segment shows `EST`, and the `inside-value` readout shows the zoned string. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > segments populated with defaultValue - ZonedDateTime")
- Given a melt date field whose entered date is rejected by `isDateUnavailable`, when the full date is typed, then each of the `month`, `day`, `year` segments has `data-invalid` and `aria-invalid`. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > if selected date unavailable, mark field as invalid")
- Given a melt date field whose entered date is rejected by `isDateUnavailable`, when the full date is typed, then the `field` element has `data-invalid=""`. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > if selected date unavailable, mark field as invalid")
- Given a melt date field with an `ids` object supplying ids for `field`, `label`, `validation`, `description`, and every segment, when rendered, then each element's `id` equals the supplied id and a description element with the supplied id exists in the document. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given a melt date field with a custom `description` id, when rendered, then the `field` element's `aria-describedby` equals that description id. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given a bits date field with `modelValue`/`value` of `CalendarDate(1980, 1, 20)`, when rendered, then the `month`, `day`, `year` segments show `1`, `20`, `1980` and the value readout shows `1980-01-20`. - Given a bits date field with `value` of `CalendarDateTime(1980, 1, 20, 12, 30, 0, 0)`, when rendered, then the `hour` segment shows `12` and the `minute` segment shows `30`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should populate segment with value - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a bits date field with a `ZonedDateTime` in `America/New_York`, when rendered, then the `dayPeriod` segment shows `PM` and the `timeZoneName` segment shows `EST`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should populate segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a bits date field with a `validate` callback returning `"Invalid date"` for day 19, when `2`, `19`, `1111` are typed, then every segment has `aria-invalid="true"` and `data-invalid`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should marks the field as invalid if the value is invalid")
- Given a bits date field with a failing `validate`, when the invalid date is entered, then both the input wrapper and the label carry `data-invalid`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should marks the field as invalid if the value is invalid")
- Given a bits date field with a time granularity and no value, when rendered, then the `hour` segment shows the time placeholder `––`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not allow changing the dayPeriod without a value")

### Keyboard
- Given a date field with a `ZonedDateTime` and `granularity` of `second`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on each of `day`, `month`, `year`, `minute`, and `second`, then that segment shows the value cycled up by one. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > increments segment on arrow up")
- Given a date field whose `hour` shows `12` in a 12-hour cycle, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `hour`, then the `hour` segment shows `1`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > increments segment on arrow up")
- Given a date field with a `ZonedDateTime` and `granularity` of `second`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed on each of `day`, `month`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, and `second`, then that segment shows the value cycled down by one. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > decrements segment on arrow down")
- Given a date field whose `placeholder` is `CalendarDate(2025, 4, 30)` (a 30-day month), when `ArrowUp` is pressed twice on the `day` segment before any month is entered, then the `day` segment shows `31`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > allow the maximum day to be 31 when no month field")
- Given a date field with segments `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `dayPeriod`, `timeZoneName`, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly from `month`, then focus advances one segment at a time and stops on `timeZoneName`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > navigates segments using the arrow keys")
- Given focus on the last segment, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus moves back one segment at a time and stops on `month`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > navigates segments using the arrow keys")
- Given a date field with eight segments, when `Tab` is pressed repeatedly from `month`, then focus advances through each segment and ends on `timeZoneName`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > navigates the segments using tab")
- Given focus on the last segment, when `Shift+Tab` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks back through `dayPeriod`, `second`, `minute`, `hour`, `year`, `day`, `month`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > navigates the segments using tab")
- Given any of `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, when `0` is typed, then focus stays on that segment and only `Tab` moves it away. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > doesn't change focus prematurely with segment value of 0")
- Given any of `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, when `1` is typed, then focus stays on that same segment (no auto-advance on an ambiguous first digit). (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > doesn't change focus prematurely with segment value of 0")
- Given a date field with a `ZonedDateTime`, when `Backspace` is pressed on the `month` segment, then `month` shows `mm` while `day` and `year` keep their values. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > preserve other segment when one segment's value is deleted")
- Given a date field with a two-digit `day` value, when `Backspace` is pressed twice on `day`, then `day` shows `dd` and `year` still keeps its value. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > preserve other segment when one segment's value is deleted")
- Given a `readonly` date field, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on each of `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, then each segment still shows its original value from the model value. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > prevents modification when `readonly`")
- Given a date field with `hourCycle` of `24` and `hour` showing `12`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `hour`, then `hour` shows `13`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > adjusts the hour cycle with the `hourCycle` prop")
- Given a date field with `granularity` of `second`, when `3` is typed repeatedly starting in `month`, then focus advances after one keystroke in `month`, two in `day`, four in `year`, one in `hour`, two in `minute`, two in `second`, landing on `dayPeriod`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > takes you all the way through the segment with spamming 3")
- Given a date field whose `dayPeriod` is focused with a `CalendarDateTime` at 12:30 PM, when `a` is typed, then the model value moves back 12 hours; when `p` is typed, it returns to 12:30 PM. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > updates the hour on the modelValue if the dayPeriod is updated")
- Given a focused `dayPeriod` segment, when the uppercase `A` and `P` keys are typed, then the model value flips to AM and back to PM exactly as the lowercase keys do. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > updates the hour on the modelValue if the dayPeriod is updated")
- Given an empty `month` segment showing `mm`, when `Backspace` is pressed, then the segment stays empty and still shows `mm`. - Given a `year` segment showing `1980`, when `Backspace` is pressed once, then the `year` segment shows `198`. - Given a bits date field with a `ZonedDateTime` and `granularity` of `second`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed on each of `day`, `month`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, then that segment shows the cycled-down value. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should decrement segment on arrow down")
- Given a bits date field with eight segments, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly from `month`, then focus ends on `timeZoneName`, and `ArrowLeft` repeatedly walks it back to `month`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should navigate segments using the arrow keys")
- Given a bits date field with eight segments, when `Tab` is pressed repeatedly from `month`, then focus ends on `timeZoneName`, and `Shift+Tab` walks it back through each earlier segment. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should navigate the segments using tab")
- Given a `readonly` bits date field, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on each of `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second`, then each segment keeps the value read from the model value. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should prevent modification when `readonly`")
- Given a bits date field with `hourCycle` of `24` and `hour` showing `12`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then `hour` shows `13`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should adjust the hour cycle with the `hourCycle` prop")
- Given a bits date field with a 12:30 PM `CalendarDateTime`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `dayPeriod`, then `dayPeriod` shows `AM` and the value readout shows `1980-01-20T00:30`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should change the value when the dayPeriod segment is changed")
- Given a bits date field with `granularity` of `second`, when `3` is spammed from `month`, then focus advances after one keystroke in `month`, two in `day`, four in `year`, one in `hour`, two in `minute`, two in `second`, ending on `dayPeriod`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should go all the way through the segment with spamming 3")
- Given a bits `day` segment showing `20`, when `Backspace` is pressed, then it shows `2`; a second `Backspace` shows `dd` and keeps focus; a third `Backspace` moves focus to `month`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should move to the previous segment when backspace is pressed while empty - `day`")
- Given a bits `year` segment showing `1980`, when `Backspace` is pressed four times, then it shows `198`, `19`, `1`, then `yyyy` while keeping focus; a fifth `Backspace` moves focus to `day`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should to the previous segment when backspace is pressed while empty - `year`")
- Given a bits date field with no value, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on the `dayPeriod` segment, then the `hour` segment still shows the `––` placeholder (no value is created). (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not allow changing the dayPeriod without a value")
- Given a bits date field with `granularity` of `hour` and an empty `year`, when `0`, `0`, `9`, `8` are typed, then focus auto-advances to `hour`; `ArrowLeft` returns to `year`, `Backspace` twice shows `009` then `00`, and typing `8`, `7` yields `0087` and advances focus to `hour`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should handle backspacing the year segment appropriately")
- Given a bits `year` segment where `1` was typed then deleted, when `2` is typed, then `year` shows `2`, keeps focus, and the `hour` segment does not receive focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should keep focus on the year after correcting its first digit")
- Given a bits date field at 12:30 PM, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `dayPeriod`, then `hour` still shows `12` and `dayPeriod` shows `AM` (12 PM to 12 AM does not display hour 0). (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should allow going from 12PM -> 12AM without changing the display hour to 0")
- Given a 12-hour cycle field at 12 AM, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `hour`, then `hour` shows `01` and never `12`; flipping `dayPeriod` to PM keeps `01`, and `ArrowDown` on `hour` returns it to `12`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should never allow the hour to be 0 when in a 12 hour cycle")
- Given a bits date field with October 12, 2023, when `1` is typed in `month` and `ArrowRight` moves focus away, then `month` shows the zero-padded `01`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should add missing leading zeroes to the day,month, and year segments on focusout")
- Given `1` typed in `day` followed by `ArrowRight`, when focus lands on `year`, then `day` shows the zero-padded `01`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should add missing leading zeroes to the day,month, and year segments on focusout")
- Given a `year` segment reduced to `202` by `Backspace`, when `ArrowLeft` moves focus to `day`, then `year` shows the zero-padded `0202`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should add missing leading zeroes to the day,month, and year segments on focusout")
- Given a bits `month` segment holding `12`, when `Shift+1`, `Ctrl+2`, and `Meta+2` are pressed, then the segment still shows `12` (modified number keys are not intercepted). (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not intercept number keys when the ctrl or meta key is pressed, allowing default browser behavior")
- Given a bits date field with a 12-hour cycle, when `1` then `4` are typed into `hour`, then `hour` shows `04` and focus advances to `minute`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not allow typing 24 hour cycle hours when the hourcycle is 12")
- Given a 12-hour-cycle `hour` segment showing `04`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed four times, then `hour` shows `12` rather than `0`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not go to zero on arrow navigation with a 12 hour cycle")
- Given a bits `minute` segment, when `0` is typed twice, then the segment shows `00`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should allow double zeroes to be set in the minute segment")
- Given a bits `minute` segment, when `0` is typed twice, then focus advances to the `dayPeriod` segment. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should advance to the next segment when typing two zeroes into the minute segment")
- Given a bits `second` segment showing `30`, when `0` is typed twice, then the segment shows `00`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should allow double zeroes to be set in the second segment")
- Given a bits `second` segment, when `0` is typed twice, then focus advances to the `dayPeriod` segment. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should advance to the next segment when typing two zeroes into the second segment")
- Given a bits `dayPeriod` segment showing `PM`, when `i`, `d`, `k` are typed, then the segment still shows `PM`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not allow typing characters that are not `a` or `p` into the dayPeriod segment")
- Given each of the `day`, `month`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second` segments, when `i`, `d`, `k` are typed, then the segment text never becomes `idk`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not allow typing non-numeric characters into the date/time segments")
- Given a bits `dayPeriod` segment showing `PM`, when `Shift+a`, `Shift+p`, `a`, and `p` are typed in turn, then the segment shows `AM`, `PM`, `AM`, `PM`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should allow changing the day period with capital or lowercase `a` and `p`")
- Given an emptied bits `year` segment, when the digit `2` is typed six times, then the segment shows `2222` and never `222222`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not allow more than 4 digits in the year segment, even if the user types more")
- Given a bits date field with `hourCycle` of `24`, when `22` is typed into the focused `hour` segment, then `hour` shows `22`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should handle 24 hour time appropriately")
- Given a bits date field with `hourCycle` of `24`, when `00` is typed into the focused `hour` segment, then `hour` shows `00`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should allow 00 to be entered when hourCycle is 24")
- Given a bits date field with `hourCycle` of `24` and `hour` at `1`, when `ArrowDown` is pressed, then `hour` shows `00` and not the bare `0`; a further `ArrowDown` shows `23` and `ArrowUp` returns to `00`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > navigating to 00 with ArrowUp/Down when hourCycle is 24 should show 00 and not 0")
- Given a bits date field with `value` of October 12, 2023, when `Backspace` is pressed on the `year` segment, then `day` still shows `12` and `month` still shows `10`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not affect day/month segments when backspacing the year")

### Pointer
- Given a date field with a `ZonedDateTime`, when each of `day`, `month`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `dayPeriod`, `timeZoneName` is clicked, then that segment receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > focuses segments on click")
- Given a `disabled` date field, when each segment is clicked, then no segment receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > prevents interaction when `disabled`")
- Given a melt date field, when the `month` segment is clicked, then it receives focus. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > focuses first segment on click")
- Given a `disabled` melt date field, when the `month`, `day`, and `year` segments are clicked, then none of them receives focus. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > disabled prop prevents interaction")
- Given a bits date field with a `ZonedDateTime`, when each of `day`, `month`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `dayPeriod`, `timeZoneName` is clicked, then that segment receives focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should focus segments on click")
- Given a `disabled` bits date field, when a click is attempted on each segment, then the click is rejected as not actionable. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should prevent interaction when `disabled`")

### Focus management
- Given a date field with a `Label` bound by `for`/`id`, when the label is clicked, then the first child of the input container receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > focuses first segment on label click")
- Given a melt date field, when the label is clicked, then the `month` segment receives focus. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > clicking the label focuses the first segment")
- Given a bits date field, when the label is clicked, then the `month` segment receives focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should focus first segment on label click")
