### Forms
- Given a bits date field with a `name` prop, when rendered, then a hidden `input` exists with `name="date-field"` and `aria-hidden="true"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should render a hidden input if the `name` prop is passed")
- Given a bits date field without a `name` prop, when rendered, then no `input` element exists in the container. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not render a hidden input if the name prop isn't passed")
- Given a bits date field with a `name` and a `CalendarDateTime` value, when rendered, then the hidden input's value is the date string; pressing `ArrowUp` on `year` updates it to the value plus one year. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should keep the value of the hidden input in sync with the fields value")

### RTL and i18n
- Given a date field with `locale` of `en-UK`, when rendered, then the first, third, and fifth children of the input show `dd`, `mm`, `yyyy` (the even indices are literal separators). (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > changes segment positioning based on `locale`")
- Given a date field with `locale` of `en-UK` and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then no `dayPeriod` segment is in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > doesnt show the day period for locales that don't use them")
- Given a date field with the default locale and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then a `dayPeriod` segment is in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > does show the day period for locales that do use them")
- Given a date field with `dir` of `rtl`, when `2` is typed in `month`, then focus advances to `day`; typing `19` advances to `year`; typing `1980` leaves `year` showing `1980` (focus follows DOM order, not visual order). (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > advances focus through segments in DOM order when typing in RTL")
- Given a melt date field with `locale` of `en-UK`, when rendered, then the first, third, and fifth children of the field show `dd`, `mm`, `yyyy`. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > locale changes segment positioning")
- Given a melt date field with `locale` of `en-UK` and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then no `dayPeriod` segment exists. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > certain locales do not show day period segment")
- Given a melt date field with the default `en` locale and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then a `dayPeriod` segment exists. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > certain locales do show day period segment")
- Given a bits date field with `locale` of `en-UK`, when rendered, then the first, third, and fifth children of the input show `dd`, `mm`, `yyyy`; the assertion is skipped under WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should change segment positioning based on `locale`")
- Given a bits date field with `locale` of `en-UK` and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then no `dayPeriod` segment exists; the assertion is skipped under WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should not show the day period for locales that don't use them")
- Given a bits date field with the default locale and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then a `dayPeriod` segment exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should show the day period for locales that do use them")
- Given a bits date field with `locale` of `de-DE` and `granularity` of `minute`, when `3`, then `15`, then `23`, then `18` are typed into `hour`, then the segment shows `03`, `15`, `23`, `18` and no `dayPeriod` segment exists; the assertion is skipped under WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should allow typing hours 0-23 with non en-US locales that use 24-hour format")
- Given a bits date field with `locale` of `fr-FR` and `hour` at `14`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed nine times, then `hour` reaches `23`, a further `ArrowUp` wraps to `00`, and `ArrowDown` returns to `23`; the assertion is skipped under WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should allow arrow key navigation through full 0-23 range with 24-hour locales")
- Given a bits date field with `locale` of `sv-SE` and an 18:30 value, when rendered, then `hour` shows `18` with no `dayPeriod` segment; typing `20` shows `20` and `ArrowDown` shows `19`; the assertion is skipped under WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-field/date-field.browser.test.ts: "date field > should display and allow typing hours > 12 with sv-SE locale (24-hour format)")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default date field, when the container is run through `axe`, then no accessibility violations are reported. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a default melt date field, when the container is run through `axe`, then no accessibility violations are reported. (melt: src/tests/date-field/DateField.spec.ts: "DateField > Accessibility > has no accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a date field with `granularity` of `day` and a `CalendarDateTime` value, when rendered, then `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `dayPeriod` are absent and `month`, `day`, `year` are visible. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > overrides the default displayed segments with the `granularity` prop - `day`")
- Given a date field with `granularity` of `minute`, when rendered, then `second` is absent while `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `dayPeriod` are visible. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > overrides the default displayed segments with the `granularity` prop - `minute`")
- Given a date field with `modelValue` of `now('America/Los_Angeles')`, when rendered, then the `timeZoneName` segment shows `PDT` during daylight saving time and `PST` otherwise. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > displays correct timezone with ZonedDateTime value - `now`")
- Given a date field with `parseAbsoluteToLocal('2023-10-12T12:30:00Z')`, when rendered, then the `timeZoneName` segment shows the short zone name the host `Intl` resolves for that instant (`EDT` under the suite's pinned `TZ=US/Eastern`). (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > displays correct timezone with ZonedDateTime value - absolute -> local")
- Given a date field with `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` and `stepSnapping` enabled, when `23` is typed into `minute` and focus leaves, then `minute` shows `30`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > snaps typed minute value to nearest step")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` with snapping, when `15` is typed into `minute` and focus leaves, then `minute` stays `15`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > does not change typed minute value already on the step boundary")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 10 }` with snapping, when `26` is typed into `minute` and focus leaves, then `minute` shows `30`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > snaps typed minute value using custom step")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` with snapping, when `07` is typed into `minute` and focus leaves, then `minute` shows `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > snaps typed minute value down to the nearest step")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 1 }` with snapping, when `23` is typed into `minute` and focus leaves, then `minute` stays `23`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > does not snap typed minute value when step is 1")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 7 }` with snapping, when `23` is typed into `minute` and focus leaves, then `minute` shows `21`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > snaps typed minute value to nearest non-divisor step")
- Given `step` of `{ hour: 4 }`, `hourCycle` of `24`, and snapping, when `10` is typed into `hour` and focus leaves, then `hour` shows `12`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > snaps typed hour value to nearest step")
- Given `step` of `{ second: 7 }` with snapping, when `10` is typed into `second` and focus leaves, then `second` shows `7`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > snaps typed second value to nearest step")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` with `stepSnapping` false, when `23` is typed into `minute` and focus leaves, then `minute` stays `23`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "dateField > stepSnapping > does not snap typed values when stepSnapping is false")
- Given a focused segment, when a cancelable `beforeinput` with `inputType` of `insertText` and `isComposing` false is dispatched, then the event is default-prevented so the raw character cannot leak in (Safari fires `beforeinput` before `keydown` with an IME active). (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "handle IME composition > should block direct text insertion into the segment (Safari fires beforeinput before keydown with an IME active)")
- Given a focused segment, when a `beforeinput` with `inputType` of `insertCompositionText` and `isComposing` true is dispatched, then the event is not default-prevented. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "handle IME composition > should let composition input through beforeinput")
- Given a focused `day` segment, when a `keydown` with `key` of `1` and `keyCode` 229 (IME active but not composing) fires, then `day` shows `1`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "handle IME composition > should still apply a directly-typed digit when a CJK IME is active (keyCode 229, not composing)")
- Given a focused `day` segment, when a `keydown` with `key` of `Process`, `keyCode` 229 and `isComposing` true fires, then `day` still shows `dd`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "handle IME composition > should not update segment during IME keydown (keyCode 229)")
- Given a segment left unchanged by an IME `keydown`, when a `compositionend` carrying data `5` fires, then `day` shows `5`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateField/DateField.test.ts: "handle IME composition > should process committed digit after compositionend")

## date-range-field

### Roles and attributes
- Given a date range field with `modelValue` of start 2022-01-01 and end 2022-03-01, when rendered, then the start `month`, `day`, `year` show `1`, `1`, `2022` and the end ones show `3`, `1`, `2022`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > populates segment with value - `CalendarDate`")
- Given a date range field with `CalendarDateTime` values and `granularity` of `second`, when rendered, then both the start and end `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second` segments show the corresponding parts of each endpoint. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > populates segment with value - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a date range field with `ZonedDateTime` values in `America/New_York` and `granularity` of `second`, when rendered, then both start and end `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second` segments show the local wall-clock parts of each endpoint. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > populates segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a melt date range field with `defaultValue` of a `CalendarDate` range, when rendered, then every `start-` and `end-` prefixed `month`, `day`, `year` segment shows the matching part of its endpoint. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > segments populated with defaultValue - CalendarDate")
- Given a melt date range field with `defaultValue` of a `CalendarDateTime` range, when rendered, then both endpoints' `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute` segments are populated and `start-dayPeriod` shows `PM`. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > segments populated with defaultValue - CalendarDateTime")
- Given a melt date range field with `defaultValue` of a `ZonedDateTime` range, when rendered, then both endpoints' `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute` segments show the local wall-clock parts and `start-dayPeriod` shows `PM`. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > segments populated with defaultValue - ZonedDateTime")
- Given a melt date range field with `ids`, `startIds`, and `endIds`, when rendered, then the `field`, `label`, `validation` ids and every start and end segment id equal the supplied values. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given a melt date range field with a custom `description` id, when rendered, then a description element with that id exists and the `field` element's `aria-describedby` equals it. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given a bits date range field with a `CalendarDate` range, when rendered, then both endpoints' `month`, `day`, `year` segments and the `start-value`/`end-value` readouts match each endpoint. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `CalendarDate`")
- Given a bits date range field with a `CalendarDateTime` range and `granularity` of `second`, when rendered, then both endpoints' `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `second` segments and the value readouts match each endpoint. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a bits date range field with a `ZonedDateTime` range and `granularity` of `second`, when rendered, then both endpoints' segments show the local wall-clock parts and the value readouts show each endpoint's string. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")

### Keyboard
- Given a date range field with a `CalendarDate` range, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly from `start-month`, then focus walks `start-day`, `start-year`, `end-month`, `end-day`, `end-year` in order. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > navigates between the fields")
- Given a date range field, when `Tab` is pressed repeatedly from `start-month`, then focus walks `start-day`, `start-year`, `end-month`, `end-day`, `end-year` in order. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > navigates between the fields")
- Given focus on `end-year`, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks `end-day`, `end-month`, `start-year`, `start-day`, `start-month`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > navigates between the fields - right to left")
- Given focus on `end-year`, when `Shift+Tab` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks `end-day`, `end-month`, `start-year`, `start-day`, `start-month`. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > navigates between the fields - right to left")
- Given a date range field with a `CalendarDate` range, when `2` is typed into `start-month`, then `start-month` shows `2` and `end-month` keeps its original value. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > binds to the value")
- Given a melt date range field, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly from `start-month`, then focus walks through the remaining start segments and into the end segments in order. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > navigation between fields - left to right")
- Given a melt date range field, when `Tab` is pressed repeatedly from `start-month`, then focus walks through the remaining start segments and into the end segments in order. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > navigation between fields - left to right")
- Given focus on `end-year` in a melt date range field, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks backwards through the end segments and into the start segments. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > navigation between fields - right to left")
- Given focus on `end-year` in a melt date range field, when `Shift+Tab` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks backwards through the end segments and into the start segments. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > navigation between fields - right to left")
- Given a melt date range field with `readonlySegments` of `{ start: ['month'], end: ['month', 'year'] }`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `start-month`, then it keeps its original value. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > readonlySegments prop prevents modifying given segments")
- Given the same `readonlySegments` config, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `start-day`, then it increments by one. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > readonlySegments prop prevents modifying given segments")
- Given the same `readonlySegments` config, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `start-year`, then it increments by one. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > readonlySegments prop prevents modifying given segments")
- Given the same `readonlySegments` config, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `end-month`, then it keeps its original value. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > readonlySegments prop prevents modifying given segments")
- Given the same `readonlySegments` config, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `end-day`, then it increments by one. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > readonlySegments prop prevents modifying given segments")
- Given the same `readonlySegments` config, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `end-year`, then it keeps its original value. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > readonlySegments prop prevents modifying given segments")
- Given a bits date range field with a `CalendarDate` range, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly from `start-month`, then focus walks through the remaining start segments and into the end segments; `Tab` does the same. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should navigate between the fields")
- Given focus on `end-year` in a bits date range field, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks backwards into the start field; `Shift+Tab` does the same. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should navigate between the fields - right to left")
- Given a bits date range field, when `2142020` then `2152020` are typed starting at `start-month`, then the start value is `2020-02-14` and the end value is `2020-02-15`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate calendar date with keyboard")
- Given an empty bits date range field, when `2`, `02`, `2025`, `12`, `31`, `2025` are typed in sequence, then `end-day` shows `31`, the start value is `2025-02-02`, and the end value is `2025-12-31`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should allow valid days in end month regardless of start month")
- Given a bits date range field prepopulated with end 2025-05-31, when `end-day` is focused and `ArrowDown` is pressed, then it shows `30`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should allow valid days in end month when a value is prepopulated")

### Pointer
- Given a bits date range field with a `CalendarDate` range, when `start-month` is clicked and `2` typed, then the start value becomes `2022-02-01` while the end value is unchanged. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should respect `bind:value` to the value")

### Focus management
- Given a melt date range field, when the label is clicked, then `start-month` receives focus. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > clicking the label focuses the first segment")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a melt date range field whose `onValueChange` returns a fixed override range, when `ArrowDown` is pressed on `start-day`, then both the `start-value` and `end-value` readouts show the override range rather than the decremented start. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > overridable store functions as expected")

### Forms
- Given a bits date range field with `startProps.name` of `start-hidden-input` and `endProps.name` of `end-hidden-input`, when rendered, then an `input` with each of those names is in the document. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should render an input for the start and end")

### RTL and i18n
- Given a date range field with `dir` of `rtl`, when `2` is typed in `start-month`, then focus moves to `start-day`; typing `19` moves to `start-year`; typing `1980` moves focus to `end-month` (DOM order, not visual order). (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > advances focus through segments in DOM order when typing in RTL")
- Given a bits date range field with `locale` of `en-GB`, a start in a 30-day month and an end in a 31-day month, when `31` is typed into `end-day`, then `end-day` shows `31`, the end value is `2026-08-31`, and the start value stays `2024-11-01`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should allow valid days in the end month with a day-first locale")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default date range field, when the container is run through `axe`, then no accessibility violations are reported. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a default melt date range field, when the container is run through `axe`, then no accessibility violations are reported. (melt: src/tests/date-range-field/DateRangeField.spec.ts: "DateField > Accessibility > has no accessibility violations")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a reka `DateRangeFieldInput`, when it is rendered, then it requires a `type` prop of `start` or `end` to bind the segment to the matching endpoint, and `literal` parts are rendered as non-interactive segments. (reka: packages/core/src/DateRangeField/DateRangeField.test.ts: "dateField > populates segment with value - `CalendarDate`")
- Given a bits `DateRangeField.Root`, when rendered, then each `DateRangeField.Input` takes a `type` of `start` or `end` and exposes its `segments` through a `children` snippet. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-range-field/date-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `CalendarDate`")

## time-field

### Roles and attributes
- Given a time field with `modelValue` of `Time(9, 15, 29)`, when rendered, then the `hour` segment shows `9`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > populates segment with value - `Time`")
- Given a time field with `modelValue` of `CalendarDateTime(1980, 1, 20, 12, 30, 0, 0)`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `12` and `minute` shows `30`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > populates segment with value - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a time field with a `ZonedDateTime` in `America/New_York`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `12`, `minute` shows `30`, `dayPeriod` shows `PM`, and `timeZoneName` shows `EST`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > populates segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a `disabled` time field, when each segment is inspected, then no segment has a `tabindex` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > prevents interaction when `disabled`")

- Given a time field with `granularity` of `second` and no value, when the `minute` segment is inspected, then it has `data-placeholder=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "useDateField – time segment characterization tests (coverage gaps) > backspace on empty/null time segments (lines 785, 814, 842) > backspace on an empty minute segment is a no-op (data-placeholder stays)")
- Given a time field with `modelValue` of `Time(9, 30, 0)`, when the `hour` segment is inspected, then it has no `data-placeholder` attribute. - Given a bits time field with `value` of `Time(12, 30, 0, 0)`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `12`, `minute` shows `30`, and the value readout shows the time string. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `Time`")
- Given a bits time field with a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `12`, `minute` shows `30`, `dayPeriod` shows `PM`, and the readout shows the date-time string. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a bits time field with a `ZonedDateTime` in `America/New_York`, when rendered, then `dayPeriod` shows `PM` and `timeZoneName` shows `EST`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a bits time field with `minValue` of 12:30 and value 12:30, when `ArrowDown` moves the hour below the minimum, then `hour` has `aria-invalid="true"` and both the input and the label carry `data-invalid`. - Given a bits time field with `maxValue` of 12:30 and value 12:30, when `ArrowUp` moves the hour above the maximum, then `hour` has `aria-invalid="true"` and both the input and the label carry `data-invalid`. - Given a bits time field with `hideTimeZone` false and a `ZonedDateTime`, when rendered, then a `timeZoneName` segment exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should show timezone when hideTimeZone is false")

### Keyboard
- Given a time field with a `ZonedDateTime` at 12:30:00 PM and `granularity` of `second`, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `hour`, then `hour` shows `1`; `minute` and `second` each show their cycled-up value. ### Pointer
- Given a time field with a `ZonedDateTime`, when each of `hour`, `minute`, `dayPeriod`, `timeZoneName` is clicked, then that segment receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > focuses segments on click")
- Given a `disabled` time field, when each segment is clicked, then none receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > prevents interaction when `disabled`")
- Given a bits time field with a `ZonedDateTime`, when each of `hour`, `minute`, `dayPeriod`, `timeZoneName` is clicked, then that segment receives focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should focus segments on click")
- Given a `disabled` bits time field, when each segment is force-clicked, then none receives focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should prevent interaction when `disabled`")

### Focus management
- Given a time field with a `Label` bound by `for`/`id`, when the label is clicked, then the first child of the input container receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > focuses first segment on label click")
- Given a bits time field, when the label is clicked, then the `hour` segment receives focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should focus first segment on label click")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a time field with `hour` showing `12`, when it is clicked and `3` typed, then the segment fully replaces its value with `3`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > fully overwrites on first click and type - `hour`")
- Given a bits `hour` segment showing `12`, when clicked and `1` typed, then it shows `1`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should overwrite on first click and type - `hour`")
- Given a bits `minute` segment showing `30`, when clicked and `1` typed, then it shows `1`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should overwrite on first click and type - `minute`")
- Given a bits `second` segment showing `0`, when clicked and `1` typed, then it shows `1`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should overwrite on first click and type - `second`")
- Given a bits time field bound with `bind:value`, when an external reset button sets the value to `undefined`, then `hour` and `minute` revert to `––`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should reset the segment values when the value is reset")
- Given a bits time field whose `value` is a `CalendarDateTime`, when `ArrowUp` changes the hour, then `onValueChange` receives a `CalendarDateTime` instance with a defined `day` and no `timeZone`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should type the onValueChange callback with the type of the provided value (CalendarDateTime)")
- Given a bits time field whose `value` is a `Time`, when `ArrowUp` changes the hour, then `onValueChange` receives a `Time` instance with a defined `hour` and no `day`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should type the onValueChange callback with the type of the provided value (Time)")
- Given a bits time field whose `value` is a `ZonedDateTime`, when `ArrowUp` changes the hour, then `onValueChange` receives a `ZonedDateTime` instance with defined `hour` and `timeZone`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should type the onValueChange callback with the type of the provided value (ZonedDateTime)")

### Forms
- Given a bits time field with a `name` prop, when rendered, then a hidden input exists with `name="time-field"` and `aria-hidden="true"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should render a hidden input if the `name` prop is passed")
- Given a bits time field without a `name` prop, when rendered, then no `input[aria-hidden]` element exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should not render a hidden input if the name prop isn't passed")
- Given a bits time field with a `name` and a `CalendarDateTime` value, when rendered, then the hidden input's value is the extracted `Time` string; `ArrowUp` on `hour` updates it to the time plus one hour. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should keep the value of the hidden input in sync with the fields value")

### RTL and i18n
- Given a time field with `dir` of `rtl`, when `11` is typed into `hour`, then focus advances to `minute` (DOM order, not visual order). (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > advances focus through segments in DOM order when typing in RTL")
- Given a time field with `locale` of `en-UK` and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then no `dayPeriod` segment is in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > doesn't show the day period for locales that don't use them")
- Given a time field with the default locale and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then a `dayPeriod` segment is in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > does show the day period for locales that do use them")
- Given a time field with `locale` of `zh-TW` and `hideTimeZone` true, when rendered, then the input text contains neither `[` nor `]`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > filter time zone brackets for specific locales")
- Given a bits time field with `locale` of `en-UK` and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then no `dayPeriod` segment exists; the assertion is skipped under WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should not show the day period for locales that don't use them")
- Given a bits time field with the default locale and a `CalendarDateTime`, when rendered, then a `dayPeriod` segment exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should show the day period for locales that do use them")
- Given a bits time field with `locale` of `en-UK` and a value of 13:30, when rendered, then `hour` shows `13` (24-hour clock by default for that locale); the assertion is skipped under WebKit. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should default to a 24 hour clock for locales that use it")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default time field, when the container is run through `axe`, then no accessibility violations are reported. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a time field with `granularity` of `hour`, when rendered, then `minute` and `second` are absent and `hour` is visible. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > overrides the default displayed segments with the `granularity` prop - `hour`")
- Given a time field with `granularity` of `minute`, when rendered, then `second` is absent and `hour`, `minute`, `dayPeriod` are visible. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > overrides the default displayed segments with the `granularity` prop - `minute`")
- Given a time field with `modelValue` of `now('America/Los_Angeles')`, when rendered, then `timeZoneName` shows `PDT` in daylight saving time and `PST` otherwise. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > displays correct timezone with ZonedDateTime value - `now`")
- Given a time field with `parseAbsoluteToLocal('2023-10-12T12:30:00Z')`, when rendered, then `timeZoneName` shows the short zone name the host `Intl` resolves for that instant (`EDT` under the suite's pinned `TZ=US/Eastern`). (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > displays correct timezone with ZonedDateTime value - absolute -> local")
- Given `Time(0, 30, 0)` with `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `12` and `dayPeriod` shows `AM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > 12-hour format display > displays midnight (hour 0) as 12 AM")
- Given `Time(12, 30, 0)` with `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `12` and `dayPeriod` shows `PM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > 12-hour format display > displays noon (hour 12) as 12 PM")
- Given `Time(13, 30, 0)` with `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `1` and `dayPeriod` shows `PM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > 12-hour format display > converts afternoon hours (13-23) to 12-hour format")
- Given `Time(23, 30, 0)` with `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `11` and `dayPeriod` shows `PM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > 12-hour format display > converts late evening hour (23) to 11 PM")
- Given `Time(9, 30, 0)` with `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `9` and `dayPeriod` shows `AM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > 12-hour format display > displays morning hours (1-11) correctly")
- Given `CalendarDateTime(2024, 1, 15, 15, 45, 0, 0)` with `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `3` and `dayPeriod` shows `PM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > 12-hour format display > works with CalendarDateTime values")
- Given a `ZonedDateTime` at midnight in `America/New_York` with `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then `hour` shows `12` and `dayPeriod` shows `AM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > 12-hour format display > works with ZonedDateTime values")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` and `stepSnapping` true, when `23` is typed into `minute`, then it shows `30`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > stepSnapping > snaps typed minute value to nearest step")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` and `stepSnapping` true, when `17` is typed into `minute`, then it shows `15`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > stepSnapping > snaps typed minute value down to nearest step")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` and `stepSnapping` false, when `23` is typed into `minute`, then it stays `23`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > stepSnapping > does not snap typed values when stepSnapping is false")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` and `stepSnapping` false with `minute` at 0, when `ArrowUp` is pressed, then `minute` shows `15` (arrows always use the step). (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > stepSnapping > arrow keys still use step regardless of stepSnapping setting")
- Given `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` and `stepSnapping` true, when `58` is typed into `minute`, then it snaps down to `45`, the last step before 60. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "timeField > stepSnapping > snaps to max boundary when value exceeds max")
- Given `step` of `{ hour: 6 }` with `stepSnapping` and an hour of 9, when `7` is typed into `hour` so focus leaves, then the snapped hour 6 sets `dayPeriod` to `AM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "useDateField – time segment characterization tests (coverage gaps) > handleSegmentFocusOut – hour step snapping with dayPeriod (lines 927-931) > hour step snap sets dayPeriod to AM when snapped value < 12")
- Given `step` of `{ hour: 6 }` with `stepSnapping` and an hour of 14, when `2` is typed into `hour` so focus leaves, then the snapped hour 12 sets `dayPeriod` to `PM`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "useDateField – time segment characterization tests (coverage gaps) > handleSegmentFocusOut – hour step snapping with dayPeriod (lines 927-931) > hour step snap sets dayPeriod to PM when snapped value >= 12")
- Given `step` of `{ second: 15 }` with `stepSnapping`, when `17` is typed into `second` and focus leaves, then it shows `15`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "useDateField – time segment characterization tests (coverage gaps) > handleSegmentFocusOut – hour step snapping with dayPeriod (lines 927-931) > second step snapping works on focusout")
- Given an empty time field with `step` of `{ minute: 15 }` and `stepSnapping`, when `3` is typed into `minute` and `Tab` moves focus away, then nothing throws and the `minute` segment keeps a value (no model update, because not every segment is filled). (reka: packages/core/src/TimeField/TimeField.test.ts: "useDateField – time segment characterization tests (coverage gaps) > handleSegmentFocusOut – not all segments filled skips modelValue update (line 941) > partial fill with stepSnapping does not crash and preserves partial values")
- Given a bits time field with `granularity` of `hour`, when rendered, then `minute` and `second` are absent and `hour` is visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should override the default displayed segments with the `granularity` prop - `'hour'`")
- Given a bits time field with `granularity` of `second`, when rendered, then `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `dayPeriod` are all visible. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should override the default displayed segments with the `granularity` prop - `'second'`")
- Given a bits time field with `parseAbsoluteToLocal('2023-10-12T12:30:00Z')`, when rendered, then `timeZoneName` shows the short zone name the host `Intl` resolves for that instant. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "displays correct timezone with ZonedDateTime value - absolute -> local")
- Given a bits time field with `hourCycle` of `24` and an hour of 0, when rendered, then `hour` shows `00`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-field/time-field.browser.test.ts: "should display correct hour when prepopulated with value and hourCycle is 24")

## time-range-field

### Roles and attributes
- Given a time range field with `modelValue` of start 09:15:29 and end 17:45 and `locale` of `en-GB`, when rendered, then `start-hour` shows `09` and `end-hour` shows `17`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > populates segment with value - `Time`")
- Given a time range field with `CalendarDateTime` endpoints and `locale` of `en-GB`, when rendered, then `start-hour` shows `9`, `start-minute` shows `15`, `end-hour` shows `17`, and `end-minute` shows `45`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > populates segment with value - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a time range field with `ZonedDateTime` endpoints, `locale` of `en-US`, and `hourCycle` of `12`, when rendered, then `start-hour` shows `9` with `start-dayPeriod` of `AM`, `end-hour` shows `5` with `end-dayPeriod` of `PM`, and both `start-timeZoneName` and `end-timeZoneName` show `EST`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > populates segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given a time range field with start 17:00 and end 09:00 (start after end), when rendered, then the root input has `data-invalid=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > displays data-invalid when start is after end")
- Given a time range field with a valid ascending range, when rendered, then the root input has no `data-invalid` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > does not display data-invalid for valid range")
- Given a time range field with `minValue` of 10:00 and a start of 09:15, when rendered, then the root input has `data-invalid=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > displays data-invalid when value is outside min/max")
- Given a bits time range field with `Time` endpoints 12:30 and 17:30 and `granularity` of `second`, when rendered, then the start segments show `12`, `30`, `0` with `start-dayPeriod` of `PM`, the end `hour` shows `05` with `end-dayPeriod` of `PM`, and the end value readout shows `17:30:00`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `Time`")
- Given a bits time range field with `CalendarDateTime` endpoints and `granularity` of `second`, when rendered, then both endpoints' `hour`, `minute`, `second` segments and `dayPeriod` of `PM` match, and each value readout shows the endpoint string. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given a bits time range field with `ZonedDateTime` endpoints and `granularity` of `second`, when rendered, then both endpoints' segments match the local wall clock, both `dayPeriod` segments show `PM`, and both `timeZoneName` segments show `EST`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")

### Keyboard
- Given a time range field with `locale` of `en-GB`, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly from `start-hour`, then focus walks `start-minute`, `end-hour`, `end-minute`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > navigates between the fields")
- Given the same field, when `Tab` is pressed repeatedly from `start-hour`, then focus walks `start-minute`, `end-hour`, `end-minute`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > navigates between the fields")
- Given focus on `end-minute`, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks `end-hour`, `start-minute`, `start-hour`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > navigates between the fields - right to left")
- Given focus on `end-minute`, when `Shift+Tab` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks `end-hour`, `start-minute`, `start-hour`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > navigates between the fields - right to left")
- Given a time range field with start 09:15 and end 17:45, when `2` is typed into `start-minute`, then it shows `2` and `end-minute` keeps `45`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > binds to the value")
- Given a time range field, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `end-hour`, then `start-hour` still shows `09` and `start-minute` still shows `15`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > modifying end value does not affect start value")
- Given a time range field with a start hour of 9, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `start-hour`, then it shows `10`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > increments start hour on arrow up")
- Given a time range field with an end minute of 45, when `ArrowDown` is pressed on `end-minute`, then it shows `44`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > decrements end minute on arrow down")
- Given a time range field, when `1` then `4` are typed into `start-hour`, then it shows `14`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > types a digit into start segment")
- Given a time range field, when `3` then `0` are typed into `end-minute`, then it shows `30`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > types a digit into end segment")
- Given a `readonly` time range field, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `start-hour`, then it keeps `09`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > prevents modification when readonly")
- Given a `readonly` time range field, when `ArrowUp` is pressed on `end-hour`, then it keeps `17`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > prevents modification when readonly")
- Given a time range field, when `0` then `9` are typed into `start-hour`, then focus advances to `start-minute`; typing `1` then `5` there advances focus to `end-hour`. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > navigates from start to end with keyboard typing")
- Given a bits time range field with `granularity` of `second` and `locale` of `en-US`, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly from `start-hour`, then focus walks the remaining start segments (`minute`, `second`, `dayPeriod`) and then all four end segments. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should navigate between the fields")
- Given the same field, when `Tab` is pressed repeatedly from `start-hour`, then focus walks the same order as `ArrowRight`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should navigate between the fields")
- Given focus on `end-dayPeriod`, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks back through `end-second`, `end-minute`, `end-hour` and then the start segments in reverse. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should navigate between the fields - right to left")
- Given focus on `end-dayPeriod`, when `Shift+Tab` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks back in the same order as `ArrowLeft`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should navigate between the fields - right to left")
- Given a bits time range field at start 12:30 PM in 12-hour mode, when `2` is typed into `start-hour`, then the start value becomes `14:30:00` and the end value is unchanged. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should respect `bind:value` to the value")
- Given a bits time range field with `hourCycle` of `24` and a start of 14:30, when `2` is typed into `start-hour`, then the start value becomes `02:30:00` and the end value stays `17:30:00`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should keep 24 hour semantics when typing the start hour with hourCycle 24")
- Given a bits time range field, when `1`, `2` are typed into `start-hour`, then focus advances to `start-minute`; `3`, `4` there advance focus to `start-dayPeriod`; `P` then `ArrowRight` moves focus to `end-hour`; `1`, `2`, `3`, `5` fill the end hour and minute and advance to `end-dayPeriod`, leaving the start value `12:34:00` and the end value `12:35:00`. (bits: tests/src/tests/time-range-field/time-range-field.browser.test.ts: "should populate calendar date with keyboard")

### Pointer
- Given a `disabled` time range field, when each of `start-hour`, `start-minute`, `end-hour`, `end-minute` is clicked, then none receives focus. (reka: packages/core/src/TimeRangeField/TimeRangeField.test.ts: "timeField > prevents interaction when disabled")

## date-picker

### Roles and attributes
- Given a date picker with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the trigger is disabled and the `day`, `month` and `year` segments have no `tabindex` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts: "prevents interaction and picker to be opened when `disabled` is `true`")
- Given an open picker whose `isDateUnavailable` returns true for day 3, when the cell for January 3 is inspected, then it has text `3`, `data-unavailable` and `aria-disabled="true"`, and clicking it throws (not clickable) and leaves it without `data-selected`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should handle unavailable dates appropriately")
- Given an open picker whose `isDateDisabled` returns true for day 5, when the cell for January 5 is inspected, then it has text `5`, `data-disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"` and clicking it throws (not clickable). (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should handle disabled dates correctly")
- Given an open picker with `minValue` November 25 1979 and value January 20 1980, when the prev button is clicked once to December 1979, then the prev button has neither `aria-disabled="true"` nor `data-disabled`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should not allow navigation before the `minValue` (prev button)")
- Given that same picker, when the prev button is clicked again to November 1979, then the prev button gains `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled` and a further click throws while the heading stays `November 1979`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should not allow navigation before the `minValue` (prev button)")
- Given an open picker with `maxValue` March 25 1980, when the next button is clicked once to February 1980, then the next button has neither `aria-disabled="true"` nor `data-disabled`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should not allow navigation after the `maxValue` (next button)")
- Given that same picker, when the next button is clicked again to March 1980, then the next button gains `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled` and a further click throws while the heading stays `March 1980`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should not allow navigation after the `maxValue` (next button)")
- Given a picker with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the trigger element is disabled. (melt: src/tests/date-picker/DatePicker.spec.ts: "trigger is disabled when `disabled` prop is true")
- Given `dateFieldIds` overrides for every field part, when the picker is opened, then the `month`, `day`, `year`, `hour`, `minute`, `dayPeriod`, `timeZoneName`, `field`, `label` and `validation` elements each carry the supplied `id`. (melt: src/tests/date-picker/DatePicker.spec.ts: "custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given `dateFieldIds.description`, when the picker is opened, then the field element's `aria-describedby` equals that id and an element with that id exists in the document. (melt: src/tests/date-picker/DatePicker.spec.ts: "custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given `popoverIds` overrides, when the picker is opened, then the content element's `id` is `id-content` and the trigger element's `id` is `id-trigger`. (melt: src/tests/date-picker/DatePicker.spec.ts: "custom ids are applied when provided")
- Given `calendarIds` overrides, when the picker is opened, then the calendar element's `id` is `id-calendar` and an accessible heading element with id `id-heading` exists in the document. (melt: src/tests/date-picker/DatePicker.spec.ts: "custom ids are applied when provided")

### Keyboard
- Given a focused trigger, when `Enter` is pressed, then the popover content exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should open on %s" with `kbd.ENTER`)
- Given a focused trigger, when `Space` is pressed, then the popover content exists. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should open on %s" with `kbd.SPACE`)
- Given a `ZonedDateTime` value with `granularity: 'second'`, when each of the `day`, `month`, `year`, `hour`, `minute` and `second` segments is focused and `ArrowUp` pressed, then that segment shows the value cycled up by one (the hour reads `1` after cycling from 12 PM). (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts: "increments segment on arrow up")
- Given a `ZonedDateTime` value with `granularity: 'second'`, when each of the `day`, `month`, `year`, `hour`, `minute` and `second` segments is focused and `ArrowDown` pressed, then that segment shows the value cycled down by one. (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts: "decrements segment on arrow down")
- Given a `ZonedDateTime` value with `granularity: 'second'` and focus on the month segment, when `ArrowRight` is pressed repeatedly, then focus moves month, day, year, hour, minute, second, dayPeriod, timeZoneName and finally to the trigger. (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts: "navigates segments using the arrow keys")
- Given focus on the trigger after walking right, when `ArrowLeft` is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks back through timeZoneName, dayPeriod, second, minute, hour, year, day and ends on the month segment. - Given an open picker with `fixedWeeks: true`, when the next button is clicked sixteen times, then every month renders exactly six `[data-week]` rows. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts: "should render six weeks when `fixedWeeks` is `true`")
- Given `fixedWeeks: false` and the calendar advanced until no sixth week renders, when the `fixedWeeks` option store is toggled to true, then a sixth week row appears. (melt: src/tests/date-picker/DatePicker.spec.ts: "dynamically change fixedWeeks option even if fixedWeeks option is set")
- Given `numberOfMonths: 1`, when the `numberOfMonths` option store is incremented, then a second grid element appears alongside the first. (melt: src/tests/date-picker/DatePicker.spec.ts: "dynamically change numberOfMonths option even if numberOfMonths is specified as an option")
- Given `granularity: 'minute'` and a `CalendarDateTime` model value that is then set to `undefined` by the parent, when the picker is opened and January 1 selected, then the emitted value is a `CalendarDateTime` whose hour, minute, second and millisecond are all `0` rather than the stale placeholder time. (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts: "resets stale placeholder time when selecting a date after the model value is cleared")
- Given `granularity: 'second'` and a zoned model value that is then set to `undefined`, when the picker is opened and January 1 selected, then the emitted value keeps `timeZone` `America/New_York` and has hour, minute, second and millisecond all `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts: "resets stale ZonedDateTime placeholder time when selecting a date after the model value is cleared")
- Given `granularity: 'minute'` with the model value cleared to `undefined` and the parent echoing every `update:modelValue` back as the new `modelValue`, when `2`, `3`, `2020`, `9` and `45` are typed into the month, day, year, hour and minute segments, then those segments read `2`, `3`, `2020`, `9` and `45`, so typed time is not overwritten by a placeholder reset. (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts: "preserves typed time when typing a date after the model value is cleared")
- Given the reka test fixture, when any test renders it, then the root defaults to `granularity="second"` and `isDateUnavailable` marking every 19th day unavailable, which every test in the file inherits unless it overrides those props. (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/story/_DatePicker.vue via packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts)
- Given reka's vitest setup pinning `process.env.TZ` to `US/Eastern`, when a `ZonedDateTime` in `America/New_York` is rendered, then the `timeZoneName` segment resolves to `EST` and the day period to `PM`; the same assertion would differ under another host timezone. (reka: packages/core/src/DatePicker/DatePicker.test.ts: "populates segment with value - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given melt's builder return shape, when `createDatePicker` is destructured, then `elements` supplies `calendar`, `heading`, `grid`, `cell`, `field`, `prevButton`, `nextButton`, `segment`, `trigger`, `content`, `label` and `validation`, `states` supplies `value`, `months`, `headingValue`, `weekdays` and `segmentContents`, and `options` exposes writable `locale`, `weekdayFormat`, `numberOfMonths`, `fixedWeeks` and `weekStartsOn` stores that the dynamic-option tests mutate directly. (melt: src/tests/date-picker/DatePickerTest.svelte via src/tests/date-picker/DatePicker.spec.ts)
- Given bits' test component, when `open` is bound and a `clear` button sets `value = undefined`, then the picker's open state and value are both controlled from outside through Svelte 5 `bind:` on `DatePicker.Root`. (bits: tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker-test.svelte via tests/src/tests/date-picker/date-picker.browser.test.ts)

## month-picker

### Roles and attributes
- Given a month picker with `placeholder`, when the January cell trigger is rendered, then its `month` attribute is `null`, so the `month` prop is not forwarded as a DOM attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "does not forward month prop as a DOM attribute")
- Given `isMonthUnavailable` returning true for month 3, when the March cell trigger is inspected, then it has text `Mar`, `data-unavailable` and `aria-disabled="true"`, and clicking it leaves it without `data-selected`. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "handles unavailable months appropriately")
- Given `isMonthDisabled` returning true for month 3, when the March cell trigger is inspected, then it has text `Mar`, `data-disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"`, and clicking it leaves it without `data-selected`. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "handles disabled months appropriately")
- Given `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the grid has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, the January cell trigger has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, and the prev and next buttons are both disabled. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "doesnt allow focus or interaction when `disabled` is `true`")
- Given `readonly: true`, when rendered, then the grid has `aria-readonly="true"` and `data-readonly`. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "prevents selection but allows focus when `readonly` is `true`")
- Given `minValue` of June 1 1979, when the prev button has paged back to 1979, then it has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "should not allow navigation before the `minValue` (prev button)")
- Given `maxValue` of June 30 1981, when the next button has paged forward to 1981, then it has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "should not allow navigation after the `maxValue` (next button)")

- Given a placeholder of January 1980 and focus on the January cell, when `ArrowRight` is pressed, then February has focus. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "month picker - keyboard navigation > navigates with arrow keys within the grid")

- Given a selected January and focus on it, when `Space` is pressed, then no `[data-selected]` element remains. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "allows deselection with %s key" with `kbd.SPACE`)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given `modelValue` of `CalendarDate(1980, 1, 20)`, when rendered, then the selected cell reads `Jan` and the heading reads `1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "respects a default value if provided - `CalendarDate`")

- Given `modelValue` of that value zoned to `America/New_York`, when rendered, then the selected cell reads `Jan` and the heading reads `1980`. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "respects a default value if provided - `ZonedDateTime`")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default month picker, when `axe` runs over the picker element, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given the month picker's component markup, when a grid renders, then `MonthPickerGrid` carries `role="application"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the heading id plus `aria-readonly`/`aria-disabled`, `MonthPickerGridRow` carries `role="row"`, `MonthPickerCell` carries `role="gridcell"` with `aria-selected` and `aria-disabled`, and `MonthPickerCellTrigger` carries `role="button"` with an `aria-label`; the tests assert the grid and trigger attributes through the `grid` and `month-<n>` test ids. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "doesnt allow focus or interaction when `disabled` is `true`")
- Given the month picker's default grid shape, when arrow keys move down a row, then the jump is four months (January to June via February), so the grid is laid out three rows of four. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "month picker - keyboard navigation > navigates with arrow keys within the grid")
- Given Vue's controlled pattern, when the test passes `emits['onUpdate:modelValue']` that calls `rerender` with the emitted value, then deselection and multiple-selection behavior is verified against a parent-controlled `modelValue` rather than internal state. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "allows months to be deselected by clicking the selected month")
- Given `MonthPickerPrev` rendered with `as="div"` instead of a button, when it is disabled by `minValue`, then the click still does not navigate, so the guard does not depend on the native `disabled` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthPicker/MonthPicker.test.ts: "does not navigate when prev is disabled and rendered as div")

## month-range-picker

- Given `maximumMonths: 3` and a start selected at March, when June is clicked, then June has `data-disabled` and does not gain `data-selected`, while May has no `data-disabled`. - Given `maximumMonths: 3` and a start selected at March, when January is hovered, then January has `data-highlighted-start`, February has `data-highlighted`, March has `data-highlighted-end` and April has no `data-highlighted`. - Given `isMonthDisabled` marking January 1981, when the grid pages to 1981, then the January cell has `data-disabled`. (reka: packages/core/src/MonthRangePicker/MonthRangePicker.test.ts: "month range picker - keyboard navigation > skips disabled candidate month when paging by year")
