- Given only a placeholder, when 1980 is clicked twice, then exactly one cell is selected and both `[data-selection-start]` and `[data-selection-end]` exist on it. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "allows same year selection")
- Given a single-year range built by clicking 1980 twice, when 1980 is clicked a third time, then zero cells are selected. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "allows deselection")
- Given a `modelValue` range 1980 to 1983, when the next button is clicked, then the heading reads `1992 - 2003`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "navigates pages forward using the next button")
- Given the same range, when the prev button is clicked, then the heading reads `1968 - 1979`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "navigates pages backwards using the prev button")
- Given `defaultValue` 1980 to 1983 and `fixedDate: 'start'`, when 1985 is clicked, then 1984 gains `data-selected`, 1980 keeps `data-selection-start` and 1985 becomes `data-selection-end`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "handles fixedDate with start correctly")
- Given `defaultValue` 1980 to 1983 and `fixedDate: 'end'`, when 1985 is clicked, then 1984 gains `data-selected`, 1980 keeps `data-selection-start` and 1985 becomes `data-selection-end`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "handles fixedDate with end correctly")
- Given that same `fixedDate: 'end'` picker, when 1982 is then clicked, then 1982 becomes `data-selection-start` while 1985 stays `data-selection-end`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "handles fixedDate with end correctly")
- Given `allowNonContiguousRanges: true` and `isYearUnavailable` marking 1982, when 1980 then 1984 are clicked, then 1983 has `data-selected`, so the range spans across the unavailable year. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "allows non-contiguous ranges")
- Given `maximumYears: 3` and a start at 1983, when 1985 is clicked, then 1983, 1984 and 1985 all have `data-selected`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "year range picker - maximumYears > limits the maximum number of years that can be selected")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a `modelValue` range of `CalendarDate`s from January 20 1980 to March 25 1983, when rendered, then four cells are selected and the heading reads `1980 - 1991`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "respects a default value if provided - `CalendarDate`")
- Given the equivalent `CalendarDateTime` range, when rendered, then four cells are selected and the heading reads `1980 - 1991`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "respects a default value if provided - `CalendarDateTime`")
- Given the equivalent range zoned to `America/New_York`, when rendered, then four cells are selected and the heading reads `1980 - 1991`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "respects a default value if provided - `ZonedDateTime`")
- Given `modelValue` of `null`, when rendered, then zero cells are selected and no error is thrown, and rerendering with the 1980 to 1983 range then selects four cells. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "does not crash when modelValue is null")
- Given a controlled range whose parent substitutes the previous end when the emitted end is missing, when a new start is chosen, then the preserved end is kept and the full range stays highlighted. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "keeps controlled end when parent preserves it after start edit")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default year range picker mounted with `@vue/test-utils`, when `axe` runs over the root element, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given `maximumYears` and a backwards hover, when the hovered year precedes the selected start, then the highlight runs from the hovered year as `data-highlighted-start` to the start year as `data-highlighted-end` without inverting the anchor. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "year range picker - maximumYears > highlights backwards within maximumYears without inverting")
- Given the year range picker fixture, when rendered, then it uses the same parts as the single year picker (`YearRangePickerRoot`, `Header`, `Prev`/`Heading`/`Next`, `Grid`, `GridBody`, `GridRow`, `Cell`, `CellTrigger`) with cell triggers addressed as `year-<n>`. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/story/_YearRangePicker.vue via packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts)
- Given the year range picker has no `maximumYears`-equivalent out-of-bounds controlled-range tests, when compared with the month range picker, then the `fixedDate` plus maximum enforcement cases for pre-existing out-of-bounds controlled values are covered only for months. (reka: packages/core/src/YearRangePicker/YearRangePicker.test.ts: "year range picker - maximumYears > limits the maximum number of years that can be selected")

## color-area

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `ColorArea` with `defaultValue: '#bf40bf'`, `colorSpace: 'hsl'`, `xChannel: 'saturation'`, `yChannel: 'lightness'`, when rendered, then an element with `role="group"` exists as the root. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "root has role=\"group\"")
- Given the same setup, when rendered, then the area element has `role="application"` and `aria-roledescription="Color picker"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "area has role=\"application\" and aria-roledescription=\"Color picker\"")
- Given the same setup, when rendered, then the thumb has `role="slider"` and `aria-roledescription="Color thumb"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "thumb has role=\"slider\" and aria-roledescription=\"Color thumb\"")
- Given the same setup, when rendered, then the thumb's `aria-label` is `Saturation, Lightness`, naming both axes. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "thumb aria-label names both channels")
- Given the same setup, when rendered, then `aria-valuenow` is `50`, the x-axis saturation value. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuenow = 50 (saturation)")
- Given the same setup, when rendered, then `aria-valuemin` is `0` and `aria-valuemax` is `100`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuemin = 0, aria-valuemax = 100")
- Given the same setup, when rendered, then `aria-valuetext` reports both channels in the form `Saturation 50, Lightness 50`, which is how the y-axis value is exposed at all. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuetext reports both channels")
- Given the same setup, when rendered, then the thumb has `tabindex="0"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "thumb is focusable (tabindex=0)")
- Given a `ColorArea` with no `colorSpace`, `xChannel`, or `yChannel`, when rendered, then the defaults are HSL hue on x and saturation on y and the thumb's `aria-label` is `Hue, Saturation`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-label names hue and saturation")
- Given the default channels with `defaultValue: '#ff0000'`, when rendered, then `aria-valuenow` is `0`, the hue. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuenow = 0 (hue)")
- Given the default channels, when rendered, then `aria-valuemin` is `0` and `aria-valuemax` is `360`, the hue range. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuemin = 0, aria-valuemax = 360 (hue range)")
- Given the default channels, when rendered, then `aria-valuetext` reports hue and saturation together. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuetext reports hue and saturation")
- Given `colorSpace: 'hsb'` with saturation on x and brightness on y, when rendered, then the thumb's `aria-label` is `Saturation, Brightness`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-label names saturation and brightness")
- Given `defaultValue: '#800080'` in HSB, when rendered, then the x saturation reads `100`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "initial saturation = 100")
- Given the same HSB setup, when rendered, then the y brightness reads `50`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "initial brightness = 50")
- Given the same HSB setup, when rendered, then `aria-valuemin` is `0` and `aria-valuemax` is `100`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuemin = 0, aria-valuemax = 100")
- Given `colorSpace: 'rgb'` with red on x and green on y, when rendered, then the thumb's `aria-label` is `Red, Green`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-label names red and green")
- Given `defaultValue: '#7f007f'` in RGB, when rendered, then `aria-valuenow` is `127`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuenow = 127 (red)")
- Given the same RGB setup, when rendered, then `aria-valuemin` is `0` and `aria-valuemax` is `255`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuemin = 0, aria-valuemax = 255 (RGB range)")
- Given the same RGB setup, when rendered, then the y green value reads `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "initial green = 0")
- Given the same RGB setup, when rendered, then `aria-valuetext` is exactly `Red 127, Green 0`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "aria-valuetext reports red and green")
- Given `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the area has `data-disabled=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "area has data-disabled=\"\"")
- Given `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the area has `aria-disabled="true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "area has aria-disabled=\"true\"")
- Given `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the thumb has `data-disabled=""` and no `tabindex`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "thumb has data-disabled=\"\" and no tabindex")

### Keyboard
- Given saturation on x at 50, when ArrowRight is pressed, then saturation becomes 51 and lightness stays 50. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowRight increments saturation by 1, lightness unchanged")
- Given the same, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then saturation becomes 49 and lightness stays 50. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowLeft decrements saturation by 1, lightness unchanged")
- Given the same, when Shift+ArrowRight is pressed, then saturation becomes 60. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "shift+ArrowRight increments saturation by 10")
- Given the same, when Shift+ArrowLeft is pressed, then saturation becomes 40. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "shift+ArrowLeft decrements saturation by 10")
- Given lightness on y at 50, when ArrowUp is pressed, then lightness becomes 51 and saturation stays 50. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowUp increments lightness by 1, saturation unchanged")
- Given the same, when ArrowDown is pressed, then lightness becomes 49 and saturation stays 50. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowDown decrements lightness by 1, saturation unchanged")
- Given the same, when Shift+ArrowUp is pressed, then lightness becomes 60. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "shift+ArrowUp increments lightness by 10")
- Given the same, when Shift+ArrowDown is pressed, then lightness becomes 40. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "shift+ArrowDown decrements lightness by 10")
- Given the same, when PageUp is pressed, then lightness becomes 60 and saturation stays 50, so PageUp is the large y-axis step. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "pageUp increments lightness by 10, saturation unchanged")
- Given the same, when PageDown is pressed, then lightness becomes 40 and saturation stays 50. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "pageDown decrements lightness by 10, saturation unchanged")
- Given the same, when Home is pressed, then saturation becomes 40 and lightness stays 50, so Home is a large x-axis decrement rather than a jump to the minimum. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "home decrements saturation by 10, lightness unchanged")
- Given the same, when End is pressed, then saturation becomes 60 and lightness stays 50, so End is a large x-axis increment. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "end increments saturation by 10, lightness unchanged")
- Given `defaultValue: '#ff0000'` where saturation is already 100, when ArrowRight is pressed, then saturation stays 100. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "saturation cannot exceed 100")
- Given `defaultValue: '#808080'` where saturation is 0, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then saturation stays 0. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "saturation cannot go below 0")
- Given `defaultValue: '#ffffff'` where lightness is 100, when ArrowUp is pressed, then lightness stays 100. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "lightness cannot exceed 100")
- Given `defaultValue: '#000000'` where lightness is 0, when ArrowDown is pressed, then lightness stays 0. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "lightness cannot go below 0")
- Given saturation already 0, when Home is pressed, then saturation stays 0 with no underflow. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "home at saturation=0 clamps to 0 (no underflow)")
- Given saturation already 100, when End is pressed, then saturation stays 100 with no overflow. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "end at saturation=100 clamps to 100 (no overflow)")
- Given `disabled: true`, when ArrowRight is pressed, then saturation is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowRight does not change saturation")
- Given `disabled: true`, when ArrowUp is pressed, then lightness is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowUp does not change lightness")
- Given the default hue and saturation channels, when ArrowRight is pressed, then hue becomes 1 and saturation stays 100. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowRight increments hue by 1")
- Given hue at 0, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then hue stays 0, so hue clamps at the minimum rather than wrapping to 360. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "hue cannot go below 0 (clamped at min)")
- Given `defaultValue: '#804040'` with default channels, when ArrowUp is pressed, then saturation increases by 1 and hue is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowUp increments saturation by 1, hue unchanged")
- Given HSB saturation 100, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then saturation becomes 99 and brightness stays 50. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowLeft decrements saturation by 1")
- Given HSB saturation 100, when ArrowLeft is pressed five times, then saturation becomes 95 and brightness stays 50, so repeated steps accumulate without drift through the HSB round trip. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowLeft 5× decrements saturation by 5")
- Given HSB brightness 50, when ArrowDown is pressed, then brightness becomes 49 and saturation stays 100. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowDown decrements brightness by 1")
- Given HSB brightness 50, when ArrowUp is pressed, then brightness becomes 51 and saturation stays 100. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowUp increments brightness by 1")
- Given HSB saturation already 100, when ArrowRight is pressed, then it stays 100. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "saturation cannot exceed 100 (already at max)")
- Given `defaultValue: '#ff00ff'` in HSB where brightness is 100, when ArrowUp is pressed, then brightness stays 100. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "brightness cannot exceed 100")
- Given RGB red 127, when ArrowRight is pressed, then red becomes 128 and green stays 0. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowRight increments red by 1, green unchanged")
- Given RGB red 127, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then red becomes 126. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowLeft decrements red by 1")
- Given RGB green 0, when ArrowUp is pressed, then green becomes 1 and red stays 127. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowUp increments green by 1, red unchanged")
- Given RGB green 0, when ArrowDown is pressed, then green stays 0. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "arrowDown at green=0 stays at 0 (clamp)")
- Given RGB red 127, when Shift+ArrowRight is pressed, then red becomes 137, so the large step is 10 even on the 0 to 255 scale. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "shift+ArrowRight increments red by 10")
- Given RGB green 0, when Shift+ArrowUp is pressed, then green becomes 10. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "shift+ArrowUp increments green by 10")
- Given `defaultValue: '#ff00ff'` in RGB where red is 255, when ArrowRight is pressed, then red stays 255. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "red cannot exceed 255")
- Given `defaultValue: '#0000ff'` in RGB where red is 0, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then red stays 0. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "red cannot go below 0")

### Pointer
- Given a mounted `ColorArea` with the thumb unfocused, when `pointerdown` fires on the area at client coordinates 100,100, then the thumb becomes `document.activeElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "thumb gains focus when dragging starts")
- Given `disabled: true`, when the same `pointerdown` fires, then the thumb does not become the active element. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "thumb does not gain focus when disabled")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a `ColorArea` in HSL saturation and lightness mode, when audited with axe with the `label` rule disabled, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "passes axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given jsdom implements none of them, `setPointerCapture`, `releasePointerCapture`, and `hasPointerCapture` are stubbed on `HTMLElement.prototype` for the whole file. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorArea/ColorArea.test.ts: "colorArea pointer interaction")

## color-field

### Roles and attributes
- Given `defaultValue: '#ff0000'` in hex mode, when rendered, then the input's value is `#ff0000`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should render input with hex value")
- Given `channel: 'hue'` with `colorSpace: 'hsl'` and `defaultValue: '#ff0000'`, when rendered, then the input's value is `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should render hue value")
- Given `channel: 'saturation'` and `defaultValue: '#7f007f'`, when rendered, then the input's value is `100`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should render saturation value")
- Given `channel: 'lightness'` and `defaultValue: '#bf40bf'`, when rendered, then the input's value is `50`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should render lightness value")
- Given `channel: 'alpha'` and `defaultValue: 'rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)'`, when rendered, then the input's value is `50`, so alpha is expressed as a percentage. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should render alpha value")
- Given channel mode, when rendered, then the input has `inputmode="numeric"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should have numeric inputmode")
- Given `placeholder: 'Enter color'` and no value, when rendered, then the input's `placeholder` attribute is that string. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should show placeholder when empty")
- Given `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the input has a `disabled` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should have disabled attribute")
- Given `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the input has `data-disabled=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should have data-disabled attribute")
- Given `readonly: true`, when rendered, then the input has a `readonly` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should have readonly attribute")

### Keyboard
- Given channel mode on hue at 0, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the input reads `1`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should increment on ArrowUp")
- Given channel mode on lightness at 50, when ArrowDown is pressed, then the input reads `49`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should decrement on ArrowDown")
- Given channel mode on the RGB red channel, when End is pressed, then the input reads `255`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should jump to max on End key")
- Given the same, when Home is pressed, then the input reads `0`, so in the field (unlike the area) Home and End jump to the channel bounds. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should jump to min on Home key")
- Given channel mode on lightness at 50, when PageUp is pressed the input reads `60` and when PageDown is pressed it returns to `50`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should step by page amount on PageUp/PageDown")
- Given `step: 10` on the hue channel at 0, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the input reads `10`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should respect custom step prop")
- Given hue at 0, when ArrowDown is pressed, then the input stays `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should clamp at channel boundaries")
- Given hex mode with `#000000`, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the input reads `#000001`, so hex mode steps the integer value of the whole color. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should increment hex value on ArrowUp")
- Given hex mode with `#000002`, when ArrowDown is pressed, then the input reads `#000001`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should decrement hex value on ArrowDown")
- Given hex mode with `#000000`, when End is pressed, then the input reads `#ffffff`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should jump to #ffffff on End")
- Given hex mode with `#ff0000`, when Home is pressed, then the input reads `#000000`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should jump to #000000 on Home")
- Given hex mode, when the input is set to `#00ff00` and Enter is pressed, then the input's value is `#00ff00`, so Enter commits. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should commit on Enter key")
- Given `disabled: true` on the hue channel, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the input stays `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should not increment when disabled")
- Given `readonly: true` on the hue channel, when ArrowUp is pressed, then the input stays `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should not increment when readonly")
- Given channel mode, when a `keydown` with `key: 'ArrowUp'` and `isComposing: true` fires the value stays `0`, and when a plain ArrowUp follows it becomes `1`, so arrow keys during IME candidate navigation do not step the value. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should not step the value during composition (arrow keys are IME candidate navigation)")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given hex mode, when the input is set to `#00ff00` and blurred, then the component emits, so blur commits the typed value. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should update value on input")
- Given hex mode, when a valid hex is typed and blurred, then the component emits rather than rejecting the value. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should accept valid hex colors")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a hex-mode `ColorField`, when audited with axe with the `label` rule disabled, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given channel mode, when a cancelable `beforeinput` carrying `data: 'あ'` and `isComposing: true` is dispatched, then `defaultPrevented` is `false`, so the numeric filter does not block IME composition. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorField/ColorField.test.ts: "should not block beforeinput during IME composition")

## color-slider

### Roles and attributes
- Given `channel: 'hue'` with `colorSpace: 'hsl'` and `defaultValue: '#ff0000'`, when rendered, then a `[role="slider"]` thumb exists with `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="360"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should render with initial value")
- Given the same setup, when rendered, then the thumb has `aria-label="Hue"` and `aria-orientation="horizontal"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should have correct aria attributes")
- Given `channel: 'saturation'`, when rendered, then `aria-label` is `Saturation` and `aria-valuemax` is `100`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should render saturation slider")
- Given `channel: 'lightness'`, when rendered, then `aria-label` is `Lightness` and `aria-valuemax` is `100`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should render lightness slider")
- Given `channel: 'alpha'`, when rendered, then `aria-label` is `Alpha` and `aria-valuemax` is `100`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should render alpha slider")
- Given `channel: 'red'` with `colorSpace: 'rgb'`, when rendered, then `aria-label` is `Red` and `aria-valuemax` is `255`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should render red slider with RGB range")
- Given `orientation: 'vertical'`, when rendered, then the thumb has `aria-orientation="vertical"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should have vertical aria-orientation")
- Given `channel: 'alpha'` with `defaultValue: 'rgba(127, 0, 127, 0.5)'`, when rendered, then `aria-valuetext` is `50%`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should display correct percentage for alpha")
- Given `channel: 'alpha'` with an opaque `#ff0000`, when rendered, then `aria-valuetext` is `100%`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should display 100% for full alpha")
- Given `step: 10` on the hue channel, when rendered, then the thumb still reports `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="360"`, so a custom step does not change the reported range. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should use custom step value")
- Given `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the thumb has no `tabindex` attribute. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should not have tabindex when disabled")
- Given `disabled: true`, when rendered, then the thumb has `data-disabled=""`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should have data-disabled attribute")

### Keyboard
- Given a hue slider, when ArrowRight is pressed, then `aria-valuenow` is greater than its previous value. The test asserts an inequality rather than an exact number because the hex to HSL round trip loses precision. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should increment on ArrowRight")
- Given a hue slider incremented once, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then `aria-valuenow` is less than the incremented value. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should decrement on ArrowLeft")
- Given a red-channel slider with `defaultValue: '#7f007f'`, when Home is pressed, then `aria-valuenow` is exactly `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should jump to min on Home key")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a hue `ColorSlider`, when audited with axe with the `label` rule disabled, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given jsdom lacks them, the file installs a no-op `ResizeObserver` class and stubs `scrollIntoView`, `hasPointerCapture` (returning its own id argument), `releasePointerCapture`, and `setPointerCapture` on `HTMLElement.prototype`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSlider/ColorSlider.test.ts: "given default ColorSlider")

## color-swatch

### Roles and attributes
- Given `color: '#E5484D'`, when rendered, then the element has `role="img"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should render with role=\"img\"")
- Given the same, when rendered, then it has `aria-roledescription="color swatch"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should render with aria-roledescription=\"color swatch\"")
- Given `color: '#ff0000'` with no `label`, when rendered, then `aria-label` is a non-empty string that is not the hex itself, so a human-readable colour name is derived. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should derive color name as aria-label for hex color")
- Given `label: 'Brand Red'`, when rendered, then `aria-label` is exactly `Brand Red`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should use custom label when provided")
- Given `color: '#ff000000'` (alpha 0), when rendered, then `aria-label` is `transparent`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should show \"transparent\" for alpha=0 color")
- Given `color: ''`, when rendered, then `aria-label` is `transparent`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should show \"transparent\" for empty color")
- Given no `color` prop at all, when rendered, then `aria-label` is `transparent`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should show \"transparent\" when no color prop provided")
- Given `color: '#ff000000'`, when rendered, then `data-no-color=""` is set. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should set data-no-color when alpha is 0")
- Given `color: ''`, when rendered, then `data-no-color=""` is set. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should set data-no-color when no color")
- Given an opaque `#E5484D`, when rendered, then `data-no-color` is absent. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should not set data-no-color for opaque color")
- Given `color: '#000000'`, when rendered, then `data-color-contrast` is `light`, meaning overlaid text should be light. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should set data-color-contrast to light for dark colors")
- Given `color: '#ffffff'`, when rendered, then `data-color-contrast` is `dark`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should set data-color-contrast to dark for bright colors")
- Given `color: '#E5484D'`, when rendered, then the inline style contains `--reka-color-swatch-color: #E5484D`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should set --reka-color-swatch-color")
- Given `color: '#E5484D'`, when rendered, then the inline style contains `--reka-color-swatch-alpha: 1`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should set --reka-color-swatch-alpha")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given `color: '#E5484D'`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a `Color` object such as `{ space: 'hsl', h: 120, s: 50, l: 50, alpha: 1 }` instead of a string, when rendered, then the element renders and carries a non-empty `aria-label`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should accept Color object")
- Given a default slot, when rendered, then the slot receives `color` and `alpha` scope values, and the rendered text contains both `#E5484D` and `1`. (reka: packages/core/src/ColorSwatch/ColorSwatch.test.ts: "should expose color and alpha via slot")

## color-utils

### Notes and edge cases
- Given `#ff0000`, `#00ff00`, and `#0000ff`, when `parseColor` runs, then each returns `{ space: 'rgb', r, g, b, alpha: 1 }` with the expected channel values. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "parseColor > should parse hex colors")
- Given the shorthand `#f00`, when `parseColor` runs, then it expands to `{ space: 'rgb', r: 255, g: 0, b: 0, alpha: 1 }`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should parse shorthand hex colors")
- Given `#ff000080`, when `parseColor` runs, then `alpha` is close to `0.5` within 0.01. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should parse hex with alpha")
- Given `rgb(255, 128, 64)`, when `parseColor` runs, then it returns the RGB triple with `alpha: 1`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should parse rgb() colors")
- Given `rgba(255, 128, 64, 0.5)`, when `parseColor` runs, then `alpha` is `0.5`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should parse rgba() colors")
- Given `hsl(120, 50%, 50%)`, when `parseColor` runs, then it returns `{ space: 'hsl', h: 120, s: 50, l: 50, alpha: 1 }`, so the HSL space is preserved rather than converted. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should parse hsl() colors")
- Given `hsla(120, 50%, 50%, 0.5)`, when `parseColor` runs, then `alpha` is `0.5`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should parse hsla() colors")
- Given `not a color` or `#gggggg`, when `parseColor` runs, then it throws. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should throw for invalid colors")
- Given `#ff0000`, `rgb(255, 0, 0)`, and `hsl(0, 100%, 50%)`, when `isValidColor` runs, then all return `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "isValidColor > should return true for valid colors")
- Given `not a color` or `#gggggg`, when `isValidColor` runs, then both return `false` rather than throwing. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "isValidColor > should return false for invalid colors")
- Given the string `#ff0000`, when `normalizeColor` runs, then the result has `space: 'rgb'` and equals `parseColor('#ff0000')`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "normalizeColor > should parse string colors")
- Given an existing colour object, when `normalizeColor` runs, then the same object reference comes back. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "normalizeColor > should return color objects as-is")
- Given `{ space: 'rgb', r: 255, g: 128, b: 64, alpha: 1 }`, when `colorToHex` runs, then the result is `#ff8040`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "colorToHex > should convert RGB to hex")
- Given `{ space: 'hsl', h: 0, s: 100, l: 50, alpha: 1 }`, when `colorToHex` runs, then the result is `#ff0000`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "colorToHex > should convert HSL to hex")
- Given an RGB colour with `alpha: 0.5`, when `colorToHex` runs, then the result includes the alpha byte as `#ff000080`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "colorToHex > should include alpha for transparent colors")
- Given an opaque RGB colour, when `colorToRgb` runs, then the result is `rgb(255, 128, 64)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "colorToRgb > should format RGB color")
- Given an RGB colour with `alpha: 0.5`, when `colorToRgb` runs, then the result is `rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "colorToRgb > should format RGBA for transparent colors")
- Given an opaque HSL colour, when `colorToHsl` runs, then the result is `hsl(120, 50%, 50%)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "colorToHsl > should format HSL color")
- Given an HSL colour with `alpha: 0.5`, when `colorToHsl` runs, then the result is `hsla(0, 100%, 50%, 0.5)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "colorToHsl > should format HSLA for transparent colors")
- Given `hsl(0, 100%, 50%)` as an object, when `convertToRgb` runs, then the result has `space: 'rgb'` with r close to 255 and g and b close to 0. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "convertToRgb > should convert HSL to RGB")
- Given an RGB colour, when `convertToRgb` runs, then the same object reference comes back. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "convertToRgb > should preserve existing RGB")
- Given pure red in RGB, when `convertToHsl` runs, then hue is close to 0, saturation to 100, and lightness to 50. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "convertToHsl > should convert RGB to HSL")
- Given an HSL colour, when `convertToHsl` runs, then the same object reference comes back. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "convertToHsl > should preserve existing HSL")
- Given pure red in RGB, when `convertToHsb` runs, then the result has `space: 'hsb'` with hue close to 0 and saturation close to 100. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "convertToHsb > should convert RGB to HSB")
- Given an HSB colour, when `convertToHsb` runs, then the same object reference comes back. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "convertToHsb > should preserve existing HSB")
- Given the channel `hue`, when `getChannelRange` runs, then it returns `{ min: 0, max: 360, step: 1 }`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "getChannelRange > should return correct ranges for hue")
- Given `saturation`, `lightness`, `brightness`, or `alpha`, when `getChannelRange` runs, then each returns `{ min: 0, max: 100, step: 1 }`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should return correct ranges for saturation/lightness/brightness/alpha")
- Given `red`, `green`, or `blue`, when `getChannelRange` runs, then each returns `{ min: 0, max: 255, step: 1 }`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should return correct ranges for RGB channels")
- Given an RGB colour, when `getChannelValue` is asked for `red`, `green`, and `blue`, then it returns the raw channel numbers. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "getChannelValue > should get RGB values")
- Given an HSL colour, when `getChannelValue` is asked for `hue`, `saturation`, and `lightness`, then it returns those numbers. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "getChannelValue > should get HSL values")
- Given a colour with `alpha: 0.5`, when `getChannelValue` is asked for `alpha`, then it returns `50`, so alpha is exposed as a percentage. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should get alpha as percentage")
- Given an HSL colour, when `getChannelValue` asks for `saturation`, then it reads the HSL saturation directly without a conversion. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should get HSL saturation directly from HSL color")
- Given an HSB colour, when `getChannelValue` asks for `saturation`, then it reads the HSB saturation directly, which is a different quantity from HSL saturation. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should get HSB saturation directly from HSB color")
- Given an HSB colour, when `getChannelValue` asks for `brightness`, then it returns the HSB brightness. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should get HSB brightness directly from HSB color")
- Given an HSB colour with `s: 0, b: 50`, when `setChannelValues` sets saturation to 10 and brightness to 50 in one call, then the result stays in HSB and both channels read back exactly, with no cross-contamination between them. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "setChannelValues > should set HSB saturation and brightness without cross-contamination")
- Given an RGB colour such as one parsed from hex, when `setChannelValues` sets saturation and brightness, then the result's space is `hsb` rather than being converted back to RGB. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should return HSB color when starting from RGB with saturation/brightness channels")
- Given an HSB colour, when only saturation changes in a `setChannelValues` call, then brightness still reads its previous value. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should update only saturation when brightness unchanged")
- Given an RGB colour, when `setChannelValue(rgb, 'red', 255)` runs, then the result stays RGB with `r === 255`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "setChannelValue > should set RGB values")
- Given an HSL colour, when `setChannelValue(hsl, 'hue', 180)` runs, then the result stays HSL with `h === 180`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should set HSL values preserving color space")
- Given a colour, when `setChannelValue(color, 'alpha', 50)` runs, then `alpha` becomes `0.5`, converting the percentage back. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should set alpha value")
- Given an HSL colour, when hue is set to 500, then it clamps to 360. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should clamp values to valid range")
- Given an HSL colour, when `setChannelValue(hsl, 'red', 255)` sets a channel from another space, then the result's space is still `hsl`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/utils.test.ts: "should maintain color space when setting cross-space channels")

## color-gradient

### Notes and edge cases
- Given red and the `hue` channel in HSL, when `getSliderGradient` runs, then the string contains the six rainbow stops `#ff0000`, `#ffff00`, `#00ff00`, `#00ffff`, `#0000ff`, and `#ff00ff`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue channel > should return full rainbow spectrum")
- Given the same, when `getSliderGradient` runs, then the string contains `linear-gradient`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue channel > should use linear-gradient")
- Given `hsl(0, 100%, 50%)` and the `saturation` channel in HSL, when the gradient is built, then it runs from `hsl(0, 0%, 50%)` (grey) to `hsl(0, 100%, 50%)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "saturation channel > should return gray-to-color gradient for HSL")
- Given `hsb(0, 100%, 100%)` and the `saturation` channel in HSB, when the gradient is built, then it still runs from `hsl(0, 0%, 50%)` to `hsl(0, 100%, 50%)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "saturation channel > should return gray-to-color gradient for HSB")
- Given the `lightness` channel, when the gradient is built, then it spans `hsl(0, 100%, 0%)`, `hsl(0, 100%, 50%)`, and `hsl(0, 100%, 100%)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "lightness channel > should span from black through color to white")
- Given the `brightness` channel in HSB, when the gradient is built, then it spans `rgb(0, 0, 0)` to `rgb(255, 0, 0)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "brightness channel > should span from black to full-brightness color")
- Given `#808080` and the `red` channel, when the gradient is built, then it runs `rgb(0, 128, 128)` to `rgb(255, 128, 128)`, holding green and blue constant. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "should return red gradient holding g/b constant")
- Given `#808080` and the `green` channel, when the gradient is built, then it runs `rgb(128, 0, 128)` to `rgb(128, 255, 128)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "should return green gradient holding r/b constant")
- Given `#808080` and the `blue` channel, when the gradient is built, then it runs `rgb(128, 128, 0)` to `rgb(128, 128, 255)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "should return blue gradient holding r/g constant")
- Given hue on x and saturation on y in HSL, when `getAreaBackgroundStyle` runs, then `backgroundImage` contains the exact bottom layer `linear-gradient(to right, #ff0000, #ffff00, #00ff00, #00ffff, #0000ff, #ff00ff, #ff0000)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Saturation(y) — HSL > includes the full hue rainbow as bottom layer")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then it also contains `linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, rgb(128, 128, 128))`, fading from full saturation at the top to neutral grey at the bottom. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "overlays transparent-to-gray fade (top=full sat, bottom=desaturated)")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then `backgroundBlendMode` is undefined. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Saturation(y) — HSL > does not use any CSS blend mode")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is undefined, so the layers stack with transparency instead of over a solid fill. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Saturation(y) — HSL > does not set a solid background color")
- Given red and green input hues on the same axes, when the styles are built, then both contain `rgb(128, 128, 128)`, because saturation 0 at lightness 50 is always neutral. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "gray stop is rgb(128,128,128) regardless of hue (S=0, L=50 is always neutral)")
- Given hue on x and lightness on y in HSL, when the style is built, then it contains the full rainbow bottom layer. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Lightness(y) — HSL > includes the full hue rainbow as bottom layer")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to top, #000000, transparent, #ffffff)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "overlays black → transparent → white for the lightness axis")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then `backgroundBlendMode` is undefined. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Lightness(y) — HSL > does not use any CSS blend mode")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is undefined. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Lightness(y) — HSL > does not set a solid background color")
- Given hue on x and brightness on y in HSB, when the style is built, then it contains the full rainbow bottom layer. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Brightness(y) — HSB > includes the full hue rainbow as bottom layer")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to top, #000000, transparent)` with no white stop, because HSB brightness tops out at the pure hue. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "overlays black → transparent for the brightness axis")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then `backgroundBlendMode` is undefined. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Brightness(y) — HSB > does not use any CSS blend mode")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is undefined. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "hue(x) / Brightness(y) — HSB > does not set a solid background color")
- Given saturation on x and lightness on y in HSL with red, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(255, 0, 0)`, the pure hue at saturation 100 and lightness 50. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "uses pure hue (S=100, L=50) as the background color")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to right, rgb(128, 128, 128), transparent)`, starting at grey rather than white. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "saturation gradient starts at gray (#808080) — NOT white")
- Given the same axes, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to top, #000000, transparent, #ffffff)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "lightness gradient spans black → transparent → white")
- Given green instead of red on the same axes, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(0, 255, 0)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "background color reflects the input hue")
- Given blue on the same axes, when the style is built, then the grey stop is still `rgb(128, 128, 128)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "gray stop is always rgb(128,128,128) regardless of hue")
- Given saturation on x and brightness on y in HSB with red, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(255, 0, 0)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "uses pure hue (S=100, B=100) as the background color")
- Given the same HSB axes, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to right, #ffffff, transparent)`, starting at white because saturation 0 at brightness 100 is white in HSB. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "saturation gradient starts at white (S=0 + B=100 = white in HSB)")
- Given the same HSB axes, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to top, #000000, transparent)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "brightness gradient fades black → transparent")
- Given cyan on the same HSB axes, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(0, 255, 255)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "saturation(x) / Brightness(y) — HSB > background color reflects the input hue")
- Given red on x and green on y in RGB, when the style is built, then `backgroundBlendMode` is `screen`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "rGB Red(x) / Green(y) > uses screen blend mode")
- Given `#7f007f` with red on x and green on y, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(0, 0, 127)`, the constant blue z-channel. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "background is the constant blue z-channel value")
- Given the same, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to right, rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 0, 0))`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "horizontal gradient: black → full red (x-axis)")
- Given the same, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to top, rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(0, 255, 0))`, so the y axis runs black at the bottom to full green at the top. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "vertical gradient: black at bottom → full green at top (y-axis, correct direction)")
- Given `#ff0000` where blue is 0, with red on x and green on y, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(0, 0, 0)`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "background is black when z-channel (blue) = 0")
- Given red on x and blue on y, when the style is built, then `backgroundBlendMode` is `screen`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "rGB Red(x) / Blue(y) > uses screen blend mode")
- Given `#7f007f` with red on x and blue on y, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(0, 0, 0)`, the constant green z-channel of zero. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "background is the constant green z-channel (0 here)")
- Given the same, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to right, rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 0, 0))`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "rGB Red(x) / Blue(y) > horizontal gradient: black → full red")
- Given the same, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to top, rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(0, 0, 255))`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "rGB Red(x) / Blue(y) > vertical gradient: black at bottom → full blue at top")
- Given green on x and blue on y, when the style is built, then `backgroundBlendMode` is `screen`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "rGB Green(x) / Blue(y) > uses screen blend mode")
- Given `#7f007f` with green on x and blue on y, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(127, 0, 0)`, the constant red z-channel. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "background is the constant red z-channel")
- Given the same, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to right, rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(0, 255, 0))`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "rGB Green(x) / Blue(y) > horizontal gradient: black → full green")
- Given the same, when the style is built, then it contains `linear-gradient(to top, rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(0, 0, 255))`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "rGB Green(x) / Blue(y) > vertical gradient: black at bottom → full blue at top")
- Given the axes swapped to green on x and red on y for `#7f007f`, when the style is built, then `backgroundColor` is `rgb(0, 0, 127)`, the horizontal gradient uses green, and the vertical gradient uses red, so the axis assignment follows the props rather than a fixed channel order. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/color/gradient.test.ts: "rGB swapped axes — Green(x) / Red(y) > assigns x-gradient horizontally and y-gradient vertically")

## label

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `Label`, when rendered, then it carries `data-label-root`. (bits: tests/src/tests/label/label.browser.test.ts: "should have bits data attrs")
- Given a bare `Label` with no props or slot, when rendered, then the HTML is exactly `<label></label>`. (reka: packages/core/src/Label/Label.test.ts: "should render without crashing")
- Given a `Label` with a default slot, when rendered, then the HTML is exactly `<label>Label</label>`. (reka: packages/core/src/Label/Label.test.ts: "should render with a default slot")
- Given a `Label` with `for="input"`, when rendered, then the HTML is exactly `<label for="input"></label>`. (reka: packages/core/src/Label/Label.test.ts: "should render with a `for` attribute")
- Given a `Label` with both `for` and a slot, when rendered, then the HTML is `<label for="input">Label</label>`. (reka: packages/core/src/Label/Label.test.ts: "should render with a `for` attribute and a default slot")
- Given a `Label` with text, when rendered, then its text content is `Label`. (bits: tests/src/tests/label/label.browser.test.ts: "should render the label text")
- Given a label harness with `inputId: 'test'`, when rendered, then the text `Test` is in the document. (melt: src/tests/label/Label.spec.ts: "renders the label with the correct text")

### Focus management
- Given a `Label` with no `for` and a sibling `input`, when the label is clicked, then the input is not the active element. (reka: packages/core/src/Label/Label.test.ts: "should not focus the input when click on the label without a `for` attribute")
- Given a `Label for="input"` next to an `input` whose id is `input2`, when the label is clicked, then the input is not focused. (reka: packages/core/src/Label/Label.test.ts: "should not focus the input when click on the label with a `for` attribute that does not match any input")
- Given a label wired to an input, when the label is clicked, then the input has focus. (melt: src/tests/label/Label.spec.ts: "focuses the input when the label is clicked")
- Given a label wired to an input, when the label is clicked, then the input has focus. (bits: tests/src/tests/label/label.browser.test.ts: "should focus the associated input on click")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a `Label for="input"` paired with a matching `input`, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Label/Label.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

## separator

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `Separator`, when rendered, then it carries `data-separator-root`. (bits: tests/src/tests/separator/separator.browser.test.ts: "Separator > should have bits data attrs")
- Given a horizontal separator, when rendered, then it is visible. (melt: src/tests/separator/Separator.spec.ts: "should render an horizontal separator")
- Given `orientation: 'vertical'`, when rendered, then the vertical separator is visible. (melt: src/tests/separator/Separator.spec.ts: "should render a vertical separator")
- Given a non-decorative vertical separator, when rendered, then it has `role="separator"`. (melt: src/tests/separator/Separator.spec.ts: "should have a role of separator")
- Given a decorative separator, when rendered, then it has `role="none"`. (melt: src/tests/separator/Separator.spec.ts: "should have a role of none when decorative is true")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default horizontal `Separator` and a second one with `orientation: 'vertical'`, when both are audited with axe, then neither has violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Separator/Separator.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

## aspect-ratio

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default `AspectRatio` wrapping an `img`, when snapshotted, then the outer element has `data-reka-aspect-ratio-wrapper=""` with inline `position: relative; width: 100%; padding-bottom: 100%`, and the inner element has `position: absolute; inset: 0px`. (reka: packages/core/src/AspectRatio/AspectRatio.test.ts: "should render as snapshot")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default `AspectRatio` wrapping an `img` with alt text, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/AspectRatio/AspectRatio.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

## visually-hidden

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default `VisuallyHidden`, when rendered, then the element's tag name is `SPAN`. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "renders a span by default")
- Given a default `VisuallyHidden`, when rendered, then its inline `position` is `absolute` and its `clipPath` is `inset(50%)`. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "applies visually-hidden styles")
- Given a `VisuallyHidden` with slot content, when rendered, then its text is that content. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "renders slot content")
- Given `feature="focusable"`, when rendered, then `aria-hidden` is `"true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "given feature=\"focusable\" (default) > sets aria-hidden=\"true\"")
- Given `feature="focusable"`, when rendered, then no `tabindex` attribute is set, so the element keeps its natural tab order. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "does not set tabindex")
- Given `feature="focusable"`, when rendered, then no `data-hidden` attribute is set. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "does not set data-hidden")
- Given `feature="fully-hidden"`, when rendered, then `data-hidden` is the empty string. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "given feature=\"fully-hidden\" > sets data-hidden attribute")
- Given `feature="fully-hidden"`, when rendered, then `tabindex` is `"-1"`. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "sets tabindex=\"-1\"")
- Given `feature="fully-hidden"`, when rendered, then `aria-hidden` is `"true"`, which the test notes is safe precisely because the element is non-focusable and which prevents axe `label` and `nested-interactive` violations for the hidden form inputs that depend on it. (reka: packages/core/src/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.test.ts: "given feature=\"fully-hidden\" > sets aria-hidden=\"true\"")

## viewport

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default `Viewport`, when rendered, then an element with the `data-reka-viewport` attribute exists. (reka: packages/core/src/Viewport/Viewport.test.ts: "renders an element with data-reka-viewport attribute")
- Given a default `Viewport`, when rendered, then that element has `role="presentation"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Viewport/Viewport.test.ts: "renders with role=\"presentation\"")
- Given a default `Viewport`, when rendered, then its inline `overflow` is `auto`. (reka: packages/core/src/Viewport/Viewport.test.ts: "applies overflow:auto style")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given `Viewport` with `nonce: 'abc123'`, when rendered, then the injected `<style>` tag carries `nonce="abc123"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Viewport/Viewport.test.ts: "puts nonce attribute on the style tag when nonce prop is provided")

- Given a melt toolbar, when each item in the single group is focused and Space is pressed, then that item gets `aria-checked="true"` and `data-state="on"`, so the single group uses a radio-style ARIA attribute rather than a pressed state.
