### Pointer
- Given a melt toolbar, when each multiple-group item is clicked, then it gets `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-state="on"`. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "items can be selected with mouse")
- Given a melt toolbar, when each single-group item is clicked, then it gets `aria-checked="true"` and `data-state="on"`. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "items can be selected with mouse")
- Given a melt multiple group, when all three of its items are clicked, then all three carry `data-state="on"`. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "multiple items can be selected in `multiple` groups")
- Given a melt single group, when all three of its items are clicked in turn, then exactly one carries `data-state="on"`. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "multiple items cannot be selected in `single` groups")
- Given a bits single-type toggle group, when left then center are clicked, then the bound value becomes `left` then `center`. (bits: tests/src/tests/toolbar/toolbar.browser.test.ts: "should toggles when clicked when toolbar toggle group, type 'single'")
- Given a bits multiple-type toggle group starting at `bold`, when italic, strikethrough, bold, italic, and strikethrough are clicked in sequence, then the bound value goes `bold`, `bold,italic`, `bold,italic,strikethrough`, `italic,strikethrough`, `strikethrough`, then empty, so clicking an active item removes it. (bits: tests/src/tests/toolbar/toolbar.browser.test.ts: "should allow multiple items to be selected with toolbar toggle group type 'multiple'")
- Given a bits toolbar link, when it is clicked, then the click binding reads `link`. (bits: tests/src/tests/toolbar/toolbar.browser.test.ts: "should forward click event when the link is clicked")
- Given a bits toolbar button, when it is clicked, then the click binding reads `button`. (bits: tests/src/tests/toolbar/toolbar.browser.test.ts: "should forward click event when the button is clicked")

### Focus management
- Given a toolbar with the default mix of two toggle groups, a link, and a button, when Tab is pressed, then the first item takes focus, a second Tab does not move focus to the second item, Shift+Tab returns focus to the first item, and a further Shift+Tab leaves the toolbar. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "tab enters toolbar but doesn't navigate between items - ")
- Given a toolbar with `linksFirst: true`, so the link precedes the toggle groups, when Tab is pressed, then the first item takes focus, a second Tab does not move focus to the second item, Shift+Tab returns focus to the first item, and a further Shift+Tab leaves the toolbar. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "tab enters toolbar but doesn't navigate between items - first item is a link")
- Given a toolbar with `buttonsFirst: true`, so the button precedes the toggle groups, when Tab is pressed, then the first item takes focus, a second Tab does not move focus to the second item, Shift+Tab returns focus to the first item, and a further Shift+Tab leaves the toolbar. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "tab enters toolbar but doesn't navigate between items - first item is a button")
- Given a toolbar with `linksButtonsOnly: true, linksFirst: true`, so only a link and a button exist, when Tab is pressed, then the first item takes focus, a second Tab does not move focus to the second item, Shift+Tab returns focus to the first item, and a further Shift+Tab leaves the toolbar. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "tab enters toolbar but doesn't navigate between items - no group items, first item is a link")
- Given a toolbar with `linksButtonsOnly: true, buttonsFirst: true`, so only a button and a link exist, when Tab is pressed, then the first item takes focus, a second Tab does not move focus to the second item, Shift+Tab returns focus to the first item, and a further Shift+Tab leaves the toolbar. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "tab enters toolbar but doesn't navigate between items - no group items, first item is a button")
- Given a `ToolbarRoot` whose only toggle items are all `disabled`, when mounted, then the element with `role="toolbar"` has `tabindex="-1"`, so the whole toolbar drops out of the tab order. (reka: packages/core/src/Toolbar/Toolbar.test.ts: "should not be tabbable when all toggle items are disabled")
- Given a `ToolbarRoot` where one toggle item is enabled and two are disabled, when mounted, then the `role="toolbar"` element has `tabindex="0"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Toolbar/Toolbar.test.ts: "should be tabbable when at least one toggle item is not disabled")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given melt groups with `defaultValue: ['item-1','item-2']` and `defaultValue: 'item-5'`, when rendered, then the multiple group has exactly those two items on and the single group has exactly `item-5` on. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "default value sets initial pressed/checked items")
- Given melt groups whose `onValueChange` returns a fixed value, when a different item is clicked, then the clicked item does not turn on and the value returned by the callback stays on, so `onValueChange` can veto the change. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "onValueChange function can override value")
- Given melt groups with both `defaultValue` and a `value` store, when rendered, then the store's value wins and the defaults are ignored. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "value prop overrides default value")
- Given melt groups driven by empty `value` stores, when the stores are updated programmatically, then the matching items turn on after a tick without any user interaction. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "can be programmatically updated using value store")
- Given bits groups with `disabled: true`, when rendered, then all six group items report as disabled. (bits: tests/src/tests/toolbar/toolbar.browser.test.ts: "should disable group items when the `disabled` prop is set to true")
- Given bits groups with `onValueChange` callbacks, when strikethrough then the single group's right item are clicked, then the multiple callback receives `["bold","strikethrough"]` and the single callback receives `"right"`. (bits: tests/src/tests/toolbar/toolbar.browser.test.ts: "should fire the `onChange` callback when changing")
- Given a bits toolbar with `bind:value` on both groups starting at `bold` and empty, when the external binding buttons are clicked, then the value text updates and the corresponding items flip `data-state` from `off` to `on` with `aria-pressed`/`aria-checked` following, so the binding drives the DOM in both directions. (bits: tests/src/tests/toolbar/toolbar.browser.test.ts: "should respect binding to the `value` prop")

### Accessibility tooling
- Given a default `Toolbar` story, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/Toolbar/Toolbar.test.ts: "given default Toolbar > should pass axe accessibility tests")
- Given a default melt toolbar, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (melt: src/tests/toolbar/Toolbar.spec.ts: "has no accessibility violations")

## presence

### Animation and presence
- Given a `Presence` with `present` bound to a `false` ref, when rendered, then the content text is absent from the markup. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "given a default Presence > should not show content")
- Given the same `Presence`, when the toggle button is clicked, then the content text appears. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "given a default Presence > after clicking trigger > should show content")
- Given the toggled-open `Presence`, when the toggle is clicked again, then the content text is gone. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "after clicking trigger again > should not show content")
- Given a `Presence` with `forceMount` and `present: false`, when rendered, then the content is in the markup and the slot's `present` scope value renders as `data-present="false"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "given a forceMounted Presence > should show content")
- Given the force-mounted `Presence`, when the toggle is clicked, then the content stays mounted and `data-present` becomes `"true"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "given a forceMounted Presence > after clicking trigger > should show content")
- Given the force-mounted `Presence`, when the toggle is clicked again, then the content is still mounted and `data-present` is `"false"` again. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "should always show content")
- Given a `Presence` whose content has `animation: fadeIn 2s` for `data-state=open` and `fadeOut 2s` for `data-state=closed` injected as a real `<style>` element, when rendered closed, then the content is absent. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "given a Presence with animated content > should not show content")
- Given the animated `Presence`, when the toggle is clicked, then the content appears. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "given a Presence with animated content > after clicking trigger > should show content")
- Given the animated `Presence`, when the toggle is clicked again, then the content is removed. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "given a Presence with animated content > after clicking trigger again > should not show content")
- Given a present `Presence` wrapping a child element, when an `animationend` event with a foreign `animationName` is dispatched on the presence element itself then `getComputedStyle` is called with that element, and when the same bubbling event is dispatched on the child then `getComputedStyle` is not called with the presence element, so bubbled descendant animations are ignored before styles are read. (reka: packages/core/src/Presence/Presence.test.ts: "should ignore bubbled animation events before reading styles")

## dismissable-layer

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `div` carrying `data-dismissable-layer`, when `isLayerExist` is called with `document` and with a text node as the target, then both return `false` without throwing. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "isLayerExist > should return false for non-Element targets without throwing")

### Keyboard
- Given an open `DismissableLayer` story, when Escape is dispatched on `document.body`, then the content is removed and the layer emits `escapeKeyDown` once and `dismiss` once. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "pressing Escape > should close layer")
- Given the same layer with `preventEscapeKeyDownEvent: true`, when Escape is dispatched, then the content stays and `escapeKeyDown` is still emitted once while no dismissal happens. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "pressing Escape > should not close layer when prevented")
- Given a layer mounted with `present: false`, when Escape is dispatched on `document`, then neither `escapeKeyDown` nor `dismiss` is emitted, because a hidden layer's stack index of `-1` must not be mistaken for the top layer. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should not emit escapeKeyDown or dismiss on Escape while not present")
- Given a layer mounted with `present: true`, when Escape is dispatched on `document`, then `escapeKeyDown` and `dismiss` are each emitted once. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should emit escapeKeyDown and dismiss on Escape once present")

### Pointer
- Given an outer and a nested layer and a touch `pointerdown` on `document.body` that is never followed by a `click`, when the next touch tap lands on a button inside the nested layer, then the outer layer emits neither `pointerDownOutside` nor `dismiss`, and a later completed outside tap does emit both once. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should not dismiss on the next tap inside a nested layer")
- Given a single layer and a cancelled outside touch `pointerdown`, when the next tap lands inside the layer itself, then neither `pointerDownOutside` nor `dismiss` is emitted. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should not dismiss on the next tap inside the layer itself")
- Given a layer mounted with `present: false`, when a touch `pointerdown` fires, `present` flips to `true`, and the tap's `click` arrives, then neither `pointerDownOutside` nor `dismiss` is emitted, and a later outside tap does emit both once. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should not dismiss on the tap that made it present")
- Given an open Bits DropdownMenu, when an outside click sequence of `pointerdown`, `mousedown`, `pointerup`, `mouseup`, and `click` is dispatched during the opening mutation while the content still has `data-starting-style`, then `onInteractOutside` fires once with `document.documentElement` as the target, the content is removed, `onSelect` never fires, and the same holds on an immediate reopen. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/opening-outside-click.browser.test.ts: "DropdownMenu dismisses an outside click during opening and immediate reopen")
- Given an open Bits Combobox, when the same outside click sequence is dispatched during opening, then `onInteractOutside` fires once, the content is removed, the value binding still reads `empty`, and the same holds on an immediate reopen. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/opening-outside-click.browser.test.ts: "Combobox dismisses an outside click during opening and immediate reopen")
- Given a registered layer, when an outside click happens 0ms after registration, then the layer closes. Twenty cases in total sweep delays of 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 20ms twice each, because the regression only reproduced in the 4 to 14ms window where a stale 20ms timer cleared the `isResponsibleLayer` flag. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/outside-click-timing.browser.test.ts: "should close on an outside click 0ms after the layer registers (rep 0)")
- Given a registered layer, when the outside click happens after each of the remaining sweep delays (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 20ms, two repetitions each), then the layer closes in every case. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/outside-click-timing.browser.test.ts: "should close on an outside click Nms after the layer registers (rep N)")
- Given a registered layer whose ref node is rerendered during an in-flight outside `pointerdown`, when the interaction completes, then the dismissal count reaches `1` and the revision count is `1`, so the interaction survives the rerender. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/registration-lifecycle.browser.test.ts: "keeps an in-flight outside interaction when the same ref rerenders")
- Given a layer whose ref is replaced by a new node, when the old node is removed and an outside `pointerdown` fires, then the dismissal count reaches `1`, so the replacement ref is registered. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/registration-lifecycle.browser.test.ts: "registers the replacement ref after the previous node is removed")
- Given a layer that mounts synchronously from an outside `pointerdown`, when 20ms pass, then the dismissal count is still `0`, and a subsequent outside `pointerdown` does dismiss it. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/registration-lifecycle.browser.test.ts: "does not dismiss from the pointerdown that synchronously mounts the layer")
- Given a layer that mounts and then unmounts during the same opening mutation, when 20ms pass, then the global `bitsDismissableLayers` registry holds no entry for that node and a later `pointerdown` on `document.body` never reads the destroyed layer's ref getter. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/registration-lifecycle.browser.test.ts: "does not leave a layer registered when it unmounts from the opening mutation")
- Given an outside element whose own handler calls `stopPropagation`, when a `pointerdown` fires on it, then after 20ms the dismissal count is `0`, and a `pointerdown` on a plain outside element still dismisses. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/registration-lifecycle.browser.test.ts: "does not dismiss an interaction whose delegated target stops propagation")
- Given a touch `pointerdown` outside that defers dismissal to the following `click`, when the layer is disabled before that `click` arrives, then the dismissal count stays `0`. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/registration-lifecycle.browser.test.ts: "cancels a pending touch click when the layer is disabled")

### Focus management
- Given an open layer story with an outside focusable element, when that element is focused, then the layer's content is removed. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "focus Outside > should close layer")
- Given the same story with `preventFocusOutsideEvent: true`, when the outside element is focused, then the content stays. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "focus Outside > should not close layer when prevented")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given a `DismissableLayerBranch`, when mounted the shared `context.branches` set contains its element and has size `1`, and when unmounted the set is empty. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should leave the branch registry empty after unmounting")
- Given a `DismissableLayer` story that is closed, when rendered, then the close label is not in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should render button without content")
- Given the same story, when the trigger is clicked, then the close label is in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "after clicking a trigger > should render the content")
- Given an outer layer with `disableOutsidePointerEvents` open, when a nested layer opens and then closes while the outer stays open, then `document.body.style.pointerEvents` stays `none` throughout (regression 2674). (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should keep body pointer-events none after a nested layer closes while outer stays open")
- Given the same nesting, when the inner layer's `disableOutsidePointerEvents` is toggled to `false` without unmounting and the inner layer is then unmounted, then the body stays `none` at every step because the outer layer still owns the lock. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should keep body pointer-events none when a nested layer toggles disableOutsidePointerEvents to false while mounted")
- Given a single layer whose `disableOutsidePointerEvents` toggles `true`, `false`, then `true` again, when each toggle settles, then the body reads `none`, then the empty string, then `none` again, proving the layer leaves and rejoins the tracking set cleanly. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should restore and re-lock body pointer-events as the only layer toggles disableOutsidePointerEvents")
- Given one open disabling layer, when it unmounts, then the body pointer-events is restored to the empty string. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should restore body pointer-events after the last layer closes")
- Given an older sibling layer with `disableOutsidePointerEvents` and a newer one that mounts while the older is still animating out, when the older unmounts, then the body stays `none`, and only closing the newer restores it. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should keep body pointer-events none after the older layer unmounts while a newer one is open")
- Given the same sibling pair, when the older closes and the newer opens in the same tick, then the body stays `none` and is restored only when the newer closes. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should keep body pointer-events none when the handoff happens in the same tick")
- Given a modal layer that also holds a `useBodyScrollLock`, and an overlay-less modal layer with no scroll lock opened over it, when the scroll-lock holder unmounts, then the body stays `none` because the remaining layer still owns it, and closing that layer restores the empty string (regression 2784). (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should keep body pointer-events none when the scroll-lock holder unmounts while a modal layer remains open")
- Given an overlay-less modal layer open first, when a scroll-locking modal layer opens on top and then closes, then the body stays `none` throughout and is restored only when the original layer closes. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should keep body pointer-events none when a scroll-locking layer opens and closes over a modal layer")
- Given a layer mounted with `disableOutsidePointerEvents: true`, when the prop is set to `false` while it stays mounted, then the body pointer-events is restored to the empty string. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should restore body pointer-events when toggled off while staying mounted")
- Given two mounted layers both disabling outside pointer events, when the topmost sets the prop to `false`, then the body stays `none`, and it is restored only after the first also sets it to `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "should keep body locked while another layer still disables pointer events")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given jsdom has no `PointerEvent`, the reka touch tests construct a `MouseEvent('pointerdown')` and define `pointerType: 'touch'` on it by hand, because `fireEvent.pointerDown` would otherwise drop `pointerType` and take the mouse code path. (reka: packages/core/src/DismissableLayer/DismissableLayer.test.ts: "given a DismissableLayer after a cancelled touch tap outside")
- Given the bits layer registry is exposed on `globalThis.bitsDismissableLayers`, the browser tests read it directly to assert registration and to wait for a layer's listeners to attach, so the library deliberately exposes internal state for testing. (bits: tests/src/tests/dismissible-layer/registration-lifecycle.browser.test.ts: "does not leave a layer registered when it unmounts from the opening mutation")

## escape-keydown

### Keyboard
- Given a single layer with `behaviorType: 'close'`, when Escape is dispatched on `document.documentElement`, then the handler is called once. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided 'close', on escape should close")
- Given a single layer with `behaviorType: 'ignore'`, when Escape is dispatched, then the handler is not called. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided 'ignore', on escape should not close")
- Given a single layer with `behaviorType: 'defer-otherwise-close'`, when Escape is dispatched with no other layer to defer to, then the handler is called once. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided 'defer-otherwise-close', on escape should close")
- Given a single layer with `behaviorType: 'defer-otherwise-ignore'`, when Escape is dispatched with no other layer, then the handler is not called. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided 'defer-otherwise-ignore', on escape should not close")
- Given two layers both `close`, when Escape is dispatched, then only the topmost handler runs. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided behaviors 'close,close', expected invocations 'false,true'")
- Given a `close` layer under a `defer-otherwise-close` layer, when Escape is dispatched, then the lower handler runs and the topmost does not, so the top layer defers downward. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided behaviors 'close,defer-otherwise-close', expected invocations 'true,false'")
- Given a `close` layer under a `defer-otherwise-ignore` layer, when Escape is dispatched, then the lower handler runs and the topmost does not. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided behaviors 'close,defer-otherwise-ignore', expected invocations 'true,false'")
- Given a `close` layer under an `ignore` layer, when Escape is dispatched, then neither handler runs, so `ignore` swallows the key for the whole stack. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided behaviors 'close,ignore', expected invocations 'false,false'")
- Given two `defer-otherwise-close` layers, when Escape is dispatched, then only the lower handler runs. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided behaviors 'defer-otherwise-close,defer-otherwise-close', expected invocations 'true,false'")
- Given two `defer-otherwise-ignore` layers, when Escape is dispatched, then neither handler runs. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "provided behaviors 'defer-otherwise-ignore,defer-otherwise-ignore', expected invocations 'false,false'")
- Given a `close` layer that has been destroyed, when Escape is dispatched, then the handler is not called. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "does not call handler after unmounting")
- Given a `close` layer, when Space is dispatched instead of Escape, then the handler is not called. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "does not call handler when other key is pressed")
- Given two `close` layers, when Escape runs only the top handler and the top layer is then destroyed, then a second Escape runs the lower handler once, so the listener stack unwinds correctly. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "correctly unmounts event listener and calls handler of top-most layer")
- Given two `close` layers, when the lower layer's options are updated to `ignore`, then the topmost layer still handles Escape and the lower layer's position in the stack is unchanged. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "does not change position of layer in the stack when options update")
- Given the lower layer's `behaviorType` supplied as a store, when that store is set to `ignore`, then the topmost layer still handles Escape and stack order is unchanged. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "does not change position of layer in the stack when updating behaviorType store")
- Given a `close` layer under a `defer-otherwise-close` layer where the lower handler ran first, when the top layer is updated to `close`, then the next Escape runs the top handler instead. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "respects updated behaviorType")
- Given the top layer's `behaviorType` supplied as a store holding `defer-otherwise-close`, when that store is set to `close`, then the next Escape runs the top handler. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "respects updated behaviorType store")
- Given two `close` layers, when the top layer's `behaviorType` is swapped from the string `'close'` to a store holding `'ignore'`, then the next Escape runs neither handler. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/escape-keydown.spec.ts: "respects updating behaviorType from string value to store")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given an open root dialog with a `dialog` opened inside it and the child configured `escapeBehavior: close`, when the child trigger is clicked and Escape is pressed, then the child content is removed and the root dialog content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + dialog > `escapeBehavior: close` on child should only close child")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: ignore`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `dialog` content and the root dialog content stay visible. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + dialog > `escapeBehavior: ignore` on child should neither close child nor parent")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-close`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `dialog` content and the root dialog content are removed. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + dialog > `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-close` on child should close both parent and child")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-ignore`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `dialog` content and the root dialog content are removed. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + dialog > `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-ignore` on child should close both parent and child")
- Given the same nesting with the child set to `close`, when the parent dialog is switched to `escapeBehavior: ignore` while the `dialog` is open and Escape is pressed, then the child closes and the parent stays open, proving the parent keeps its original position in the stack rather than being pushed to the top. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + dialog > updating parent `escapeBehavior` should not intercept escape key press")
- Given an open root dialog with a `combobox` opened inside it and the child configured `escapeBehavior: close`, when the child trigger is clicked and Escape is pressed, then the child content is removed and the root dialog content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + combobox > `escapeBehavior: close` on child should only close child")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: ignore`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `combobox` content and the root dialog content stay visible. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + combobox > `escapeBehavior: ignore` on child should neither close child nor parent")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-close`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `combobox` content and the root dialog content are removed. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + combobox > `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-close` on child should close both parent and child")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-ignore`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `combobox` content and the root dialog content are removed. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + combobox > `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-ignore` on child should close both parent and child")
- Given the same nesting with the child set to `close`, when the parent dialog is switched to `escapeBehavior: ignore` while the `combobox` is open and Escape is pressed, then the child closes and the parent stays open, proving the parent keeps its original position in the stack rather than being pushed to the top. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + combobox > updating parent `escapeBehavior` should not intercept escape key press")
- Given an open root dialog with a `link-preview` opened inside it and the child configured `escapeBehavior: close`, when the child trigger is hovered and Escape is pressed, then the child content is removed and the root dialog content stays visible. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + link-preview > `escapeBehavior: close` on child should only close child")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: ignore`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `link-preview` content and the root dialog content stay visible. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + link-preview > `escapeBehavior: ignore` on child should neither close child nor parent")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-close`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `link-preview` content and the root dialog content are removed. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + link-preview > `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-close` on child should close both parent and child")
- Given the same nesting with `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-ignore`, when Escape is pressed, then both the `link-preview` content and the root dialog content are removed. (melt: src/tests/escape-keydown/EscapeKeydown.spec.ts: "dialog + link-preview > `escapeBehavior: defer-otherwise-ignore` on child should close both parent and child")

## focus-scope

### Keyboard
- Given a `FocusScope asChild loop trapped` wrapping a form with two inputs and a submit button, when the first input is focused and Tab is pressed, then the second input has focus. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should focus the next element in the scope on tab")
- Given the same scope, when the first input is focused and Shift+Tab is pressed, then the submit button has focus, so the trap wraps backward. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should focus the last element in the scope on shift+tab from the first element in scope")
- Given the same scope, when the submit button is focused and Tab is pressed, then the first input has focus. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should focus the first element in scope on tab from the last element in scope")
- Given a scope whose first field has `tabIndex="-1"`, when the submit button is focused and Tab is pressed, then focus lands on the second field, skipping the negative-tabindex element. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should skip the element with a negative tabindex on tab")
- Given the same scope, when the second field is focused and Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus lands on the submit button rather than the negative-tabindex field. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should skip the element with a negative tabindex on shift+tab")

### Focus management
- Given a trapped scope whose focused element is removed from the DOM, when the removal settles, then the scope container itself has focus. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should focus container when focused element is removed from the DOM")
- Given a scope with a `blur` handler on the last focusable button, when focus cycles from the first element backward and then forward, then the blur handler fires exactly once, so cycling does not double-blur. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should properly blur the last element in the scope before cycling back")
- Given a Dialog containing an input followed by a `SelectTrigger`, when the dialog opens then the input has focus, and after closing with Escape and reopening the input has focus again rather than the `SelectTrigger` (regression 2550). (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should auto-focus the first tabbable element when SelectTrigger is present")
- Given a Dialog containing a Combobox whose portaled content holds a `ComboboxInput`, when the dialog and then the combobox are opened, then the input has focus and an explicit `input.focus()` also sticks, because the combobox content's `FocusScope` (registered without a `present` prop) pauses the dialog's trap (regression 2749). (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should let the Combobox input keep focus inside a Dialog")
- Given a Dialog containing a Select whose content is portaled out of the dialog, when the dialog and then the select are opened, then `document.activeElement` is inside the select content rather than being yanked back to the dialog. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should move focus into the Select content, not trap it back to the Dialog")
- Given a Dialog whose Combobox item select swaps the dialog's view for a form that focuses its own input on mount, when the item is clicked, then the new form input keeps focus even though the dialog's `lastFocusedElementRef` still points at the removed combobox trigger (regression 2886). (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "should keep focus on the input the swapped-in view focused on mount")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given the portaled-Select-in-Dialog case, `hasPointerCapture`, `releasePointerCapture`, and `scrollIntoView` are stubbed on `HTMLElement.prototype` because jsdom implements none of them, which is what makes the Select trigger usable at all in that environment. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusScope/FocusScope.test.ts: "given a FocusScope with portaled Select content inside Dialog (#2749)")

## focus-guards

### Focus management
- Given no guards in the document, when a `FocusGuards` component mounts, then exactly two `[data-reka-focus-guard]` elements exist in `document.body`, added synchronously by a `watchEffect`. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusGuards/FocusGuards.test.ts: "adds exactly 2 guard elements to document.body on mount")
- Given a mounted `FocusGuards`, when it unmounts, then no guard elements remain. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusGuards/FocusGuards.test.ts: "removes guard elements from document.body on unmount")
- Given two `FocusGuards` consumers mounted, when both are present, then there are still exactly two guard elements, because the existing guards are reused. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusGuards/FocusGuards.test.ts: "does not double-add guards when two consumers are mounted")
- Given two consumers, when the first unmounts then two guards remain, and only after the second unmounts do they drop to zero. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusGuards/FocusGuards.test.ts: "keeps guards when only one of two consumers unmounts")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a `FocusGuards` with slot content, when mounted, then the slotted element is present in the document. (reka: packages/core/src/FocusGuards/FocusGuards.test.ts: "renders slot content")

## body-scroll-lock

### Dismissal and layering
- Given `useBodyScrollLock()` with no argument, when the returned ref is set to `true` then `false`, then `document.body.style.overflow` goes from the empty string to `hidden` and back. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useBodyScrollLock.test.ts: "should lock the body properly")
- Given a component calling `useBodyScrollLock(true)`, when mounted the body overflow is `hidden`, and when unmounted it is restored to the empty string. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useBodyScrollLock.test.ts: "should lock and unlock the body when mounted and unmounted")
- Given two components each holding a lock, when the first unmounts the body stays `hidden`, and only after the second unmounts does the overflow clear. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useBodyScrollLock.test.ts: "should only unlock once all are unmounted")
- Given two locks created directly with `useBodyScrollLock(true)`, when the first is set to `false` the body stays `hidden`, and only after the second is set to `false` does it clear. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useBodyScrollLock.test.ts: "should only unlock once all are unlocked")
- Given `useBodyScrollLock()` with no argument, when nothing else happens, then the body is never locked. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useBodyScrollLock.test.ts: "should not automatically lock")
- Given a lock toggled `true` then `false` inside the same synchronous tick, when the tick flushes, then both `body.style.overflow` and `body.style.pointerEvents` are the empty string, so a rapid toggle does not leave the page permanently locked. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useBodyScrollLock.test.ts: "should not permanently lock when toggled rapidly in the same tick")
- Given `document.body.style.overflow` is already `scroll`, when a lock is applied and released, then the overflow goes `scroll`, `hidden`, and back to `scroll`, so the user's own value is preserved rather than cleared. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useBodyScrollLock.test.ts: "should preserve user overflow")
- Given a `BodyScrollLock(true)` in a Svelte effect root whose body style was `color: red; overflow: auto;`, when the root is destroyed and the delayed 24ms cleanup runs while the global `document` has been stubbed to `undefined`, then the cleanup does not throw, the original body style attribute is restored exactly, `--scrollbar-width` is cleared, and no other document's body is touched. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/body-scroll-lock.svelte.test.ts: "restores the original body when the global document is unavailable before delayed cleanup")
- Given the same setup but with the global `document` replaced by a different `HTMLDocument` whose body style is `color: blue`, when the delayed cleanup runs, then the original document's body style is restored and the replacement document's body style attribute is left unchanged. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/body-scroll-lock.svelte.test.ts: "restores the original body when the global document is replaced before delayed cleanup")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given `window.innerWidth` 200 and `documentElement.clientWidth` 190 with a mocked `ConfigProvider` supplying `dir: 'ltr'` and `scrollBody: true`, the reka lock tests run against a 10px scrollbar gap, which is the value the `ConfigProvider` suite asserts as `padding-right`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useBodyScrollLock.test.ts: "useBodyScrollLock")
- Given the bits lock schedules its restore work on a 24ms `setTimeout`, the test finds that exact delay in the `setTimeout` spy's calls and invokes the captured callback by hand, so the 24ms window is part of the observable contract. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/body-scroll-lock.svelte.test.ts: "BodyScrollLock")

## typeahead

### Keyboard
- Given the values `['apple','banana','cherry','date','elderberry']` and no current match, when `getNextMatch(values, 'b')` runs, then it returns `'banana'`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should return the first match when no current match is provided")
- Given search `'c'`, when the current match is already `'cherry'`, then the result is `undefined`, and when the current match is `'banana'` the result is `'cherry'`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should return the next match when a current match is provided")
- Given a repeated-character search `'aaa'`, when the current match is `'apple'` the result is `undefined`, and when it is `'banana'` the result is `'apple'`, so repeated characters collapse to a single-character search. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should handle repeated characters in search")
- Given search `'a'` with current match `'elderberry'`, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it wraps around and returns `'apple'`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should wrap around the array when reaching the end")
- Given searches `'B'` and `'cH'`, when `getNextMatch` runs, then matching is case-insensitive and returns `'banana'` and `'cherry'`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should be case-insensitive")
- Given an empty search string, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it returns `undefined`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should handle empty search string")
- Given an empty values array, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it returns `undefined`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should handle empty values array")
- Given a single-character search equal to the current match's initial, when `getNextMatch` runs, then the current match is excluded from the candidates. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should exclude current match when search is a single character")
- Given a multi-character search that matches only the current item, when `getNextMatch` runs, then the result is `undefined`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should not exclude current match when search is multiple characters")
- Given values sharing the prefix `'prefix'` plus `'other'` and the multi-character search `'pre'`, when the current match is any prefixed value, then the result is `undefined`, and when it is `'other'` the result is `'prefix1'`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should handle values with common prefixes")
- Given the same values and the single-character search `'p'`, when `getNextMatch` is called repeatedly, then it cycles `other -> prefix1 -> prefix2 -> prefix3 -> prefix1`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should cycle through values with common prefixes using single character search")
- Given the search `'p'` with no current match then `'prefix1'`, and the search `'o'` with no current match then `'other'`, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it returns `'prefix1'`, `'prefix2'`, `'other'`, and `undefined` in that order. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should handle single character search with prefixed values")
- Given values containing spaces, when searches `'b'`, `'banana '`, `'banana b'`, `'banana s'`, `'banana  '`, `'apple'`, and `'apple p'` run, then they resolve to `'banana split'`, `'banana split'`, `'banana bread'`, `'banana split'`, `undefined`, `'apple pie'`, and `'apple pie'`, so spaces are matched literally and a double space matches nothing. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "getNextMatch > should handle search with spaces")
- Given `['a','b','c','d']` and start index 2, when `wrapArray` runs, then the result is `['c','d','a','b']`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "wrapArray > wraps the array around itself at the given start index")
- Given start index 0, when `wrapArray` runs, then the order is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "wrapArray > returns the same order when start index is 0")
- Given start index 5 over four items, when `wrapArray` runs, then the modulo applies and the result is `['b','c','d','a']`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "wrapArray > handles start index larger than length via modulo")
- Given `['Apple','Banana','Cherry']` and search `'b'`, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it returns `'Banana'`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "getNextMatch > matches a basic prefix")
- Given search `'B'` against title-case values and `'BA'` against lowercase values, when `getNextMatch` runs, then both match, so comparison is case-insensitive in both directions. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "getNextMatch > matches case-insensitively")
- Given `['Apple','Avocado','Banana']`, search `'aa'`, and current match `'Apple'`, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it returns `'Avocado'`, because a repeated-character search normalises to one character and then excludes the current match. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "getNextMatch > cycles to the NEXT value on repeated-character search, excluding current match")
- Given current match `'Cherry'` at the end of the list and search `'a'`, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it wraps around and returns `'Apple'`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "getNextMatch > searches forward from the current match and wraps past the end of the array")
- Given search `'z'` with no matching value, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it returns `undefined`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "getNextMatch > returns undefined when nothing matches")
- Given search `'a'` where the only match is the current match `'Apple'`, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it returns `undefined` so focus does not move. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "getNextMatch > returns undefined when the only match IS the current match")
- Given search `'ap'` and current match `'Apple'` where `'Apricot'` also matches, when `getNextMatch` runs, then it returns `undefined`, because a multi-character non-repeated search keeps the current match in the candidate set and it still matches. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "getNextMatch > does not exclude the current match for multi-character (non-repeated) searches")
- Given three items with stubbed `focus` methods, when `handleTypeaheadSearch('b', items)` runs, then only the Banana item's `focus` is called once and the function returns that element ref. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "useTypeahead > focuses the matching element when typing")
- Given two items with `tabIndex = -1` attached to `document.body`, when a typeahead search runs, then `document.activeElement` is the matching element, so real focus moves rather than only the stub being called. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "focuses via document.activeElement when elements are attached to the body")
- Given an item whose `textContent` is `'Zzz'` but whose `value.textValue` is `'Banana'`, when searching `'b'`, then that item is focused, so `textValue` takes precedence over `textContent`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "uses item.value.textValue with precedence over textContent")
- Given a fresh typeahead, when `'b'` then `'a'` are searched, then the `search` buffer reads `'b'` then `'ba'` and the Banana item stays the match. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "accumulates the search buffer across calls")
- Given a search that set the buffer to `'a'`, when 1000ms of fake time passes, then the buffer is the empty string. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "resets the search buffer after 1000ms")
- Given a search that set the buffer to `'a'`, when `resetTypeahead()` is called, then the buffer is immediately the empty string without waiting for the timer. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "resetTypeahead clears the buffer immediately")
- Given `useTypeahead(callback)`, when a search runs, then the callback is called once with `'b'`, neither item's `focus` is called, the `search` buffer still updates to `'b'`, and the return value is `undefined`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useTypeahead.test.ts: "invokes the callback with the key and does NOT focus when a callback is provided")

## arrow-navigation

### Keyboard
- Given an empty array, when `back([], 0, 1, true)` is called, then it returns `undefined`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "back([], 0, 1, true) -> undefined")
- Given `['a','b','c','d']` at index 3 with increment 2 and no looping, when `back` runs, then it returns `'b'`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "back(a,b,c,d, 3, 2, false) -> b")
- Given index 2 with increment 5 and looping disabled, when `back` runs, then it clamps and returns the first element `'a'`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "back(a,b,c,d, 2, 5, false) -> a")
- Given index 0 with increment 5 and looping enabled, when `back` runs, then it wraps and returns the last element `'d'`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "back(a,b,c,d, 0, 5, true) -> d")
- Given an empty array, when `forward([], 0, 1, true)` is called, then it returns `undefined`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "forward([], 0, 1, true) -> undefined")
- Given index 0 with increment 2 and no looping, when `forward` runs, then it returns `'c'`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "forward(a,b,c,d, 0, 2, false) -> c")
- Given index 0 with increment 5 and looping disabled, when `forward` runs, then it clamps to the last element `'d'`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "forward(a,b,c,d, 0, 5, false) -> d")
- Given index 0 with increment 5 and looping enabled over four items, when `forward` runs, then it wraps to `'a'`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "forward(a,b,c,d, 0, 5, true) -> a")
- Given an empty array, when `last([])` is called, then it returns `undefined`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "last([]) -> undefined")
- Given `['a','b','c']`, when `last` is called, then it returns `'c'`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "last(a,b,c) -> c")
- Given an empty array, when `next([], 0, true)` is called, then it returns `undefined`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "next([], 0, true) -> undefined")
- Given `['a','b','c']` and an out-of-bounds index 4, when `next` runs, then it returns `undefined`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/array.spec.ts: "next(a,b,c, 4, true) -> undefined")

- Given a zero increment, when `forward` runs, then it returns the element at the starting index. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "forward function > handles zero increment")

- Given negative increments with looping disabled, when `forward` runs, then it clamps to the first element. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "forward function > handles negative increments with looping disabled")

- Given three `[data-reka-collection-item]` children and `arrowKeyOptions: 'horizontal'`, when ArrowRight fires from the first child, then the second child is returned. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should navigate horizontally")

(reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should not navigate with arrow keys when arrowKeyOptions is not set to both")

- Given `loop: false` and the current element being the first child, when ArrowLeft fires, then the result is `null`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should not loop through items if loop is set to false")
- Given the second and third children both carrying `disabled="true"`, when ArrowRight fires from the first child, then the result is `null`, so disabled items are skipped and there is nothing left to land on. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should skip disabled items")
- Given `dir: 'rtl'`, when ArrowRight fires from the first child, then the third child is returned, so the horizontal axis is mirrored. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should navigate correctly in rtl")
- Given three children, when Home fires from the first child, then the third child is returned. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should navigate to the first item")
- Given three children, when End fires from the second child, then the first child is returned. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should navigate to the last item")
- Given a container with exactly one collection item and a current element that is an unrelated `input`, when ArrowDown fires, then that single item is returned. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should navigate to the first item when there is only one item and currentElement is not in the collection")
- Given a container with three items and an external `input` as the current element, when ArrowUp fires, then the last item is returned. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useArrowNavigation.test.ts: "should navigate to the last item when pressing ArrowUp from an external element")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given two empty arrays, when `arraysAreEqual` runs, then it returns `true`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should return true for two empty arrays")
- Given two arrays with the same elements in the same order, when compared, then the result is `true`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should return true for two arrays with the same elements in the same order")
- Given arrays of different lengths, when compared, then the result is `false`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should return false for two arrays with different lengths")
- Given arrays differing in one element, when compared, then the result is `false`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should return false for two arrays with different elements")
- Given the same elements in a different order, when compared, then the result is `false`, so the comparison is order-sensitive. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should return false for two arrays with elements in different orders")
- Given two distinct objects with identical fields, when compared, then the result is `true`, so comparison is structural not referential. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should handle arrays with non-primitive values")
- Given two objects with different field values, when compared, then the result is `false`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should handle arrays with different non-primitive values")
- Given nested arrays, when compared, then equal nesting returns `true` and reordered nesting returns `false`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should handle nested arrays")
- Given `[1, "2", true]` against itself and against `[1, 2, true]`, when compared, then the first is `true` and the second is `false`, so types are not coerced. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should handle arrays with different types of elements")
- Given a sparse array `[1, , 3]` and `[1, undefined, 3]`, when compared, then the result is `true`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should handle sparse arrays")
- Given `[NaN]` against `[NaN]`, when compared, then the result is `true`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "arraysAreEqual > should handle NaN values")
- Given an empty array, when `chunk([], 2)` runs, then it returns an empty array. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "chunk > should return an empty array when given an empty array")
- Given a size at or above the array length, when `chunk` runs, then it returns a single chunk holding everything. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "chunk > should return an array with one chunk when size is greater than or equal to array length")
- Given `[1,2,3,4]` size 2 and `[1,2,3,4,5]` size 2, when `chunk` runs, then it returns even pairs and a trailing partial chunk `[5]`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "chunk > should chunk the array into arrays of the specified size")
- Given mixed-type arrays, when `chunk` runs, then values are grouped without coercion. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "chunk > should work with arrays containing different types")
- Given size 0 or `-1`, when `chunk` runs, then it returns an empty array rather than looping forever. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/arrays.test.ts: "chunk > should handle negative or zero size")

## grace-area

### Pointer
- Given `useGraceArea(triggerRef, containerRef)` with a 100x100 trigger at the origin and a 100x100 container at x 200 to 300, when a `pointerleave` at (100, 50) fires on the trigger, then `isPointerInTransit` becomes `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "sets isPointerInTransit to true on a trigger pointerleave")
- Given a grace polygon built by a trigger `pointerleave` at (100, 50), when a document `pointermove` at (150, 50) lands inside the hull with `document.body` as target, then `isPointerInTransit` stays `true` and the `onPointerExit` callback is not called. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "keeps isPointerInTransit true and does not fire exit for a pointermove inside the hull")
- Given a grace polygon built by a trigger `pointerleave` at (100, 50), when a document `pointermove` at (150, 500) lands outside the hull, then `onPointerExit` is called exactly once and `isPointerInTransit` resets to `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "fires onPointerExit and resets when a pointermove leaves the hull")
- Given a grace polygon in transit, when a `pointermove` is dispatched on the container element itself at coordinates (150, 500) that are outside the hull, then `onPointerExit` is not called and `isPointerInTransit` resets to `false`, so the entered-target branch wins over the geometry check. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "removes the grace area without firing exit when the pointer enters the container")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given a grace polygon entered by a trigger `pointerleave` under fake timers, when 300ms are advanced without any pointer movement, then `isPointerInTransit` auto-resets to `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "auto-resets isPointerInTransit after 300ms")
- Given a grace polygon entered by a trigger `pointerleave`, when the owning component unmounts, then `isPointerInTransit` becomes `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "resets isPointerInTransit to false on unmount")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given jsdom's all-zero `getBoundingClientRect`, when these tests run, then both element rects are stubbed by hand and the event constructor falls back from `PointerEvent` to `MouseEvent`, so the hull geometry under test is supplied rather than measured. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "useGraceArea")
- Given the documented hull for the stubbed rects, when a trigger `pointerleave` exits the right side at (100, 50), then the padded exit points sit near (99, 49) and (99, 51) and the convex hull spans x from 99 to 300, which is why (150, 50) counts as inside and (150, 500) as outside. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "keeps isPointerInTransit true and does not fire exit for a pointermove inside the hull")
- Given the composable's return shape, when set up in a component, then it exposes `isPointerInTransit` as a ref and `onPointerExit` as a callback registrar, and the document `pointermove` listener is only attached after a `nextTick` following the `pointerleave`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useGraceArea.test.ts: "fires onPointerExit and resets when a pointermove leaves the hull")

## roving-focus

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `RovingFocusGroup` with `defaultValue: 'one'` over four buttons, when rendered, then the first button has `data-active=""` and the second and third have no `data-active`. (reka: packages/core/src/RovingFocus/RovingFocus.test.ts: "should have default selected value based on `defaultValue`")

### Keyboard
- Given `defaultValue: 'two'` and the third button disabled, when Tab focuses the group and ArrowRight is pressed, then focus skips the disabled third button and lands on the fourth, and a further ArrowRight leaves focus on the fourth because `loop` defaults to false. (reka: packages/core/src/RovingFocus/RovingFocus.test.ts: "[loop=false]: should stop at last item")
- Given `defaultValue: 'two'` and `loop: true`, when Tab focuses the group and ArrowRight is pressed twice, then focus wraps past the fourth button to the first. (reka: packages/core/src/RovingFocus/RovingFocus.test.ts: "[loop=true]: should loop through items")

### Focus management
- Given a `RovingFocusGroup` with four buttons and nothing focused, when Tab is pressed once then focus is on the first button, and when Tab is pressed again then focus leaves the group back to `document.body`, so the group is a single tab stop. (reka: packages/core/src/RovingFocus/RovingFocus.test.ts: "should only receive focus once, and select first item")

## collection

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a provider with three registered `CollectionItem`s, when the DOM settles, then `itemMapSize` is `3` and `reactiveItems` holds three entries whose values are `a`, `b`, and `c`. (reka: packages/core/src/Collection/Collection.test.ts: "registers items into reactiveItems and itemMapSize reflects the count")
- Given three items whose registration order is not guaranteed to match the template, when `getItems()` is called, then the values come back in DOM order and match the order of `document.querySelectorAll('[data-reka-collection-item]')`. (reka: packages/core/src/Collection/Collection.test.ts: "getItems() returns items in DOM order even when registration order differs")
- Given a middle item rendered with `data-disabled=""`, when `getItems()` is called, then it returns only `['a','c']`, and `getItems(true)` returns `['a','b','c']` in DOM order. (reka: packages/core/src/Collection/Collection.test.ts: "filters out items with data-disabled=\"\" by default, includes them with getItems(true)")
- Given three registered items, when the middle one is spliced out of the reactive source and unmounts, then `itemMapSize` drops to `2` and `getItems()` returns `['a','c']`. (reka: packages/core/src/Collection/Collection.test.ts: "removes an item from the map when it unmounts")
- Given one enabled and one disabled item, when `getItem(element)` is called, then the enabled element resolves to its registered entry, the disabled element resolves to `undefined`, `getItem(disabled, true)` resolves to its entry, and an unregistered element resolves to `undefined`. (reka: packages/core/src/Collection/Collection.test.ts: "looks up registered items by element and preserves disabled filtering")
- Given a single registered item whose element is detached from the document, when `getItem(element)` is called, then the registered entry still comes back, and after the item unmounts the same lookup returns `undefined`. (reka: packages/core/src/Collection/Collection.test.ts: "finds detached registered items but not unmounted items")
- Given a provider whose `CollectionSlot` is never mounted, when the collection is queried, then `getItem` returns `undefined`, both `getItems()` and `getItems(true)` return `[]`, and `itemMapSize` is `0`. (reka: packages/core/src/Collection/Collection.test.ts: "getItems() returns [] when no CollectionSlot element is mounted")

## popper

### Roles and attributes
- Given a default Popper with anchor, content, and arrow, when rendered, then the snapshot pins a floating wrapper `div` carrying `data-reka-popper-content-wrapper` and `dir="ltr"`, an inner content `div` with `data-align="center"`, `data-side="bottom"` and `dir="ltr"`, and an arrow `span` wrapping a 10x6-viewBox `svg` with `width="10"`, `height="5"`, `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, `rounded="false"` and path `M0 0L6 6L12 0`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "give default Popper > should render correctly and match snapshot")
- Given a `PopperContent` with `dir="rtl"`, when mounted, then the `[data-reka-popper-content-wrapper]` element has `dir="rtl"` so placement and transform origin agree. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "popper wrapper dir attribute > sets dir on the floatingRef wrapper so placement and origin are consistent")
- Given a `PopperContent` with `dir="ltr"` passed explicitly, when mounted, then the `[data-reka-popper-content-wrapper]` element has `dir="ltr"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "popper wrapper dir attribute > sets dir=ltr on the wrapper when explicitly passed")

### Positioning
- Given the default Popper snapshot, when rendered in jsdom, then the wrapper's inline style is `position: fixed; left: 0px; top: 0px; transform: translate(0, -200%); min-width: max-content;`, so the off-screen pre-measurement transform and `min-width: max-content` are pinned. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "give default Popper > should render correctly and match snapshot")
- Given the default Popper snapshot, when rendered, then the arrow span's inline style is `position: absolute; top: 0px; transform-origin: center 0; transform: rotate(180deg); visibility: hidden;`, pinning the bottom-side arrow rotation and its hidden state before measurement. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "give default Popper > should render correctly and match snapshot")
- Given the default Popper snapshot, when rendered, then the content element's inline style is `animation: none;`, so entry animation is suppressed until the first position is computed. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "give default Popper > should render correctly and match snapshot")

### RTL and i18n
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow and `dir: 'rtl'` at placement `bottom-start`, when the middleware runs, then the returned `x` origin is `100%`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "bottom placement > rTL flips start origin to 100%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow and `dir: 'ltr'` at placement `bottom-start`, when the middleware runs, then the returned `x` origin is `0%`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "bottom placement > lTR keeps start origin at 0%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow and `dir: 'rtl'` at placement `bottom-end`, when the middleware runs, then the returned `x` origin is `0%`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "bottom placement > rTL flips end origin to 0%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow and `dir: 'ltr'` at placement `bottom-end`, when the middleware runs, then the returned `x` origin is `100%`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "bottom placement > lTR keeps end origin at 100%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow at plain `bottom` placement, when run with `dir: 'rtl'` and with `dir: 'ltr'`, then the `x` origin is `50%` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "bottom placement > center is unaffected by dir")
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow and `dir: 'rtl'` at placement `top-start`, when the middleware runs, then the returned `x` origin is `100%`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "top placement > rTL flips start origin to 100%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow and `dir: 'ltr'` at placement `top-start`, when the middleware runs, then the returned `x` origin is `0%`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "top placement > lTR keeps start origin at 0%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow and `dir: 'rtl'` at placement `top-end`, when the middleware runs, then the returned `x` origin is `0%`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "top placement > rTL flips end origin to 0%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with no arrow and `dir: 'ltr'` at placement `top-end`, when the middleware runs, then the returned `x` origin is `100%`. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "top placement > lTR keeps end origin at 100%")
- Given `transformOrigin` at placement `right-start`, when run with `dir: 'rtl'` and `dir: 'ltr'`, then the `y` origin is `0%` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "left/right placements use Y-axis alignment, unaffected by dir > right-start: y origin is 0% for both RTL and LTR")
- Given `transformOrigin` at placement `right-end`, when run with `dir: 'rtl'` and `dir: 'ltr'`, then the `y` origin is `100%` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "left/right placements use Y-axis alignment, unaffected by dir > right-end: y origin is 100% for both RTL and LTR")
- Given `transformOrigin` at placement `left-start`, when run with `dir: 'rtl'` and `dir: 'ltr'`, then the `y` origin is `0%` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "left/right placements use Y-axis alignment, unaffected by dir > left-start: y origin is 0% for both RTL and LTR")
- Given `transformOrigin` at placement `left-end`, when run with `dir: 'rtl'` and `dir: 'ltr'`, then the `y` origin is `100%` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "left/right placements use Y-axis alignment, unaffected by dir > left-end: y origin is 100% for both RTL and LTR")
- Given `transformOrigin` with `dir` left undefined at `bottom` placement, when run, then `bottom-start` yields `x` of `0%` and `bottom-end` yields `100%`, matching LTR. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "default dir (undefined) > bottom placement defaults to LTR: start → 0%, end → 100%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with `dir` left undefined at `top` placement, when run, then `top-start` yields `x` of `0%` and `top-end` yields `100%`, matching LTR. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "default dir (undefined) > top placement defaults to LTR: start → 0%, end → 100%")
- Given `transformOrigin` with `arrowWidth: 10`, `arrowHeight: 5` and arrow middleware data `{ x: 20, y: 15 }` at `bottom-start`, when run with both `dir` values, then the `x` origin is `25px` in both cases, computed as arrow `x` plus half the arrow width. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "arrow-visible scenario: arrow-based x/y positioning is not affected by dir > bottom placement uses arrow x center regardless of dir")
- Given the same arrow data at `top-end`, when run with both `dir` values, then the `x` origin is `25px` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "arrow-visible scenario: arrow-based x/y positioning is not affected by dir > top placement uses arrow x center regardless of dir")
- Given the same arrow data at `right-start`, when run with both `dir` values, then the `y` origin is `17.5px` in both cases, computed as arrow `y` plus half the arrow height. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "arrow-visible scenario: arrow-based x/y positioning is not affected by dir > right placement uses arrow y center regardless of dir")
- Given the same arrow data at `left-end`, when run with both `dir` values, then the `y` origin is `17.5px` in both cases. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "arrow-visible scenario: arrow-based x/y positioning is not affected by dir > left placement uses arrow y center regardless of dir")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given `transformOrigin` under test, when invoked, then it is called as a bare floating-ui middleware with a hand-built `{ placement, rects.floating, middlewareData.arrow }` payload and asserted through `result.data`, so the CSS custom properties the Popper writes (`--reka-popper-transform-origin`, `--reka-popper-available-width`, `--reka-popper-available-height`, `--reka-popper-anchor-width`, `--reka-popper-anchor-height`) are exercised only through this returned origin data and never asserted as inline custom properties, and the snapshot does not record them either. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "transformOrigin direction-aware logic")
- Given reka's Popper tests, when they run, then `globalThis.ResizeObserver` is stubbed with no-op methods in both the default and `dir` describe blocks. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "popper wrapper dir attribute")
- Given the Popper suite, when read as a whole, then it asserts no collision behavior: `avoidCollisions`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary`, `sticky`, `updatePositionStrategy`, `side`/`align` overrides, and `arrowPadding` are all untested here. (reka: packages/core/src/Popper/Popper.test.ts: "give default Popper > should render correctly and match snapshot")

## portal

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `Teleport` with `forceMount` inside a host `div`, when mounted, then the slot content exists in the document but `host.contains(content)` is `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/Teleport/Teleport.test.ts: "teleports slot content into document.body by default")
- Given a `Portal` with no `to`, when rendered, then the content's `parentElement` is `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should portal content to document.body by default")
- Given a `Portal` with a `content` prop, when rendered, then the portalled node has that text content. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should display the portal content")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given `Teleport disabled` with `forceMount`, when mounted, then the content renders inline and the host `div` contains it. (reka: packages/core/src/Teleport/Teleport.test.ts: "renders inline when disabled=true")
- Given `Portal disabled`, when rendered, then the main container contains the content and its `parentElement` is not `document.body`. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should render inline when disabled")
- Given `Portal to="#string-target" disabled`, when rendered, then the target does not receive the content and the main container keeps it, so `disabled` overrides `to`. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should not portal when disabled even with target")

### Dismissal and layering
- Given a popover containing a tooltip trigger, run once with sibling portals (`portal: 'body'`) and once with a single portal (`portal: undefined`), when the tooltip content is clicked, then the tooltip stays visible and the popover stays open. (melt: src/tests/portal/Portal.spec.ts: "Portal Behaviors > Popover & Tooltip > should not close the popover when the tooltip content is clicked")
- Given an open popover with an open tooltip inside it, when the popover content is clicked, then the tooltip closes and the popover stays open. (melt: src/tests/portal/Portal.spec.ts: "should close the tooltip content when the popover content is clicked and tooltip is open")
- Given an open popover with an open tooltip inside it, when Escape is pressed, then only the tooltip closes, and a subsequent outside click closes the popover. (melt: src/tests/portal/Portal.spec.ts: "should not close the popover when escape is pressed while tooltip is open")
- Given an open popover with an open tooltip configured `tooltipEscapeBehavior: 'ignore'`, when Escape is pressed, then both the tooltip and the popover stay visible. (melt: src/tests/portal/Portal.spec.ts: "should not close the popover nor the tooltip when escape is pressed while tooltip is open and tooltip `closeOnEscape` is false")
- Given an open popover containing a tags input, when a tag is double-clicked into edit mode and then an outside element is clicked, then the edit input loses focus but the popover stays open. (melt: src/tests/portal/Portal.spec.ts: "Popover & Tags Input > should not close popover on click outside while editing tag")
- Given an open popover containing a tags input in edit mode, when Escape is pressed, then the edit input loses focus and the popover stays open. (melt: src/tests/portal/Portal.spec.ts: "should not close popover on escape while editing tag")
- Given an open popover containing an open select menu, when Escape is pressed, then the select menu closes, the popover stays open, and ten Tab presses keep focus inside the popover content. (melt: src/tests/portal/Portal.spec.ts: "Popover & Select > should not deactivate popover focus trap on escape while select is open")
- Given an open popover containing an open select menu, when an outside element is clicked, then the select menu closes, the popover stays open, and its focus trap still holds for ten Tab presses. (melt: src/tests/portal/Portal.spec.ts: "should not deactivate popover focus trap on outside click while select is open")
- Given a recursive nesting of dialog inside dialog inside dropdown-menu inside select, and popover inside dialog and popover, and a sibling select, run across the four combinations of `portal: 'body'`/`undefined` and `forceVisible: true`/`false`, when each trigger is clicked depth-first, then every level's content becomes visible, its immediate children's triggers become visible, grandchildren stay hidden until their parent opens, and each level closes on Escape and on outside click while its own trigger and outside element stay visible. (melt: src/tests/portal/PortalNested.spec.ts: "recursive component test")

### Positioning
- Given `Teleport to="#custom-container"`, when mounted, then the container contains the teleported node. (reka: packages/core/src/Teleport/Teleport.test.ts: "teleports to a custom container element")
