- Given a `ConfigProvider` with `teleportTo="#config-container"` wrapping a `Teleport` with no `to`, when mounted, then the config container contains the teleported node. (reka: packages/core/src/Teleport/Teleport.test.ts: "uses the ConfigProvider `teleportTo` target as the default")
- Given a `ConfigProvider teleportTo="#config-fallback"` wrapping a `Teleport to="#explicit-target"`, when mounted, then the explicit target contains the node and the config fallback does not. (reka: packages/core/src/Teleport/Teleport.test.ts: "prefers an explicit `to` prop over the ConfigProvider `teleportTo`")
- Given `Portal to="#string-target"`, when rendered, then the content's `parentElement` is the element with that id. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should portal to element by ID selector")
- Given `Portal to=".class-target"`, when rendered, then the content's `parentElement` is the element matching that class. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should portal to element by class selector")
- Given `Portal to='[data-testid="custom-target"]'`, when rendered, then the content's `parentElement` is the element matching that attribute selector. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should portal to element by attribute selector")
- Given `Portal to` set to a live `HTMLElement` reference rather than a selector string, when rendered, then the content's `parentElement` is that element. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should portal to HTMLElement target")
- Given `Portal to` set to a `div` that was appended through a `DocumentFragment`, when rendered, then the content's `parentElement` is that container. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should portal to DocumentFragment target")
- Given two `Portal` instances targeting `#string-target` and `.class-target`, when both render, then two portal nodes exist and each sits under its own target. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should handle multiple portals to different targets")

### Animation and presence
- Given a `Portal` that has rendered content, when the component unmounts, then the portalled node is removed from the document. (bits: tests/src/tests/portal/portal.browser.test.ts: "should clean up portal content when component unmounts")

## slot

### Roles and attributes
- Given a `Primitive` with no `as` prop, when rendered, then it renders a `div`. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should render div element correctly")
- Given a `Primitive` with `as="button"`, when rendered, then it renders a `button`. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should render button element correctly")
- Given a `Primitive` with a non-component attribute such as `type="button"` and no `as`, when rendered, then the rendered `div` carries `type="button"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should renders div element with custom attribute")
- Given a `Primitive` with three sibling `div` children, when rendered, then all three children are present. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should renders multiple child elements")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given `as="template"` and a slot whose first node is an HTML comment, when rendered, then the comment is skipped and the parent's `data-parent-attr` lands on the first element node alongside the child's own `data-child-attr`. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should by pass the comment tag")
- Given `as="template"` with three sibling children, when mounted, then all three render and no "invalid children" error is thrown. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "render as template (asChild) > should not throw error when multiple child elements exists")
- Given `as="template"` with three sibling children and a `type="button"` prop, when rendered, then only the first child receives `type="button"` and the second and third have it undefined. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should pass custom attribute to first element")
- Given `as="template"` with `class="parent-class"` and a child with `class="child-class more-child-class"`, when rendered, then the child's `class` is the concatenation `parent-class child-class more-child-class`, parent first. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should merge child's class together")
- Given a `Primitive as="template" class="parent-class"` nested inside a component that re-renders on click, when the subtree re-renders twice, then the merged class stays exactly `parent-class child-class more-child-class` and does not accumulate duplicates. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should merge child's class after update")
- Given `as` set to a `markRaw` component that renders `<button id="custom-button">` and a parent `class="parent-class"`, when rendered, then the output HTML is exactly `<button id="custom-button" class="parent-class"></button>`. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should render the Component that passed in as")
- Given `as="template"` with an `<a>` child, when rendered, then the `<a>` tag is preserved rather than replaced by a wrapper. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should render the child class element tag")
- Given a `Primitive` wrapping a child component, when rendered, then the child component's own markup `<div id="child">Hello world</div>` is emitted unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should render the child component")
- Given `as="template"` with parent `data-parent-attr` and child `data-child-attr`, when rendered, then the child element carries both attributes. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should inherit parent attributes and the child attributes")
- Given `as="template"` with parent `id="parent" data-type="button"` and child `id="child" data-type="primary"`, when rendered, then the child's values win: `id="child"` and `data-type="primary"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "should replace parent attributes with child's attributes")
- Given `asChild: true` with `class="parent-class"` and a `<button class="child-class">` child, when rendered, then the button renders with merged `class="parent-class child-class"`, identical to `as="template"`. (reka: packages/core/src/Primitive/Primitive.test.ts: "'asChild=true' should work the same as 'as=template'")

## direction

### RTL and i18n
- Given a default `ConfigProvider`, when rendered, then the subtree contains `dir="ltr"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ConfigProvider/ConfigProvider.test.ts: "should render direction=\"ltr\"")
- Given a `ConfigProvider dir="rtl"`, when rendered, then the subtree contains `dir="rtl"`. (reka: packages/core/src/ConfigProvider/ConfigProvider.test.ts: "should render direction=\"rtl\"")
- Given no `dir` and no `orientation`, when `getNextKey` is called, then it returns `ArrowRight`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getNextKey(undefined, undefined) -> ArrowRight")
- Given `dir: 'rtl'`, when `getNextKey` is called, then it returns `ArrowLeft`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getNextKey(rtl, undefined) -> ArrowLeft")
- Given `orientation: 'vertical'`, when `getNextKey` is called, then it returns `ArrowDown`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getNextKey(undefined, vertical) -> ArrowDown")
- Given `dir: 'rtl'` and `orientation: 'vertical'`, when `getNextKey` is called, then it still returns `ArrowDown`, so RTL does not invert the vertical axis. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getNextKey(rtl, vertical) -> ArrowDown")
- Given no `dir` and no `orientation`, when `getPrevKey` is called, then it returns `ArrowLeft`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getPrevKey(undefined, undefined) -> ArrowLeft")
- Given `dir: 'rtl'`, when `getPrevKey` is called, then it returns `ArrowRight`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getPrevKey(rtl, undefined) -> ArrowRight")
- Given `orientation: 'vertical'`, when `getPrevKey` is called, then it returns `ArrowUp`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getPrevKey(undefined, vertical) -> ArrowUp")
- Given `dir: 'rtl'` and `orientation: 'vertical'`, when `getPrevKey` is called, then it still returns `ArrowUp`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getPrevKey(rtl, vertical) -> ArrowUp")
- Given no arguments, when `getDirectionalKeys` is called, then it returns `{ nextKey: ArrowRight, prevKey: ArrowLeft }`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getDirectionalKeys(undefined, undefined)")
- Given `dir: 'rtl'`, when `getDirectionalKeys` is called, then it returns `{ nextKey: ArrowLeft, prevKey: ArrowRight }`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getDirectionalKeys(rtl, undefined)")
- Given `orientation: 'vertical'`, when `getDirectionalKeys` is called, then it returns `{ nextKey: ArrowDown, prevKey: ArrowUp }`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/keyboard.spec.ts: "getDirectionalKeys(undefined, vertical)")
- Given no arguments, when `getDirectionalKeys` is called, then it returns `{ nextKey: ArrowRight, prevKey: ArrowLeft }`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/get-directional-keys.test.ts: "should return correct keys for default direction and orientation")
- Given `("rtl", "horizontal")`, when `getDirectionalKeys` is called, then it returns `{ nextKey: ArrowLeft, prevKey: ArrowRight }`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/get-directional-keys.test.ts: "should return correct keys for rtl direction and horizontal orientation")
- Given `("ltr", "vertical")`, when `getDirectionalKeys` is called, then it returns `{ nextKey: ArrowDown, prevKey: ArrowUp }`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/get-directional-keys.test.ts: "should return correct keys for ltr direction and vertical orientation")
- Given `("rtl", "vertical")`, when `getDirectionalKeys` is called, then it returns `{ nextKey: ArrowDown, prevKey: ArrowUp }`, matching Melt's rule that RTL leaves the vertical axis alone. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/get-directional-keys.test.ts: "should return correct keys for rtl direction and vertical orientation")
- Given an invalid direction or an invalid orientation string, when `getDirectionalKeys` is called, then it falls back to `{ nextKey: ArrowRight, prevKey: ArrowLeft }` instead of throwing. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/get-directional-keys.test.ts: "should handle invalid direction and orientation values")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a `ConfigProvider` with its default slot, when mounted, then the provider and all slotted content render. (reka: packages/core/src/ConfigProvider/ConfigProvider.test.ts: "it should render config provider, and all it's slot correctly")
- Given `window.innerWidth` 200 and `documentElement.clientWidth` 190 and a default `ConfigProvider`, when mounted, then `document.body` gets `padding-right: 10px`, `margin-right: 0px`, `overflow: hidden`, and `documentElement` gets `--scrollbar-width: 10px`. (reka: packages/core/src/ConfigProvider/ConfigProvider.test.ts: "should add scrollBody's css to body")
- Given `ConfigProvider scrollBody={false}`, when mounted, then body `padding-right` and `margin-right` are both `0px`. (reka: packages/core/src/ConfigProvider/ConfigProvider.test.ts: "should set 0 padding, 0 margin body")
- Given `ConfigProvider scrollBody={{ padding: 20 }}`, when mounted, then body `padding-right` is `20px` and `margin-right` is `0px`. (reka: packages/core/src/ConfigProvider/ConfigProvider.test.ts: "should set 0 padding body")
- Given `ConfigProvider scrollBody={{ margin: 20, padding: 0 }}`, when mounted, then body `padding-right` is `0px` and `margin-right` is `20px`. (reka: packages/core/src/ConfigProvider/ConfigProvider.test.ts: "should set 0 margin body")
- Given `ConfigProvider useId={() => 'provided-id'}` and a consumer calling `useId(undefined, 'reka-test')`, when rendered, then the element id is `reka-test-provided-id`, so the injected generator takes precedence over Vue's own `useId`. (reka: packages/core/src/ConfigProvider/ConfigProvider.test.ts: "uses the provided id generator before Vue useId")

## vue-adapter

### Roles and attributes
- Given the package entry point, when every name listed in the repo's `constant.ts` `components` and `utilities` maps is checked, then each one is present in the `index` exports, running as one `it.each` case per exported name. (reka: packages/core/src/index.test.ts: "it should export %s")
- Given a bare `Arrow` component, when audited with axe, then there are no violations. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/component/Arrow.test.ts: "should pass axe accessibility tests")

### Focus management
- Given a component that calls `useForwardExpose` and binds `forwardRef` to an inner `span`, when the parent reads `ref.$el`, then it is the `HTMLSpanElement`, not the component's own root `div`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should forward plain DOM element ref")
- Given `forwardRef` invoked manually as `forwardRef({ $el: node })`, when the parent reads `ref.$el`, then it is the `HTMLSpanElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should forward plain DOM element ref - 2")
- Given a multi-root component whose second root contains the forwarded `span`, when the parent reads `ref.$el`, then it is still the `HTMLSpanElement`, so a fragment root does not break ref forwarding. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should forward plain DOM element ref - fragment")
- Given the forwarded `span` nested inside two explicit `Fragment` components, when the parent reads `ref.$el`, then it is the `HTMLSpanElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should forward plain DOM element ref - fragment - 2")
- Given the forwarded `span` nested inside a bare `<template>` block, when the parent reads `ref.$el`, then it is the `HTMLSpanElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should forward plain DOM element ref - fragment - 3")
- Given `forwardRef` bound to a child component rather than an element, when the parent reads `ref.$el`, then it resolves to that child's rendered `HTMLSpanElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should forward component instance for component")
- Given a `Primitive asChild` whose single child conditionally switches from `button` to `span`, when the condition flips, then `currentElement` updates from `button` to `span` within a post-flush effect. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should update currentElement when as-child conditional child swaps")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given an inner component that calls `expose({ innerValue, innerMethod })` and is bound to `forwardRef`, when the parent reads its own ref, then `innerValue` is `'inner-value'` and `innerMethod()` returns `'inner-method-result'`, so child exposes are merged upward. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should forward child component exposed properties to parent ref")
- Given a middle component with its own prop `parentProp` and an inner component exposing `childExposedValue`, when the parent reads the ref, then `parentProp` is `'custom-value'`, `childExposedValue` is `'child-exposed'`, and `$el` is an `HTMLSpanElement`, so props and child exposes coexist. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should merge child component exposed properties with parent component props")
- Given an inner component exposing `count`, `message`, `increment`, and `getMessage`, when the parent calls `increment()` through the forwarded ref, then `count` goes from `0` to `1`, `getMessage()` returns `'hello'`, and `$el` is an `HTMLButtonElement`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts: "should forward multiple exposed properties from child component")
- Given a component declaring prop `id: String` with no value passed, when `useForwardProps` emits its result, then the forwarded object is `{}`, so undeclared and unpassed props are omitted rather than forwarded as `undefined`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardProps.test.ts: "should forward nothing as no props provided")
- Given a prop with `default: 'test'` and no value passed, when forwarded, then the result is `{ id: 'test' }`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardProps.test.ts: "should forward default props")
- Given props `{ id: 'new-test', number: 0, enabled: false }` passed over a defaulted `id`, when forwarded, then the result equals those exact values, so falsy `0` and `false` survive. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardProps.test.ts: "should forward provided props instead of default")
- Given a defaulted `id` prop, when the parent calls `setProps({ id: 'new-test' })`, then a second forwarded payload `{ id: 'new-test' }` is emitted. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardProps.test.ts: "should be reactive")
- Given an extra prop the component does not declare plus a fallthrough `class` attribute, when forwarded, then only `{ id: 'test' }` is emitted, so attribute fallthrough stays out of the forwarded prop bag. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardProps.test.ts: "should not forwarded not provided props")
- Given `reactivePick(props, 'id')` handed to `useForwardProps` while the component also declares `extra`, when `id` changes, then only `id` is emitted and `extra` never appears. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardProps.test.ts: "should not forwarded props that is not passed as parameters")
- Given a `computed` wrapper around the props object instead of the raw reactive props, when `id` changes, then the forwarded payload updates the same way. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardProps.test.ts: "with computedRef > should be reactive")
- Given a parent with `<style scoped>` rendering a multi-root `Checkbox`, when mounted, then the inner `button` carries the same `data-v-*` scope id found on the parent's own marker element, because a multi-root component loses Vue's automatic scope-id fallthrough. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardScopeId.test.ts: "forwards the parent scope id onto a multi-root component root")
- Given `RadioGroupItem`, which sets `inheritAttrs: false` and wraps a multi-root `Radio`, inside a scoped parent, when mounted, then the inner `button` still carries the parent scope id (regression for issue 2751). (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardScopeId.test.ts: "forwards the parent scope id through RadioGroupItem onto its control")
- Given `ToggleGroupItem` wrapping a multi-root `Toggle` inside a scoped parent, when mounted, then the inner `button` carries the parent scope id. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardScopeId.test.ts: "forwards the parent scope id through ToggleGroupItem onto its control")
- Given a parent with no `<style scoped>`, when mounted, then the `button` carries no `data-v-*` attribute at all, so forwarding nothing is the correct no-op. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useForwardScopeId.test.ts: "forwards nothing when the parent has no scoped styles")
- Given a mocked `ConfigProvider` context supplying `nonce: 'global-nonce'`, when `useNonce()` is called with no argument, then it returns `'global-nonce'`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useNonce.test.ts: "should return global nonce value from ConfigProvider")
- Given the same global nonce, when `useNonce(ref('local-nonce'))` is called, then the local value wins. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useNonce.test.ts: "should return local nonce value when overridden")
- Given a focused `button` appended to `document.body`, when `getActiveElement()` is called, then it returns that button. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/getActiveElement.test.ts: "should return the active element when it is a regular element")
- Given a shadow root containing a nested shadow root whose inner `button` is focused, when `getActiveElement()` is called, then it returns the innermost focused button, so it walks through shadow boundaries. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/getActiveElement.test.ts: "should return the deepest active element in shadow DOM")
- Given a fresh component using `useIsUsingKeyboard`, when nothing has happened, then the value is `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useIsUsingKeyboard.test.ts: "should be false by default")
- Given the same component, when `ArrowDown` keydown fires on `document`, then the value becomes `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useIsUsingKeyboard.test.ts: "should be true after keydown")
- Given the value is `true` after a keydown, when `pointermove` fires on `document`, then it resets to `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useIsUsingKeyboard.test.ts: "should reset to false after pointermove")
- Given the value is `true` after a keydown, when `pointerdown` fires on `document`, then it resets to `false`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useIsUsingKeyboard.test.ts: "should reset to false after pointerdown")
- Given a component calling `useSize` on a bound element with a mocked `ResizeObserver`, when mounted, then `observe` is called exactly once and `disconnect` zero times, and on unmount `disconnect` is called once. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSize.test.ts: "disconnects the observer on unmount")
- Given the same setup in jsdom where `offsetWidth` and `offsetHeight` are `0`, when mounted, then `width` and `height` are numbers equal to `0`, so the initial read comes from offset dimensions rather than staying undefined. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSize.test.ts: "sets initial size from offsetWidth/offsetHeight on mount")
- Given `useSize` on a ref that never gets an element, when mounted and then unmounted, then `observe` is never called and unmount does not throw. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSize.test.ts: "does not create an observer when element is null")

## svelte-adapter

### Roles and attributes
- Given `createBitsAttrs({ component: 'dialog', parts: ['root', 'trigger', 'content'] })`, when the attrs object is read, then the part names map to `data-dialog-root`, `data-dialog-trigger`, and `data-dialog-content`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/attrs.test.ts: "creates attrs object with component prefix when no variant")
- Given the same config plus `getVariant: () => 'mobile'`, when the attrs object is read, then the prefix becomes the variant: `data-mobile-root` and `data-mobile-trigger`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/attrs.test.ts: "creates attrs object with variant prefix when variant is provided")
- Given `getVariant: () => null`, when the attrs object is read, then it falls back to the component prefix `data-dialog-root`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/attrs.test.ts: "creates attrs object with component prefix when variant returns null")
- Given a created attrs object, when `selector('root')` is called, then it returns `[data-dialog-root]` wrapped in brackets for querying. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/attrs.test.ts: "provides selector function that wraps attr in brackets")
- Given a created attrs object, when `getAttr('root')` is called, then it returns the bare attribute name `data-dialog-root`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/attrs.test.ts: "provides getAttr function that returns the attribute name")
- Given a config with a single part, when read, then both the property and the `selector`/`getAttr` helpers resolve to `data-button-root`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/attrs.test.ts: "works with single part")
- Given a config with an empty `parts` array, when read, then `selector` and `getAttr` are still functions. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/attrs.test.ts: "handles empty parts array")

### Focus management
- Given a rendered form, when `focus(element)` is called with the `HTMLElement`, then that element has focus. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/dom.spec.ts: "focuses the given HTMLElement")
- Given the same form, when `focus('#name')` is called with a selector string, then the matching element has focus, so the helper accepts either form. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/dom.spec.ts: "finds the element by querySelector and focuses it")
- Given a form containing two inputs and an `<hr />`, when `getTabbableNodes(form)` is called, then it returns exactly the two inputs. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/dom.spec.ts: "returns only tabbable nodes")

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a list whose first option is enabled, when `getFirstOption(list)` is called, then it returns that first option. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/list.spec.ts: "returns the first option")
- Given a list whose first option is disabled, when `getFirstOption(list)` is called, then it returns the second option. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/list.spec.ts: "returns the second option if the first is disabled")
- Given an empty container with `role="menu"`, when `getFirstOption` is called, then it returns `null`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/list.spec.ts: "returns null if there are no options")
- Given a list with several options, when `getOptions(list)` is called, then it returns exactly the elements with `role="option"` in order. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/list.spec.ts: "returns all options")
- Given an empty container, when `getOptions` is called, then it returns an empty array. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/list.spec.ts: "returns an empty array if there are no options")
- Given a list whose first option is disabled, when `getOptions` is called, then the disabled option is excluded from the result. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/list.spec.ts: "doesnt return disabled options")
- Given a `\0` null character anywhere in an identifier, when `cssEscape` runs, then each null becomes `�`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should handle null characters")
- Given an existing `�` replacement character, when `cssEscape` runs, then it is left as is. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should handle replacement characters")
- Given control characters `\x01\x02\x1E\x1F`, when `cssEscape` runs, then they become the hex escapes `\1 \2 \1e \1f ` with trailing spaces. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should escape control characters")
- Given an identifier starting with any digit `0` through `9`, when `cssEscape` runs, then the leading digit becomes a hex escape such as `\30 `. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should escape digits at start")
- Given digits in the middle of an identifier, when `cssEscape` runs, then they are left untouched. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should not escape digits in middle")
- Given an identifier starting with a hyphen followed by a digit, when `cssEscape` runs, then the hyphen stays and the digit is escaped, as in `-\30 a`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should handle hyphen with digits")
- Given the identifiers `-`, `-a`, `--`, and `--a`, when `cssEscape` runs, then a lone hyphen becomes `\-` and the other three are unchanged. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should handle hyphens")
- Given high-range and Latin characters including `\x7F` and the full ASCII alphabet, when `cssEscape` runs, then only `\x7F` is escaped to `\7f ` and letters and digits pass through. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should handle various characters")
- Given the characters space, `!`, `x`, `y`, when `cssEscape` runs, then space and `!` are backslash-escaped and the letters are not. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should escape special characters")
- Given a surrogate pair for U+1D306 and each lone surrogate, when `cssEscape` runs, then all three are passed through unchanged. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/css-escape.test.ts: "should handle unicode surrogates")

## svelte-adapter-config

### Notes and edge cases
- Given no `BitsConfig` in scope, when a consumer reads `portal` and `locale`, then both read `undefined`. (bits: tests/src/tests/utilities/bits-config/bits-config.browser.test.ts: "should show undefined values when no config is set")
- Given a root `BitsConfig` with `portal: '#root-portal'` and `locale: 'en'`, when a consumer under it reads them, then it sees those exact values. (bits: tests/src/tests/utilities/bits-config/bits-config.browser.test.ts: "should show configured values at root level")
- Given a nested `BitsConfig` that sets neither key, when a consumer under it reads them, then it inherits `#parent-portal` and `en` from the parent. (bits: tests/src/tests/utilities/bits-config/bits-config.browser.test.ts: "should inherit values from parent when child doesn't specify them")
- Given a nested `BitsConfig` that sets only `portal`, when a consumer reads both, then `portal` is the child's `#child-portal` and `locale` is still the parent's `en`, so overrides are per key rather than per config node. (bits: tests/src/tests/utilities/bits-config/bits-config.browser.test.ts: "should allow child to override parent values")
- Given three nested `BitsConfig` levels where level 1 sets `portal` and level 2 sets `locale`, when the deepest consumer reads both, then it sees `#level1` and `es`. (bits: tests/src/tests/utilities/bits-config/bits-config.browser.test.ts: "should handle deep nesting inheritance correctly")
- Given a chain where level 2 overrides `locale` and level 3 overrides `portal`, when the deepest consumer reads both, then it sees `#override` and `fr`. (bits: tests/src/tests/utilities/bits-config/bits-config.browser.test.ts: "should handle partial override chains correctly")

## builder-api

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a Melt builder such as `createAccordion`, when it is called, then it returns `{ ids, elements, states, helpers, options }`, where `elements` holds one readable store per part (`root`, `item`, `trigger`, `content`, `heading`), `states` holds the writable value store, `helpers` holds derived predicates such as `isSelected`, and `options` holds the reactive option stores. Every spec in `src/tests` exercises this shape indirectly through a `.svelte` harness rather than asserting on the returned object. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: harness `AccordionTest.svelte`)
- Given a builder element store, when it is subscribed, then its value is a prop bag that always includes `data-melt-<part>: ''` plus an `action`, and parameterised parts such as `$trigger(id)` are functions returning that bag. Tests locate elements by `data-testid` on the consumer's own element, not by the melt marker attribute. (melt: src/tests/accordion/Accordion.spec.ts: harness `AccordionTest.svelte`)
- Given the source text `use:melt={$trigger(id)}`, when `extractMeltAttribute` runs, then it returns `{ builder: '$trigger', args: 'id' }`. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "extractMeltAttribute - use:melt={$trigger(id)}")
- Given `use:melt={$trigger}`, when `extractMeltAttribute` runs, then it returns `{ builder: '$trigger' }` with no `args`. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "extractMeltAttribute - use:melt={$trigger}")
- Given `use:melt={$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )}`, when `extractMeltAttribute` runs, then it returns `{ builder: '$trigger', args: "{helpme: 'god'} " }`, preserving the inner whitespace. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "extractMeltAttribute - use:melt={$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )}")
- Given `use:melt={$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )} awesome={coolio}`, when `extractMeltAttribute` runs, then it extracts only the melt attribute and ignores the trailing unrelated attribute. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "extractMeltAttribute - use:melt={$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )} awesome={coolio}")
- Given `use:melt={$thumbs[0]}`, when `extractMeltAttribute` runs, then it returns `{ builder: '$thumbs', index: '0' }`, so indexed element arrays are recognised. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "extractMeltAttribute - use:melt={$thumbs[0]}")
- Given `use:melt={thumb}` with no `$` prefix, when `extractMeltAttribute` runs, then it returns `{ builder: 'thumb' }`, marking a non-store builder. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "extractMeltAttribute - use:melt={thumb}")
- Given `use:melt={$trigger(id)} awesome={coolio}`, when `processMeltAttributes` runs, then it rewrites to `{...$trigger(id)} use:trigger awesome={coolio}`, so the prop bag is spread and the action applied separately. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "processMeltAttributes - use:melt={$trigger(id)} awesome={coolio}")
- Given `use:melt={$trigger}`, when `processMeltAttributes` runs, then it rewrites to `{...$trigger} use:trigger`. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "processMeltAttributes - use:melt={$trigger}")
- Given `use:melt={$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )}`, when `processMeltAttributes` runs, then it rewrites to `{...$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )} use:trigger`. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "processMeltAttributes - use:melt={$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )}")
- Given `use:melt={$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )} awesome={coolio}`, when `processMeltAttributes` runs, then the unrelated attribute is preserved after the rewrite. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "processMeltAttributes - use:melt={$trigger({helpme: 'god'} )} awesome={coolio}")
- Given `use:melt={$thumbs[0]}`, when `processMeltAttributes` runs, then it rewrites to `{...$thumbs[0]} use:thumbs`, so the action name drops the index. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "processMeltAttributes - use:melt={$thumbs[0]}")
- Given `use:melt={thumb}`, when `processMeltAttributes` runs, then it rewrites to `{...thumb} use:thumb.action`, reaching into `.action` because the value is a plain object rather than a store. (melt: src/docs/pp.spec.ts: "processMeltAttributes - use:melt={thumb}")
- Given a `readable(1)` store, when wrapped with `withGet`, then `get()` returns `1` without a subscription. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/withGet.spec.ts: "properly gets the value of a readable store")
- Given a `writable(1)` wrapped with `withGet`, when `set(2)` is called, then `get()` returns `2`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/withGet.spec.ts: "properly gets the value of a writable store")
- Given a `withGet` wrapper over an original writable, when the original store is set directly, then `get()` reflects the new value. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/withGet.spec.ts: "When updating the original store, withGet has the latest value")
- Given a derived store `$w + 1` wrapped with `withGet`, when the source changes from `1` to `2`, then `get()` goes from `2` to `3`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/withGet.spec.ts: "properly gets the value of a derived store")
- Given `withGet.writable(1)`, when `set(2)` is called, then `get()` returns `2`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/withGet.spec.ts: "withGet.writable")
- Given `withGet.derived` over a `withGet.writable(1)` adding one, when the source is set to `2`, then the derived `get()` returns `3`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/withGet.spec.ts: "withGet.derived")
- Given `effect([], fn)` with no dependencies, when created, then `fn` runs once immediately. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/effect.spec.ts: "Gets called initially")
- Given `effect(store, fn)`, when the store changes, then `fn` has run twice in total, once on creation and once on change. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/effect.spec.ts: "Gets called when a store changes")
- Given an effect whose callback returns a cleanup function, when the store changes, then the previous cleanup runs exactly once before the new execution. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/effect.spec.ts: "Returned callback gets called before new execution")
- Given an effect whose callback returns a cleanup function, when the effect is unsubscribed, then the cleanup runs once. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/effect.spec.ts: "Returned callback gets called when unsubscribed")
- Given `effect(store, fn, { skipFirstRun: true })`, when created, then `fn` has not run, and it runs once on the first store change. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/effect.spec.ts: "Respect `skipFirstRun` prop")
- Given three functions that each run immediately and return a cleanup, when passed to `executeCallbacks` and the returned function is invoked, then the three immediate calls happened at registration time and the three cleanups fire only on invocation. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/callbacks.spec.ts: "groups callbacks and executes them together")
- Given an object with `sweet` and `savory` keys, when `omit(obj, 'sweet')` is called, then the result is strictly equal to the object without `sweet`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/object.spec.ts: "omits keys from a given object")

## controlled-state

### State and controlled/uncontrolled
- Given `overridable(writable(1))` with no `onChange`, when `set(2)` is called, then `get()` returns `2`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/overridable.spec.ts: "works as expected without setting onChange fn")
- Given `overridable(store)`, when the underlying store is set directly, then the overridable reflects the new value. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/overridable.spec.ts: "updates when original store updates")
- Given `overridable(store, ({ next }) => next + 1)`, when `set(2)` is called, then the stored value is `3` and the callback was invoked, so `onChange`'s return value decides the committed state. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/overridable.spec.ts: "onChange is called when original store updates")
- Given `overridable` with an `onChange` that records its arguments, when `set(2)` is called on a store holding `1`, then `onChange` received `curr: 1` and `next: 2`. (melt: src/lib/internal/helpers/tests/overridable.spec.ts: "curr and next are passed to onChange")
- Given `type: 'single'` and `modelValue: 'test'`, when the composable initialises, then `modelValue` is `'test'`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSingleOrMultipleValue.test.ts: "should initialize with correct type and modelValue")
- Given `type: 'single'` with value `'test'`, when `changeModelValue('newTest')` runs and then `changeModelValue('newTest')` runs again, then the value becomes `'newTest'` and then `undefined`, so reselecting the current single value clears it. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSingleOrMultipleValue.test.ts: "should change modelValue for single type")
- Given `type: 'multiple'` with value `['test']`, when `changeModelValue('newTest')` then `changeModelValue('test')` run, then the value becomes `['test', 'newTest']` then `['newTest']`, so selection toggles per item. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSingleOrMultipleValue.test.ts: "should change modelValue for multiple type")
- Given no explicit `type` and a string `modelValue`, when values change, then behavior follows single mode, including allowing `''` as a value. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSingleOrMultipleValue.test.ts: "should infer type from modelValue given `single`")
- Given no explicit `type` and an array `modelValue`, when values change, then behavior follows multiple mode. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSingleOrMultipleValue.test.ts: "should infer type from modelValue given `multiple`")
- Given `type: 'single'` with an array `modelValue`, when values change, then the explicit `type` wins over the inferred one and the value becomes a plain string. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSingleOrMultipleValue.test.ts: "should overwrite type given `single`")
- Given `type: 'multiple'` with a string `modelValue`, when values change, then the explicit `type` wins and the value becomes an array. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSingleOrMultipleValue.test.ts: "should overwrite type given `multiple`")
- Given `multiple` with `selectionBehavior: 'toggle'` and value `[1, 2]`, when `onSelectItem(3, v => v === 3)` runs, then the value becomes `[1, 2, 3]`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "onSelectItem - multiple + toggle > adds the value when condition matches nothing")
- Given the same setup with value `[1, 2, 3]`, when `onSelectItem(2, v => v === 2)` runs, then the value becomes `[1, 3]` and the other entries keep their order. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "removes the matched index and preserves other entries")
- Given `multiple` with `selectionBehavior: 'replace'` and value `[1, 2, 3]`, when `onSelectItem(9, () => false)` runs, then the value becomes `[9]` and `firstValue` becomes `9`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "onSelectItem - multiple + replace > replaces modelValue with [val] and sets firstValue to val")
- Given single mode with `toggle` and value `{ id: 1 }`, when a non-matching `{ id: 2 }` is selected, then the value becomes `{ id: 2 }`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "onSelectItem - single + toggle > sets { ...val } when selecting a non-matching value")
- Given single mode with `toggle` and value `{ id: 1 }`, when the condition matches the existing value, then the value becomes `undefined`, so the condition is evaluated against the currently selected item. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "clears to undefined when the current value matches condition")
- Given single mode with `replace`, when any item is selected, then the value is always set to that item regardless of the condition. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "onSelectItem - single + replace > always sets { ...val }")
- Given single mode with `replace`, when an object with a nested field is selected, then the stored value is deep-equal but not reference-equal to the input, because the source spreads into a shallow copy. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "single + replace assigns a copy of val, not the same reference")
- Given single mode with `toggle` and a non-matching condition, when an object is selected, then the stored value is a shallow copy rather than the same reference. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "single + toggle (non-matching) assigns a copy of val, not the same reference")
- Given `multiple` + `replace` where `firstValue` was never set, when `handleMultipleReplace('next', ...)` runs, then the value is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "handleMultipleReplace - early returns (no change) > returns early when firstValue is unset")
- Given `multiple: false`, when `handleMultipleReplace` runs, then it short-circuits before `firstValue` matters and the value is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "returns early when multiple is false")
- Given `multiple` + `replace` with `firstValue` set but the value replaced by a non-array object, when `handleMultipleReplace` runs, then it bails and the object is unchanged. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "returns early when modelValue is not an array")
- Given options `[10, 20, 30, 40, 50]` and `firstValue` `10`, when `handleMultipleReplace('next', <element for 40>)` runs, then the value becomes the inclusive range `[10, 20, 30, 40]`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "handleMultipleReplace - range selection > 'next' sets modelValue to the inclusive range firstValue..lastValue")
- Given the same options and `firstValue` `10`, when `handleMultipleReplace('prev', <element for 30>)` runs, then the value becomes `[10, 20, 30]`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "'prev' sets modelValue to the inclusive range firstValue..lastValue")
- Given `firstValue` `10` and a current element whose value is `50`, when `handleMultipleReplace('first', ...)` runs, then the range end is `options[0]` and the value becomes `[10]`, so the current element's own value is ignored for the range. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "'first' selects from firstValue back to options[0]")
- Given `firstValue` `10`, when `handleMultipleReplace('last', ...)` runs, then the value becomes the whole range `[10, 20, 30, 40, 50]`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useSelectionBehavior.test.ts: "'last' selects from firstValue to options.at(-1)")

## composition-ime

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a fresh `useComposing`, when `handleCompositionStart` is called before any `compositionupdate`, then `shouldDeferInput` flips from `false` to `true`, so input is held by default during composition. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should defer input while composing before any compositionupdate")
- Given an Android user agent, when composition starts and a Latin `compositionupdate` with data `'Br'` arrives, then `shouldDeferInput` becomes `false`, so soft-keyboard autocorrect is processed live. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should process plain-text composition live on Android (soft-keyboard autocorrect)")
- Given a non-Android user agent, when composition starts and a Latin `compositionupdate` with data `'xiang'` arrives, then `shouldDeferInput` stays `true`, because desktop Pinyin preedit must not be processed live. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should keep deferring plain-text composition off Android (e.g. desktop Pinyin preedit)")
- Given an Android user agent, when a `compositionupdate` carries Han data `'香'`, then `shouldDeferInput` stays `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should defer IME-script composition even on Android (Han)")
- Given an Android user agent, when a `compositionupdate` carries Hiragana data `'かん'`, then `shouldDeferInput` stays `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should defer IME-script composition even on Android (Hiragana)")
- Given an Android user agent, when a `compositionupdate` carries Katakana data `'カナ'`, then `shouldDeferInput` stays `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should defer IME-script composition even on Android (Katakana)")
- Given an Android user agent, when a `compositionupdate` carries a Hangul syllable `'한'`, then `shouldDeferInput` stays `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should defer IME-script composition even on Android (Hangul syllable)")
- Given an Android user agent, when a `compositionupdate` carries Hangul jamo `'ㅂ'`, then `shouldDeferInput` stays `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should defer IME-script composition even on Android (Hangul jamo)")
- Given an Android user agent, when a `compositionupdate` carries Bopomofo `'ㄅㄆ'`, then `shouldDeferInput` stays `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should defer IME-script composition even on Android (Bopomofo)")
- Given an Android romaji-mode session that starts with `'k'` and `'ka'` (both live), when the data becomes `'か'` and then `'かん'`, then `shouldDeferInput` becomes `true` and stays `true` even after the data backspaces to `'kan'`, so the IME verdict is sticky within a session. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should stay deferred once IME script appears mid-session (Android romaji → kana)")
- Given an Android session that was marked deferred by kana data, when `compositionend` fires and a fresh session begins with Latin `'Br'`, then `shouldDeferInput` is `false` again, so the verdict does not leak across sessions. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should not carry the IME verdict into the next composition session")
- Given an Android session, when a `compositionupdate` arrives with empty data after `'Br'` and again after `'香'`, then the previous classification is preserved in each case (`false` then `true`). (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should keep the previous classification on empty compositionupdate data")
- Given an Android session with an `onEnd` callback, when `compositionend` fires, then `isComposing` and `shouldDeferInput` both become `false`, `onEnd` is called with the `compositionend` event, and a new `compositionstart` sets `shouldDeferInput` back to `true`. (reka: packages/core/src/shared/useComposing.test.ts: "should reset composing state and call onEnd after compositionend")

## internal-helpers

### Notes and edge cases
- Given a value inside the range, when `clamp` runs, then it is returned unchanged, and the boundary values are returned as is. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/clamp.test.ts: "should return the number if it is within the range")
- Given a value below the minimum, when `clamp` runs, then the minimum is returned. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/clamp.test.ts: "should return the minimum value if the number is below the range")
- Given a value above the maximum, when `clamp` runs, then the maximum is returned. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/clamp.test.ts: "should return the maximum value if the number is above the range")
- Given equal minimum and maximum, when `clamp` runs, then that single value is always returned. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/clamp.test.ts: "should handle equal minimum and maximum values")
- Given a negative range, when `clamp` runs, then values inside are returned and values outside clamp to the negative bounds. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/clamp.test.ts: "should handle negative minimum and maximum values")
- Given decimal bounds such as `1.2` and `7.8`, when `clamp` runs, then decimals are preserved without rounding. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/clamp.test.ts: "should handle decimal values")
- Given the strings `'123'`, `'0'`, `'-42'`, and `'3.14'`, when `isNumberString` runs, then all return `true`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/is.test.ts: "should return true for valid number strings")
- Given `'abc'`, `'1a2b3c'`, `'number'`, and `'--123'`, when `isNumberString` runs, then all return `false`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/is.test.ts: "should return false for strings that are not valid numbers")
- Given an empty string, when `isNumberString` runs, then it returns `false`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/is.test.ts: "should return false for empty string")
- Given numbers with surrounding whitespace, when `isNumberString` runs, then it returns `true`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/is.test.ts: "should return true for strings with leading or trailing whitespace")
- Given whitespace mixed with letters, when `isNumberString` runs, then it returns `false`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/is.test.ts: "should return false for strings with non-numeric characters and whitespace")
- Given exponential forms `'1e3'`, `'2.5e-4'`, and `'-3.2E+5'`, when `isNumberString` runs, then all return `true`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/is.test.ts: "should return true for strings with exponential notation")
- Given `linearScale([0,1],[0,100])`, when applied to 0.5, 0.33, and 0, then it returns 50, 33, and 0, and `linearScale([0,1],[10,90])(0.5)` returns 50. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/math.test.ts: "correctly scales the value")
- Given a value outside the domain, when the scale is applied, then it clamps to the range ends, so 2 maps to 100 and `-5` maps to 0. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/math.test.ts: "is minimum when below minimum")
- Given a domain of `[-1, 1]`, when 0 is scaled to `[0, 100]`, then the result is 50. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/math.test.ts: "correctly handles negative scales")
- Given a reversed range `[100, 0]`, when 0.5, 0, and 2 are scaled, then the results are 50, 100, and 0, with the last clamped. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/math.test.ts: "handles reversed ranges")
- Given non-zero domains `[10,20]` and `[100,200]`, when midpoints are scaled, then the results are 50 and 0.5. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/math.test.ts: "works with non-zero based domains")
- Given `clamp` disabled as the third argument, when values outside the domain are scaled, then the results extrapolate to 200 and `-100`. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/math.test.ts: "handles unclamped values when clamp is false")
- Given tiny domains such as `[0, 1e-6]`, when the midpoint is scaled, then the result is close to 0.5 to six decimal places. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/math.test.ts: "maintains precision with small numbers")
- Given `debounce(fn, 100)`, when called once, then `fn` has not run immediately and has run once after 200ms of real time. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/debounce.test.ts: "should execute the function after the specified wait time")
- Given three calls inside the wait window, when 150ms total elapses, then `fn` has run exactly once. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/debounce.test.ts: "should debounce multiple calls within the wait time")
- Given a debounced call with arguments `(1, "hello", true)`, when it fires, then `fn` receives those exact arguments. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/debounce.test.ts: "should handle arguments correctly")
- Given a call at 0ms and another at 50ms, when 150ms more elapses, then `fn` has run once, and a further call plus wait brings it to twice, so each call restarts the timer. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/debounce.test.ts: "should reset the timer on subsequent calls")
- Given a pending debounced call, when `destroy()` is called, then `fn` never runs. (bits: packages/bits-ui/src/lib/internal/debounce.test.ts: "should cancel the debounced function when destroy is called")

## Test infrastructure notes

### Reka UI

- Runner is Vitest 4 with `globals: true`, configured in `packages/core/vite.config.ts`. Include glob is `./**/*.test.{ts,js}`, so tests sit next to the component source rather than in a separate tests package.
- Environment is jsdom 26 with `environmentOptions.jsdom.resources: 'usable'`, so `<img>` and stylesheet loads actually fire. That is what makes the Avatar loading-status tests possible without stubbing.
- `vitest.global.ts` pins `process.env.TZ = 'US/Eastern'` for the whole run. Every date and time component test is written against that zone, which is worth copying: a floating timezone makes calendar tests flap.
- `vitest.setup.ts` does four things: extends `expect` with `vitest-axe/matchers` and `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`, loads `vitest-canvas-mock` (inlined via `server.deps.inline`), stubs `HTMLElement.prototype.scrollIntoView` with `vi.fn()`, and monkey-patches `window.getComputedStyle` to drop the pseudo-element argument. The last one exists because jsdom throws "Not implemented" when axe-core asks for `::before` styles, and axe does that on every audit.
- axe is configured once globally through `configureAxe` with the `region` rule disabled, because component fragments are mounted without a landmark wrapper. 62 of the 100 test files import `axe` from `vitest-axe` and assert `expect(await axe(wrapper.element)).toHaveNoViolations()`. The convention is a single test named "should pass axe accessibility tests" per `describe` block, repeated once per meaningful state (closed and open, single and multiple, disabled), so a component with five states gets five axe assertions rather than one.
- Two mounting styles coexist. 66 files use `@vue/test-utils` `mount`, which gives `wrapper.html()`, `wrapper.find`, `wrapper.setProps`, and `wrapper.emitted()` for asserting `update:modelValue` payloads. 36 files use `@testing-library/vue` `render` with `screen` queries and `findByRole`. Several files use both. 21 files drive interaction through `@testing-library/user-event`; the rest use `trigger('keydown', ...)` directly on the wrapper, which skips real focus and event ordering.
- `packages/core/src/test/utils.ts` is the entire shared helper surface: a `handleSubmit` `vi.fn()` that calls `preventDefault` and returns `Object.fromEntries(new FormData(e.target))`, and a promise-based `sleep`. Form tests assert against the object `handleSubmit` returns, which is how hidden-input naming and serialisation get checked.
- Fake timers appear in only five files: `shared/useGraceArea.test.ts`, `shared/useTypeahead.test.ts`, `Select/Select.test.ts`, `Menu/Menu.test.ts`, `NavigationMenu/NavigationMenu.test.ts`. Everything else waits on `nextTick`, `sleep`, or `waitFor`. Delay-heavy components such as Tooltip and HoverCard therefore test real elapsed time.
- Snapshot tests are rare and deliberate: `AspectRatio`, `Avatar`, `ScrollArea`, `Tree`, and `Popper` write `.snap` files under `__snapshots__`, They pin generated inline styles and CSS custom properties, which is exactly the part of a positioning primitive that is tedious to assert attribute by attribute. `pnpm test-update` runs `vitest -u`. `Drawer/Drawer.snap.test.ts` is a false friend: the "snap" is snap points, not snapshots, and it has no `__snapshots__` directory. It asserts CSS custom properties such as `--drawer-snap-point-offset` and `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` directly against a mocked 800px popup.
- SSR is covered in two files only. `Accordion.test.ts` and `Tabs.test.ts` build a second app with `createSSRApp`, run `renderToString` from `@vue/server-renderer`, inject the HTML into a container, then hydrate and assert no mismatch. Nothing else in the repo tests SSR.
- Coverage uses the istanbul provider. `size-limit` guards bundle size but is not part of the test run.
- There is no Playwright config and no `packages/core/e2e` directory at this commit. The histoire stories under `.histoire` and `playground/vue3` are development harnesses with no assertions.

### Melt UI

- Runner is Vitest 1 through the SvelteKit Vite plugin, configured in `vite.config.ts`. Include glob is `src/**/*.spec.{js,ts}` plus in-source tests via `includeSource: ['src/**/*.{js,ts,svelte}']`.
- Environment is jsdom 24. Notably `retry: 5` is set globally, and `allowOnly` is gated on `!process.env.CI`. Five retries on every test is a loud signal that the timing-sensitive tests are flaky in jsdom.
- An alias rewrites `svelte` to `svelte/internal` for tests, and `clsx` is inlined.
- `scripts/setupTest.ts` extends `expect` with `@testing-library/jest-dom/matchers` and with `toHaveNoViolations` from `jest-axe`, sets `configure({ asyncUtilTimeout: 1500 })` on `@testing-library/dom`, mocks all three SvelteKit runtime modules (`$app/environment` with `browser: false`, `$app/navigation`, `$app/stores`), installs `resize-observer-polyfill` as the global `ResizeObserver`, and stubs `Element.prototype.scrollIntoView` with a no-op.
- axe comes from `jest-axe`, not `vitest-axe`, and is called as `expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations()` on the container returned by `render`. Unlike Reka there is no global rule configuration, so the `region` rule is active. Roughly a dozen specs carry an axe assertion, usually the first `it` in the file named "No accessibility violations", and usually only in the default closed state.
- Interaction is `@testing-library/svelte` `render` plus `@testing-library/user-event` (32 of the specs). `act`, `waitFor`, and `fireEvent` appear where user-event cannot express the interaction.
- `src/tests/utils.ts` is the shared helper set and is worth copying wholesale as a conformance-suite pattern:
  - `testKbd` wraps the library's internal `kbd` map into user-event's curly-brace syntax, so tests name keys through the same constant the implementation uses. A renamed key cannot silently desync the tests.
  - `exists(get, testId)` turns a throwing `getByTestId` into a boolean.
  - `touch(node)` fires the full browser sequence `pointerdown`, `touchstart`, `pointerup`, `touchend`, `mousedown`, `mouseup`, `click`. Melt tests touch behavior by replaying that exact order rather than trusting a single synthetic event.
  - `assertActiveFocusTrap(user, element, tabsPresses = 10)` presses Tab ten times and asserts `document.activeElement` stays inside the element after each press. Every dialog-like component reuses it.
- Each spec renders a small `.svelte` harness next to it (`src/tests/<component>/<Component>.svelte`) that calls the builder and spreads the returned actions. The harness is where the builder API shape is exercised: tests assert on the DOM the spread prop bag produces, not on the builder's return value directly. A handful of specs additionally assert store values pulled out of the builder.
- Playwright is configured in `playwright.config.ts` against `./e2e`, running chromium, firefox, and webkit with `hasTouch: true`, `fullyParallel`, two retries on CI, trace on first retry, and a `webServer` that runs `pnpm dev` locally or `build && preview` on CI. Only two e2e specs exist. `e2e/dialog.spec.ts` runs and uses `page.tap` plus bounding-box maths on the real docs route to prove an overlay tap does not leak through to a button underneath, which is exactly the thing jsdom cannot check. `e2e/dropdown.spec.ts` is entirely disabled: both of its blocks are `test.describe.skip`. So the real-browser coverage in Melt is one touch-event test.
- Storybook with `@storybook/addon-a11y` and `@storybook/addon-interactions` is present, and one spec lives under `src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts`. `src/docs/pp.spec.ts` tests the `@melt-ui/pp` preprocessor rather than a component.
- Coverage uses the v8 provider.

### Bits UI

- Two separate Vitest setups. `packages/bits-ui/vite.config.ts` runs pure unit tests for internal helpers in jsdom with `globals: true` and in-source testing enabled (`pnpm test:utils`). `tests/vite.config.ts` defines a single project named `browser` covering `src/tests/**/*.browser.test.ts` (`pnpm test:browser`).
- The browser project is the interesting one: `environment: "browser"`, `browser.enabled: true`, `headless: true`, `provider: "playwright"`, `isolate: true`, and two instances, chromium and webkit. Every component test therefore runs twice in two real engines. `testTimeout: 5000`, `retry: 3`, `poolOptions.forks.maxForks: 7`.
- This is the sharpest divergence from the other two libraries. Reka and Melt assert component behavior in jsdom; Bits asserts it in real browsers and keeps jsdom only for pure functions. Consequences visible in the tests: real layout means `getBoundingClientRect` returns true numbers, so submenu grace-area and slider drag tests compute coordinates from measured rects instead of mocking them; real focus means focus assertions are trustworthy; and there is no `ResizeObserver` or `scrollIntoView` stubbing anywhere.
- Rendering is `render` from `vitest-browser-svelte`, queries and interaction come from `@vitest/browser/context` (`page`, `userEvent`, `Locator`), and assertions use `expect.element(locator).toHaveAttribute(...)` style retrying matchers. `vi.waitFor` covers the rest.
- A `vitestBrowserConditionPlugin` unshifts the `browser` export condition when `process.env.VITEST` is set, in both configs.
- `tests/src/tests/utils.ts` holds a local copy of the `kbd` map plus `getTestKbd()`, which wraps every key in braces and adds `SHIFT_TAB: "{Shift>}{Tab}"`. Unlike Melt the map is duplicated in the test package rather than imported from the library.
- `tests/src/tests/browser-utils.ts` is where the real-browser advantage is spent, and it is the most reusable artifact in all three repos:
  - `getSubmenuPlacementSide(triggerRect, contentRect)` derives which side a submenu actually landed on from measured centers, so the same test works whichever way collision detection flipped it.
  - `getPointerLeaveTowardSubmenuClientCoords`, `getPointerMidpointTowardSubmenuClientCoords`, and `getPointerAwayFromSubmenuIntentClientCoords` produce pointer coordinates that are just inside the trigger, halfway across the gap, and clearly off the intent path. Submenu grace-area behavior is tested by moving a real pointer through those three points.
  - `expectNotExists(loc)` waits for `loc.element()` to throw; `expectExists(loc)` is the retrying positive. `expectNotClickableLoc(loc)` asserts `loc.click()` rejects, which is how pointer-events blocking gets verified.
  - `waitForDismissibleLayer(loc)` reads the global `globalThis.bitsDismissableLayers` map and waits until a layer whose `opts.ref.current` is the node is registered. The library deliberately exposes that registry for tests, and the helper's own comment says opening-click regression tests dispatch *before* waiting on it, to prove the layer does not eat the click that opened it.
  - `focusAndExpectToHaveFocus(loc)` focuses then asserts focus.
  - `observeTransitionAttrs(node)` attaches a `MutationObserver` filtered to `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` and records a history of snapshots. Animation tests assert on the *sequence* of those attributes over time rather than a single sampled state, which is the only honest way to test enter and exit styling.
- `tests/src/tests/helpers/calendar.ts` and `helpers/select.ts` hold per-family query helpers. `tests/other/setup-browser-test.ts` contains only triple-slash type references, so there is no runtime setup file.
- No axe anywhere. Bits has no automated accessibility audit; it asserts roles and ARIA attributes by hand instead. Given the browser runner that is a real gap, since axe would work better there than in jsdom.
- No snapshot tests. Bits asserts attributes individually.
- Test harnesses are Svelte 5 components next to each test (`<component>-test.svelte`, plus variants like `-force-mount-test.svelte`, `-multi-test.svelte`, `-value-child-test.svelte`). The variant naming encodes the API surface under test: `child` snippet delegation, `forceMount`, multiple selection, and controlled bindings each get their own harness rather than a prop toggle.
- `pnpm test` at the root runs the packages and tests workspaces in parallel. The `tests/package.json` `test:jsdom` script passes `--project=jsdom`, but no project by that name is defined in `tests/vite.config.ts` at this commit, so that script is dead.

### Parity mechanisms across the three

- There is no shared conformance suite. Each repo re-implements the same behavior checks in its own idiom, and the divergences are mostly accidental rather than intentional.
- The closest thing to a parity mechanism is the shared `kbd` constant pattern (Melt imports the library's own map into tests, Bits copies it) and the shared naming of `data-state`, `data-disabled`, `data-highlighted`, `data-side`, `data-align`, and `data-orientation` attributes inherited from Radix. Those attribute names are the de facto contract all three honor, and they are the strongest candidates for a cross-framework conformance suite.
- CSS custom property names are namespaced per library (`--reka-*` versus `--bits-*`), so any shared suite has to parameterise the prefix.
- Reka and Bits both ship a `forceMount` escape hatch and both test it; Melt handles the same case with `forceVisible` on the builder. All three test that content stays mounted while a transition runs.
- Reka tests `asChild`/`as` prop delegation through `Primitive`; Bits tests the equivalent Svelte 5 `child` snippet; Melt has no equivalent because the builder returns a prop bag the consumer spreads onto whatever element it likes, so the question does not arise. That asymmetry is the single biggest difference in what the three suites can even express.

### Requested areas with no tests to mine

These came up in the brief but produced no bullets, because nothing in the three repos asserts them.

- `button`. Bits ships `src/lib/bits/button` and reka ships no button at all; neither has a test file. `hide-others` is the same: `reka-ui/packages/core/src/shared/useHideOthers.ts` exists and is never tested directly.
- Reka shared composables with source but no test file: `useId`, `useDirection`, `useEmitAsProps`, `useForwardPropsEmits`, `usePrimitiveElement`, `useHideOthers`, `useFocusGuards` (the `FocusGuards` component is tested, the composable only through it), and `useStateMachine`. `useId` is exercised indirectly by the `ConfigProvider` test and by the two hydration tests.
- Melt builders with no spec at all: `toast`, `table-of-contents`, `tree`, `toggle`, `listbox`, `progress`, `date-range-picker`, and `menu` (the last is covered only through `dropdown-menu` and `context-menu`). `collapsible` has no spec under `src/tests`; its only coverage is `src/stories/Collapsible/Collapsible.spec.ts`.
- Bits components with no test file: `button` and `aspect-ratio`. `menu` is covered only through `dropdown-menu`, `context-menu`, and `menubar`.
- Popper CSS custom properties (`--reka-popper-transform-origin`, `--reka-popper-available-width`/`-height`, `--reka-popper-anchor-width`/`-height`) are asserted nowhere. Neither are `avoidCollisions`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionBoundary`, `sticky`, `updatePositionStrategy`, or `arrowPadding`. The only positioning evidence is the Popper snapshot and a couple of `data-side` assertions.
- Collapsible and accordion content-height custom properties (`--reka-collapsible-content-height` and friends) exist in the source and are asserted by no test, because jsdom reports zero for every measurement.
- Splitter keyboard resizing, handle dragging, and persisted layout storage are asserted nowhere; the Splitter coverage is one axe check, two regression tests, and pure unit maths.
